ZGOD Leaves GodLike Esports, Says He Was “Going Through a Lot”
items.content:
In a surprising turn of events, Abhishek “ZGOD” Choudhary has bid farewell to GodLike Esports after being a part of the organization for several years. He announced the departure via an Instagram story on 14 November, where he wrote “Left GodLike!” He did not say when the split took effect, whether it was his decision, or the exact reason behind it. Furthermore, GodLike has not commented on his departure.
In the same Instagram Story, ZGOD acknowledged he had been “inactive lately” and said he “was going through a lot”. He added that he had “a lot to unpack” and would speak about it soon on stream.
ZGOD’s 5+ Year Stint With GodLike Esports Comes To An End
ZGOD joined GodLike Esports as a part of the team when the organization signed TSMEntity’s former Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI) roster. He competed as a player of GodLike Esports BGMI roster for four years, from August 2021 to August 2025.
During his tenure with GodLike Esports, the team showcased strong performance, winning Skyesports Championship 3.0, securing 4th position at Battlegrounds Mobile India Series 2021 (BGIS 2021), representing India at PUBG Mobile Global Championship 2021, securing the runner-up position in BGMI Masters Series Season 1, and more.
After 2021, the team failed to win an A-Tier tournament. As a result, in August 2025, the organization decided to rebuild its roster, and ZGOD was among the players released. Following his departure, he joined 4TR as a BGMI esports player but stayed with GodLike Esports as a content creator. Notably, he hasn’t played competitive BGMI since March 2026.
Since leaving GodLike Esports’ BGMI roster, ZGOD was seen actively creating content for GodLike Esports, including collabs with other creators from the organization. From the outside, the partnership looked stable. His recent quiet spell was the only hint that something might be off. For now, the details will have to wait for his stream or GodLike Esports’ statement.

items.title: BLAST Rivals 2026 Season 2 Semifinals Recap: FURIA to Face Spirit in Grand Final
items.content:
Gracing us with back-to-back matches, the semi-finals of the BLAST Rivals Season 2 2026 have reached the Grand Final. FURIA and Spirit secured dominant 2-0 victories against Falcons and MOUZ, respectively, giving us a highly exciting Grand Final clash to look forward to, and here is how it happened.
Spirit outclass MOUZ
.@TEAM__SPIRIT ARE YOUR FIRST GRAND FINALISTS! #BLASTPremier #MMarkEvents pic.twitter.com/ArDe8EQzr1
— BLAST Premier (@BLASTPremier) November 14, 2026
Despite their drop in form coming into the tournament, Spirit started strong with 9 rounds on the defence on MOUZ’s pick of Mirage. Having won only 3 rounds before switching sides, MOUZ went into their defence with 3 rounds to their name. Despite winning the pistol, Spirit dropped the ball, giving the momentum back to MOUZ, who managed to cut down on the lead but failed to keep their streak going. Winning 3 rounds in a row, Spirit managed to push the game over the line, taking an early lead in the series.
A 3-0 start to the second map saw MOUZ take the early lead on their CT side, only for Spirit to overtake them with 4 rounds of their own. As MOUZ managed a single round, Spirit closed the first half with 4 in a row as they took the lead with an 8-4 lead. MOUZ managed to stun Spirit early on after switching sides with a 7-round streak, giving them the lead for the second time in the series. As the MOUZ offence kept building momentum, it came crashing down when Spirit secured their first round on their CT side. Hitting the board on the defence, they managed to secure a 5-round streak to close the series with a 13-11 win.
FURIA breeze past Falcons
.@FURIA ARE HEADING TO THE GRAND FINAL! #BLASTPremier #MMarkEvents pic.twitter.com/sAfd2VuQc0
— BLAST Premier (@BLASTPremier) November 14, 2026
Falcons’ solid start fell apart in no time as FURIA’s defence started racking up rounds. Despite losing the pistol, FURIA converted the gun rounds later in the series to close out the first half with a narrow 7-5 lead. Having lost momentum, Falcons played catch-up for the entirety of the second half only to win the final two rounds of regulation to take the game to OT. Losing the first round, the Falcons had little room left as FURIA closed the opening map with two successful retakes on the CT side and took the lead in the series.
Despite starting with a 3-0 lead for the second time in the series, Falcons were left trailing as FURIA’s defence put up a rock-solid performance. Winning their first gun round, the Brazilian side managed to secure 7 rounds in a row to close the first half with a narrow lead. Winning the pistol, FURIA continued on their winning ways in the second half as a helpless Falcons side failed to secure a single round, closing the map with a 13-5 loss as FURIA secured the Grand Final spot with a statement performance.
Grand Final Schedule
In a grand final that can potentially be a major final before the major final, we are blessed with two of the top-performing teams in the tournament. On their day, the Grand Final is anybody’s to win, but Spirit edged FURIA out in terms of raw firepower, while FURIA have that experience under their belt to pull off a miracle in the Grand Final. Only time will tell how the best-of-five unfolds, but we have a very open clash to look forward to.

Red Bull will crown its Red Bull Wings Cup India champion at Kettle Studio in Bengaluru on 15 November. Eight EA Sports FC 27 finalists will play a knockout bracket for the national title. The winner will represent India at the Red Bull Wings Cup World Final in Miami. Rohit J Abraham faces Vanshaj Sharma and Saransh Jain plays Fadl Afridi in the quarter-finals.
The national final ends an Indian qualifying phase that ran from 28 September to 14 November. Players reached Bengaluru through two routes, the on-campus University League and the online Open League on PS5. Red Bull launched the Indian competition in Mumbai on 5 October.
Red Bull Wings Cup India National Final format and schedule
The eight finalists start in the quarter-finals, with the winners moving on to the semi-finals. The two semi-final winners then meet in a best-of-three championship final. A player must win all three rounds to take the national title and the Miami place. Red Bull has not said whether the quarter-finals and semi-finals are single matches or series.
Gates at Kettle Studio open at 5:30pm IST. Red Bull said a limited number of tickets are available through RSVP.
Vanshaj Sharma and Saransh Jain among eight Red Bull Wings Cup India finalists
The quarter-final draw pairs Rohit J Abraham with Vanshaj Sharma and Saransh Jain with Fadl Afridi. Satyam Jha meets Dhruv Keshwani, and Sharuk Sanjay plays Akshay S. Red Bull has not said how the winners of each tie will be paired in the semi-finals.
Vanshaj arrives in Bengaluru after representing RNTX at the FC Pro Open Global Qualifier in London earlier this month. He earned his place at that event through the Asia South qualifier before RNTX signed him on 4 November.
Saransh, 25, played for M42 Esports and then GodLike Esports from October 2022 to April 2025. He won eISL Season 2 in 2023 with NorthEast United and represented India at the FIFAe Nations Cup 2023. His career winnings stand at about $29,262.
Team GodLike, Team Apex Gaming and Banter TV join the Bengaluru programme
Team GodLike, Team Apex Gaming and Banter TV will make appearances at the national final. The evening also includes guest conversations and exhibition matches between the competitive rounds. Red Bull has not named the individual guests or said who will play in the exhibition games.
Both organisations have expanded beyond their core titles in recent weeks. Team Apex Gaming moved into EA FC Mobile on 7 November, signing DeMYSTeRIO and HaloZeus. GodLike is also returning to Valorant ahead of the VCT 2027 open qualifiers.
Red Bull Wings Cup gives players exclusive in-game rewards and a route from national competition to an international final. Its World Final combines EA Sports FC 27 matches with physical football challenges. Red Bull Wings Cup India feeds into the Miami World Final, which is expected in January 2027.

items.title: Nvidia Investors With $2.1 Billion at Stake Ask Board to Keep Jensen Huang’s Return on the Table
items.content:
Two investors whose funds held about $2.1 billion of Nvidia stock in June have asked its board not to rush into naming a new chief executive, and to keep Jensen Huang’s possible return open. Brad Gerstner, chief executive of Altimeter Capital, and Gavin Baker, managing partner and chief investment officer of Atreides Management, made their joint letter public on Friday.
In it, they urge the board to “pursue a slow, measured, and deliberate process regarding the future leadership of Nvidia that leaves all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang”. Nvidia has not responded publicly to the letter.
The request came a day after Huang resigned as president, chief executive and director, effective immediately, while an investigation into his conduct was under way. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is now interim chief executive, and former Synopsys chief executive Harvey Jones became the board’s first chair, according to Nvidia’s announcement and its filing with US regulators. The letter also differs sharply from the viral “employee letter” that spread the same day, which copied OpenAI’s 2023 staff letter almost word for word. This one was published by the two investors who signed it.
The letter asks Nvidia’s board for time and accepts its final say
The letter runs to four short paragraphs, and most of it argues against speed. “There are more questions about recent events than answers,” the two investors write. They say the board “should avoid a rush to replace Jensen that undermines and thwarts the best interests of shareholders”. In their view, the company “will be capably led in the interim by Colette Kress and team”, which means the board has time to get the decision right.
Gerstner and Baker also accept that the decision belongs to the board. “If after all the facts are known the Board decides that it is not in shareholders’ best interest to have Jensen Huang back as CEO, that is the Board’s prerogative,” the letter says. They add that Huang, as founder and long-time leader, “has earned the right for a deliberate process that avoids any needless rush to replace him before all the facts are known”. The letter does not dispute the reports about Huang’s conduct, and it does not ask for him to be reinstated now.
Some viral summaries said the investors wanted “a more thorough investigation” before any decision. The letter does not use that phrase, and it does not mention the review led by former federal prosecutor Joon Kim and Wachtell Lipton, which the board’s independent directors commissioned before Huang left. It asks only that no successor be chosen before “all the facts are known”, and it sets no timetable. The board has not said when the review is expected to finish.
Two funds holding 0.04% of Nvidia cannot force the board’s hand
In voting terms, the two funds are small holders. Altimeter held about 9.4 million Nvidia shares at the end of June and Atreides about 1.25 million, according to figures from their quarterly 13F filings reported by FourWeekMBA. Together those stakes were worth roughly $2.1 billion at the time, or about 0.04% of Nvidia’s shares. Huang himself owns around 3.6% of the company.
Under Nvidia’s bylaws, the board appoints and removes the chief executive, and a majority of its directors can dismiss one with or without cause. Shareholders elect the directors at the annual meeting. Between meetings, they can call a special meeting only if they own at least 15% of the shares “continuously for at least one year”, according to the company’s 2026 proxy statement. Altimeter and Atreides are nowhere near that threshold, and adding Huang’s own stake would still leave any group far short of it. The letter is a request, and its authors present it as one.
The board’s own search is at an early stage. Nvidia’s board told CNBC this week that it was “in the process of selecting a search firm” and had “not formally engaged any potential candidates”. Reports have named Arm chief executive Rene Haas as one of the executives approached, while Nvidia has called speculation about candidates “premature”, according to Bloomberg. The board has said it “will consider internal and external candidates”, a field TalkEsport examined when it looked at who could replace Huang.
Gerstner and Baker add an investor voice to pressure from staff and Musk
The letter adds shareholders to a campaign that has been building inside and around Nvidia since Huang left. Inside the company, a post on Nvidia’s internal suggestion box urging the board to share its findings has drawn more than 1,600 comments, according to internal messages reviewed by WIRED. Before he resigned, 88% of Nvidia staff who answered a Blind survey said he should stay as chief executive. That support falls well short of the signed staff revolt the viral letter claimed, although it shows where many employees stand.
Outside the company, Elon Musk has said that hiring Huang “would be an honour”, and he has since backed an online petition called Stand with Jensen. The petition asks the board to restore Huang as chief executive until the investigation is complete, and to publish the inquiry’s scope and expected completion date. That goes further than Gerstner and Baker, who asked only that his return remain possible. Musk said he intended to sign it, and an entry bearing his name later appeared on the site, although the petition does not explain how it verifies signatures or say who runs it.
Nvidia’s next scheduled update for investors comes when it reports third-quarter results on 17 November. Kress has said her focus as interim chief executive is on customers, partners and shareholders. The board has not said whether it will address the leadership search on that call. The results will be Nvidia’s first since Huang’s resignation.
The post Nvidia Investors With $2.1 Billion at Stake Ask Board to Keep Jensen Huang’s Return on the Table appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Zupee Raised $100+ Million as a Gaming Company, When the Money Games Ended, It Called Itself AI
items.content:
Zupee told the market on 16 October that it was leaving gaming to build “AI-led” businesses for India. A month later, it has laid off its entire remaining workforce and looks close to shutting down, Inc42 reported, with severance covering staff until January 2027. Along the way, it closed its microdrama app Zupee Studio and its astrology platform NeoAstro. Investors had put more than $121 million into the company, roughly ₹1,000 crore at today’s exchange rate, on the promise that it was one of India’s leading gaming platforms.
The collapse was triggered by a law, not by a scandal, and nothing reported suggests Zupee broke any rules. Yet its rise and fall show how easily a fashionable label can stand in for a business. Zupee called itself a gaming company from 2018 until October, and when the money ran out it reached for the next label investors like. The question is what, beneath both labels, anyone was actually backing.
Zupee’s profits came from money contests, not from games
Zupee was founded in 2018 by Dilsher Singh Malhi and Siddhant Saurabh, two IIT Kanpur graduates. Malhi studied chemical engineering and worked as a research associate at EPFL in Switzerland, according to his IIT Kanpur profile, while Saurabh was a software engineer at the trading firm Graviton Research Capital. Neither had worked in games before Zupee, according to those profiles. The company started as a quiz app, then found its market in Ludo, Snakes and Ladders and Carrom, played for cash entry fees and cash prizes.
That model made serious money while it lasted. Zupee reported revenue of more than ₹1,100 crore and its first full-year profit, ₹146 crore, in the 2024 financial year, according to Entrackr. It closed a $102 million round in January 2022, with reports putting its valuation above $500 million, and signed a content partnership with Reliance Jio. Those numbers, however, came from players paying to compete for cash, not from players buying or playing games for their own sake.
The difference became obvious once paid contests ended. Zupee shut all of its paid games in August 2025 and kept free versions of Ludo Supreme, Ludo Turbo and Snakes and Ladders running. Without the entry fees, those games could not carry the company, and it cut about 170 jobs in September 2025 and about 200 more in January, YourStory reported. A business that loses its revenue overnight when cash prizes are removed was a contests business with games attached.
The regulatory risk was visible years before the ban
None of this should have surprised anyone writing cheques. Karnataka and Tamil Nadu both tried to outlaw real-money games before 2025. The 28% GST on the full value of deposits, in force since October 2023, showed how little goodwill the sector had left with policymakers. The industry’s defence rested on a label: these were games of skill, it argued, and so they were “gaming”, not gambling. Investors priced Zupee as a gaming platform, while its revenue depended on a legal distinction that the government could remove.
The central government removed that distinction in 2025. The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act received presidential assent on 22 August 2025 and banned money games outright, whether based on skill or chance. It came into full force on 1 May 2026, along with a ban on advertising such games and on processing their payments. Dream11, MPL and Gameskraft also stopped paid contests after the bill passed. Companies that earned money from games themselves, such as Krafton with BGMI, carried on, and Indian esports kept funding events such as the ₹1 crore BGMI Showdown.
‘AI’ became the next label, without a plan behind it
Zupee’s last move followed a pattern that is familiar from other start-ups. Before October, it had already tried microdramas and astrology, two of the more fashionable consumer bets of the past year. Its October statement then promised AI-led businesses built on its real-time multiplayer technology and its experience with first-time internet users, but named no product, partner or timeline. “There was no AI plan,” a source told Inc42.
The one asset Zupee could point to was scale, as it cited experience serving more than 200 million users. That audience, however, was built around cash contests that Indian law no longer allows. An audience gathered by prize money is hard to carry into an unrelated AI product, and Zupee never said how it would try.
Zupee is far from the only company to lean on the word. Builder.ai, backed by Microsoft, raised more than $450 million on the promise of AI-assisted app development, before entering insolvency in May 2025 amid questions over its sales figures, TechCrunch reported. In the US, the Securities and Exchange Commission fined two investment advisers in 2024 for what it called “AI washing”. “Such AI washing hurts investors,” then chair Gary Gensler said.
The contrast with companies that actually build things is stark. Krafton, which makes games, released its own on-device AI model this week with published specifications, a licence and a model card. Zupee’s pivot came with a press statement and nothing anyone could test. Investors who funded a cash-contest platform as a games company, and then heard “AI” as a next step, were buying the label both times.
What is left of Zupee, and of its investors’ money, is unclear. Inc42 said the company’s remaining cash, assets and liabilities are unknown, and its proposed purchase of the microdrama start-up Vertical TV fell through.
The post Zupee Raised $100+ Million as a Gaming Company, When the Money Games Ended, It Called Itself AI appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Man Arrested in Delhi Over Death of Kolkata Woman He Met Through PUBG
items.content:
Police have arrested Dharambir Kumar, a man from Uttar Pradesh, outside Anand Vihar railway station in New Delhi over the death of 26-year-old Anjali Shaw in Baranagar, north of Kolkata. Kumar was picked up late on 12 November in a joint operation by a special team from Baranagar police station and Delhi Police. According to police and her family, the two had met while playing PUBG. Kumar is being brought to West Bengal on transit remand for questioning, OJAS reported.
Shaw’s body was found with injury marks on the night of 10 November in a fifth-floor flat in the Lakepally area of Baranagar. The flat belongs to her elder sister and brother-in-law, who now live mostly in Srirampore, and it was empty at the time. Shaw had collected the key from a neighbour that afternoon, and police broke the door down that night after her sister could not reach her by phone, OJAS reported. Police have not disclosed the cause of death, and the case was first treated as a possible suicide before injuries and missing valuables pointed investigators towards a suspected murder. A cousin has alleged that she had injury marks on her neck and face.
Baranagar police look into a possible dispute between Anjali Shaw and Dharambir Kumar
Police suspect that a personal or financial dispute between the two may have led to her death, although they have not confirmed a motive. Police sources told OJAS they are also examining a disagreement over playing PUBG together. Shaw’s father said the pair were friends and that Kumar used to call her his sister, and he said Kumar had given his home address as somewhere near Lucknow. Kumar’s age has not been made public, and police have not said what charges he faces or whether he has a lawyer.
Kuntal Banerjee, Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) of the Barrackpore Police Commissionerate, said the accused was being brought from Delhi and that his questioning would reveal more about the case. Investigators believe Kumar left with Shaw’s jewellery and mobile phone. Her family says the missing items include her watch, a ring, a bracelet and earrings. Investigators also say Kumar repeatedly switched the phone on and off after the incident, apparently to confuse attempts to track his location.
Police believe he used her phone to send WhatsApp messages to her father and to make a brief, silent call to her mother. Her family told OJAS that a reply from her number invited them to ask whatever they wanted. A second message then read, “I’m among you, but you won’t catch me.” The family handed screenshots of those messages to police, who traced Kumar through mobile tower data and other inputs.
Police still checking CCTV footage in Lakepally
Officers are reviewing CCTV footage from Shitala Mata Lane and Lakepally, partly to check whether anyone else was involved. Footage from the housing complex helped investigators identify the suspect earlier in the week, OJAS reported. Police have not named any other suspect, and they are also questioning family members, neighbours and other residents of the building. Local MLA Sajal Ghosh, who visited the family, said the culprit would be caught but that police needed time to complete the investigation.
It is not clear which version of the game the pair played. PUBG Mobile itself has been blocked in India since 2020, and many players still use the name for BGMI, KRAFTON’s Indian version of the game. Police have not said whether they have examined either player’s game account or in-game chats.
Police in several countries have investigated cases in which victims first met a suspect through online games. Disputes linked to mobile games have also turned violent in India before, including the stabbing of a 17-year-old in Thane after a match. In the US, a missing Utah teenager was rescued after asking for help through an Among Us player, and the UK is considering a ban on in-game voice chat with strangers for under-16s. Police expect his questioning to establish the motive and the sequence of events at the flat.
The post Man Arrested in Delhi Over Death of Kolkata Woman He Met Through PUBG appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: PUBG MOBILE FLASH Is Out Worldwide: Under 1GB, Runs on 2GB RAM and Shares Your PUBG MOBILE Account
items.content:
PUBG MOBILE FLASH, the official lightweight version of PUBG MOBILE, is now available worldwide for free on Android and iOS. The app launched on 13 November with an initial download of 0.96GB on Android and under 2GB on iOS, and it runs on phones with as little as 2GB of RAM. It was co-developed by Tencent Games’ LightSpeed Studios and KRAFTON, and picked up 27 million pre-registrations before launch, according to the official launch announcement. Players who log in keep the same account, friends, matches and items they already have in PUBG MOBILE.
That last point is what separates FLASH from the old PUBG Mobile Lite. Lite, released in 2019 and since discontinued, used its own accounts and smaller matches, so players on budget phones were effectively cut off from everyone else. FLASH is a lighter client for the same game, with cross-play against the full app and updates synchronised with it. It was first shown at the PUBG Mobile World Cup in August as PUBG Mobile Light, before it was renamed FLASH in September.
The move targets the players PUBG MOBILE has found hardest to keep. Much of the audience it still wants to reach plays on budget Android phones with little free storage, in markets where Garena’s Free Fire built its lead by running on modest hardware. A sub-1GB client with a 2GB RAM floor brings PUBG MOBILE into that segment without splitting its player base, which was the main weakness of Lite.
FLASH ships with Erangel only and downloads everything else on demand
The size saving comes from what FLASH leaves out of the first install. Only Erangel and Classic Battle Royale are pre-installed, while other maps, modes, events and higher-quality graphics packs are downloaded when players choose them, the press release says. A confirmation step stops those packs from downloading automatically, which matters on prepaid data plans. The lobby is simplified, icons are lightweight by default, and players who have not downloaded a cosmetic item see a temporary outfit in its place until they fetch the files.
Performance settings run at 25, 30, 40 or 60 frames per second, depending on the device. Compared with the FLASH beta, PUBG MOBILE says it is targeting a 10% higher average frame rate, 10% better frame-rate stability and 3% lower power use. It is also aiming for 12% less memory use, a 15% shorter startup screen and 20% faster loading before matches. The company describes those numbers as targets, not results guaranteed on every phone, so real gains will vary by chipset and storage speed.
Security is shared with the main game too. FLASH uses the same Ban Pan anti-cheat system as PUBG MOBILE, including real-time cheat detection, enforcement and its Investigator system. Since FLASH players share matches with players on the full game, PUBG MOBILE says they are covered by the same protections.
For players on high-end phones, the full PUBG MOBILE app still makes more sense. FLASH tops out at 60 frames per second, while the main app offers 90 frames per second and higher on supported devices. Because progress is shared between the two apps, switching later costs nothing more than the download.
The launch lands a day after PUBG MOBILE’s 4.7 update
FLASH arrived a day after PUBG MOBILE version 4.7, the winter update built around the Arctic Chronicles theme mode. Since the two apps stay in sync, FLASH players get the same seasonal content, although large modes have to be downloaded separately. PUBG MOBILE has also set aside more than US$2.3 million in launch rewards and incentives for players and creators, and its UK announcement highlights a US$1 million Perks Station event.
“We’ve listened closely to player feedback throughout beta testing,” said Rick Li, producer of PUBG MOBILE and deputy general manager of Quantum Studio at LightSpeed Studios. Vincent Wang, general manager and head of PUBG MOBILE publishing at Tencent Games, framed the launch as part of a wider push on access. “Expanding access to PUBG MOBILE has always been an important part of our long-term vision,” he said. Players can download it from the App Store and Google Play, with links on the official FLASH website.
India gets BGMI Air instead on 10 December
FLASH is not available in India, according to tbreak, where PUBG MOBILE has been blocked since 2020. Indian players have their own lightweight option from KRAFTON India, as BGMI Air launches on 10 December after crossing 14 million pre-registrations. Like FLASH, it promises a download of about 1GB and keeps existing progress, in its case through players’ BGMI accounts.
For everyone else, FLASH is live now and replaces the need to free up several gigabytes before joining friends on the full game. The 13 November release date was confirmed earlier this week, and the app went live on schedule on both stores. PUBG MOBILE says future updates to FLASH will be fully synchronised with the main game.
The post PUBG MOBILE FLASH Is Out Worldwide: Under 1GB, Runs on 2GB RAM and Shares Your PUBG MOBILE Account appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: LoL Esports 2027: First Stand changes, all host cities
items.content:
Riot Games unveiled their plans for League of Legends (LoL) Esports in 2027. The first event of the year, First Stand: All In, promises to feature the most amount of teams in an international ever. It also announced the host cities for all international events, as well as a potential integration for the Demacia Cup into Worlds.
Key Takeaways
First Stand: All In is a one-time event featuring the most amount of teams in an international LoL Esports event ever.
China, Spain, Japan, and South Korea will host First Stand, MSI, and Worlds.
First Stand 2028 confirmed for Southeast Asia.
The Demacia Cup might be integrated into teams’ Path to Worlds.
LoL Esports host cities for 2027
First Stand: All In 2027 – China (moved from Southeast Asia)
MSI 2027 – Valencia, Spain
Worlds 2027
Swiss Stage – Nagoya, Japan
Quarters and Semis – Suwon, South Korea
Grand Final – Seoul, South Korea
First Stand 2027 was initially announced for Southeast Asia. Riot has opted to move the event, now officially named First Stand: All In, to China.
MSI 2027 will be in Feria de Valencia in Spain. (Image credit: Riot Games)
MSI 2027 will take place in Valencia, Spain. This places it in the same city as the second VALORANT Masters of 2027, possibly reducing logistical and operational costs for the organizer.
Worlds 2027 Swiss Stage will be in Nagoya, Japan. (Image credit: Riot Games)
Worlds 2027 will be split between two host countries and three cities: Nagoya, Japan, and Suwon and Seoul, South Korea.
First Stand: All In 2027
Riot revealed the “All In” branding through a LoL Esports post. It said that with the change comes a major expansion and All In will be “a one-time event that will bring more teams, more players, and more of our global community together to kick off the competitive season.”
(Image credit: Riot Games)
It also says that First Stand: All In 2027 will be the largest tournament Riot has ever produced. As part of this expansion, the event veers away from the initial plan of being hosted in Southeast Asia to China.
SEA fans need not worry though, as Riot promises to deliver First Stand 2028 to the region.
The LoL Esports team will share more about First Stand: All In 2027 on January.
Demacia Cup in Worlds 2027?
Riot will bring Worlds 2027 to Japan for the Swiss Stage and South Korea for the Knockouts Stage. More importantly, it is “evaluating whether [Demacia Cup] could replace” the Play-In Stage for Worlds 2027.
This comes after great reception of the Demacia Cup Global Invitational, which welcomed international teams for the first time in 2026.
Worlds 2027 Grand Final will be in the brand-new Seoul Arena in South Korea. (Image credit: Riot Games)
Nothing has been finalized so far, but we can expect to hear whether DCGI will be integrated into the path to Worlds as it gets closer.

The latest Fortnite Music Pass added popular virtual singer Kasane Teto as a playable skin. This is the first Music Mini-Pass, which unfortunately launched with issues that prevents players the ability to gift it to others.

You can gift the Music Pass, but the option is currently disabled
Epic Games has not provided any updates regarding when it will work again
The current Music Pass will remain in place until Dec. 11, 2026
Can you gift the Music Pass in Fortnite?
Yes, you can normally gift the Music Pass in Fortnite. Unfortunately, players are currently unable to gift it to other players. If you go to the Music Pass tab in-game, you will find the ‘Gift Pass’ option grayed out.

Hey Vanessa – this Music Mini Pass can’t be gifted due to a technical issue. Other Passes aren’t affected.

Marvel Rivals Nightcrawler abilities, team-ups, and skins
items.content:
Marvel Rivals Season 11 is now live, which means players can duke it out as Nightcrawler. Here’s everything you need to know about Nightcrawler’s abilities, team-ups, skins, and more.
Key takeaways
Nightcrawler became playable in Marvel Rivals with the launch of Season 11 on Nov. 13.
As a strategist hero, Nightcrawler has teleportation abilities, sword attacks, and healing grenades to damage foes and support teammates.
His Phasing Finale ultimate teleports nearby teammates one by one, gives them a damage boost, grants them healing over time, and creates a Smoke Domain.
Nightcrawler’s team-ups at launch are Protective Siblings with Rogue and Demon Disciple with Magik.
At launch, Nightcrawler has the Steadfast Swordsman, Hope Soared, and X-Force costumes.
Table of contents
Marvel Rivals Nightcrawler abilities
Marvel Rivals Nightcrawler team-ups
Marvel Rivals Nightcrawler skins
Marvel Rivals Nightcrawler FAQs
Marvel Rivals Nightcrawler abilities
In Marvel Rivals, Nightcrawler can toss grenades that explode on impact thanks to Forged Brimstone. These grenades damage enemies and heals teammates. His right-click, meanwhile, is Three-Sword Style, which allows him to potentially land critical hits. In terms of Nightcrawler’s teleportation powers, they are represented by Swift Intervention, Smoke Shift, Tandem Teleport, and his Phasing Finale ultimate. This hero can also cling to walls thanks to his Crawler Cling passive.
Nightcrawler AbilityDetails
Forged Brimstone (Left-click)Toss three consecutive grenades forward that explode on impact. Forged Brimestone damages enemies and heals allies.
Three-Sword Style (Right-click)Strike forward with continuous thrusts using two cutlasses and the Hopesword. Three-Sword Style can deal critical damage.
Phasing Finale (Q) (Ultimate) Select a target location to teleport all nearby allies there one by one, giving them a damage boost and healing over time while creating a Smoke Domain at the destination. Nightcrawler can also cast Phasing Finale again to teleport to and slash all enemies within his Smoke Domain, pulling them to his location.
Swift Intervention (Shift)Target an ally and teleport to their side, granting them an instant heal, a healing boost, and healing over time.
Smoke Shift (E)Mark a starting point with brimstone smoke and dash forward in a spinning slash to deal damage to enemies. The dash creates a smoke blast that damages and launches enemies while healing allies. Smoke Shift can also be recast shortly after, with the third activation teleporting Nightcrawler back to the initial point.
Tandem Teleport (F)Send an invitation to an ally. Upon confirmation, teleport to their side and pull them back to Nightcrawler’s original location, granting both players instant healing and healing over time.
Crawler Cling (Spacebar) (Passive)Hold the space bar to cling to walls and crawl freely along vertical surfaces.
Marvel Rivals Nightcrawler team-ups
In terms of Nightcrawler’s team-ups at launch, they’re with Rogue and Magik. Both of these team-ups have a base and enhanced effect.
Team-Up AbilityDetails
Protective Siblings (Rogue)Base Effect: Rogue infuses Nightcrawler with Chronovium Power. Upon activation, briefly vanish, and the energy radiates outward from your vanishing point, damaging enemies and healing allies. After a short delay, reappear above your original location, slamming down with three swords to deal secondary damage and apply a Slow to enemies in range.
Enhanced Effect: Nightcrawler recalls the Chronovium Power after his downward strike. The recall heals allies, damages enemies, and launches enemies toward him.
Demon Disciple (Magik)Base Effect: Magik empowers Nightcrawler with Limbo’s demonic magic. Each spatial warp (all 3 stages of Smoke Shift, both stages of Tandem Teleport, or the single stage of Swift Intervention) generates a spell field that damages enemies and heals allies.
Enhanced Effect: Each warp also generates demonic armor, granting bonus health.
Nightcrawler at launch (Image credit: NetEase Games)
Marvel Rivals Nightcrawler skins
Steadfast Swordsman Nightcrawler
Hope Soared Nightcrawler
X-Force Nightcrawler
As for Nightcrawler’s starting skins, Marvel Rivals players can get his Steadfast Swordsman one plus the Hope Soared and X-Force recolors at launch.
Nightcrawler in Marvel Rivals (Image credit: NetEase Games)
Marvel Rivals Nightcrawler FAQs
When was Nightcrawler released in Marvel Rivals?
Nightcrawler entered Marvel Rivals in Season 11 on Nov. 13.
What role does Nightcrawler play in Marvel Rivals?
Nightcrawler is a strategist hero in Marvel Rivals.
What are Nightcrawler’s abilities in Marvel Rivals?
Nightcrawler’s abilities are Forged Brimstone, Three-Sword Style, Phasing Finale, Swift Intervention, Smoke Shift, and Tandem Teleport. His passive is Crawler Cling.
What is Nightcrawler’s ultimate ability in Marvel Rivals?
His ultimate is called Phasing Finale in Marvel Rivals. It teleports nearby allies to a location and gives them a damage boost plus healing over time.
Which heroes have team-up abilities with Nightcrawler?
In Marvel Rivals, Nightcrawler has two team-up abilities at launch. They are Protective Siblings with Rogue and Demon Disciple with Magik.
What skins does Nightcrawler have in Marvel Rivals?
At launch, Nightcrawler has the Steadfast Swordsman, Hope Soared, and X-Force costumes.

China’s State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) has cleared Savvy Games Group’s parent entity Saudi Electronic Games Holding Company’s planned acquisition of MOONTON Games, the developer of Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MLBB). This brings the reported $6 billion-plus deal with ByteDance one step closer to completion.
The approval, completed on Oct. 29 and published on Nov. 6, advances the acquisition that ByteDance agreed to in March 2026. Nearly eight months after the agreement was announced, the transaction has yet to close.
Key takeaways
China’s SAMR approved Saudi Electronic Games Holding Company’s acquisition of MOONTON Games.
Saudi Electronic Games Holding Company is a parent company of Savvy Games.
The acquisition would bring the publisher of MLBB under the same Saudi-backed investment ecosystem as ESL FACEIT Group and the Esports World Cup.
Table of contents
Savvy Games Group agreed to acquire Moonton for more than $6 billion
What Savvy Games Group’s acquisition of MLBB means for its esports scene
Savvy Games Group agreed to acquire Moonton for more than $6 billion
SAMR included the acquisition in its list of mergers approved without conditions between Oct. 26 and Nov. 1. The notice identifies Saudi Electronic Games Holding Company as the acquirer and Moonton Holdings Limited and Shanghai Moonton Technology Co., Ltd. as the target companies.
The notice does not mention Savvy Games Group by name. However, Saudi Electronic Games Holding Company is its parent entity, according to the Canadian trademark registration. Savvy is wholly owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF).
Savvy confirmed in March that it had signed an agreement to acquire Moonton from ByteDance for a reported price exceeding $6 billion. Neither company has disclosed the exact purchase price. ByteDance acquired MOONTON Games back in 2021 for approximately $4 billion before revealing its plans to restructure its gaming business in 2023.
What Savvy Games Group’s acquisition of MLBB means for its esports scene
The acquisition could have broader implications for esports. This is considering the number of major gaming and tournament organizations connected to Saudi Arabia’s PIP.
Savvy owns ESL FACEIT Group. Meanwhile, a PIF-led consortium completed its $55 billion acquisition of Electronic Arts in August 2026. The Esports Foundation, which organizes the Esports World Cup (EWC), is also part of Saudi Arabia’s esports ecosystem.
MOONTON Games would add one of mobile esports’ biggest titles to these holdings. The company operates MLBB and organizes its professional leagues and annual M-series world championship.
MLBB sees around 40 to 50 million monthly players and over 1.5 billion installs worldwide. The game is also featured at the EWC, with the 2026 MLBB Mid Season Cup carrying a $3 million prize pool. It’s currently the biggest mobile esports title in Southeast Asia (SEA) and is slowly gaining global traction. Its largest markets include Indonesia and the Philippines.
It is still unclear whether MOONTON Games’ esports operations will remain independent or eventually coordinate more closely with ESL FACEIT Group.

Leaked Marvel Rivals characters

Jubilee, Gorr, and now Nightcrawler were leaked by dataminers before they officially joined Marvel Rivals.

Marvel Rivals typically adds a new hero at the start of each season and another hero at the season’s halfway point.

items.title: This Gaming Chair Lets You Actually Feel Every Gunshot and Crash
items.content:
Razer Soma Pro is a new gaming chair that adds haptic motors, built-in speakers, and reactive RGB lighting to one seat. Razer announced it alongside the Razer Soma Sensa HD Haptics, a cheaper model that focuses on haptic feedback only. The Soma Pro costs $999.99. The Soma Sensa HD Haptics costs $569.99. Both chairs are on sale now.
Below, you can read how the haptics work, what each chair includes, and how they compare with the Soma Chroma.
Razer Soma Pro launch, price, and availability
Razer announced the Razer Soma Pro and the Soma Sensa HD Haptics today. Both are wireless gaming chairs with haptic feedback built into the seat. The Soma Pro also adds speakers and RGB lighting.
The Soma Pro costs $999.99 in the US, £999.99 in the UK, and €1,029.99 in Europe. The Soma Sensa HD Haptics costs $569.99, £569.99, and €589.99. These are the MSRP figures Razer listed.
See the sights, hear every sound and feel the moments. Project Madison comes to life with the Razer Soma Pro: https://t.co/96VRH7bWB0.
The ultimate gaming throne for those who want to immerse themselves fully, the Razer Soma Pro combines Razer Chroma RGB, THX Spatial Audio and… pic.twitter.com/LjeGoCQVgF
— R Λ Z Ξ R (@Razer) November 13, 2026
Both chairs are available now at Razer.com, RazerStores, and select retailers worldwide. Razer is also offering US$50 in store credit for Soma Pro orders placed during launch week.
The new models follow the Razer Soma Chroma, the company’s first RGB gaming chair.
How Razer Sensa HD Haptics works in the chair
Both new chairs use 6 haptic motor actuators. Razer Sensa HD Haptics technology powers them. The motors produce vibrations that follow the intensity, direction, and distance of supported in-game events.
According to Razer, players can tell sensations apart. For example, an explosion on the left feels different from an impact nearby. Razer describes the result as multi-zone feedback rather than a simple rumble.
The chairs also work with content that has no native haptic support. Razer Synapse software converts audio into vibrations. This applies to unsupported games, movies, and music. The haptics are built into the seat, so no external accessories are needed.
A built-in control panel handles the settings. Players can change the vibration intensity and switch between haptic profiles. The same panel switches between wireless connection types.
Soma Pro speakers and Chroma RGB lighting
The Soma Pro is the only new model with speakers. They support THX Spatial Audio, so game audio plays directly from the chair. Players can use the speakers alone or pair them with front speakers for a wider surround sound setup.
The Soma Pro also has Razer Chroma RGB lighting. It reacts to in-game events in more than 300 integrated games. Razer claims 16.8 million colors. Players can sync the lighting with other compatible Razer devices through Synapse.
Razer says the Soma Pro is the only gaming chair that combines haptics, THX Spatial Audio, and Chroma RGB in one seat. The Soma Sensa HD Haptics focuses on physical feedback only.
Comfort features and build
Both chairs share a built-in lumbar arch and a dual-density, cold-cured foam seat cushion. The backrest reclines up to 132 degrees. A steel frame supports both models.
The Soma Pro adds 4D armrests, a magnetic head cushion, and a frog tilt mechanism. It also has a 5-star powder-coated aluminum alloy wheelbase. Razer says this gives it the most adjustable fit in the line.
Razer backs both chairs with a 3-year warranty on mechanisms and moving parts. Electronic parts get a 2-year warranty.
Power and connectivity
Both chairs support Razer HyperSpeed Wireless (2.4 GHz) for PC. They also support Bluetooth LE for compatible mobile devices.
Neither chair needs a permanent power cable to a wall outlet. A single USB Type-C connection draws power from a wall outlet or a compatible power bank.
Razer does not include the power bank or the power adapter. It lists the required specs as a 20,000 mAh power bank rated 45 W or above with PD 2.0 or above. The adapter must be 45 W or above for the Soma Pro and 27 W or above for the Soma Sensa HD Haptics.
The Soma Pro includes a USB Type-C extension cable. The Soma Sensa HD Haptics does not.
Soma Pro, Soma Sensa HD Haptics, and Soma Chroma compared
The Soma Pro is the only chair with all 3 features. The Soma Sensa HD Haptics adds haptics only. The Soma Chroma has RGB lighting only, based on Razer’s own product comparison.
The Soma Pro costs $430 more than the Soma Sensa HD Haptics. That gap covers the speakers, the lighting, and the extra comfort parts. The Razer gaming chair range now has 3 models, and each one targets a different budget.
The post This Gaming Chair Lets You Actually Feel Every Gunshot and Crash appeared first on TalkEsport.

How Rocket League MMR works
Rocket League players can now display their MMR if they wish to do so. Enabling this option shows their MMR in competitive playlists and the scoreboard after a ranked match.
Rocket League content creator Americas_F1nest also explained how MMR works in a video. According to him, players usually gain around 9 to 10 MMR per game. However, this can be higher during placement matches and vary slightly based on rank differences between teammates.
At the start of a season, players can also gain around 25 to 30 MMR during their first 10 placement matches before gains gradually return to normal.
What MMR is SSL in Rocket League?
Rocket League has 22 competitive ranks, starting with Bronze 1 and ending at SSL. SSL is the highest rank in the game and the only rank without divisions. According to data from rocketleague.tracker.network, the SSL MMR for Ranked Duel 1v1, Ranked Doubles 2v2, and Ranked Standard 3v3 are 1,353 to 1,606, 1,863 to 2,002, and 1,868 to 1,894, respectively.

Rocket League season rewards
Rocket League seasons typically last about 3 to 4 months, and players unlock rewards based on their seasonal rank. Once a new season begins, players start receiving their rewards.
At the start of each season, players begin in the Unranked tier and must progress toward rewards by winning ranked matches. After achieving 10 match wins, players receive a rank based on their skill level. To unlock the next reward tier, players must then earn another 10 wins at that rank or higher.

Rocket League ranks FAQs
How many Rocket League ranks are there?
Rocket League has 22 competitive ranks, starting at Bronze 1 and ending at SSL. Each rank from Bronze 1 through Grand Champion 3 is divided into four divisions. The SSL rank is the only one without divisions.
What is the highest Rocket League rank?
The highest Rocket League rank is SSL.
What is MMR in Rocket League?
MMR is the rating that determines your Rocket League rank. Players gain MMR by winning competitive matches. Match difficulty is factored in as well.
What MMR is SSL?
The MMR required to reach SSL in Rocket League varies by playlist. The SSL MMR for Ranked Duel 1v1, Ranked Doubles 2v2, and Ranked Standard 3v3 are 1,353 to 1,606, 1,863 to 2,002, and 1,868 to 1,894.
How many SSL players are there?
The number of SSL players in Rocket League varies by playlist as well. Epic Games has not officially revealed the number of Rocket League players in each rank, but we do know that SSL makes up only a small percentage of the player base.
Can you see MMR in Rocket League?
Yes. Rocket League players can display their MMR in competitive playlists. MMR appears on the scoreboard after a ranked match as well.
What rank is the average Rocket League player?
Most Rocket League players sit around the Gold rank.
How do you rank up faster in Rocket League?
The fastest way to rank up is by consistently winning competitive matches. Practice, have map awareness, communicate with your teammates, and get familiar with each competitive mode to rank up faster.
Do casual matches affect your Rocket League rank?
No. Casual matches do not affect your competitive rank in Rocket League.

A jury of media outlets and creators decides 90% of the result in the main categories. Fan votes make up the other 10%. Fans vote here until Wednesday, December 9, at 6pm PT.

Together, they struck out on their own, founding the two-person indie studio Freshly Baked Games and trading the security of industry jobs for the creative freedom — and financial uncertainty — of building something entirely theirs. Many years later, the result was a prototype for a game… that was way too ambitious (but they fully intend to return to). So they went back to a different concept, a stripped-down first-person fantasy inspired by FromSoftware's cult-classic King's Field. That was supposed to take a year to build. Three years later, the game, Queen’s Domain, is an ambitious torrent of weaponry, monster encounters, and Berger’s patented 3D level design, all spread across an low-poly open-world map.

items.title: Hugo Martin returns as id Software begins work on its next game
items.content:
While DOOM: The Dark Ages players will soon be getting a new endless combat mode, id Software is already at work on its next game. As part of Xbox's 25th anniversary celebrations, Xbox and Bethesda have confirmed that a new project is now in development under long-time DOOM director Hugo Martin.
Before moving on entirely, id Software still has one more update planned for DOOM: The Dark Ages. Slaughter Mode launches next week as a free addition for players who own the Revelations DLC, Premium Edition or Premium Upgrade. The new mode throws players into endless, randomised combat encounters where each run can be extended for greater rewards, or cashed out early to secure earned Skulls before disaster strikes.
Looking beyond The Dark Ages, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirmed that id Software's next game has officially entered development. In a follow-up statement, the studio revealed that teams across its Texas and Frankfurt offices are already working on the project, with Hugo Martin returning as Game Director.
The announcement comes just months after widespread concern over id Software's future following Xbox's latest round of layoffs. At the time, reports suggested that a significant portion of the studio's workforce had been affected, leading to fears that one of Xbox's most important studios could be reduced to a support role. However, developers later reassured fans that the studio remained capable of producing major releases, noting that its size was now comparable to the team that created DOOM (2016).
As things stand, id Software isn't ready to reveal what the new game actually is. Given Microsoft's renewed focus on its biggest franchises and id's long-running success with DOOM, another entry in the series appears the most likely outcome. For now, though, Bethesda and id have only confirmed that development is underway and that it may be some time before more details are shared.
KitGuru says: DOOM: The Dark Ages is still receiving new content, but where would you like to see id Software go next? Another DOOM game, or something completely different?

HAVN has teamed up with the Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team for a special edition version of its HS 420 chassis. The officially licensed case combines HAVN's panoramic dual-chamber design with a collection of motorsport-inspired details drawn from Formula One.
Based on the existing HS 420 Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team Edition, the new case adopts the team's familiar black-and-teal colour scheme alongside Mercedes branding, a hexagonal design pattern and an individually numbered plaque. HAVN has also extended the teal highlights into the interior, including the SimpliCable management system and bundled fans.
The Formula One influence extends beyond the colour scheme too. HAVN has integrated the silhouette of the 2026 Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 W17 race car into the chassis, while the power button takes inspiration from the start/stop control found on the team's steering wheel. The motorsport theme even extends to the swappable hard drive bays, which feature a carbon fibre-effect finish and official Mercedes-AMG Petronas branding.
Underneath the custom styling, the case retains the same core design as the standard HS 420, including HAVN's dual-chamber layout and GPU-focused design.
Unsurprisingly, all of that exclusivity comes at a premium. The HS 420 Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team Edition is available now priced at £269.99 / $349.99 / €299.90.

items.title: Noctua introduces carbon nanotube thermal pad that never needs repasting
items.content:
Noctua has introduced the NT-CP1 AM5/4, a new carbon nanotube thermal pad for AMD Ryzen processors. Unlike traditional thermal paste, the NT-CP1 is designed to provide stable, maintenance-free performance for years without requiring reapplication.
According to Noctua, one of the biggest drawbacks of conventional thermal paste is that it can lose effectiveness over time due to pump-out, cracking and other forms of degradation. The company claims the NT-CP1 avoids those issues altogether, with performance expected to improve slightly over its first few hundred to few thousand thermal cycles before settling into stable long-term operation.
The NT-CP1 uses an aluminium backing, a phase-change polymer coating and carbon nanotubes that improve their contact with the CPU and cooler over repeated thermal cycles. Noctua also claims the pad is easier to handle than many graphite-based alternatives, while remaining electrically non-conductive on the contact surface prior to use.
Instead of applying thermal paste, users simply peel the backing, place the pad onto the CPU and remove the top layer before mounting the cooler. A slightly tacky coating helps keep everything in place during installation and also makes the pad easier to remove when swapping coolers.
The NT-CP1 is manufactured by Carbice in the US using recycled aluminium and waste carbon gas, and the finished pad can be recycled once it reaches end of life. The AM5/4 model has been specifically tuned for AMD Ryzen CPUs and APUs, measuring 33x33mm with an ultra-thin 90µm profile.
The NT-CP1 AM5/4 thermal pad is available now, priced around €24.95 / $24.95.

items.content:
Ready to duke it out competitively in Marvel Rivals? Before jumping into the fray, you should understand how the different Marvel Rivals ranks and how the game’s progression system works. From Bronze all the way to One Above All, this guide covers every rank, how matchmaking works, and what you need to do to climb the ladder.
Key takeaways
Marvel Rivals has nine main ranks, and they go from Bronze to One Above All.
Bronze through Celestial have three tiers while Eternity and One Above All have no tiers.
Bronze 3 is the lowest rank.
One Above All is the highest rank.

What are the Marvel Rivals ranks? (2026)
What are the ranks in Marvel Rivals? Marvel Rivals has nine ranks in total. These are Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Grandmaster, Celestial, Eternity, and One Above All. Bronze is the lowest one possible and Marvel Rivals’ highest rank is One Above All.
The Bronze through Celestial ranks are divided into three tiers each. Meanwhile, the Eternity and One Above All ranks are the highest ones without additional tier divisions.
Marvel Rivals
News
Interview: Gabe Kunda as Blade in Marvel Rivals and a champion of the arts
"It means the world. I don’t even think I can put into words how much this character means to me."
Amy Chen
What ranks can play together in Marvel Rivals?
Marvel Rivals uses competitive matchmaking restrictions to keep ranked games balanced. Players generally need to be within a certain rank range to queue together. Lower and mid-level ranks have more flexibility, allowing players close to each other on the ladder to form a party.
However, the restrictions become more noticeable at higher ranks to prevent large skill gaps between teammates. For example, a Bronze player cannot queue with a Grandmaster player because the difference in skill level would create unfair matches.
These restrictions apply specifically to ranked mode. Other game modes, such as Quick Match, Arcade, and custom games, have fewer restrictions and allow players of different skill levels to enter matches together.
Deadpool in Marvel Rivals (Image credit: NetEase Games)
All Marvel Rivals ranks
Here are all of the Marvel Rivals ranks in order. There are nine Marvel Rivals competitive ranks in total and 23 ranks when counting every individual tier.
Marvel Rivals RankTiersDetails
BronzeBronze 3, 2, 1The entry-level rank where newer players learn the basics of teamwork, heroes, and maps.

PlatinumPlatinum 3, 2, 1An above-average rank with players who understand positioning, hero counters, maps, and teamwork.

GrandmasterGrandmaster 3, 2, 1Players who consistently perform at a high competitive level.
CelestialCelestial 3, 2, 1Some of the strongest Marvel Rivals players in ranked matchmaking.

Marvel Rivals rank distribution (Image credit: RivalsTracker)
Marvel Rivals rank distribution
According to data from RivalsTracker, the majority of Marvel Rivals players are in Silver 3. Silver 3 accounts for 12.78% of PC players. There is also a notable number of PC players in Platinum 3 at 8.27%. As for the highest rank, One Above All, it accounts for 0.08% of players.

How to rank up in Marvel Rivals
Ranking up in Marvel Rivals requires earning points through competitive matches. Winning matches increases your points while losing matches can results in lost progress. Players need 100 points to advance to the next tier, and those who are in the Eternity and One Above All ranks earn points toward a leaderboard.
Players may see their rank adjusted with the start of a new season as well. That is, ranks are assigned based on a player’s final rank in the previous season, and after completing 10 placement matches, a player’s rank gets adjusted again.
Here are some tips on how to rank up in Marvel Rivals:
Synergize with your teammates through Team-Up abilities.
Pay attention to when enemies use their Ultimate abilities.
Coordinate with your teammates for Ultimate combos.
Manage your own abilities and combos.
Learn how to counter the most popular heroes.
Read the Marvel Rivals patch notes for the latest buffs and nerfs.
Remember map objectives instead of only chasing kills.
Adjust your playstyle or select your hero based on ally and enemy team compositions.
Communicate with your teammates.
Master a few heroes to start and play other heroes in unranked matches to understand them better.
Regroup with your teammates instead of continuously trickling into the fray and feeding.
Practice your map awareness.
Use the ping system to alert teammates of flankers or enemies that are low on health quickly.
Watch YouTube guides on the hero that you’re learning to get specific tips about them.
White Fox in Marvel Rivals (Image credit: NetEase Games)
Marvel Rivals ranks FAQ
What is the highest rank in Marvel Rivals?
The highest rank in Marvel Rivals is One Above All. It sits above Eternity and represents the best players on the competitive ladder.
How many ranks are there in Marvel Rivals?
There are nine main Marvel Rivals ranks and 23 total ranks when counting individual tiers.
Does Marvel Rivals have placement matches?
Yes, Marvel Rivals has placement matches at the start of every season.
What ranks can play together in Marvel Rivals?
Players need to be within a similar skill range in order to queue together in ranked mode. Other modes have fewer restrictions.
Does Marvel Rivals reset ranks every season?
Marvel Rivals features seasonal competitive progression, which adjusts player ranks when a new season begins.
How do you rank up faster in Marvel Rivals?
The fastest way to rank up is by consistently winning ranked matches. Play heroes that you’re good at, take notice of what your teammates and enemies are doing, and keep improving your gameplay through experience and guides.

items.title: Microsoft confirms more original Xbox games for PC with mouse and keyboard support
items.content:
Just one day after a leak revealed a new wave of original Xbox games heading to PC, Microsoft has officially confirmed the rumours. A further 21 classic Xbox titles are now available through Xbox Backward Compatibility on PC, including fan favourites like Morrowind, TimeSplitters and Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic.
Yesterday, we reported on a backend discovery that appeared to reveal Microsoft's next batch of PC-compatible Xbox games ahead of schedule. As it turns out, the leak was entirely accurate, with Microsoft now confirming the arrival of 21 additional original Xbox games as part of Xbox's 25th anniversary celebrations.
The new wave of games includes The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind, TimeSplitters 2, TimeSplitters: Future Perfect, Star Wars Battlefront, Star Wars Battlefront II, Republic Commando, Knights of the Old Republic (and its sequel), Indiana Jones and the Emperor's Tomb and more. These join the first wave of backwards compatible Xbox games released for PC earlier this year, which included Conker: Live & Reloaded, BLiNX: The Time Sweeper, Crimson Skies and Fuzion Frenzy.

Alongside the new games, Microsoft has also expanded support for mouse and keyboard controls across the entire backwards compatibility catalogue. Perhaps more interestingly, Xbox is also introducing achievement support for select original Xbox games for the first time ever, including Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II, BLiNX: The Time Sweeper and Conker: Live & Reloaded.
There will be more original Xbox titles brought over to PC through the backwards compatibility programme in the future. While still unconfirmed, datamining efforts have already shown that Microsoft is testing Xbox 360 support too.

items.title: BLAST Rivals Season 2 2026: Quarterfinals Results & Semifinals Schedule
items.content:
Falcons and MOUZ are through to the semi-finals of the BLAST Rivals Season 2 2026 playoffs as they beat G2 and Vitality. MOUZ dominated Vitality to secure a 2-0 win, followed by a m0NESY-powered reverse sweep from Falcons.
MOUZ clean-sweeps Vitality
.@mousesports send Vitality packing and book their spot in the Semi-Finals! #BLASTPremier #MMarkEvents pic.twitter.com/xe590CQ1e8
— BLAST Premier (@BLASTPremier) November 13, 2026
A 3-0 start for MOUZ on the T-side saw them hit the ground running before Vitality converted the first full-buy round to hit the board. Their 6-round streak saw the scoreline get turned on its head, with Vitality leading 6-3 before both teams traded rounds to close out the half with a 7-5 scoreline. Starting on the defence with a narrow lead, MOUZ managed to get ahead by winning 4 rounds in a row, with Vitality failing to secure anything more than a single round, which translated into an unconvincing closure of the opening map as MOUZ secured Mirage with a 13-8 win.
Starting the second map on a similar note, MOUZ remained dominant for the better part of the first half but were chased by Vitality, leaving little room to breathe. Despite struggling to keep up, they managed to push the game to OT, as the scoreline was level by the end of regulation. Overtime saw MOUZ shine as they took the lead in the first half, and while Vitality levelled it, they secured back-to-back rounds on the defence to bag an important 2-0 victory to reach the semi-finals.
Falcons vs G2
.@FalconsEsport fly high to book their spot in the Semi-Finals! #BLASTPremier #MMarkEvents pic.twitter.com/tR3p6KKShv
— BLAST Premier (@BLASTPremier) November 13, 2026
Starting with a pistol round win, Falcons managed to control the game starting from the gun round only for G2’s defence to recover the half and close the half with a levelled scoreline. While Falcons secured the pistol on their defence, they failed to keep the well-orchestrated G2 offence out, leading to a disastrous close with the older Kovac cousin coming out on top.
With a tough loss on their own map pick, Falcons pulled up their socks in the second map. Mirage saw Falcons struggle early on but settle with a dominant display on their defence. As G2 continued to struggle, a m0NESY 3K saved the day for Falcons and helped them close the half with a 10-2 scoreline. The second half began with another highlight as NiKo and Karrigan pulled off a 2v5, keeping Falcons on their winning streak. With the pistol round bagged, the map closed with a 13-2 scoreline, favouring the younger Kovac cousin to take us to the final map of the day.
With both teams struggling to find form, Falcons and G2 had their fair share of streaks to close the first half with a levelled scoreline. Falcons took the lead with a pistol win, establishing a lead, leaving G2 to trail as they failed to convert anything more than 2 rounds, leading to a dominant 13-8 close of the series.
Semi-Finals Schedule
Spirit, Falcons, FURIA, and MOUZ remain the final four, and all of them will meet shortly in the upcoming Major. Only time can tell how the semi-finals unfold, but as of now, we have back-to-back bangers of matches leading up to the Grand Finals.

items.title: Wolfenstein 3 is finally happening after years of hints from MachineGames
items.content:
Wolfenstein 3 is finally happening. After years of hints, casting activity and comments from MachineGames about the future of the franchise, Xbox has officially confirmed that the long-awaited sequel is now in production.
As part of Xbox's 25th anniversary celebrations, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is officially in development at MachineGames. The announcement may come as little surprise to longtime followers of the series, however. MachineGames had already confirmed plans to return to Wolfenstein on several occasions over the past two years, while previous casting calls strongly hinted that a new entry in the franchise was beginning to ramp up production.
MachineGames' focus on Indiana Jones and the Great Circle also helped explain the lengthy wait. Last year, the studio confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 had been planned before development priorities shifted towards Indiana Jones, leaving fans wondering when B.J. Blazkowicz's story would finally continue.
Alongside the announcement, MachineGames shared an image containing part of the game's script, offering the first small glimpse at the next chapter in B.J.'s journey. The excerpt depicts Blazkowicz interrogating a prisoner named Otto, who immediately recognises him and reacts with panic. If nothing else, it paints a picture of a protagonist whose reputation has only continued to grow following the events of The New Order and The New Colossus.
The announcement also confirmed that Brian Bloom and Debra Wilson will reprise their roles as B.J. Blazkowicz and Grace Walker. That should come as welcome news for fans of MachineGames' modern Wolfenstein games, which were always envisioned as a trilogy centred around B.J.'s fight against the Nazi regime.
After years of speculation, Wolfenstein 3 is no longer a matter of “if”, but “when”. MachineGames isn't ready to show gameplay just yet, but work on the project has seemingly been underway for at least a year now, with motion capture already underway too. With that in mind, we may only have to wait a couple more years to get our hands on the game.
KitGuru says: We all knew MachineGames would return to Wolfenstein eventually. The real question now is how long we'll have to wait before we finally see the game in action.

The 32-year-old was one of 17 athletes named for the Arjuna Award 2025, India’s second-highest national sporting honour. Women’s World Cup champion Divya Deshmukh was the other chess player honoured at the ceremony. The government announced the awardees in August.
View this post on Instagram
A post shared by TalkEsport – BGMI & Esports News (@officialtalkesport)
Vidit said it was “a great feeling” to receive the award. He added that seeing his family “happy and proud” made him very happy. The ceremony came four days after he signed for Indian esports organisation Team Apex Gaming (TAG).
Vidit Gujrathi signed for Team Apex Gaming on 9 November
TAG announced Vidit as its first chess player in a post on X on 9 November. The post said “every great game needs a Grandmaster” and welcomed him by name. Vidit replied that he was “happy to be part of” the team. TAG had posted a teaser two days earlier that described an unnamed signing as a “national treasure”.
Every great game needs a Grandmaster. Ours just arrived.
Welcome, Vidit Gujrathi.#TAGonTOP pic.twitter.com/T4gL7ZiVcV
— TAG (@Team_ApexGaming) November 9, 2026
Neither TAG nor Vidit has disclosed the length or terms of the deal. The organisation has not said which online chess events he will play under its banner. As we covered in our report on Vidit Gujrathi joining Team Apex Gaming, he is the organisation’s first chess player. TAG has expanded into other games this month, adding EA FC Mobile players DeMYSTeRIO and HaloZeus on 7 November.
Vidit Gujrathi’s results at the Grand Swiss, Candidates and Olympiad
Vidit Gujrathi at Tata Steel Chess 2024
Vidit won the FIDE Grand Swiss in 2023, which earned him a place at the 2024 Candidates Tournament in Toronto. He finished sixth at the Candidates and beat Hikaru Nakamura in both of their games. He was part of the Indian men’s team that won silver at the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou.
In September 2024 he won gold with India’s men’s team at the 45th Chess Olympiad in Budapest. India’s women’s team, including Deshmukh, also won gold at the same Olympiad. Deshmukh won the 2025 FIDE Women’s World Cup in Batumi, beating Humpy Koneru in tiebreaks, and earned the grandmaster title.
Vidit has also competed in esports chess events. He reached the India Rising: Road to EWC grand finals at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai in July. Dutch grandmaster Benjamin Bok beat him 2–1 in sets there to take the Esports World Cup 2026 chess spot, as we covered in our report on Vidit and Bok reaching the Mumbai LAN finals.

items.title: QSSR arrives in Marvel’s Spider-Man 2, Control Resonant, The Finals, ARC Raiders, and Hell Let Loose: Vietnam
items.content:
Six years after launch, PlayStation 5 is still getting better. Last month, we introduced Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR), bringing AI-guided upscaling to the console you already own. Since then, there’s been a lot of interest from developers eager to try it out. We’re happy to announce that the next set of games is on the way, with updates rolling out over the coming weeks.
Built on the same foundation as PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) on PS5 Pro, QSSR can deliver sharper details, cleaner edges, and more stable images than traditional upscalers. And because it shares its interface with PSSR, it’s a natural fit for games that already support PSSR.
Here’s what the developers have to say about it.
View and download image
Download the image

Download this image
Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 featuring QSSR upscaling
Insomniac Games
“Having seen great results integrating QSSR in Marvel’s Wolverine, our team decided to bring it to Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 as well, in an update that’s live now! We’re excited for players to swing back into our 2023 title and see QSSR’s exciting image stability and sharpness benefits in both Fidelity and Performance modes.”
-  Mike Fitzgerald, Head of Technology, Insomniac Games
Play Video
Control Resonant featuring QSSR upscaling
Remedy Entertainment
Remedy Entertainment is bringing QSSR to Control Resonant on PS5, with noticeable improvements in image stability and fine detail.
“It’s great to see PlayStation bringing the same kind of leap on the PS5 that PSSR brought to PS5 Pro. QSSR gives Control Resonant a much more stable and detailed image, and we’ve worked closely with Sony to have it ready in an update coming in December.”
– Erik Jansson, Senior Graphics Programmer, Remedy Entertainment
Play Video
The Finals and Arc Raiders featuring QSSR upscaling
Embark Studios
“With the new QSSR coming soon to ARC Raiders and The Finals, we can deliver increased sharpness, better environmental clarity and overall visual improvements to even more PlayStation players. We are very happy to see Sony’s continued investment in PlayStation technology translate into meaningful improvements for all players, bringing more immersive experiences across the PlayStation ecosystem.”
– Mikael Linderholm, Technical Art Director, Embark Studios
Play Video
No Man’s Sky featuring QSSR upscaling
Hello Games
“No Man’s Sky gives players an infinite procedural universe to explore. When every star in the night sky is a real solar system players can visit, we care a great deal about the quality of every pixel.
The team has always been passionate about pushing the boundaries of technology on PlayStation. QSSR (Quick Spectral Super Resolution) allows us to render the universe in sharper, cleaner and more beautiful detail, while delivering the best possible framerate. Look for it in the next few weeks.
It’s another step towards making the universe of No Man’s Sky even more immersive to explore.”
– Sean Murray, Founder, Hello Games
Play Video
Hell Let Loose: Vietnam featuring QSSR upscaling
Expression Games
“We’re delighted to confirm that we are adding QSSR to Hell Let Loose: Vietnam on PlayStation 5 through an upcoming update. Console visuals are something our community has been passionate about, and QSSR will bring sharper, cleaner image quality to the battlefield, from dense jungle to the chaos of a full-scale firefight. We can’t wait for our PlayStation players to see the difference.”
– Paul Rustchynsky, Game Director, Expression Games
Looking ahead
Like the upgraded PSSR on PS5 Pro, QSSR grew out of Project Amethyst, our ongoing collaboration with AMD. It’s another example of how that shared work continues to benefit players across platforms.
Developers are just getting started, and we’re excited to keep working with them to bring QSSR to more games on PS5 in the coming months.
