TenZ joins T1’s VALORANT roster, powers up the refreshed lineup for VCT 2027
items.content:
T1 is making impressive roster changes for the Valorant Champions Tour 2027 season!
The organization has signed one of the most legendary first-person shooter players, Tyson “TenZ” Ngo. Additionally, T1’s new roster features a competitor from the United States and a Brazilian head coach.
This break from a fully full-Korean team should potentially enhance T1’s competitive power and help the iconic organization claim even more trophies in the upcoming year.
Read on for essential details on the new roster and the backstories behind this star-driven lineup.
Table of contents
TenZ joins T1, bringing legendary VALORANT and CS:GO experience
Other new faces on T1’s VALORANT roster for VCT 2027
Full VALORANT roster for T1 in VCT 2027
T1 in VALORANT: A brief recap of the team’s achievements
What’s next for T1 and where to watch their VCT 2027 journey
TenZ joins T1, bringing legendary VALORANT and CS:GO experience
Tyson “TenZ” Ngo has years of experience in tactical shooters. He started with Counter-Strike in its Global Offensive era, CS:GO. TenZ played for Cloud9, participating in multiple events and achieving high placements in quite a few Tier 2 and Tier 3 tournaments.
TenZ eventually left Counter-Strike to become a VALORANT pro, quickly becoming the face of the game’s early competitive scene.
In VALORANT, TenZ reached historic heights, winning Masters Reykjavík 2021 alongside grand finals MVP and Masters Madrid 2024, making him the first Americas player to claim two VCT Masters trophies. For the initial part of his career, TenZ represented Cloud9 before switching to Sentinels. With that team, he earned most of his trophies, including a dominant era on the North American stage.
TenZ with the VALORANT Masters Madrid 2024 trophy (Image credit: Colin Young-Wolff / Riot Games)
TenZ retired from esports in September 2024, becoming a full-time content creator and one of VALORANT’s biggest co-streamers. At first, he continued representing Sentinels before making a transition to T1 in May 2026.
Perhaps stepping back into professional VALORANT competition was his plan all along with that T1 move. In November 2026, Tyson “TenZ” Ngo officially became part of T1’s main VALORANT roster.
Other new faces on T1’s VALORANT roster for VCT 2027
Alongside TenZ, T1 has gathered a few other top-tier names on the VALORANT scene.
First, the organization announced its contract with Austin “crashies” Roberts, an American player who previously represented Fnatic. His achievements include winning Masters Reykjavík 2022 and earning a top-two placement at VALORANT Champions 2022 — with OpTic Gaming.
As part of the Fnatic roster, crashies finished 2nd at three big 2025 events: Masters Toronto, the Esports World Cup, and VALORANT Champions.
Gustavo “Sacy” Rossi has become the new head coach for T1’s VALORANT roster. It’s his first coaching position.
Sacy played for Sentinels ahead of his retirement and transition into content creation. With Sentinels, Sacy won Masters Madrid 2024 and finished fourth at VALORANT Champions 2024. Earlier in his career, Sacy earned a second-place finish at Masters Reykjavík 2022 and won VALORANT Champions 2022 as part of LOUD.
For the position of coach, T1 VALORANT signed So “sungmin” Seong-min. He brings extensive coaching experience, most recently serving at Nongshim RedForce. Sungmin helped NS win VALORANT Masters Santiago 2026, finish third at the Esports World Cup 2026, and reach the top eight at VALORANT Champions 2026.
Sacy and sungmin as head coach and coach of T1’s VALORANT team (Image credit: T1)
Full VALORANT roster for T1 in VCT 2027
Despite bringing some changes to the VCT 2027 lineup, T1’s VALORANT team keeps three longstanding players.
Take a look at the full roster and the coaching staff below.
Ham “iZu” Woo-joo
Kim “stax” Gu-taek
Yu “BuZz” Byung-chul
Austin “crashies” Roberts
Tyson “TenZ” Ngo
Gustavo “Sacy” Rossi, as Head Coach
So “sungmin” Seong-min, as Coach
NEW NEO HYPER MEGA ULTRA KING IS BACK APPA T1 VALORANT✨️#T1VALORANT pic.twitter.com/20hKwGJSaV
— T1 VALORANT (@T1) November 13, 2026
Two primary players who left T1 at the end of the 2026 season are Kim “Meteor” Tae-oh and Byeon “Munchkin” Sang-beom. Kang “DH” Dong-ho also left, but he was rather a substitute and did not play at most internationals.
Meteor, Munchkin, and DH leave T1’s VALORANT team (Image credit: T1)
T1 in VALORANT: A brief recap of the team’s achievements
As an esports organization, T1 joined the VALORANT scene back in 2020. For a few years, the team competed mainly in lower-tier and regional events.
In 2023, T1 reached both the Masters Tokyo and VALORANT Champions tournaments. However, the results weren’t overly impressive, as T1 exited in the group stages within the top 10 and the top 12, respectively.
2025 became a breakthrough year for the organization, as T1 won VALORANT Masters Bangkok. Despite that triumph, T1 finished in the top 12 at VALORANT Champions later that same year.
In 2026, T1 did not shine quite as brightly at Masters Santiago, but the team bounced back to finish within the top 6 at VALORANT Champions 2026.
T1 during VALORANT Champions 2026 (Image credit: Colin Young-Wolff / Riot Games)
What’s next for T1 and where to watch their VCT 2027 journey
T1 is one of the VCT partner teams in 2027. That means the roster receives a direct invite to the next big regional tournament, Pacific Kickoff. At this LAN event, T1 will compete alongside seven other invited partners and four teams from open qualifiers.
If T1 finishes within the top three at the regional Kickoff, the team will advance to the first international event of the new season, VALORANT Masters Seoul 2027.
VCT 2027 Pacific Kickoff: January 2027.
VALORANT Masters Seoul 2027: From Feb. 20 to March 3.

We certainly can expect other big roster changes ahead of the VCT 2027 season. For example, Paper Rex let go of Wang “Jinggg” Jing Jie and Khalish “d4v41” Rusyaidee.
All the transfers should be settled ahead of the regional Kickoff tournaments, which start at the beginning of January.

items.title: Guild Saga: Vanished Worlds brings tactical adventure to PS5 in May 2027
items.content:
We’re excited to announce that Guild Saga: Vanished Worlds is coming to PS5 in May 2027.
In this story-driven tactical RPG, your first mission for the Heroes Guild takes an unexpected turn when a mysterious maelstrom leaves you stranded on an unfamiliar island. Beyond its shores lie dangerous creatures, suspicious alchemists, and a bustling town packed with people to meet, side quests to discover, and mysteries to unravel.
Today, we’re sharing a new trailer and a closer look at how we’ve approached combat, companions, and exploration.
Play Video
Create a hero and build your party
Create your hero’s appearance and choose their background, talents, and skills.
We wanted character building to leave room for creativity and experimentation. The progression system lets you combine skills across disciplines freely, as opposed to a more rigid class system. Skills let you deal damage, heal allies, change the environment, reposition across the battlefield, summon creatures, and alter the turn sequence. With hundreds of items, you can shape both your character’s build and their appearance, choosing gear that suits your playstyle and the look you want.
Your companions offer more opportunities to shape the party. Each brings a distinct history and personal quests, while their equipment, abilities, and attributes can be completely customized.
Through dialogue and shared experiences, you’ll discover more about the companions you choose to bring along. Friendships and romance can become part of your journey, giving you connections to your party members beyond the battlefield.
Make each turn count
Guild Saga: Vanished Worlds features tactical turn-based combat with approximately 200 skills across ten disciplines. Express your tactical creativity by exploring how skills across different schools work together and with the environment around you.
Surface interactions and weather are an important consideration in combat. Players will need to be mindful of how surfaces interact, how weather affects the battle, and how those conditions might alter their skills.
For example, a party member with points invested in Geomancer may summon a mandrake to join the fight. A companion with Hydromancer skills can then make it rain, watering the mandrake and causing it to grow into a more formidable force. A party member with Aeromancer skills may then use lightning to electrify the puddles, paralyzing anyone standing in them. Across three disciplines, you’ve summoned an ally, strengthened it through the weather, and turned the resulting surfaces into a tactical advantage. We want players to discover combinations like this and experiment with how their party’s abilities work together.
Preparation matters too. Looting, mining, and gathering herbs provide materials you can craft into weapons, equipment, arrows, potions, and food. Whether you’re replenishing supplies or crafting new gear for a companion, taking time to explore and gather resources can help your party prepare for the next battle.
Follow your curiosity
When designing exploration, we wanted players to feel that taking their time could lead to something worth finding. The main quest gives your journey direction, but the islands also invite you to wander, speak to NPCs, and investigate what catches your attention.
You might find yourself solving a murder mystery, hunting feared monsters for bounty money, or settling a deadly dispute between farm animals. Elsewhere, you can follow the imagination of a famed explorer or uncover an alchemical conspiracy. These side quests give you reasons to get to know the archipelago’s inhabitants and become involved in their troubles, whether sinister, strange, or absurd.
We wanted that variety to make following a new lead feel exciting. A conversation that seems like a small diversion can draw you into a story with its own characters, conflicts, and discoveries. Taking a detour is an opportunity to experience another side of the world and the people inhabiting it.
Hidden treasures, puzzles, valuable crafting resources, and unexpected encounters also reward exploration. Ancient books and forgotten notes offer glimpses into the world’s past, giving curious players more to uncover along the way.
Your adventure begins in May
We’re looking forward to welcoming PlayStation players into Guild Saga: Vanished Worlds when it launches on PS5 in May 2027. We’ll share the exact release date closer to launch.
Until then, watch the new trailer and add Guild Saga: Vanished Worlds to your wishlist on the PlayStation Store. We can’t wait for you to meet your companions, explore the Respite Archipelago, and discover the stories waiting for you.

items.title: Ex-id Software devs form new studio Hidden Horses, dedicated to single-player FPS games
items.content:
Earlier this year, as part of Microsoft’s ongoing ‘Reset’ of the Xbox brand, famed studio id Software was hit with a significant number of lay-offs, with reports claiming that as much as 50% of the team had been let go. As has been the case with many such situations in the past, a collection of these developers have banded together to form their own studio, Named ‘Hidden Horses’, the independent, employee-owned development team are already gearing up to work on their first project with a dedication “to continuing to create some of the best single-player FPS' in the genre.”
Going live with their website, a Kickstarter and even an 18-minute long mini documentary, studio Hidden Horses is officially here and ready to take on the FPS genre. Currently composed of 19 developers (ranging from senior technical designers to producers; artists; engine programmers; VFX artists and engineers), Hidden Horses already has a clear plan for its future.
Their first project – Danger Play – is said to be “a single player, first person, high-octane action FPS” which is “centered around a deadly game show with influences from 1987's The Running Man and Smash TV, featuring a sinister and deadly AI host”. Gameplay-wise, the title will feature “classic FPS gameplay, awesome weapons, crazy enemies, and will be highly optimized.”
Offering insight into the mentality behind the studio, Hidden Horses is described as being ‘employee-owned’, meaning “our studio is owned by the developers only – we split the equity of the company in equal shares. We manage the company as a cooperative, with democratic mechanisms to select project direction, leadership, and other major business decisions.”
For more details on how the studio came to be, the team have released a mini documentary (available via YouTube) which goes into the timeline between id Software’s mass lay-offs and the eventual founding of Hidden Horses.
Though yet to go live, those interested in following the team’s progress can check out the Kickstarter for Danger Play which is said to be ‘launching soon’.
Creating a new studio in today’s age is certainly an uphill battle, and so here’s to hoping that Hidden Horses is able to get the support that it needs to succeed.

items.title: How AI Is Helping Care Teams Get Patients the Right Care, Sooner
items.content:
From pediatric research to smart hospitals, AI is helping care teams spend less time on routine tasks and more time with patients.
Health systems and startups are putting it to work across healthcare, from matching patients to clinical trials to supporting radiologists, hospital teams and patients at home. Clinicians stay at the center, reviewing AI outputs and guiding decisions, while NVIDIA technologies provide the compute behind the applications.
Read on to learn how healthcare teams are using AI to improve and speed patient care.
Friday, Nov. 13, 5:00 a.m. PT
Dyania Health Uses AI to Turn Decades of Patient Records Into Better Care
Hospitals hold decades of patient history, most of it written in free text, as physicians’ notes, operative reports, imaging and pathology reads and discharge summaries. To understand one patient’s full story, a clinician would need to read through years of charts.
Dyania Health, a New Jersey-based clinical AI company, built Synapsis AI to do just that. Synapsis AI is a clinical reasoning engine: It works across every note, report and lab result in a patient’s record, connecting findings that may be years apart to answer clinical questions the way a specialist reviewing the chart would.
The output is a set of clinical signals, each traceable to its source in the record, that tells care teams which patients need attention and why. Clinicians review the evidence and make every decision.
Keeping Patient Data Inside the Hospital Walls
Synapsis AI runs on NVIDIA-accelerated computing inside a health system’s own firewall. The entire health system’s patient records can be processed onsite, so patient data is never shared and never leaves the hospital.
Processing records this way takes chart review off the desks of clinical teams and lets them spend that time with patients. But Synapsis AI still requires clinician input — it’s an assistive tool that surfaces evidence from medical records that a clinician must still confirm and act on.
Dyania builds and trains its clinical models with NVIDIA NeMo open libraries, then uses NVIDIA TensorRT and TensorRT-LLM to optimize them to run faster and more efficiently on the hospital’s own GPU servers.
Synapsis AI in the Real World
Cleveland Clinic used Synapsis AI to support a study of more than 7,800 aortic valve replacement patients between 2005 and 2021.
Synapsis AI reasoned across each patient’s record, including every echocardiogram added in the years after surgery, and used this information to build a predictive model of valve deterioration and reintervention risk at the three-, five- and ten-year mark after a patient undergoes an aortic valve replacement procedure. The AI platform completed chart review across the full cohort that would have taken clinicians years to complete by hand.
“Using technology to bring together and analyze information that can help us predict the duration of implanted heart valves is a promising step towards enhanced outcomes and more personalized care for patients,” said Dr. Lars Svensson, chief of the Heart, Vascular & Thoracic Institute at Cleveland Clinic.
The same approach can be applied to any healthcare challenge where the answer sits inside the medical record, such as identifying patients eligible for clinical trials, closing care gaps in cardiology and oncology, and populating clinical registries.
Learn more about Dyania Health.

items.title: IShowSpeed Delivers Acceptance Speech in Indonesian After Third Streamer of the Year Win
items.content:
IShowSpeed has become the first streamer in history to win The Streamer Awards three consecutive times, edging past Jynxzi, CaseOh, Stable Ronaldo, and Joe Bartolozzi to take home this year’s trophy.
always the same pic.twitter.com/zDLb3Mvdvt
— Speed (@ishowspeedsui) November 13, 2026
Speed’s streak began in 2024, when he beat Kai Cenat and Emiru to claim his first title. After securing his second victory in December 2025, he returned to Los Angeles this November as the favorite.
Alongside being crowned the Streamer of the Year, Speed was also named the Best IRL Streamer in the event, and his World Cup Tour earned him the Best Streamed Series award. As a result, the 21-year-old walked away with three awards at The Streamer Awards 2026.
When taking the stage to accept his third consecutive Streamer of the Year award, Speed surprised the entire room by delivering his acceptance speech entirely in Indonesian.
“I started from zero, just a little kid with a big dream,” Speed said, according to a rough translation. “You guys have been with me from the beginning. You’re not just fans. You’re my family. I won’t stop. I’ll keep fighting for you all. I love you all.”
After finishing his speech, he also celebrated with his signature backflip while holding the trophy.
IShowSpeed speaks a different language while accepting his award for Streamer Of The Year at the Streamer Awards pic.twitter.com/oFak71kUo4
— FearBuck (@FearedBuck) November 13, 2026
Kai Cenat also had a big night at The Streamer Awards, winning three awards of his own, including Best Streamed Event for Streamer University, Best Mainstream Collab for his work with Tyla, and the League of Their Own award. Cenat wasn’t nominated for Streamer of the Year this time, so Speed’s win didn’t come at his expense. Cenat had even said ahead of the ceremony that Speed deserved it.
If you’re curious about all the winners and nominees, be sure to check out the full list of Streamer Awards 2026 winners.
Speed could also be on the verge of another Streamer of the Year streak at the Esports Awards, where he won in 2025 and is nominated again this month. Should he win there as well, Speed could add yet another trophy to the list before the year ends.

items.content:
Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at MachineGames, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has confirmed. She shared the news on X with a photo of the game’s script. MachineGames then posted its own confirmation and showed actors Brian Bloom and Debra Wilson filming a scene. Both will return as BJ Blazkowicz and Grace Walker. No release date or platforms have been announced.
Here is what Sharma said, what the script shows, who returns, and what else is known so far.
Wolfenstein 3 Officially in Production at MachineGames
Sharma revealed the game in a post on X. She called Wolfenstein “one of gaming’s most important franchises” and said she looks forward to sharing more.
Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at @MachineGames. One of gaming's most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more. pic.twitter.com/YyX8LrbTvh
— ASHA (@asha_shar) November 12, 2026
Her post included a photo of the script. The image shows little beyond the name of the first chapter, which is “Nazitraz.” The script also confirms BJ Blazkowicz is coming back.
MachineGames posted its own message on X: “His reputation precedes him. Wolfenstein 3 is in production.” The post included a behind-the-scenes image of Bloom and Wilson recording a scene together. Motion capture is currently underway.
Wolfenstein 3 Release Date and Platforms
Wolfenstein 3 has no release date yet. No platforms have been announced either.
Sharma said more information will come later. The only concrete production detail so far is the motion capture work shown in the MachineGames post.
Wolfenstein 3 Cast
Brian Bloom will return as BJ Blazkowicz. Debra Wilson will return as Grace Walker. MachineGames confirmed both through the behind-the-scenes image.
No other cast members have been named.
MachineGames Wolfenstein Timeline
MachineGames took over the series in 2014 with Wolfenstein: The New Order. It was the sixth Wolfenstein game overall and the first in the studio’s run.
The series has been quiet for 7 years, and the last mainline game came out 9 years ago. MachineGames spent that time on Indiana Jones and the Great Circle.
MachineGames Said Wolfenstein Was Always a Trilogy
MachineGames studio head Jerk Gustafsson spoke about the series last year in an interview with Noclip. He said the team has always seen the story as a trilogy. According to him, the plans for BJ’s arc across three games existed while the team worked on The New Order.
He also said the studio was not done with Wolfenstein. His words: “We have a story to tell.”
Reports about a third Wolfenstein game had circulated for some time. The Sharma and MachineGames posts are the first official word.
A TV series based on the rebooted Wolfenstein timeline is also in development at Amazon.
Sharma made the announcement ahead of Xbox’s 25th anniversary on November 15, 2026. Other Xbox studios shared updates around the same time.
id Software said it is working on its next game, directed by Hugo Martin. Halo: Campaign Evolved will also get a free Firefight horde mode update later this winter.
The post Wolfenstein 3 Release Date, Cast, Platforms and More appeared first on TalkEsport.

Halo: Campaign Evolved to receive fan-favourite ‘Firefight’ mode later this Winter
items.content:
Depending on who you ask, Halo: Campaign Evolved is either a disappointing remake which failed to recapture much of what made the original 2001 classic an icon of the industry, or it serves as a solid way to experience the first entry in Master Chief’s saga – aided by the visual flair of Unreal Engine 5 alongside the addition of tons of new gameplay modifiers. Regardless of where you stand on the matter, Microsoft has announced a surprise addition coming to the game ‘this Winter’, bringing the fan-favourite Firefight mode via a free update.
Taking to the Xbox Wire blog to make the announcement, Halo Studios confirmed that Campaign Evolved will be getting a pretty substantial content drop “this winter”, with the horde mode-esque ‘Firefight‘ officially set to be added via a free update.
As of now, details on the mode remain light, with the only confirmed details being that it supports 4-player co-op and will include “new maps” as well as “plenty of weapons” – though whether these will be pre-existing assets restructured for the mode or entirely new additions remains to be seen.
While vague, Halo Studios also confirmed that the update will include more than just the Firefight mode, claiming that “there’s more on the way” with “additional details about this free update” set to be revealed during Halo Fest on the 12th of December.
That said, those attending Xbox FanFest can get an early taste of the update right now, meaning we should hopefully learn more in the coming days as fans share their experience with the mode.
Though far from a full-on arena-based PvP multiplayer which the series is known best for, the addition of Firefight (assuming it’s comprehensive) should help to make Campaign Evolved a more complete-feeling package.

TSMC Confirms Employee Data Leak as Seller Offers 46,000 Records for 3 Bitcoin
items.content:
TSMC has confirmed that personal data belonging to some of its current and former employees was posted on an external website without authorisation, after a seller began offering what it claims are about 46,000 employee records. In a statement filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on 12 November, the world’s largest contract chipmaker said it had “found no evidence that TSMC’s systems have been compromised”. It said the leaked information matched data stored in the system services of a third-party cloud provider, and was unrelated to its operations or to customer data. TSMC has not named the provider, however, and has not said how many people are affected.
The listing appeared on two underground forums, DarkForums and BreachForums, according to United Daily News and ETtoday. The seller is asking for 3 bitcoin, or about NT$7.4 million, for a 6.9GB data set, and has threatened to publish everything if no buyer comes forward within a week. A sample file of 499 records, each with 19 fields, was posted alongside the listing, United Daily News reported. Neither TSMC nor Taiwanese media have verified that the full set holds 46,000 records.
The listing includes national ID numbers and bank details
According to the seller’s listing, as described in Taiwanese reports, each record includes a name, date of birth, job title, nationality, national ID number, home address, mobile number and email address. Some records reportedly also contain bank account information, along with the phone numbers and addresses of employees’ emergency contacts. TSMC’s own statement does not list the fields involved, although it says the company is informing affected staff and providing them with support. A national ID number combined with a bank account and a home address is enough for convincing impersonation attempts against banks and mobile operators. That is why the exposure matters even without a breach of TSMC’s network.
The profile of the people involved also makes the data unusually valuable. TSMC’s engineers are among the most sought-after in the chip industry, and job titles tied to names and phone numbers are useful material for targeted phishing and recruitment approaches. Taiwanese prosecutors charged several people in 2025 over the alleged theft of trade secrets linked to TSMC’s 2nm process, a case that showed how much outsiders will invest to reach the company’s staff. TSMC said it is working with the cloud vendor, the relevant investigating authorities and a third-party cybersecurity firm to establish the facts.
TSMC says chip production and customer data are not affected
For gamers and the wider hardware market, TSMC’s key claim is that the incident does not touch its fabs. The company makes most of the world’s most advanced chips, including Nvidia’s GeForce and data centre GPUs and AMD’s Ryzen and Radeon processors. It also builds Apple’s A and M series chips and the custom processors inside the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles. TSMC said the data is unrelated to its operations, and Taiwanese reports said there was no evidence that wafer production or customer orders were affected. So far, there is no sign of any knock-on effect on the supply of PC or console hardware, which is already under pressure from rising memory costs.
TSMC has dealt with security incidents before, although the earlier ones followed a different pattern. In August 2018, a virus spread through several of its fabs after what the company called “misoperation during the software installation process for a new tool”. TSMC estimated the impact at about 3% of its third-quarter revenue. In 2023, the LockBit ransomware group claimed to have hacked TSMC, but the company said the incident hit a hardware supplier and exposed only server set-up information. The latest case again points to a third party, this time a cloud provider holding employee records.
Gaming companies have faced the same problem with outside vendors this year. Valve warned some European hardware buyers after a breach at a logistics partner, and last year’s Discord leak exposed tens of thousands of ID photos held by a support contractor. In each case the entry point sat outside the company’s own systems, while its users or staff carried the risk.
The next test comes if the seller follows through on its one-week deadline. A public release would put the full data set within reach of anyone, rather than a single buyer, and would show whether the 46,000 figure is accurate. TSMC has not said when it learned of the exposure, which cloud provider was involved, or whether that provider’s other clients are affected. TSMC and its subsidiaries employed more than 90,000 people at the end of 2025, according to its annual report.
The post TSMC Confirms Employee Data Leak as Seller Offers 46,000 Records for 3 Bitcoin appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Valorant Hush Nerf Hinted as Riot Plans Sentinel Changes
items.content:
Hush nerf talk has started in Valorant after Riot Games hinted at changes during a Reddit Q&A. Agent designer RiotNickwu named her ultimate as the first ability the team would consider adjusting. Riot is still watching Hush while players get used to her kit. The studio also said bigger Sentinel changes are coming after Patch 13.10.
This article covers the Hush nerf hint, why Riot is waiting, the Sentinel balance plans, and other details from the Q&A, including agent-inspired skins.
Hush Nerf Hint
Riot Games hinted that Hush might receive a nerf. RiotNickwu, an agent designer, answered questions in a Reddit Q&A session. He pointed to her ultimate as the first ability he would look at.
Her ultimate is called Suspension. It sends out a steerable projectile that levitates players where it lands.
Riot has not confirmed a change or a date. Patch 13.10 made no balance changes to Hush in normal modes. It only fixed visual bugs for Suspension and her animations.
Why Riot Is Waiting on Hush
Developers continue to monitor Hush. They are giving players time to get used to her abilities before making changes.
Penguin, the head of the agent balance team, said Hush had a relatively high win rate at the start. Teams also picked her often during the initial qualifiers. Riot designed her as a Duelist that needs more mechanical skill than most agents.
Third-party trackers show a different picture in ranked play. Reports list her at a 48.3% win rate and a 17.0% pick rate in Platinum+ games on patch 13.09, as of November 9, 2026.
Valorant Sentinel Balance and Patch 13.10
Riot continues to work on Valorant Sentinel balance. In Patch 13.10, developers cut ability cooldowns after device destruction for Cypher, Killjoy, and Vyse. The cooldown drops from 60 to 45 seconds for Cypher’s Spycam, Killjoy’s Turret, and Vyse’s Arc Rose.
The patch also improved the accuracy of Sage’s healing.
Penguin said the team is preparing more than small tweaks and buffs. Riot plans larger Sentinel changes and will share details later.
Hush Abilities and Design Notes
The Q&A also covered how Riot built Hush. The team tested her remote weapon pickup as a signature ability. It later moved to her passive.
With that passive, Hush can pick up the Spike on the attacking side. She can also activate switches from a greater distance.
Riot also shared a design note about Tejo. The team first tested his Q ability with Clove, but it made the agent too self-sufficient. Riot then reworked the mechanic for Tejo.
Agent-Inspired Skins Under Consideration
Valorant’s game director, Joe Lee, said Riot is considering agent-inspired skin collections. A set could reflect an agent’s character and abilities in the weapon’s look and visual effects.
Riot has not announced any specific sets yet.

items.title: Microsoft Outage Passes 16 Hours With Outlook and Teams Still Down, but Xbox Is Holding Up
items.content:
Microsoft’s outage across Outlook, Teams and the wider Microsoft 365 suite has now run for more than 16 hours, and the company’s own status page still shows service capacity below normal. Problems began with Teams in North America on 12 November, before Exchange Online mailboxes started failing from 17:54 UTC (11:24 pm IST). Minutes later, Microsoft confirmed that the issue could affect Microsoft 365 connectivity “for users in any region”. For gamers, the main question is whether Xbox has gone down with it, and so far the answer is mostly no.
Xbox’s own status page shows no outage
As of Friday morning UTC, the official Xbox status page listed all services as “up and running”, including sign-in, multiplayer, the store and cloud gaming. Microsoft’s service health page names Outlook.com, OneDrive, OneNote, Microsoft To Do, Teams and Microsoft 365 for the web among the affected consumer products, and Xbox is not on that list. The disruption sits mainly in Exchange Online, the email system behind Outlook, and in the services that depend on it.
Some players have still reported trouble since the outage began. Users on social media and outage trackers have described failed sign-ins, digital games that would not launch, cloud saves that did not sync and problems reaching Xbox Cloud Gaming. Windows Central, which collected those reports, said its own staff could connect normally. Microsoft has not confirmed those reports, and TalkEsport found no post from Xbox Support about the outage. Players who see errors should check the status page first, since a local network fault can produce the same errors.
The timing is awkward for Xbox, which has only just widened access to cloud play. Microsoft launched a free, ad-supported tier of Xbox Cloud Gaming on 12 November, the same day the outage began, and cloud gaming depends on Microsoft’s servers more than any other part of the platform. Xbox was not so lucky in October 2025, when a faulty configuration change to Azure Front Door took down Xbox sign-ins and Minecraft for hours along with Microsoft 365. Cloud failures have hit games elsewhere too, including Google Cloud’s outage in Europe last month.
Microsoft says an overwhelmed server process is behind the failure
Microsoft has given a detailed running account of the incident, though not a root cause. At 22:09 UTC on 12 November, it said a core process on affected servers was “becoming overwhelmed, causing capacity loss”, and that its actions so far “have not provided the anticipated relief”. Two hours later, it said servers it had returned to service could become unresponsive again “once they receive traffic”. It then began limiting which types of traffic could reach the affected infrastructure.
There has been some movement on the cause since then. Microsoft first said it had not identified any recent change linked to the start of the problem. By 21:40 UTC, however, it was assessing whether reverting “a small number of recent configuration updates” could speed up recovery. On Friday morning, it reported “positive results for service stability and increased capacity” from traffic optimisation, and said it was extending those actions across affected regions. Its latest update said service health “remains variable”, and that it has no evidence of malicious activity.
For businesses, delayed email remains the biggest worry in this outage. Microsoft has extended its email timeout window to 48 hours so that delayed messages are preserved, and says it is prioritising queue and backlog processing. Copilot, the AI assistant Microsoft has placed at the centre of its products, is also on the affected list, because it cannot reach the email, calendar and files it depends on. The company has promised a full post-incident report with the root cause once the issue is fixed.
The outage follows two years of deep job cuts at Microsoft
The outage also comes after two years of heavy job cuts across the company. Microsoft cut about 6,000 jobs in May 2025 and about 9,000 more in July 2025. More than 40% of the roughly 2,000 roles cut in Washington state that May were software engineering jobs, according to Bloomberg. In July 2026, it cut about 4,800 more roles, or around 2.1% of its workforce, mostly in its commercial business and Xbox, according to TheStreet. Further cuts followed in September, including 268 jobs across Xbox studios, alongside a voluntary retirement programme for senior staff.
There is no evidence that those cuts caused this outage, and Microsoft has not linked the two. Its chief people officer, Amy Coleman, has said the roles being eliminated were not being replaced by AI, while adding that “AI is changing how work gets done”. Chief executive Satya Nadella said in April 2025 that AI was writing 20% to 30% of the code in some of the company’s repositories. Yet more than 16 hours in, recovery still depends on restarting servers, rerouting traffic and blocking some types of requests, alongside the automated systems Microsoft says it is using. Microsoft’s status page puts its next update for business customers at 11:00 UTC (4:30 pm IST) on 13 November, and for consumer services at 12:30 UTC (6 pm IST).
The post Microsoft Outage Passes 16 Hours With Outlook and Teams Still Down, but Xbox Is Holding Up appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Resident Evil Requiem wins ‘Ultimate Game of the Year’ at the Golden Joystick Awards
items.content:
The Golden Joystick Awards is one of the oldest and longest-running ceremonies dedicated to celebrating video games as a medium, with 2026 marking its 44th year in operation. Having announced its nominees back in September, the annual event has now come and gone – with Capcom’s excellent Resident Evil Requiem officially taking home the prestigious ‘Ultimate Game of the Year’ award.
While the full list of winners across its 25 categories can be found HERE, some of the most notable wins from the evening include the following:
Best Audio Design – Onimusha: Way of the Sword
Best Early Access Game – Subnautica 2
Best Indie Game – Valheim
Best Indie Game [Self-published] – Meccha Chameleon
Best Lead Performer – Angela Sant'Albano (Grace Ashcroft) Resident Evil Requiem
Best Multiplayer Game – Meccha Chameleon
Best Soundtrack – Dispatch
Best Storytelling – Dispatch
Best Visual Design – Control Resonant
Studio of the Year – Capcom
PC Game of the Year – Crimson Desert
Ultimate Game of the Year – Resident Evil Requiem
By far the biggest winner of the event was Capcom, amassing a total of 7 awards – 4 of which can be directly attributed to RE: Requiem. Other standout winners include Meccha Chameleon (3 awards); and Dispatch (2 wins).
Given that Geoff Keighley’s Game Awards has confirmed that Grand Theft Auto VI will be eligible for their ceremony later in December, it will be interesting to see how different the TGA’s results will look like in comparison.

Culper Research Shorted Nvidia Over China in May, Stock Is Down 26% Since
items.content:
On 13 May, Culper Research published a 40-page report arguing that Nvidia had “a significant China problem”, and disclosed that it was short the stock. Investors largely ignored the warning for the next five months. Nvidia closed 2.3% higher that day at $225.83, gained another 4.4% to $235.74 the next session, and went on to close at a high of $239.24 on 6 October. By Thursday’s close of $166.19, the shares were 26% below their level on the day of the report and more than 30% below that October peak.
The six months in between have turned parts of Culper’s case from short-seller allegations into mainstream reporting. Alice Huang, the former Megaspeed executive whom the report described as “uncomfortably close” to Jensen Huang, is now at the centre of the scandal that ended his 33-year run as Nvidia’s chief executive. Megaspeed, which Culper called Nvidia’s largest buyer in Southeast Asia, is under investigation in Singapore and has hired a US law firm to count its GPUs. None of that proves Culper’s core financial argument, which concerns how much of Nvidia’s revenue still depends on Chinese demand.
Culper’s case was about revenue quality, not Huang’s private life
The report’s central claim is that Nvidia’s China business never really went to zero. Huang said in October 2025 that Nvidia had gone from a 95% share of China’s market to nothing, and that the company was “100% out of China”. Culper estimated that more than 20% of Nvidia’s fiscal 2026 compute revenue was still driven by Chinese demand, through illegal diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries. Nvidia has not publicly addressed that estimate, and no regulator has published a figure of its own.
The mechanics matter because of how Nvidia reports its sales. Its filings assign revenue to the customer’s billing location, and Nvidia has said that “end customer and shipping location may be different” from that location. According to the Wall Street Journal’s Jonathan Weil, Nvidia stopped breaking out Singapore revenue after the quarter that ended in July 2025, when the country accounted for 22% of the total. Nvidia has said shipments into Singapore itself were insignificant, but its filings do not say where the rest of that hardware went.
Culper then followed the money through Megaspeed’s accounts. It said the company’s balance sheet grew from about $33 million at the end of 2023 to $3.0 billion a year later, mostly through $2.9 billion of “refundable deposits” from an unnamed source. The report alleged that documents pointed to Alibaba as the financier, through a Singapore company called Apex Enterprise Solutions. It also said Megaspeed’s Malaysian unit, Speedmatrix, imported $4.6 billion of products between December 2024 and January 2026. About $4 billion of that came from Aivres, an Nvidia server partner that took over the US business of China’s Inspur.
Nvidia and Megaspeed both reject the diversion claims made in the report. Nvidia said in October that the allegations against Megaspeed had been “thoroughly investigated and debunked last year”, and that Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang were “not unusual or unexpected”. Megaspeed says reviews by the US Commerce Department, Malaysian authorities and Nvidia found no evidence of violations, and it has threatened legal action over a Bloomberg report that it rented computing power to Alibaba. No charges have been reported against Nvidia, Megaspeed or Alice Huang.
Regulators have since moved on the Southeast Asian channels Culper described
The first official move came less than three weeks after the report. On 31 May, the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security said it would enforce licence requirements on advanced chips sold to companies headquartered in China, even when those companies operate abroad, Reuters reported. That closed a gap that may have let Malaysian and other overseas units of Chinese firms buy Blackwell chips without a licence. An Nvidia official told Reuters that the change made no difference to the company, because it already needed a licence for such sales.
The Supermicro case shows what diversion looks like when prosecutors find it. In March, the Justice Department charged a Supermicro co-founder and two others with conspiring to divert AI servers to China through an unnamed Southeast Asian buyer. Prosecutors allege that the buyer purchased about $2.5 billion of servers in 2024 and 2025. At least $510 million of them went to China within a few weeks in 2025, they say, hidden behind dummy machines staged for audits. Nvidia was not accused, and Supermicro says the conduct broke its own policies, but Culper argued that the case reflected one corridor of a much wider network.
The revelations about Huang himself followed from late October. Reports said US intelligence had concluded that Alice Huang was gathering information for China’s Ministry of State Security, which Beijing has called a smear. Nvidia’s board opened an investigation on 8 November, and Huang resigned four days later. On the same day, Singapore said it had barred Alice Huang from re-entry after she gave police inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed.
The share price has tracked those headlines, although not only them. Nvidia fell 9.3% on 5 November, the day three House committee chairs asked Huang to brief Congress, during a wider sell-off in AI chip stocks. It lost 4.3% on 9 November, the first trading day after the board’s statement, and another 4.3% on 12 November, when Huang resigned. In Washington, OpenAI has meanwhile backed a package of tighter chip export rules that Nvidia opposes.
Nvidia’s 17 November results are the first real test of the short thesis
Christian Lamarco, Culper’s 31-year-old founder, told MarketWatch this week that the firm had found similar red flags at no fewer than six other Southeast Asian companies, which he did not name. “We were confident in the research initially, and we’re still confident in it now,” he said. He declined to say whether Culper is still short, or how much it has made from the trade. That matters, because a short seller profits when the shares fall, and the firm’s revenue estimates have not been independently verified.
Wall Street has not come round to Culper’s view. Analysts still rate Nvidia a strong buy on average, with a mean price target of about $303, according to TipRanks data, more than 80% above Thursday’s close. That optimism rests mainly on spending by US cloud providers and AI labs rather than on China. Culper argues that the risk sits in the other direction, saying analysts treat China as upside to fiscal 2027 forecasts when it sees a revenue “air gap” of more than $30 billion.
The quarterly report will be the first chance to test those claims against Nvidia’s own numbers since Huang’s exit. Investors will look for any change in how the company discloses revenue by region, for comments on sales through Southeast Asian partners, and for an update on the board’s review. Interim chief executive Colette Kress, who remains chief financial officer, will face those questions directly. Nvidia reports its third-quarter results after the US market closes on 17 November, with the earnings call at 2pm Pacific time.
The post Culper Research Shorted Nvidia Over China in May, Stock Is Down 26% Since appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Alien: Isolation will be free on the Epic Games Store next week
items.content:
Each week, Epic gives away a title or two as part of the storefront’s ‘free games’ initiative. 12 years on from its initial arrival, the excellent stealth-focused survival horror adventure ‘Alien: Isolation’ is set to be available for all to claim for free starting next Thursday – alongside the more recently-released isometric pirate-themed metroidvania souls-like ‘Mark of the Deep’.
Available to add to your library for free from the 19th of November up until the 26th, Epic Games will be giving away a total of two titles:
Alien: Isolation
Mark of the Deep
First released back in 2014, Alien: Isolation is an excellent stealth-horror experience based on the iconic Alien film franchise. Designed with the intention of capturing the vibes and essence of Ridley Scott’s 1979 classic, Alien: Isolation has you take on the role of Amanda Ripley as she tries to investigate her mother’s disappearance aboard the Sevastopol space station. Being continually stalked by a Xenomorph while also trying to avoid various androids / synthetics, Alien: Isolation was praised for its attention to detail; visual and audio design; the use of manual ‘registration (save) points’ and an overall commitment to the IP.
Though far from a perfect experience, sentiment surrounding the game has only grown over the years. If you have yet to play Alien: Isolation, now is as good a time as any to check it out, especially with a sequel finally set to arrive some time in 2027.
Mark of the Deep meanwhile is an indie developed isometric pirate-themed action-adventure title which features a mix of metroidvania-esque and souls-like mechanics. With pretty visuals; over 80 enemy types; 16 bosses and multiple different endings, there is plenty to enjoy.
Both Alien: Isolation and Mark of the Deep will be free to claim from the 19th of November. In the meantime, users can claim the turn-based strategy roguelike autobattler ‘Knightica’ for free right now.

items.title: Viral ‘Nvidia Employees’ Letter Demanding Jensen Huang’s Return Is a Copy of OpenAI’s 2023 Letter
items.content:
A post claiming that “hundreds of NVIDIA employees” have signed an internal letter demanding Jensen Huang’s return as chief executive was shared widely on X on Friday. The letter shown in the post also demands the resignation of Nvidia’s board and threatens a mass move to “the SpaceX Terafab initiative under the leadership of Jensen Huang and Elon Musk”. The first names on its signature list belong to several of Nvidia’s best-known technical leaders. There is no evidence that this letter is real.
Its wording follows, almost line for line, the letter OpenAI employees sent to their own board in November 2023, after Sam Altman was removed as chief executive. The developer’s account that shared it has not said where the letter came from. About seven hours earlier, the same account had described this exact scenario as a way for Huang to win back his job “like Sam did with the OpenAI coup”. In that version, Musk offers Huang work at Terafab and jobs for Nvidia staff, employees threaten to follow him, and Huang returns to restructure the board.
A reader note now shown on the post says that no reports confirm a signed letter like the one in the image, but the letter has kept travelling. Several crypto and finance news sites republished it on Friday as an “alleged” petition, while noting that its authenticity had not been confirmed. TalkEsport has found no public comment on the letter from Nvidia itself.
Huang’s departure, unlike the letter, is a matter of record. Nvidia announced on 12 November that Huang had resigned as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after 33 years in charge. Chief financial officer Colette Kress became interim chief executive, and former Synopsys chief executive Harvey Jones was named the company’s first board chair, according to Nvidia’s official announcement. TalkEsport is not repeating the names on the viral letter, because nothing shows that any of those executives signed it.
The viral letter borrows OpenAI’s 2023 wording almost line for line
Placed side by side, the two letters share their structure, their arguments and many of their sentences. Only the company names, the people and the rival employer have changed. The OpenAI letter, which was widely reported in November 2023, was eventually signed by 745 of the company’s 770 employees.
Several details in the viral letter also clash with the public record. It says the board “terminated” Huang, while Nvidia’s announcement and its filing with US regulators say he resigned. It claims that Elon Musk has promised jobs to every Nvidia employee, but TalkEsport found no such statement from Musk or SpaceX. Musk’s only public remark about hiring Huang so far was that it “would be an honour”. Terafab itself is real, a chip factory costing about $20 billion that Tesla and SpaceX announced in March for Austin, Texas, but nothing shows that Huang has joined it.
The real employee pushback came through Nvidia’s internal suggestion box
There is genuine anger inside Nvidia, but it looks very different from the viral letter. According to internal messages reviewed by WIRED, a longtime Nvidia engineer submitted a post to the company’s internal suggestion box before Huang’s exit. It urged the board to share its findings and to seek employee views on whether Huang should stay as chief executive. The post has drawn more than 1,600 comments, many of them calling for Huang to get another chance.
“If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss,” one anonymous comment read, according to the reports. Another employee sent a companywide email asking the board to explain its decision, and about two dozen Nvidia staff posted messages of support for Huang on LinkedIn after he resigned. None of those messages amounts to a signed demand, and none mentions SpaceX or Musk.
Loyalty to Huang inside Nvidia was already clear before he left. In a Blind survey published on 10 November, 88% of Nvidia staff who answered said he should remain chief executive, against 60% of all 1,689 professionals who responded. Only 1% of the Nvidia respondents said the board should remove him. The pressure on him grew afterwards, and sources have since alleged a third relationship, with a second Nvidia employee.
Why a copied letter found such a ready audience
The OpenAI letter is remembered because it worked. Altman was back as OpenAI’s chief executive within days of the November 2023 revolt, and most of the board that removed him was replaced. For anyone hoping for a similar outcome at Nvidia, a letter in the same words, with Musk in place of Microsoft, was an easy thing to believe and to share.
Nvidia’s situation is also very different from OpenAI’s. Huang left during an investigation into his conduct, led by former federal prosecutor Joon Kim and the law firm Wachtell Lipton, and Nvidia describes his exit as a resignation. The board has said it is searching for a permanent successor and “will consider internal and external candidates”, and Kress has said her focus is on customers, partners and shareholders. Nvidia reports its third-quarter results on 17 November, its first under an interim chief executive.

OpenAI Backs China Chip Curbs as Jensen Huang Exits Nvidia, but the ‘Targeted Takedown’ Claim Does Not Hold Up
items.content:
On the day Jensen Huang left Nvidia, Bloomberg reported that OpenAI had told US lawmakers it supports a bipartisan push to tighten China’s access to AI chips. The package also targets the tools used to make those chips, and the report was published on 12 November. The timing has fuelled a viral claim on X that Huang’s departure was “a targeted takedown” by OpenAI and Anthropic, which are said to have formed an alliance to back the curbs. The public record does not support that claim.
OpenAI’s support follows months of review, according to reports, and Anthropic has campaigned openly for chip export controls since at least 2025. Versions of the proposals now in Congress were also being debated well before Huang’s private life became a story. What has changed is that Nvidia’s most powerful opponent of those controls is no longer running the company.
Huang resigned on 12 November after a week of reports about his relationships, including with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive whom US intelligence reportedly suspects of gathering information for China. Nvidia’s board had hired former federal prosecutor Joon Kim to investigate his conduct. Nothing in the reporting so far links his departure to OpenAI, Anthropic or the export debate, and the photo of Sam Altman and Dario Amodei shared with the viral claim could not be verified.
OpenAI’s backing gives Congress a new ally against Nvidia’s lobbying
According to Bloomberg, OpenAI told lawmakers this week that it would support a package of export-related measures that Congress is weighing. Reports describe three parts to the package, each aimed at a different gap in the current rules. One would give Congress more power to review exports of advanced AI chips, and another would track where those chips end up to curb smuggling and diversion. A third would press US allies to restrict exports of chipmaking equipment to China. Lawmakers are considering attaching the measures to the annual defence bill, the National Defense Authorization Act, which must pass each year.
Nvidia has fought similar efforts before, and won. In December 2025, Congress dropped a proposal to curb chip exports from the defence bill, in what Bloomberg described as a lobbying win for Nvidia. Huang had argued for years that selling to China keeps the country dependent on American technology, and the White House has largely sided with him on chip sales. Nvidia and trade groups oppose the new package too, arguing that stricter limits would burden Nvidia and the wider industry, according to reports.
The political ground has shifted since then, largely because of the Megaspeed affair. The chairs of three House committees asked Huang for a closed-door briefing on his reported link to Alice Huang, and Singapore has said it barred her from re-entry after she gave police inaccurate information. Semafor reported on 12 November that Congress is now pushing for tighter export controls following the Nvidia scandal.
Anthropic’s push for chip controls started long before Huang’s fall
Anthropic has been the most outspoken AI developer in favour of export controls. In May 2025, Nvidia publicly accused it of telling “tall tales” about chip smuggling, after Anthropic argued for stricter rules, according to NBC News. In February 2026, chief executive Dario Amodei met senators on Capitol Hill to discuss restrictions on chip sales to China, Axios reported.
Anthropic has also put money behind its position. On 12 February 2026, it announced a $20 million donation to Public First Action, a bipartisan advocacy group, saying it supports “smart export controls on AI chips” alongside AI transparency rules. On 21 July, it gave the group a further $20 million, taking its total to $40 million, and said it backs efforts to tighten export controls on advanced chips and chipmaking equipment. Those contributions are public, and they predate Huang’s troubles by months.
Critics of the AI labs’ position make a different argument. Nvidia and its allies have said export curbs mainly hand market share to Chinese chipmakers such as Huawei, and some observers note that AI developers also benefit commercially if Chinese rivals have less computing power. Supporters of the controls argue that advanced chips are a national security asset and that smuggling, as alleged in the Megaspeed case, shows existing rules are too weak.
Nvidia’s interim leadership inherits the fight in Washington
The policy fight now lands on Nvidia’s interim chief executive, Colette Kress, and its new board chair, Harvey Jones. Huang was the face of Nvidia’s argument in Washington, meeting the president and lawmakers directly, and the company has not said who will now lead that effort. Nvidia’s board said in its announcement that it expects operations and customer commitments to continue without interruption.
For gamers, the outcome matters less directly than it does for data centres, since consumer GeForce cards are not the main target of the proposals. However, Nvidia earns most of its revenue from AI chips, and any new limits on its China business would shape the company’s finances and priorities for years. Nvidia reports its third-quarter results on 17 November, the first under Kress.
The post OpenAI Backs China Chip Curbs as Jensen Huang Exits Nvidia, but the ‘Targeted Takedown’ Claim Does Not Hold Up appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: 26 Years Later, Charles Schulz' Final Comic Strip Is Still an All-Time Peanuts Classic
items.content: While that was the first official Peanuts comic, a similar version by Charles Schulz predated Peanuts and ran in Minnesota’s St. Paul Pioneer Press. It was called Li’l Folks and also starred cute little children, although it did not have a regular cast like Peanuts would. Li’l Folks ran from 1947 until 1950, when Schulz quit after his editor refused to give him a raise from the $10 per comic he was making. After that, Schulz brought Li’l Folks to United Feature Syndicate. The national cartoon syndicator liked the comic, but needed to change its name because of a 1930s comic strip called Little Folks. The name Peanuts was chosen because The Howdy Doody Show was popular at the time and the studio audience of children on the show was called the “Peanut gallery.” Thus, Peanuts became the name.

Jensen Huang Called Colette Kress a ‘Deer in the Headlights’ Months Before She Replaced Him, WSJ Reports
items.content:
Months before Colette Kress replaced him as Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang belittled her in front of the company’s top finance team, according to a Wall Street Journal report by Anissa Gardizy and Robbie Whelan. At a meeting in August, Huang called Kress “a deer in the headlights” while interrupting her presentation, according to a person familiar with the comments. He also described her as a “reporting CFO”, rather than someone who could help him define a strategy or make decisions, the Journal reports.
Kress became interim chief executive on 12 November, when Nvidia announced that Huang had resigned after 33 years in charge.
The report also sheds light on the business pressures Huang was dealing with before the scandal broke. According to the Journal, he had summoned his senior finance executives to diagnose what it calls a “ballooning problem”. Nvidia was in talks to provide billions of dollars of guarantees to companies that could not afford its chips, and Huang was starting to question whether the dealmaking spree he had launched had gone too far. The Journal’s subheadline says Kress, now in charge, has questioned some of that dealmaking.
Huang’s own warning was about customers walking away and supply piling up
Some of the guarantee deals were led by Huang’s son-in-law, who works at Nvidia, according to the Journal. He had been offering financing to upstart cloud providers and data centre developers, in the hope of turning them into long-term Nvidia customers. TalkEsport is not naming him, as he is not a public figure, although the Journal identifies him.
During the same August meeting, Huang described a difficult picture for the company, the Journal reports. Major cloud providers were running away from Nvidia, he said, making plans to use alternative chips and reduce their reliance on the firm. The largest of those providers already build their own AI processors, such as Google’s Tensor Processing Units and Amazon’s Trainium chips. Huang also said that the supply of chip wafers and memory Nvidia had committed to buy was coming at him “like an avalanche”.
Those comments matter because they come from inside the company, and from Huang himself. They suggest that he saw financing and supply commitments as a growing risk months before his personal life became the story. The Journal’s account relies on people familiar with the matter, and TalkEsport has not found a public response from Kress, Huang or Nvidia to the report.
Kress now runs the company whose deals she questioned
Kress has been Nvidia’s chief financial officer since 2013, after senior finance roles at Cisco and Microsoft, and she keeps that job while serving as interim chief executive. In its announcement, Nvidia said the board has “full confidence in Colette and the leadership team”. Harvey Jones, a former Synopsys chief executive, became the company’s first board chair at the same time, and the board says it will consider internal and external candidates for the permanent role.
The Journal’s report gives that board a different picture of the person it has put in charge. Huang’s description of Kress as a “reporting CFO” suggests he saw her as someone who reported numbers rather than shaped strategy. The report’s account of her questioning his deals points the other way, towards an executive willing to challenge the founder on financial risk. Either way, the deals and commitments described in the August meeting now sit with her.
Kress faces her first earnings call five days after Huang’s exit
The pressure on Nvidia has not eased since the announcement. Its shares fell 4.34% on Thursday, the day the leadership change was announced, and the scandal around Huang has continued to grow. Sources have since alleged a third relationship with a second Nvidia employee, and Singapore has said it barred Alice Huang from re-entry in February.
Nvidia will report its third-quarter results on Tuesday 17 November at about 1:20 pm Pacific time, with its earnings call at 2 pm Pacific, or 22:00 UTC. It will be the company’s first results under an interim chief executive. It will also be the first chance for investors to question Kress directly about the financing deals and supply commitments described in the Journal’s report.

items.title: Singapore Barred Alice Huang From Re-Entry After She Gave Police Inaccurate Information, MHA Says
items.content:
Singapore barred Alice Huang from re-entering the country in February, after police concluded that she had given them information she knew to be inaccurate, the Ministry of Home Affairs said on 12 November. In a statement on its investigations into the cloud company Megaspeed, the ministry described her as Megaspeed’s then chief executive, chairperson and one of its key controllers.
Police found insufficient evidence that she had committed offences linked to Megaspeed’s possible false declarations, but gave her a stern warning. The ministry added that she “was not based in Singapore, and was not investigated for espionage”.
Alice Huang has been named in reports as the woman with whom Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang had a relationship, and US intelligence reportedly suspects her of gathering information for China. No charges have been reported against her, and Beijing has rejected the espionage claims as smears. Singapore’s statement does not mention Nvidia or Jensen Huang, whose board is reportedly preparing to remove him. It is Singapore’s most detailed public account of the case so far.
Singapore police say Alice Huang tried to downplay her role at Megaspeed
The ministry’s timeline starts in February 2025, when the Singapore Police Force and Singapore Customs opened an investigation into several companies and key officers, including Megaspeed. The case concerns potential false declarations in the purchase of servers, along with related offences. Home Affairs Minister K Shanmugam said in March 2025 that the investigation was not based on any request from another country. Megaspeed itself began operating in its current form in March 2023, when Alice Huang was listed as its managing director.
US officials visited Megaspeed a few months later, in the middle of 2025. On 24 June 2025, the US Bureau of Industry and Security carried out a voluntary post-shipment verification check at the company, with Alice Huang present. The ministry said that was Singapore’s first sign of US interest in Megaspeed and in her. Singapore police interviewed her on the same day, and impounded her passport to make sure she attended further questioning. Police returned the passport on 26 February 2026, and she left Singapore that day.
By then, police had concluded that she had provided information she knew to be inaccurate, in order to downplay her role in Megaspeed. She was given a stern warning and barred from re-entering the country, and the ministry said other cases had been dealt with in a similar way in the past. The investigation into Megaspeed and six other individuals is still continuing. None of those six people has been in Singapore since it began in February 2025, according to the ministry.
Singapore says Washington has shared little about Megaspeed
The statement also gives a rare public account of how cooperation with the US has gone. Singapore raised the matter with US authorities in July 2025, and since September 2025 police have repeated their requests to the US Department of Justice and the FBI on several occasions. “Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance in respect of the company,” the ministry said. Police also sought information from Supermicro, a US server supplier relevant to the investigation, which the ministry said provided limited cooperation.
That contrasts with the pressure on Megaspeed in Washington. Senator Tom Cotton urged the Commerce Department to investigate the company in an October 2025 letter, and US lawmakers have put Megaspeed’s Nvidia hardware imports at more than $4.6 billion. Megaspeed was set up as an offshore unit of the Chinese games and cloud company 7Road, which is part of why it sits at the centre of the Huang scandal.
Singapore also drew a clear line on export rules. The country “does not enforce unilateral export controls imposed by other countries”, the ministry said, although it expects companies to take such rules into account in their international business. Its own case is about possible false declarations under Singapore law, not US export controls. “We will not allow companies or individuals to misuse Singapore’s business environment to engage in fraud or dishonest practices,” the ministry added.
The statement lands on the same day Megaspeed promised a GPU census
Megaspeed issued its own statement on 12 November, saying it had hired a US law firm to count its GPUs and check its export compliance. That statement is signed by Tan Yong Pong as chairman and chief executive, the same roles the ministry says Alice Huang held when police began their investigation. Megaspeed’s statement does not mention her, the Singapore investigation or the re-entry ban. Nvidia, for its part, said in 2025 that its own checks had found Megaspeed “legally qualified”, with “no signs of diversion”.
The chip trail has also widened beyond Singapore. The Information has reported that Alice Huang was linked to Shanghai Century Litong, a Chinese Nvidia cloud partner that it says helped move at least $7.5 billion of Nvidia chips into China since 2023. The Wall Street Journal has also reported that her husband, a businessman who had known Jensen Huang for about a decade, introduced the two of them.
For Nvidia’s board, the key question is whether the relationship created a security or governance problem. After the first reports, the board said it had “no reason to believe” that national security or Nvidia’s secrets had been compromised, and it has since hired former federal prosecutor Joon Kim to investigate. The board has not announced a decision on Huang, and Nvidia reports its third-quarter results on 17 November.
The post Singapore Barred Alice Huang From Re-Entry After She Gave Police Inaccurate Information, MHA Says appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Jensen Huang Had Third Relationship, With Second Nvidia Employee, Sources Say
items.content:
Former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second Nvidia employee, two sources told Reuters on 12 November. The allegation is the third relationship linked to Huang in less than two weeks. The woman has not been named, and her role at the company has not been disclosed. Reuters could not reach her for comment.
The allegation emerged on the same day Nvidia said Huang had stepped down after 33 years as chief executive. Chief financial officer Colette Kress became interim chief executive while keeping her finance role. Harvey C. Jones, a former Synopsys chief executive who has sat on Nvidia’s board since 1993, was named the company’s first chair.
Jensen Huang’s earlier admission and the Kimberly Powell allegation
Huang admitted on 8 November that he had been “unfaithful” to his wife, Lori Huang, in a letter to Nvidia staff that the company also issued as a press release. He apologised and said the board had opened an independent investigation, which he supported. The letter did not name anyone or say how many relationships were involved.
The admission followed weeks of scrutiny over Huang’s ties to Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. US and Singapore authorities investigated Megaspeed in 2025 over suspected breaches of chip export controls. Claims that US officials suspect Alice Huang of working for China’s Ministry of State Security have not been confirmed, and she has not commented publicly. Nvidia said on 29 October that Huang’s meetings with her were “not unusual or unexpected” for a chief executive.
On 11 November, five former and current Nvidia staff alleged that Huang had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. That allegation remains unconfirmed. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not commented on it.
Nvidia shares fall as Congress seeks Huang’s testimony
Nvidia headquarters in Santa Clara, California
Nvidia shares fell as much as 14% at the open on 12 November, their lowest level since June 2025. The stock recovered part of the loss and closed at $166.19, down 4.34%. The fall cut Nvidia’s market value from $4.498 trillion to $4.005 trillion. Shares had already dropped more than 5% on 9 November, the first trading day after Huang’s letter.
The Rayburn House Office Building in Washington
Three House committee chairs, John Moolenaar, Brian Mast and Rick Crawford, asked Huang on 5 November for a closed-door briefing. Mast later said Huang had agreed to testify before Thanksgiving after being warned of a subpoena. No date has been set. Rosen Law Firm has filed a proposed class action on behalf of Nvidia shareholders.
As we covered in our report on Jensen Huang’s resignation as Nvidia chief executive, the board met on 11 November before announcing the change. Our profile of interim chief executive Colette Kress covers her 13 years as finance chief. Nvidia has not said whether the board investigation will examine the new allegation, or whether Huang will keep any role at the company. Elon Musk said on 12 November that hiring Huang “would be an honour”.

items.title: Overwatch Hero 55: Hudson changes from support to DPS omnic detective
items.content:
Overwatch game director Aaron Keller and associate game director Alec Dawson just announced that the new omnic detective will be a damage hero instead of a support. Overwatch Hero 55’s name will also be Hudson.
Overwatch’s new hero is a DPS instead of a support
Originally announced as a support hero, Overwatch’s omnic detective will soon debut as a damage hero instead of a support in Season 6. Dawson revealed this change during a Twitch livestream with content creators Emongg and Flats.
“The core mechanic and the thing that we were really falling in love with on this hero didn’t really match with being a support, and we kind of leaned into the things we loved the most about the hero, and it definitely fits DPS a lot better,” Dawson said. “So we’re really excited for him pretty soon. He has a very fun accent, I’ll say that. I’m allowed to say that.”
Prior to this change, a tarot card handed out in person at BlizzCon 2026 pointed to the omnic detective being a support hero.
The Overwatch omnic detective hero’s tarot card given out at BlizzCon 2026 (Image credit: Shroomiiee)
Overwatch Hudson is Hero 55
After this explanation, Keller accidently revealed that the omnic detective’s name will be Hudson. “There was a bit of a pivot on Hudson,” he said before realizing it.
Shortly after this, the official Overwatch account on social media made an announcement to confirm the name.
Casefile Status: Declassified 🗂️
We can’t wait for you to meet the newest Damage Hero, Hudson, in Season 6! pic.twitter.com/AWGVOrR7yy
— Overwatch (@PlayOverwatch) November 12, 2026
“We can’t wait for you to meet the newest damage hero, Hudson, in Season 6!” the post stated.
Before the reveal, some folks within the Overwatch community embraced Rigby as the omnic detective’s name. This name also appeared alongside Hudson on a business card found in Midtown.
