items.title: BETBY becomes first company to receive ESIC’s CPU v CPU Gold Standard accreditation
items.content:
The Esports Integrity Commission (ESIC) has awarded BETBY the first CPU v CPU Gold Standard accreditation, recognizing the betting provider’s effort and commitment to comply with ESIC’s integrity requirements for automated esports competitions.
The certification follows an on-site audit, an assessment of additional evidence, and an independent audit review conducted in August 2026. BETBY will also undergo annual audit reviews to maintain its accreditation.
The recognition marks the first time an organization has met the requirements under ESIC’s newly introduced framework, which aims to strengthen trust in automated esports competitions used in betting markets.
ESIC Introduces 17 Mandatory Controls for Automated Esports
Another of ESIC’s Gold Standard accreditation, only awarded to a few esports event organizers (Image credit: ESIC)
The CPU v CPU Gold Standard was introduced to address integrity concerns surrounding automated esports competitions, where match outcomes are generated by software rather than human players. Examples include virtual football and basketball matches, which have gained popularity in betting markets because they are available around the clock and typically take only a few minutes to finish.
According to ESIC, the framework establishes 17 mandatory control areas covering the systems responsible for generating and validating match results, the infrastructure supporting these competitions, and the personnel authorized to operate or modify them.
These requirements provide a basis for independently assessing how automated competitions are managed and whether the necessary safeguards are in place to protect their integrity.
ESIC CEO Stephen Hanna explained that the framework allows the industry to examine everything from the software version used in a match to deployment procedures, access controls, and incident response.
“When software determines how a competition unfolds, confidence depends on knowing what ran, who could change it and what evidence is available if something goes wrong. The CPU v CPU Gold Standard turns those questions into specific requirements for the technology and for the organization responsible for it.”
BETBY Commits to Annual Audits to Maintain ESIC Accreditation
Following the assessment, BETBY became the first organization to receive the CPU v CPU Gold Standard accreditation. The company has also committed to annual audit reviews as part of maintaining its certification.
Ilze Ramolina, General Counsel at BETBY, welcomed the introduction of the framework, noting that integrity oversight must evolve alongside new forms of esports content.
She also emphasized the importance of transparency and accountability in building trust among betting operators and their partners.
“We were very pleased to see ESIC broaden the scope of its certification framework with the introduction of the CPU v CPU Gold Standard. As the market evolves and new forms of esports content emerge, integrity oversight and control frameworks have to evolve with them.”
With BETBY’s achievement, ESIC is encouraging other providers in the sector to undergo independent assessments under the same framework. The commission believes wider adoption could establish more consistent integrity expectations and give betting operators a clearer way to evaluate automated esports competitions.
What is BETBY?
An example of an automated virtual football match (Image credit: BETBY)
BETBY is a B2B sports betting technology provider that develops sportsbook platforms, esports products, and betting solutions for operators worldwide. Rather than operating as a traditional betting site, the company provides the technology and services that allow its partners to run their own betting platforms.
BETBY’s portfolio includes sportsbook software, virtual sports, live esports betting, and BETBY.Games, which features AI-powered competitions in sports simulators. The company also provides tools for odds management, risk management, and live betting, allowing operators to customize their platforms based on their business needs.
Also read: BETBY secures partnership with Satoshi Gaming Group to grow in Asian market
Why Does BETBY’s ESIC Accreditation Matter?
BETBY receiving ESIC’s CPU v CPU Gold Standard accreditation is an important step toward improving trust in automated esports betting. It serves as proof that betting providers can meet independent integrity standards and demonstrate their commitment to transparency, accountability, and fair competition.
As more betting providers introduce simulated competitions, having independent standards for software, match results, and operational security becomes increasingly important. This accreditation also gives betting operators a clearer way to assess the integrity measures behind the content they offer.
If more providers follow BETBY’s example, it could help establish consistent integrity standards across the automated esports betting industry.

Once Human: Season 5 gameplay showcases co-op Colossus boss battle, live November 18
items.content:
What if a sky-spanning Colossus didn’t just loom overhead as a static backdrop, but actively listened and responded to your every gunshot? That’s the core question driving our upcoming fifth season, Dissonant Resonance, free to play and launching globally on November 18. Today, I want to take you behind the scenes to share how we are turning sound and emotion into your greatest weapons – and your biggest threats.
New weird meets a symphony of dread
Once Human thrives on the New Weird design philosophy – taking the familiar and twisting it into a nightmare. For Season 5, we wanted to apply this philosophy not just to the visuals, but to the audio itself. As we realized players always take background music for granted, we decided to weaponize it.
Inspired by the cathedral pipe organ, a human symbol of sanctity and solemnity, and through the lens of the New Weird, we distorted this familiar object into a cosmic, biomechanical monstrosity: What if the music wasn’t just playing in your headset, but was the literal breathing and judgment of a cosmic monstrosity watching your every move?
This idea birthed the Sky Living-Machine Colossus. By merging the sacred with the grotesque, this massive pipe-organ titan transforms the very rhythm of the world into an active, weaponized mechanic.
Emotion zones & rhythmic gunplay
To ground this massive concept in actual gameplay, we’ve warped the open world with four distinct Emotion Zones: Joy, Anger, Sorrow, and Fear.
In these erratic regions, your arsenal becomes an instrument. Defeating enemies scatters musical notes across the battlefield. By shooting these notes, you not only trigger pitch-tuned audio to improvise your own battle rhythms, but also collect them to purify dissonant, corrupted scores. Once these notes are rearranged into harmonious melodies, the scores grant your squad powerful rewards. And as you perform these deadly battle rhythms, the Sky Colossus above will react dynamically, shifting its visual expressions in real-time.
Once the Sky Colossus descends and lingers long enough, the world itself splits open—a rift portal emerges, daring your squad to step through and face the music directly.
Conducting the Colossus & a new companion
Stepping through that portal initiates a high-stakes, four-player co-op Colossus Raid. But this is no traditional boss fight. Taking center stage, the titan becomes a maestro of destruction, dynamically shifting the battlefield’s combat score.
As the boss and the arena pulse to a new rhythm, your squad must adapt on the fly. You need to sprint to silence glowing resonating pipes in a ruined cathedral, and disrupt the melody before the deadly track concludes. You aren’t just surviving a boss fight – you are conducting it.
To help you survive this apocalyptic symphony, we are also introducing the brand-new Deviant, Silent Statue. Appearing initially as a shattered, gray monument, it silently absorbs the elemental chaos of your firefights. For those who can unlock its true potential, the ruins will mend and spread brilliant golden wings—bestowing a massive elemental blessing across the squad.
Gear up, tune your weapons, and get ready to conduct the apocalypse when Once Human Season 5: Dissonant Resonance drops November 18 on PS5!

items.title: Available for XBOX Insiders: More Ways to Personalize Your Home, Library, and Guide
items.content:
Starting today, we’re introducing new ways for XBOX Insiders to make Home, My games & apps, and the Guide work better for them.
Keep your console Home fresh with rotating backgrounds, find games in your library more easily, or move the Guide to the other side of the screen. Give these updates a try and tell us what you think and what we could make better.
Alpha Skip-Ahead members can try them first. We’ll bring them to more XBOX Insiders and players over time.
Rotating Home Backgrounds
Want a new look for Home without picking a new background every time? XBOX Insiders can now save favorite dynamic backgrounds and shuffle through them automatically.
To save a favorite, go to Settings > General > Personalization > My background > Dynamic backgrounds > Dynamic backgrounds, choose a background, and press X. You’ll find it in the new Favorites category. Pro tip: If you have a controller with an exclusive background, like the XBOX Wireless Controller X25 Special Edition, saving that background as a favorite lets you use it even when the controller isn’t connected!
You can also choose Shuffle at the start of any background category. Have your background change each time you sign in, or set it to change hourly, daily, or weekly. Shuffle your favorites or explore a whole category, it’s an easy way to keep Home feeling fresh.
New Ways to Organize Digital Licenses for Disc-Based Games
Since August, XBOX players have been able to claim digital licenses for their disc-based games. You’ve told us you want more control over how those games appear in your library, so we’re adding a couple of options.
Starting today, XBOX Insiders who’ve claimed a digital license from a disc-based games will see those games in a separate category in their full library. Prefer to keep them alongside your other owned games? You can switch back in Settings > General > Personalization > Games & apps. From that same page, you can also hide the digital license icon on game tiles.
Your Guide, Your Side
Prefer the guide on the right? Now you can put it there. XBOX Insiders can choose whether the Guide opens on the left or right side of the screen to switch up how you navigate XBOX.
Pick your side in Settings > General > Personalization > Guide. Tell us if you’re team left or team right.
How to Get XBOX Insider Support and Share Your Feedback
Thanks to XBOX Insiders for all of the feedback. You can also visit aka.ms/XBOXplayervoice to share what you think.
If you’re an XBOX Insider looking for support, please join our community on the XBOX Insider subreddit. Official XBOX staff, moderators, and fellow XBOX Insiders are there to help. We recommend adding to threads with the same topic before posting a brand new one. This helps us support you the best we can!
If you aren’t part of the XBOX Insider Program yet and want to help create the future of XBOX and get early access to new features, join the Program today by downloading the XBOX Insider Hub for XBOX Series X|S & XBOX One or Windows PC. For more information on the XBOX Insider Program, follow us on Twitter at @XBOXInsider and keep an eye on this blog for all the latest news.

Candy Crush Saga Gives Halo, Fallout, Forza and More a Sweet Makeover for XBOX’s 25th
items.content:
XBOX’s 25th anniversary has arrived in Candy Crush Saga. Out now, the Game On! Season brings together Halo, Fallout, Sea of Thieves, Forza, DOOM, Banjo-Kazooie, Crash Bandicoot and Spyro for four weeks of collectible pins and some very familiar music with a distinctly Candy Crush sound.
For anyone who’s spent years with these games, there’s plenty to recognize. But putting them in the Candy Kingdom meant working out which details to keep, which to play with.
A different kind of armor collection
At the center of the season is an XBOX 25 pin collection. Players earn pins as they progress through Candy Crush Saga levels, collecting characters and moments from across all eight franchises. Look out for Master Chief’s helmet, DOOM’s Cacodemon and Crash Bandicoot’s Dr. Neo Cortex, alongside Candy Crush characters getting into costume.
The teams behind those worlds worked with King on the designs. For Halo, that meant finding room for both the franchise’s most recognizable armor and the personalities of the characters wearing it.
“Halo’s music is such an iconic part of the franchise, and seeing it ‘candified’ into something playful and unexpected, while still being unmistakably Halo, was a lot of fun,” Corrine Robinson, Sr. Halo Franchise Manager, explains. “We took the same approach with the pins: start with the Candy Crush characters and bring in some of the most recognizable elements of Halo. Tiffi in pink Mjolnir armor, topped off with her signature bow, was a perfect Spartan mash-up, while Dachs in Grunt armor quickly became my personal favorite. The Candy Crush team was a fantastic creative partner, and we enjoyed bringing our two very different worlds together in a way that feels authentic to both franchises and, most importantly, fun for the fans.”
Fallout takes the costume changes in another direction. Vault Boy makes an appearance, Dachs borrows Dogmeat’s armor, and Bubblegum Troll gets a Vault Suit. As Daniel Lee, Associate Art Director at Bethesda Game Studios, points out, the Wasteland already knows a thing or two about candy:
“Sugar Bombs, Fancy Lad Snack Cakes, Radioactive Gumdrops, the Wasteland is certainly no stranger to sweet treats. Working with King to bring together two vastly different worlds together has been a real pleasure.
“In addition to our very own Vault Boy making an appearance, you’ll also find Dachs donning Dogmeat’s armor and even the Bubblegum Troll in a Vault Suit! My favorite part however has to be how they’ve paired the music of Fallout with their own incredible soundtrack. What an incredibly fun way to celebrate 25 years of XBOX.”
Turn the sound up
The music deserves a closer listen. Six themes, drawn from Halo, Fallout, Sea of Thieves, Forza, DOOM and Banjo-Kazooie, have been reworked in Candy Crush style and woven into gameplay throughout the season.
The recordings bring together an orchestra, the Bulgarian Voices Berlin choir and, yes, an accordion. Composer Federico Truzzi worked on the arrangements, with King’s Head of Audio Dominique Devoucoux and Audio Lead Sebastian Aav sharing the thinking behind the project in a behind-the-scenes video.
It’s a chance to hear music you know well in a different setting, whether you first heard it exploring the Wasteland, setting sail or playing Banjo-Kazooie. The six tracks will also be available across streaming platforms and participating studio channels, so you can listen outside the game.
For Rare, the collaboration brings both its characters and its music to a new audience.
“Candy Crush is a game which has a universal appeal that brightens up whatever platform you choose to play it on, and the same is true of Rare’s colourful, exuberant worlds and characters,” says Adam Park, Head of Brand and Licensing at Rare. “That’s why the opportunity to bring heroes like Banjo, Kazooie and Pendragon into the Candy Crush universe, where a whole new audience can be charmed by them, was just too good to pass up. And, of course, it’s a huge honor to have iconic tunes from our games reimagined by artists whose interpretations bring a whole new candy flavor to fan-favorite tracks. A perfect match!”
Start your collection
The Game On! Season runs through December 6, 2026, in Candy Crush Saga on iOS and Android. Alongside the pin collection and music, an arcade-themed Leagues event gives players a chance to compete and climb the standings.
Some of the pins are making the jump out of the game, too. VIP players in the US can enter a contest at candycrush.com for a chance to win one of 1,000 limited-edition physical pin packs.
Candy Crush Saga is free to download on iOS and Android. Pick up the game, start collecting, and leave the sound on. You’ll want to hear how those themes have been candified, trust us.

items.title: Genshin Impact Cheater Selling Paid Stygian Onslaught Carries Reportedly Arrested While Meeting Customers
items.content:
Chinese police allegedly detained a Genshin Impact player who allegedly used cheats to sell paid Stygian Onslaught clears, while the player was meeting customers in a clothing store. The arrest has not been confirmed by police or by HoYoverse, the game’s developer. The player’s name, the city and the date of the arrest have not been disclosed.
Security camera images from inside the store, dated 3 November, circulated online alongside the claims. A second image showed a Chinese-language apology to HoYoverse on a phone screen. Neither the police nor HoYoverse has commented publicly on the case.
Genshin Impact player apologised to HoYoverse over Stygian Onslaught cheats
In the apology, the player admitted to posting videos of themselves “using cheats in Genshin Impact” without authorisation. The player said the actions “seriously violated” the official rules of miHoYo and Genshin Impact, which prohibit cheating. The player has since deleted the posts that advertised the service.
The player promoted the service through videos on Bilibili that showed the cheats in use. The videos directed viewers to a store on Xianyu, a Chinese second-hand marketplace, that sold the boosting service. Prices for the service have not been disclosed.
Stygian Onslaught is a combat challenge in Genshin Impact made up of three timed battles. Higher difficulty levels add tougher enemies and stricter time limits, and the mode rewards players who clear them quickly. The allegations first surfaced on the Chinese gaming forum NGA before spreading on other platforms.
HoYoverse’s earlier action against Genshin Impact cheats and boosting studios
HoYoverse said in March 2026 that it removed more than one million illegal links and pieces of content during 2025, including cheat software and pirated resources. In 2023, the company threatened legal action against cheaters after malicious plug-ins affected other players’ accounts.
In September 2025, a Shanghai court ordered a Genshin Impact boosting studio to pay 3 million yuan (about $420,000) in damages for using cheats to complete orders for customers. The studio had used unauthorised tools to clear in-game content on clients’ accounts.
The case comes weeks after HoYoverse released the latest update, as we covered in our report on the Genshin Impact 7.2 patch notes. HoYoverse has not said whether it will pursue civil action against the detained player.

Naughty Dog’s Intergalactic is playable and in final polish, Druckmann says
items.content:
Naughty Dog's Neil Druckmann says that Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet has reached the final stage of production, with the game now playable, Inven Global reported. It's the first proper status check we’ve had on the PS5 project since its reveal, and it seems that all systems are go.
Druckmann, the studio head and the game's director and writer were speaking at Comic Creators Block Party 2026. Host and comedian Patton Oswalt asked for more details but Druckmann was keen to keep his lips sealed where the story is concerned.
"We've only teased it, so I can't talk too much about it," he said before adding "we're kind of like at the last stages of production, where we can play it, and we're refining it and polishing it, and I can't wait to show it to the world."
DateMilestone
2024Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet revealed
SeptemberNaughty Dog says it will stay quiet for the rest of 2026
Nov. 7Comic Creators Block Party 2026 conversation streamed
2027Gameplay and more story due
What Naughty Dog plans to show in 2027
While he may be resistant to saying much more at the moment, Druckmann reassured Oswalt and everyone else that the studio will reveal more next year. "We're going to show gameplay, more of the story," he revealed, which fits an earlier September update when Naughty Dog said it needed "to cook for just a little bit longer."
No release date or window has been given, though, and for now only PS5 is a confirmed platform, where Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet will be published by Sony Interactive Entertainment.
A blend of three Naughty Dog worlds
Jak and Daxter is one of the inspirations for the new Intergalactic game
Despite expressing reluctance to dive deeper into the story, Druckmann fed fans a few crumbs when he described the new game as a mix of Jak and Daxter, The Last of Us and action-adventure title Uncharted. He says the team were eager to recreate the sci-fi and fantasy of Jak and Daxter, while mixing in the pulp adventure of Uncharted, before ramping things up with the punishing drama of The Last of Us. If all this is accurate, it’ll be the studio’s first sci-fi-tinged outing since Jak and Daxter.
Druckmann also pointed to the studio's two decades on "relatively grounded" Earth-bound series. The goal now is deeper systems. "Can we sustain the cinematic storytelling we're used to doing, and go even deeper with gameplay systems?" he asked.
And while we don’t know a lot about the story, what we do know is that Intergalactic will be centered on a bounty hunter by the name of Jordan A. Mun, who’s stranded on a planet called Sempiria 2,000 years from now while tracking down a criminal.
Writer's take
Naughty Dog is largely known for two franchises; a new IP with a stated goal of deeper gameplay systems is something new for the studio, and we’re certain they’re feeling super excited right now. Druckmann sounds confident about the game, he’s happy to say it’s playable and in polish, and it sends out a strong sign that 2027 will be a showing year, not another teaser.
Naughty Dog hasn't set a date for the full reveal. Druckmann has only said gameplay and more story are coming in 2027, and new The Last of Us projects are in development at the studio alongside it.

While Naughty Dog remains tight-lipped on the finer details, the latest update suggests development is progressing smoothly ahead of the game's planned full reveal in 2027. items.title: Jonathan Calls Kronten’s Allegations “Completely Wrong” in First Response to GodLike Dispute
items.content:
Jonathan “Jonathan” Amaral, founder of Team Apex Gaming, has called the allegations made against him by GodLike Esports owner Chetan “Kronten” Chandgude “completely wrong”. He spoke during a livestream on Kick on 12 November, his first spoken response since the dispute began. Jonathan said he would not address most of the claims in detail. He did not respond point by point to the ownership or salary figures Kronten gave.
Jonathan said he did not like getting involved in such matters and that the statements made “no sense”. He said he had “no idea” what some of the claims referred to. He added that he would only address “a few things”, and that one claim had made him laugh.
Jonathan denies Kronten’s claim about how he reacts to losses
The one claim Jonathan addressed directly concerned his emotions after poor results. Kronten had said on his stream that Jonathan appeared upset on camera after defeats but behaved differently once the cameras were off. Jonathan said anyone who plays sport or esports and comes close to a goal without reaching it would be upset. He said players who lose “won’t dance” afterwards.
He also made a sarcastic remark about money while discussing the claim. Jonathan suggested that Kronten might not have emotions, before adding a reference to “crores of rupees”. He did not name Kronten at any point in the comments.
The response followed an Instagram story Jonathan posted after Kronten’s stream, which read “I choose me, I’m sorry”. The line is from Kendrick Lamar’s song “Mirror”. Jonathan did not explain the story or say whether it was a reply to Kronten.
Kronten’s allegations over GodLike ownership, salaries and Madhur Agarwal
Kronten made the allegations during a livestream in early November. He said management never benched Jonathan at BGIS 2026, and that Jonathan sat out the first day of the Survival Stage because of a shoot. As we covered in our report on Kronten’s claim that GodLike never benched Jonathan, Jonathan had said at the time that the decision was taken in the team’s interest.
Kronten said Jonathan held a 33% ownership stake in GodLike, the second-largest in the organisation. He said someone on Jonathan’s side, possibly his parents, later asked for a 50-50 ownership arrangement. Kronten also said Jonathan asked for a salary of ₹25 lakh a month. None of these figures has been backed by published documents, and Jonathan has not confirmed or denied them.
Kronten said GodLike spent about ₹15 lakh a month on its roster while BGMI was banned in India, rising to about ₹25 lakh after the ban was lifted. He also said Jonathan told him around 28 February that he planned to leave. Jonathan left GodLike in April and later launched Team Apex Gaming.
Kronten also accused Jonathan’s manager, Madhur Agarwal, of passing on information and of taking GodLike players to meetings in Mumbai’s BKC area to discuss joining Team Apex Gaming. He said he gave former GodLike member Hades between ₹10 lakh and ₹15 lakh, and claimed an FIR had been filed. As we covered in our report on Kronten’s full stream and the FIR claim, the FIR’s details have not been made public.
Madhur said in a public message that he would address the matter in detail “at the right time” with facts and evidence. He said he wanted due process to be followed in ongoing legal matters. Team Apex Gaming founding member Shreeman Legend told viewers on his own stream that he did not know enough about the dispute to comment. Hades has not publicly responded to Kronten’s latest claims, and Team Apex Gaming has not issued a formal statement.
The post Jonathan Calls Kronten’s Allegations “Completely Wrong” in First Response to GodLike Dispute appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: The Game Awards will be livestreamed on Disney+ this year
items.content:
Geoff Keighley has announced that this year's The Game Awards will be streamed live on Disney+ for the first time, bringing gaming's biggest annual awards show to one of the world's largest streaming platforms.
Keighley revealed the news in a post on X, confirming that viewers will be able to watch The Game Awards live on Disney+ when the show returns on the 10th of December. Importantly, this does not appear to be an exclusive streaming deal. Keighley specifically stated that fans can “also watch” the event on Disney+, so you'll still be able to catch it on Twitch or YouTube if that's your preference.
The move represents another major step forward for The Game Awards, which has steadily grown from a niche gaming event into one of the gaming industry's flagship annual showcases. Alongside the award presentations, the show has become known for major game announcements, world premieres and surprise reveals.
This is perhaps the biggest move towards bringing in mainstream viewers since the TGA's inception. Keighley initially hosted the Spike Video Game Awards from 2003 to the early 2010s, which did air on traditional television. When that ended, Keighley went independent and spun up The Game Awards with a more web-streaming focus.
KitGuru says: The Game Awards has become much more than an awards show over the years. Will you be watching on YouTube, Twitch or Disney+ this December?

Starting today, XBOX Playback brings highlights from your available XBOX history across every generation in a personalized experience. For the first time, you can look back and re-live the part you played in XBOX’s story. Starting today, you can watch your Playback directly on your console (look for the option on your dashboard) or watch your personalized video on the web by signing in with your XBOX account here.

After watching your Playback, scan the QR code at the end of the console video or select “share” on web to get your personalized Playback card. Share it with friends or post it with #XBOXPlayback on social.
XBOX Playback brings together years of XBOX history in a brand-new way. We hope Playback evokes a few memories, surprises you, or reminds you of a game you haven’t thought about in a while. Playback is based on available account data, so some parts of your history may be incomplete or take time to appear. Playback is available in 15 countries* from today through December 31.

items.title: TimeSplitters and Star Wars classics may be heading to Xbox’s PC emulator
items.content:
Microsoft may be preparing another wave of original Xbox games for PC, with newly discovered backend changes pointing towards support for several classic titles through the Xbox PC app.
The discovery was shared over on Reddit, where someone spotted a number of original Xbox titles appearing in Microsoft's backend with Windows package records similar to those used by games that have already been added to the Xbox PC emulator.
The next wave of games appears to include the likes of The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind, TimeSplitters: Future Perfect, Star Wars Battlefront, Star Wars Battlefront II, Republic Commando and Jedi Academy. Other titles listed include Indiana Jones and the Emperor's Tomb, Red Faction II, Secret Weapons Over Normandy and even Disney's Chicken Little.
If accurate, this next wave of supported games coming over to PC from the original Xbox will be much larger than the initial first wave. Morrowind, TimeSplitters and a bunch of Star Wars classics also feels more exciting to me personally, although some of the games on the list do already have well-known native PC versions.
This isn't the first time datamining efforts and sleuthing have hinted at Microsoft's plans for Xbox console emulation on PC. Previously, code strings hinted at upcoming support for Xbox 360 games on PC as well.

RNTX Announces New Valorant Roster With Hoax, hellff, DcRulz, venka and Lightningfast
items.content:
Revenant XSpark (RNTX) has announced a new five-player Valorant roster of Aman “Hoax” Yadav, Sagnik “hellff” Roy, Daivik “DcRulz” Chauhan, Venkatesh “venka” Sharma and Abhirup “Lightningfast” Paul Choudhury. The line-up brings together two Indian cores that finished first and third at VCT Challengers 2026 South Asia Split 2 in June.
Hoax and venka are the two players staying from the previous RNTX roster. Lightningfast, hellff and DcRulz join together. The three played as a unit at Gods Reign and then under the NSP tag, where they won Challengers South Asia Split 2. As per our sources, Shravana “Techno” Kumar Sahoo will stay on as the substitute. He joined RNTX with Hoax and venka on 18 February. The organisation has not confirmed his status publicly.
RNTX Valorant Roster:
Hoax to lead RNTX, with Lightningfast on smokes and venka on duelist
As per our sources, Hoax will make the calls for the team and share the initiator and flex roles with hellff. Lightningfast is expected to play controller and anchor sites. venka stays on duelist, and DcRulz is set to play sentinel and flex. hellff is expected to fill whatever roles are left in each composition.
venka’s long-term future with the side is less certain. TalkEsport’s sources said the 20-year-old plans to go abroad for studies in January 2027, which would make him a short-term signing. This has not been confirmed by venka or RNTX.
RNTX signs the trio that won Challengers South Asia Split 2
Lightningfast, 25, has won four Challengers South Asia events since the start of 2025. He spent almost four years at Global Esports between November 2020 and August 2024, winning the Skyesports Champions Series in 2022. At Velocity Gaming he won Challengers 2025 South Asia Split 1, Split 3 and the Grand Final, beating S8UL 3–1 in the Grand Final.
hellff, 27, started out in Counter-Strike: Global Offensive with Global Esports before moving to Valorant in 2020. He has since played for Velocity Gaming, Team Mahi, True Rippers, Orangutan and S8UL Esports. At S8UL he was part of the side that finished second at Challengers 2025 South Asia Split 3 and the Grand Final, losing both finals to Velocity.
DcRulz, 22, is the youngest of the three. He played for Medal Esports, Aster Army, Orangutan and DOT EXE before joining Gods Reign on 12 March 2026. He won Predator League India 2025 with Orangutan and finished third at the 2025 South Asia Grand Final with DOT EXE.
All three left Gods Reign on May 2026 and went on to compete as NSP. That team beat S8UL 3–2 to win Challengers 2026 South Asia Split 2 on 28 June and took $10,014.78 in prize money. NSP then finished fourth at the Challengers 2026 Pacific Last Chance Qualifier after a 0–2 loss to YJ.
Hoax and venka are the only holdovers at RNTX
Hoax, 24, has played for Team Valor, Gods Reign, Grayfox Esports, Velocity Gaming, Orangutan and S8UL. He won Challengers 2024 South Asia Split 1 Cup 1 with Grayfox and Predator League India 2025 with Orangutan. At S8UL he added the Predator League India 2026 title, beating GGEZ 2–0.
venka’s career has followed a similar path through Grayfox, Velocity Gaming and Orangutan. He stepped away from competition between June and October 2024 before returning with Orangutan. He first joined RNTX on 4 April 2025, left on 16 July 2025, and rejoined with Hoax and Techno on 18 February 2026.
The Valorant changes are part of a wider rebuild at the organisation this month, which included Shadow’s return to Revenant XSpark’s BGMI roster. It also entered EA FC with Vanshaj Sharma on 5 November.
RNTX’s 2026 Valorant side, with Hoax, Techno, venka and Indonesian player k1ngkappa, finished second at Challengers 2026 South Asia Split 1 after a 2–3 loss to S8UL. It then placed third at Split 2, the event NSP won. The organisation, formed on 31 October 2024 as a collaboration with Team XSpark, won Challengers 2025 South Asia Split 2 with a 3–0 win in the final.
The new roster’s first event is the VCT 2027 Kickoff Open Qualifiers for South Asia, which JioBLAST is running in place of NODWIN Gaming. The open qualifiers run from 17 to 20 November, using a Swiss format, and the top eight teams advance to a double-elimination playoff from 23 to 29 November. The top two teams earn places at Kickoff APAC. Registration closes on 13 November, and every player must be ranked at least Ascendant 1.
RNTX will also play in Predator League India 2027, the Valorant event Hoax won with both Orangutan and S8UL in its two previous editions. The online qualifiers ran from 9 to 12 November, with playoffs from 16 to 18 November and the grand final on 22 November. The India event carries a prize pool of ₹5,00,000 (about $5,650), with ₹2,50,000 for the winners. The Asia Pacific Predator League 2027 will be held in Vietnam, and Acer has not yet announced its dates.

items.title: 25 Years of XBOX
items.content:
This message was just sent to Team XBOX employees globally.
Team,
Microsoft was founded on the belief that computing could put extraordinary capabilities in the hands of ordinary people. Gaming has been part of that story since the company’s beginning.
In 1979, we released Microsoft Adventure, a text-based game that looked more like MS-DOS than an early version of Minecraft. Adapted by a single programmer, Gordon Letwin, one of Microsoft’s first 13 employees and later an architect on OS/2, the game let players explore a digital world, collect treasure, solve puzzles, and encounter mythical creatures.
A few years later, Bruce Artwick brought the magic of flight to the 16-bit IBM PC, making it possible to fly a plane from your desk. Over the following decade, Microsoft published dozens of other titles including Minesweeper, Age of Empires, and another four Microsoft Flight Simulators, while Windows helped usher in 3D gaming with partners such as id Software (which would join XBOX some 24 years later).
In the mid-1990s, a small team working on DirectX, the technology that helped developers make games for Windows, had a big idea: using PC architecture to power the first American video game console in decades. Shortly thereafter, work began on the secret “Project Midway.”
When the original XBOX launched in 2001, it was impossible to miss. It was 2-3x larger than rival consoles, with a giant X molded into a black enclosure and a bright alien green jewel at the center. It shipped with a hard drive when competitors asked players to buy standalone memory cards and an Ethernet jack when 9 in 10 households still used dial-up. It also boasted more than twice the processing power of the PlayStation and GameCube and pioneered dual analog controllers.
A year later, Xbox Live revolutionized online play with persistent friend lists and matchmaking, as well as a common service for developers to build connected experiences. And bringing all of this together was Halo: Combat Evolved, a launch title that not only defined XBOX but proved its first advertising campaign: “Games Will Never Be The Same.”
Twenty-five years later, XBOX has grown into one of the world’s largest gaming businesses. We’ve built four generations of XBOX consoles, with a fifth on the way. Today, our games reach more than a billion players every year spanning beloved and iconic franchises such as Call of Duty, Candy Crush, Diablo, Doom, Fable, Fallout, Forza, Gears of War, Halo, Minecraft, Overwatch, Sea of Thieves, The Elder Scrolls, StarCraft, Warcraft, Wolfenstein, and many more.
To Everyone Who Made XBOX, XBOX
XBOX has been built by generations of employees, studios, developers, and partners who believed in what gaming could become. To all of you, thank you. I especially want to recognize the 111 people across XBOX and our studios who have been here for 25 years or more. You’ve helped shape the history we’re celebrating today, and each of you will receive a special engraved console to commemorate what you’ve helped build.
Since joining XBOX, I’ve heard stories of friendships that began over a session and lasted a lifetime, of people who met the person they would marry, and of parents now sharing the games they grew up on with their children. I’ve also heard about people who are no longer with us, and how much those hours spent playing together still mean to those who love them. Ultimately, this is why we exist.
The story of XBOX has never been ours alone. Our fans have challenged us, cheered us on, held us accountable, and stuck with us. We’ve been celebrating this anniversary with fans around the world and special launches. Today, we are bringing the celebration home to Seattle.
The Next 25
Gaming has always been an industry driven by dreams. Not just the desire to bring something imagined to life, but to share it with others. Sometimes that dream is of a game, other times a console, a character, or an entire universe. The history of XBOX is a testament to the power of these dreams and how they can grow over time.
The first Microsoft Flight Simulator was just 160 KB, with 2D graphics, 16 colors, and 20 total airports. The 2024 version draws on more than 2.5 petabytes of data (more than 15 billion times the size of the original game). Its 200-million-square-mile map recreates almost every city, road, and landmark across the planet, with trillions of individually rendered trees and real-world weather reproduced in near real time.
While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically. As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this.
Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today’s games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982.
I believe the future of gaming will look more like its beginning, when a small team with a big idea could change how the world plays. Our responsibility is to deliver great games, unmistakable hardware, and give more people the chance to make something the world has never seen.
Happy Birthday XBOX!
Asha
The post 25 Years of XBOX appeared first on XBOX Wire.

items.content:
Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra survived fresh cancellation rumours this week, but newly reported details about the game's development may have left fans more concerned than reassured.
The latest round of speculation began after rumours spread online claiming that Marvel 1943 had been cancelled. However, according to reporting from Kotaku, Skydance leadership quickly moved to reassure developers internally that the project remains in active development and is still moving towards its next major milestone.
The bigger story revolves around what the game has apparently become behind the scenes. Ever since Marvel 1943 was unveiled, many fans have expected a high-budget action-adventure game in the mould of Amy Hennig's previous work on the Uncharted series. However, Kotaku's sources say that the project originally began life as a Netflix game before later transitioning into a full PC and console release.
It is also claimed that Marvel 1943 faced repeated development difficulties, multiple delays and significant budget overruns, despite the current game being described as “light on interaction”. The game was said to have been scaled back significantly from its original vision, though it is now approaching an internal alpha development milestone.
The revelations may come as a surprise to fans who have spent the last few years anticipating a well-rounded AAA game. The game's original reveal generated significant excitement, thanks in large part to Hennig's involvement and the promise of a story-driven action adventure, during a very interesting time in Marvel history – the World War 2 era, when Captain America first came to be.
KitGuru says: This is all rumour for now, after all we haven't seen any real gameplay for ourselves yet, but ‘light on interaction' doesn't sound great, especially after Wolverine. Hopefully the game looks a bit more fun than it currently sounds when it gets a proper reveal later.

items.title: VALORANT Bunker Returns to Mumbai on 22 November at Ballard Pier, With Rolling Loud India and Red Bull on Board
items.content:
VALORANT Bunker, Riot Games’ music and community night for Indian players, is returning to Mumbai on 22 November 2026, this time at Ballard Pier in the south of the city. Riot’s VALORANT India and South Asia team confirmed the date on 12 November with a poster that lists Red Bull, Rolling Loud India and JioBLAST among the event’s partners. “The game, the music, the community,” the official post reads, and Riot teased the comeback earlier the same day with a short video captioned “BUNKER is back”. Riot has not yet announced the line-up, timings or how fans can get in.
The game, the music, the community. It's all coming together on Nov 22nd. pic.twitter.com/mJbHWe9J7Q
— VALORANT India & South Asia (@VALORANTinsa) November 12, 2026
Bunker returns two years after its Mumbai debut
The first VALORANT Bunker took place in Mumbai on 27 November 2024, with electronic artists Ritviz and Gravero on the bill. That night also gave fans the first live preview of “Gotcha Back”, the anthem that Riot and the music collective ARB4 released as a full music video in December 2024. ARB4 had earlier made “RAJA”, the theme song for Harbor, VALORANT’s first Indian agent. Riot first announced that 2024 Bunker on 12 November 2024, exactly two years before this year’s reveal.
This year’s poster also carries a hint about the headline agent. Its artwork shows a white-haired agent in pink tones that closely resembles Hush, the telekinetic Duelist Riot added in patch 13.09 in late October. Riot’s first teaser line for the event, “No need to be Hush about this one”, points the same way. Riot has not said whether Hush will feature in any in-game tie-in or event reward.
This year’s edition moves Bunker to Ballard Pier, in the Ballard Estate area of south Mumbai beside the city’s port. Riot has been teasing the return for weeks, including a 7 November post that told fans to close their seat trays because “BUNKER is back”. It has not said how many people the venue will hold or whether entry will be free.
Riot is building VALORANT India around music as much as esports
Bunker is part of a wider push by Riot to connect VALORANT with India’s music scene. In November 2025, VALORANT ran an experience zone at the India debut of the hip-hop festival Rolling Loud in Navi Mumbai, with karaoke pods, quick duels and live art. “It’s the perfect stage for us to meet players where they are,” Arun Rajappa, Riot Games India’s director of publishing, said at the time. Rolling Loud India’s logo on this year’s Bunker poster suggests that relationship has carried over into Riot’s own event.
Red Bull, which already runs VALORANT events such as the Red Bull Campus Clutch university tournament, is the other big lifestyle name on the poster. The partners together point to a night that is closer to a gig than a tournament. That fits the original Bunker, which was built around live sets and VALORANT music rather than competitive matches.
Bunker lands the day before the VCT Kickoff qualifiers reach their playoffs
The competitive side of VALORANT India is also busy that week. JioBLAST, the third partner on the poster, is running the VCT 2027 Kickoff Open Qualifiers for South Asia, the first stage of the 2027 VALORANT Champions Tour season. The Swiss stage runs from 17 to 20 November, and the playoffs follow from 23 to 29 November, starting the day after Bunker. Two teams from the region will qualify for Kickoff APAC.
The Indian scene has new storylines to follow as well. GodLike Esports are reportedly returning to VALORANT with a roster built for the Open Qualifiers, while the global off-season has already produced big moves such as TenZ joining T1. Bunker gives Riot a chance to bring the community together before the new season begins.
Riot has not yet announced the artists, ticketing or timings for Bunker Mumbai, so fans will need to follow the official VALORANT India and South Asia channels for the next update. The 2024 edition was announced 15 days before it took place, while this year’s date reveal comes 10 days out. So far, Riot has said only that Bunker Mumbai takes place at Ballard Pier on 22 November 2026, with Red Bull, Rolling Loud India and JioBLAST on board.
The post VALORANT Bunker Returns to Mumbai on 22 November at Ballard Pier, With Rolling Loud India and Red Bull on Board appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Palworld Developer Gives Staff GTA 6 Holiday for 5 Days
items.content:
Pocketpair GTA 6 holiday plans are now official. The Palworld developer announced a special 5-day leave for all employees on November 12, 2026, so staff can play Grand Theft Auto 6 at launch. The post came from the official Palworld X account and framed the leave as a business trip to Vice City. GTA 6 releases on November 19, 2026, for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
Below, you will find the announcement details, the release date, and how other employers are handling launch day.
Pocketpair GTA 6 Holiday: What the Palworld Developer Announced
Pocketpair, the studio behind Palworld, gave all employees five days off to play GTA 6 next week. The studio shared the news through a social media post.
The post said every employee who plans to play GTA 6 at launch can use the special leave period. It described the time away as an “urgent five-day business trip in Vice City” and pointed staff to an attached notice for details.
All Pocketpair employees have been granted special leave to attend to an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City when GTA6 launches.
Please see the attached notice for details. pic.twitter.com/qJjJ7IvhhY
— Palworld (@Palworld_EN) November 12, 2026
GTA 6 Release Date and Platforms
Rockstar Games set the GTA 6 release date as Thursday, November 19, 2026. The game launches on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S.
The game was delayed by 6 months from its earlier May 26, 2026 date. Preloading started on November 10, 2026.
Pocketpair Has Done This Before
This is not the first time the studio has given staff time off for a big game. In February 2025, Pocketpair made Friday, February 28, a company-wide holiday for nearly everyone. That date matched the launch of Monster Hunter Wilds.
Pocketpair said many employees had reported they might feel unwell, so it gave an extra day off. Some departments were excluded. The studio did something similar in 2022 for Elden Ring.
Logitech Logi Game Day Offers a Day Off Too
Pocketpair is not the only company making a launch day move. On November 10, 2026, Logitech announced that all employees can take a company-approved day off tied to GTA 6, under a program called “Logi Game Day.”
Staff do not have to use the day on November 19. They can take it any time between that date and 2027. The offer covers more than 7,000 employees worldwide. Logitech will also host a streaming event in San Jose, California, on November 19.
How Many Workers Plan to Take a GTA 6 Day Off
Surveys show many workers want the day off. Some data says 18% of US salaried workers plan to take November 19 off. The figure rises to 32% for Gen Z and 27% for millennials.
According to reports, paid time off requests for November 19 were nearly 13% higher than on comparable dates in 2024 and 2025.
Research suggests about 2.1 million UK employees, or 7% of workers, expect to book the day off. Another UK report estimates the leave could cost the economy about £12 million.

items.title: Who Is Colette Kress? Nvidia’s New Interim Chief Executive
items.content:
Colette Kress became Nvidia’s interim chief executive on 12 November, after Jensen Huang resigned as president, chief executive and board member with immediate effect. Kress has been Nvidia’s chief financial officer since September 2013. She will hold both roles until the board names a permanent successor. Nvidia announced the change in a statement on its newsroom.
Before Nvidia, Kress spent years at Cisco and Microsoft
Kress spent about eight years in finance roles at Texas Instruments early in her career. She joined Microsoft in 1997 and became chief financial officer of its Server and Tools division in 2006. She moved to Cisco in 2010 as senior vice president and chief financial officer of its Business Technology and Operations Finance organisation.
Nvidia named Kress executive vice president and chief financial officer in September 2013, as its 2013 filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission shows. She holds a bachelor’s degree in finance from the University of Arizona. She also has an MBA from Southern Methodist University.
Kress has run Nvidia’s finances through its growth into one of the world’s most valuable companies. Forbes ranks her 32nd on its 2026 list of America’s richest self-made women. Her Nvidia shares were worth about $750m at the close on 11 November, down from more than $1bn at the stock’s peak in October.
Nvidia also named Harvey C. Jones, a former chief executive and executive chairman of Synopsys, as its first chair. Jones said the board has “full confidence in Colette and the leadership team”. Kress said Nvidia’s “strength has always come from its people”. The company says its operations, customer commitments and product roadmap will continue without interruption.
The board is searching for a permanent chief executive and will consider internal and external candidates. It has not given a timeline. Kress was among the possible successors in our look at who could replace Jensen Huang. Nvidia has not said whether she is a candidate for the permanent role.
Huang told staff about an extramarital affair on 8 November and the board opened an investigation. Then came Huang’s resignation after 33 years. The statement announcing the change does not mention the investigation. The board hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead it, and we have reported on the investigators. Nvidia has not said whether that review will continue or when it will end.
Nvidia reports its third-quarter results for fiscal 2027 on 17 November, the first set of results since the leadership change. The company says the date has not changed.
The post Who Is Colette Kress? Nvidia’s New Interim Chief Executive appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia CEO after 33 years
items.content:
If you've been following the Nvidia news closely this week, then today's update may not come as a surprise. After three decades as CEO, Jensen Huang is resigning from Nvidia. He will also no longer be a member of the company's Board of Directors.
The resignation takes effect immediately. Nvidia's Board of Directors has appointed Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as Interim CEO while the company conducts a search for a permanent successor. Kress will continue serving as CFO during the transition period. On top of that, Nvidia is appointing Harvey C. Jones as the company's Chair of the Board.
In a statement accompanying the announcement, Nvidia's new interim CEO emphasised that the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap will continue without interruption:
“NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years. We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.”
Regardless of who is ultimately chosen as Nvidia's next permanent CEO, the departure is one of the most significant leadership changes in the modern tech industry. Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and remained at the helm for the last 33 years. While Nvidia's announcement does not provide a reason for the leadership change, the departure follows a week of intense scrutiny surrounding Huang, including reports linking him to a potential spy scandal.
KitGuru says: This is indeed huge news, but it should also be said that Nvidia is far more than one person. Huang was the face of the company for many years, but there are a ton of hardworking engineers and programmers that were instrumental in building the company up to what it is today, and it's not like they are going anywhere.
The post Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia CEO after 33 years first appeared on KitGuru.

BLAST Rivals Season 2 2026: Day 2 Results & Highlights
items.content:
Following an action-packed Day 1, Day 2 of the BLAST Rivals Season 2 2026 has yielded the highly anticipated single-elimination playoffs. With the interesting format of BLAST Rivals, only two teams, namely Legacy and FUT, will be heading home as others prepare for the quarter-finals tomorrow.
Falcons eliminate Legacy
.@FalconsEsport secure their spot in the playoffs here in Hong Kong #BLASTPremier #MMarkEvents pic.twitter.com/Ew25qVlwGn
— BLAST Premier (@BLASTPremier) November 12, 2026
Starting with a 5-0 scoreline, the Falcons managed to set a dominant tone to the series early on before Legacy salvaged the half by taking 5 rounds, trailing by 2 rounds at the break. Winning the pistol, the second half saw Legacy manage to narrow down the lead before Falcons converted the lead. Winning on the weaker buy enabled them to hit double digits, leaving Legacy to play chase. Legacy’s poorly orchestrated offence failed to manage anything significant as they watched Falcons effortlessly close the opening map of the day.
Losing on Falcons’ map, Legacy failed to set a strong start on their own map pick of Mirage as their poor offensive display from the first map came back to haunt them. Falcons’ 9-round defensive performance gave them a solid lead to switch sides with confidence. With a big margin to their name, the Falcons dropped a few rounds but closed eventually, eliminating Legacy in the process with a 13-6 win as m0NESY dropped another chart-topping performance.
FURIA stun Vitality
A 13-0 TO SECURE THE SEMI-FINAL SPOT #BLASTPremier #MMarkEvents pic.twitter.com/G035kkZJmV
— BLAST Premier (@BLASTPremier) November 12, 2026
A statement start on FURIA’s map pick against Vitality enabled them to go 11-1 up as the Brazilian side looked helpless on their offence, having secured a single round. Switching sides, the FURIA defence pulled 4 rounds, but that barely helped, as winning two back-to-back rounds saw Vitality push the opening map over the line.
Following a tough loss, FURIA bounced back with a solid display of the CT side of their own. Winning 9 rounds saw them put Vitality on the back foot on their own map pick, leaving little room for a comeback before switching sides. FURIA hit 11 off the back of their pistol round conversion, upon which Vitality managed to pull in a few rounds before the map closed with a 13-10 scoreline in favour of the Brazilians as we headed to the deciding map.
Having recovered from a tough loss, FURIA went on a tear to hand Vitality their biggest defeat of the season with a 13-0 win. A perfectly played defence saw the first half close 12-0, upon which FURIA converted the pistol, shocking fans and rivals alike and completing the reverse sweep to reach the semis.
MOUZ edge out FUT
Kudos to @FUTesportsgg, but @mousesports were too strong on Nuke and secure their spot in the Quarter-Finals #BLASTPremier #MMarkEvents pic.twitter.com/ryXDMZDVtG
— BLAST Premier (@BLASTPremier) November 12, 2026
Starting the series on FUT’s comfort pick of Cache, MOUZ’s defence roped in enough rounds to take the lead before switching sides. Despite failing to keep up, FUT levelled the scoreline in the second half, taking the series to OT. With the first OT failing to separate both sides, FUT edged out a narrow 19-16 win in the second OT to take an early lead in the series.
MOUZ hit back on their own map pick as FUT continued to give a tough fight. Playing chase in the first half, MOUZ levelled the scoreline on their defence, taking us to the OT for the second time in the series. Unlike the opening map, FUT failed to deliver as MOUZ pulled ahead in this test of resilience as the map ended with a 16-14 scoreline.
With the series levelled, MOUZ brought their A game in the final map. Winning 11 rounds on the less favoured side of Nuke, FUT had little chance to even get going. While they did pull in 3 rounds in the second half, MOUZ closed the series with a 13-4 scoreline as they secured their place in the quarter-finals.
Spirit reverse sweep G2
A nice day off for @Team__Spirit who book their spot straight through to Semi-Final Saturday #BLASTPremier #MMarkEvents pic.twitter.com/2RV9HmqQuP
— BLAST Premier (@BLASTPremier) November 12, 2026
Opening on G2’s pick of Mirage, both teams traded rounds until Spirit secured a tight lead before switching sides. With G2 giving a tough fight on their offence, their defence is where they did the best work. With a dominant performance to kick off the series, they roped in 8 rounds to close their own map as Spirit barely reached double digits.
Spirit recovered on their own map pick with a dominant start on the offence. As they secured 8 rounds, G2 could barely keep up with 4 rounds before the end of the first half. G2 cut the lead in half, winning 2 rounds before Spirit hopped onto their streak, where they secured 6 rounds in a row to level the series and take us to the final map of the day.
Spirit’s 4-0 start was matched by a streak from G2. As the G2 offence continued to struggle, Spirit managed to edge out with a narrow 8-4 lead before the half closed. Despite converting their first buy, G2 managed to stay on the back foot as Spirit ran away with the match with a 4-round streak to close out the map and reach the semi-finals directly, as G2 will not progress beyond the quarter-finals.
Day 3 Schedule
Day 3 is set to take us further into the playoffs, with some of the favourites to win the tournament battling it out in this stage. While many teams will be keeping their strategy books away ahead of the Major, BLAST has a generous prize pool that might be enough to motivate these teams to give it their all and make the playoffs an action-packed affair.

items.content:
Jensen Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and turned a graphics-card maker for PC gamers into the company at the centre of the AI boom, is no longer its chief executive. On Thursday, 12 November, Nvidia announced that Huang has resigned as president, CEO and a member of the board, effective immediately. Chief financial officer Colette Kress takes over as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor.
The announcement ends a week in which the pressure on Huang kept building. It started with questions over his relationship with an executive whom US officials suspected of working for Chinese intelligence. Then came his own written admission to staff that he had been unfaithful to his wife, followed by fresh allegations about a second relationship, this time inside Nvidia. The board met on Wednesday night to decide his future, and the meeting ran into the evening. By Thursday morning in California, the most famous leather jacket in tech had left the building. Nvidia’s statement gives no reason for the departure, although the timing leaves little room for interpretation.
Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and ran it for 33 years. (Image: Nvidia)
From Spy Allegations to an Affair Admission: How Nvidia’s Board Lost Faith in Huang
The unravelling began in late October, when The New York Times reported that Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Singapore-based data-centre company Megaspeed. Megaspeed is an Nvidia customer, and it was already under investigation by US and Singaporean authorities over suspected chip-export violations. According to the Times, a US intelligence memo had alleged that she was working for China’s Ministry of State Security. Beijing has dismissed those claims as baseless, and Nvidia’s first response was that Huang’s interactions with her were “not unusual or unexpected” for a CEO who meets customers.
That line did not hold for long. On Sunday, 8 November, Huang wrote to employees admitting that he had been unfaithful to his wife of 40 years and apologising. The note named no one. On the same day, Nvidia’s board opened an independent investigation into whether he had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. It also said it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets had been compromised. Two days later, the independent directors brought in former acting US Attorney Joon H. Kim and his firm to run the review. Then, on Wednesday, the Times reported a second affair, citing current and former employees, this time with a senior Nvidia executive who reports directly to Huang. Neither Nvidia nor Huang has confirmed that report. Within hours, The Wall Street Journal reported that the board was preparing to remove him.
Washington was also closing in. Three House Republican committee chairmen, John Moolenaar, Brian Mast and Rick Crawford, had asked Huang for a closed-door briefing on his ties to Alice Huang. They also warned that a subpoena could follow if he did not respond. Meanwhile, Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons asked the administration to preserve Nvidia’s China-related records. President Donald Trump stood by Huang throughout, calling him “an honorable guy” and saying he should stay on. In the end, however, the decision belonged to Nvidia’s board, and Huang had little power to resist it. He owns roughly 3.6% of the company, so unlike founders at Meta or SpaceX, he had no majority voting control to fall back on.
Colette Kress Takes Over Five Days Before Nvidia’s Earnings
Colette Kress, Nvidia CFO since 2013, is now interim CEO. (Image: Nvidia)
Colette Kress has been Nvidia’s executive vice president and CFO since September 2013. Before that, she spent nearly 25 years in finance at Cisco, Microsoft and Texas Instruments. She keeps the CFO job alongside the top role. In Nvidia’s statement, she said she is committed to “building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years.” The board also named Harvey C. Jones, a former CEO and executive chairman of Synopsys, as the company’s first-ever chair. That is a telling change for a company that, until this week, had no board chair at all. According to Jones, the board has “full confidence in Colette and the leadership team” and expects operations, customer commitments and the product roadmap to carry on without interruption. The search for a permanent CEO will look at both internal and external candidates.
Kress will not get a quiet first week. Nvidia confirmed that it will still report third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Tuesday, 17 November, with the earnings call at 2 p.m. Pacific time, as originally scheduled. The market has already passed its verdict on the past week. Nvidia shares were trading around $158 in early US trading on Thursday, down roughly 9% on the day and about a third below their October record. At that price, Nvidia’s market value is below $4 trillion, and the slide is starting to look like the record $465 billion DeepSeek rout of January 2025. Bernstein had already downgraded the stock and halved its price target to $200 before the announcement, while Oppenheimer pointed to the risk of a brain drain once Huang left. Nvidia’s own annual report had long listed its reliance on key executives as a business risk. This week, that risk stopped being theoretical.
The GeForce Founder Leaves PC Gaming Without Its Biggest Showman
For gamers, Huang’s Nvidia was always GeForce before it was anything else. The company credits itself with inventing the GPU in 1999 with the GeForce 256. Under Huang, it went on to make real-time ray tracing and DLSS standard features of PC gaming. It also became a fixture of the competitive scene, from the tuning guides players use to squeeze more frames out of Counter-Strike 2 to team deals such as its partnership with Cloud9. Every big launch, including the RTX 5090, came with Huang on stage in his leather jacket, selling the hardware as much as the engineers built it. His GTC 2026 keynote in March was the latest example of that.
Highlights from Jensen Huang’s GTC 2026 keynote. (Video: NVIDIA)
Nothing changes for an RTX owner overnight. The board says the product roadmap stays on track, and drivers, DLSS updates and the GeForce line do not depend on one person’s diary. However, the balance inside the company had shifted long before this week. AI data centres now bring in the overwhelming share of Nvidia’s revenue, and the new interim chief is a finance executive rather than a product evangelist. Whoever the board eventually picks will decide how much attention GeForce gets in a company that no longer needs gamers to pay its bills. On Tuesday, for the first time since Nvidia listed on the stock market in 1999, the company will report its results with someone other than Jensen Huang as chief executive.
The post Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO After 33 Years; Colette Kress Named Interim Chief appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: Xbox Cloud Gaming Free Tier Is Live: Session Limits, Ads and Prices
items.content:
The Xbox Cloud Gaming free tier is now live for most players around the world. Xbox rolled out the ad-supported option on November 11, 2026, after testing it for several months. Players can stream select games from their library and some free-to-play titles without a Game Pass subscription. Each session starts with ads, and session time limits apply.
This article covers how the free tier works, the new Game Pass cloud limits, and Cloud Playtime prices.
Xbox Cloud Gaming Free Tier Rollout and Features
Xbox announced the free version of Xbox Cloud Gaming in July. At that stage, it was a test for Xbox Insiders. As of November 11, it has reached the vast majority of Xbox users.
The free tier lets players stream select games from their own library, along with select free-to-play games. Xbox has not said which games qualify. Players need to check the supported cloud library for the current list.
You now have more ways to stream and play your favorite games.
Purchase ad-free cloud playtime, get monthly cloud playtime with @XBOXGamePass, or stream your games for free with ad-supported cloud gaming.
Choose your way to play: https://t.co/60P9n1npR5 pic.twitter.com/Lh8phIKBEF
— XBOX (@XBOX) November 11, 2026
Xbox shared the details in a post on X. It said players can stream select games for free by watching ads before each gaming session. After a session ends, players can watch another set of ads to start a new one.
The ads appear before the session begins and seemingly not again during play. The outlet also says Xbox has been quiet about the launch so far.
A 30-minute slot will be provided to free Xbox Cloud Gaming players. After that time, the player is removed from the stream and has to start a new session.
Game Pass Cloud Playtime Limits and Prices
The free tier arrives alongside changes for Game Pass members. Xbox announced monthly cloud playtime limits for Game Pass in September. Those limits have now started to apply.
Under the new system, Game Pass tiers include these monthly cloud hours:
Game Pass Essential: 5 hours
Game Pass Premium: 10 hours
Game Pass Ultimate: 15 hours
Players who run out can buy Cloud Playtime to top up.
Xbox described the choices in its post. Players can buy ad-free cloud playtime, use the monthly cloud playtime that comes with Game Pass, or stream for free with ads.
GTA 6 and the Free Tier
The free tier could appeal to players who want to play GTA 6 on Xbox One through Xbox Cloud Gaming without paying. It adds a warning. Xbox has not confirmed whether GTA 6 will be one of the “select” games in the free tier.
Separate reports say GTA 6 will be playable through Xbox Cloud Gaming on Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S when it launches on November 19.
The post Xbox Cloud Gaming Free Tier Is Live: Session Limits, Ads and Prices appeared first on TalkEsport.

items.title: A New Dawn in the Cloud: ‘Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV’ Is Coming to GeForce NOW
items.content:
Rally the ranks this GFN Thursday. Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV is coming to GeForce NOW, allowing players to experience the battle for Kronus through cloud gaming.
There’s more on the horizon, with NVIDIA DLSS 5 technology coming to War Thunder and Where Winds Meet. Meanwhile, Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen brings new tales and encounters, alongside 10 games joining the GeForce NOW library this week.
Kronus Calls for Reinforcements
Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV, developed by KING Art Games and published by Deep Silver, is coming to GeForce NOW. Launching on Steam Thursday, Dec. 3, the real-time strategy game returns to the series’ roots with large-scale battles, base building and a renewed fight for planet Kronus.
Command the Space Marines, Orks, Necrons or the Adeptus Mechanicus, which makes their series debut. Build a base, secure resources and customize squads to the conflict across more than 70 campaign missions, playable solo or in co-op mode. The Last Stand, Skirmish and multiplayer modes offer more ways to put tactics to the test.
GeForce NOW will bring the action to supported PCs, Macs, handhelds and other devices, with game downloads and updates handled in the cloud. Save the storage space for everyday essentials and planning for the next offensive. Wishlist the game on Steam, and stay tuned to GFN Thursday to prepare for launch.
DLSS 5 Keeps on Coming
NVIDIA DLSS 5 continues to evolve, with Gaijin Entertainment’s War Thunder and Everstone Studio’s Where Winds Meet next to receive support for the technology with the 3D-Guided Neural Rendering feature.
Arriving in mid-November, War Thunder’s Eagle’s Shadow major update adds DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, dozens of new planes, ships and tanks, along with cluster bombs for planes and visual-effects enhancements increasing the realism and dynamism of battle.
In Where Winds Meet, DLSS support arrives Monday, Nov. 23, enhancing the environments and characters of its wuxia open-world action role-playing game.
Both titles will use the latest DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering model, released in October, which doubles model performance compared with the previous version. Since its initial announcement in March, model performance has improved tenfold, bringing the technology to more gamers, including GeForce NOW Ultimate members streaming with GeForce RTX 5080 cloud rigs.
Get a closer look at the DLSS updates and find more details.
A New Tale for the Arisen
Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen is streaming on GeForce NOW, expanding the deep, explorable fantasy world of Dragon’s Dogma 2 with new tales and encounters. Travel to the long-abandoned region of Norgan, join the enigmatic Eir and uncover the secrets of the undying Fallen Dragon.
Unearth forgotten relics to unlock powerful weapons and skills, take on Lost Rites’ 12 dungeon challenges and explore new hairstyles and tattoos for Arisen and Pawn customization.
Delicious in Dungeon also arrives in the world of Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen with a special collaboration.
GeForce NOW keeps all the new downloadable content available across supported devices — without a single download claiming local storage on a gamer’s hardware of choice.
In addition, members can look for the following games joining the GeForce NOW library this week:
Worst Class Ever (New release on Steam, Nov. 9)
Ashes of the Singularity II (New release on Steam, Nov. 10)
Cyberpunk 2077 (Xbox Play Anywhere, new release on Battle.net, Nov. 10)
DreamWorks Shrek 2 Remastered (New release on Steam, Nov. 10)
Warhammer Survivors (New release on Steam and Xbox, available on Game Pass, Nov. 10)
Main Sequence (New release on Steam, Nov. 12)
Deadly Days: Roadtrip (Steam)
GeForce 8800 GTX – 20 Years of a Legend (Steam, Ultimate members)
Graveyard Keeper (Steam)
Tape to Tape (Steam)
Also this week, Ultimate members can take a trip back to 2006 with GeForce 8800 GTX – 20 Years of a Legend, a playable demo celebrating the iconic GPU’s 20th anniversary with DLSS 4.5 and path tracing in the cloud.
Dates listed above reflect when games are released on their respective stores. GeForce NOW availability may vary, as games are onboarded after release and added throughout the week. Keep an eye on GeForce NOW channels and GFN Thursdays for availability updates on announced titles.
Those ready to put the next game plan into action can grab a day pass to try Performance or Ultimate, with the cost applicable toward a first monthly membership.
What’s on the gaming lineup this weekend? Let us know on X or in the comments below.

items.title: Corsair H1000i Shift Crystal (2026) PSU Review
items.content:
Today we take a look at one of Corsair’s more unusual power supplies, the HX1000i Shift Crystal. This 1000W unit features transparent panels on three sides, giving a clear view of the components inside. It combines the side-mounted modular connectors of the HXi Shift range with a 140mm RGB fan, individually sleeved cables and Cybenetics Platinum efficiency certification. Corsair also introduce their configurable PinProtect+ protection system for the 12V-2×6 connection.
The transparent chassis is clearly the main visual attraction, although how much of it you will actually see will depend on your choice of case. Corsair have carried the styling through to the internals, with white circuit boards and matching Corsair-branded capacitors. The cooling fan uses a magnetic dome bearing and supports Zero RPM operation, with lighting and fan settings accessible through iCUE.
Like the existing HXi Shift models, the Crystal incorporates an iCUE LINK System Hub, supporting up to 24 devices across two channels. PinProtect+ adds individual pin current monitoring for the native 12V-2×6 connection, with adjustable protection thresholds and activation delays available through the software. We will take a closer look at this later in the review.
Corsair back the HX1000i Shift Crystal with a ten-year warranty and quote a UK price of £249.99. We will be putting it through our usual tests to find out how well it performs and whether it justifies the asking price.
Key Features:
PinProtect+: Adjustable per-pin overcurrent protection (OCP) for the 12V-2×6 connection. It monitors and displays the current flowing through each pin in iCUE. If the current exceeds a user-defined threshold for an extended period, PinProtect+ reduces power to allow the GPU to shut down, helping prevent potential damage.
Transparent Chassis: Fully transparent on three sides, offering a unique look that showcases the high-quality components behind the unit’s excellent electrical performance and reliable power delivery.
Integrated iCUE LINK System Hub: A built-in iCUE LINK System Hub makes it easy to configure an iCUE LINK cooling system without requiring a six-pin PCIe power cable. The integrated System Hub features two channels for easy device daisy-chaining, enabling intuitive control and synchronization of up to 24 iCUE LINK components through iCUE software.
Fully Modular Individually Sleeved Cables: Premium cables and a fully modular design mean you only connect the cables your system needs, giving your build a clean, professional look.
3D Y-Pattern Fan Grille: Inspired by the FRAME Series cases, the fan grille features a three-dimensional perforated design rather than a flat surface, creating a less restrictive airflow path for improved cooling, lower temperatures, and reduced noise.
Dual EPS12V Connectors: Provides full compatibility with modern motherboards and high-end CPUs.
140mm Magnetic Dome Bearing RGB Fan: Delivers exceptionally quiet, long-lasting fan performance with vibrant, customizable RGB lighting.
Powerful CORSAIR iCUE Software: Create custom fan curves, monitor power settings, and toggle between single- and multi-rail overcurrent protection (OCP) on-the-fly.
Zero RPM Mode: At low to medium loads, the cooling fan switches off entirely for near-silent operation.
Cybenetics Platinum Certified: Up to 91% overall efficiency for low power consumption and cooler temperatures.
CORSAIR Custom 105°C Electrolytic Capacitors: Premium internal components ensure efficient power delivery and long-term reliability.
Fully Digital Platform: Resonant LLC topology and DC-to-DC conversion provide clean, consistent power and minimizes coil whine and noise for quiet operation.
Ten-Year Warranty: Your guarantee of reliable operation that will last across several system builds.
The post Corsair H1000i Shift Crystal (2026) PSU Review first appeared on KitGuru.
