items.title: Poison Ivy wins first CoD Mobile Garena Battle Royale Cup
items.content:
Poison Ivy were crowned the champions of the inaugural Call of Duty: Mobile – Garena Battle Royale Cup in front of their home crowd in Manila, Philippines. This follows their dominant Playoffs run, with the team looking forward to truly global competitions.
CODM – GBRC and the future of CODM esports
The Call of Duty: Mobile – Garena Battle Royale Cup (CODM – GBRC) is the first major LAN event dedicated to the Battle Royale aspect of CODM. It began with the Qualifier Stage on Sept. 26 and brought the top 10 teams to the offline Grand Finals last Nov. 7-8.
Teams from the Philippines, Thailand, Taiwan and Hong Kong, and Indonesia made it to the Grand Finals.
Image credit: esports.gg
For 2027, Garena announced the Rookie Circuit for both Battle Royale and Multiplayer competitors. This is a new, open circuit which runs four times a year and allows players the chance to participate in the highest form of competition: The global World Championship for Multiplayer, and the regional Garena Battle Royale Cup for BR.
Image credit: Garena
Poison Ivy are your first CODM-GBRC champions!
The grand finals were played across two days and implemented the new Endgame Protocol. In it, the winning point threshold is set to the points of the leading team after Day 1, plus 10.
Image credit: esports.gg
Since Poison Ivy ended Map 6, Day 1 at 106 points, the winning threshold was set at 116 points.
Trailing behind them were GNR Esports at 99 points and ADMT Pyrite with 82.
As Day 2 rolled by, Poison Ivy were the first to reach the threshold, and they did so on Map 7 of the tournament. They secured the map and tournament win on Map 8 as they triumphed over GNR Esports when they were left as the last two squads in the final circle.
Image credit: Garena
Poison Ivy lifted the trophy with 132 points and two map wins. SecreGIZY was awarded the Finals MVP after securing the most eliminations in the title-deciding map. He was awarded with 30,000 CP.
Poison Ivy at the CODM GBRC 2026 (Image credit: Garena)
He attributed their consistent dominance to discipline. “We practice almost every day, with scrims and tournaments, and we don’t let anything slide. We stay locked in for almost every game.”
Meanwhile, VrusGIZY is eager for more competitions and an international championship. “I think the next step for us is to compete in tournaments against teams from around the world. We’re ready to give it our all and win an international championship.”
The competitive CODM Battle Royale will resume with the Rookie Circuit in 2027.

Best competitive loadout in Modern Warfare 4 – Hardpoint and Search & Destroy
items.content:
A new Call of Duty means the competitive scene is completely wiped clean, and players can start totally fresh. Modern Warfare 4 introduces an entirely new set of rules, maps, weapons, and restrictions that players must follow if they want to play competitively. While some of what you use in public matches can carry over into competitive, you’ll need a specific loadout if you want to succeed at the highest level in Modern Warfare 4.
Fortunately, we have assembled the best pro-ready loadout for competitive play in MW4, and it comes with the weapons, attachments, perks, and equipment you’ll need on each of your classes. You can see everything you need for your competitive loadouts for both primary game modes, Hardpoint and Search & Destroy, in the guide below.
Key Takeaways
A competitive loadout in MW4 will differ drastically from ones for public matches, as competitive comes with its own rules and restrictions
Two meta weapons dominate competitive, but there are specific attachments required for both weapons
The set of perks and equipment for a competitive loadout is already pre-determined based on the restrictions that professional players follow
Table of contents
Key Takeaways
Best competitive loadout for Hardpoint in Modern Warfare 4
Best competitive loadout for Search & Destroy in Modern Warfare 4
Best competitive loadout for Hardpoint in Modern Warfare 4
We’ll begin with your loadout for Hardpoint in Modern Warfare 4, as it’s the main respawn game mode that you’ll play in competitive. While there’s also Hijack, the new third game mode in the Call of Duty League, the loadout for Hardpoint will transfer over to that mode as well.
The two current weapons that have ascended to the meta in competitive play are the HAN 86 assault rifle and the VEL-46 submachine gun. While updates and GAs could change the weapon meta, this is what has stuck in the early going of MW4. Pros have also defaulted to using the Sang 9mm pistol as the lone secondary weapon option, and that likely won’t change anytime soon.
Screenshot by esports.gg
Below, you can see the best attachments for both the HAN 86 and the VEL-46, as well as the rest of the recommended loadout for Hardpoint:
HAN 86 loadout
Optic: ZLR Type C
Muzzle: FTAC Dominion
Underbarrel: FSS Fireline Grip
Stock: Meiko L9P-Fold
Ammunition: 5.56 NATO High Velocity
VEL-46 loadout
Barrel: VB-46 Series 11
Muzzle: TA TacPro-56
Underbarrel: FSS Fireline Grip
Stock: VEL 46 Extended
Rear Grip: LM Combat Grip
Secondary Weapon
Sang 9mm
Perks
Perk 1: Kill Chain
Perk 2: Ninja
Perk 3: Battle Hardened
Equipment
Lethal: Frag Grenade / Semtex Grenade
Tactical: Concussion Grenade
Field Upgrade
Trophy System
For the perks, the Perk 1 slot is currently unbalanced for competitive play, as there are no true viable options. Hopefully, developer Infinity Ward issues a fix in the near future and rebalances the perks, but for right now, your only option is Kill Chain, which does virtually nothing in Hardpoint. As for the rest of the loadout, everything else is pretty much set in stone except for your choice of lethal equipment.
Screenshot by esports.gg
Best competitive loadout for Search & Destroy in Modern Warfare 4
Moving on, now we have your loadout for Search & Destroy, and it stays mostly the same for Hardpoint with perhaps one major change. The HAN 86 and VEL-46 are still the favorite weapons, the perks don’t change, and you still use the Trophy System. However, you have more freedom in your equipment, as you can see below:
HAN 86 loadout
Optic: ZLR Type C
Muzzle: FTAC Dominion
Underbarrel: FSS Fireline Grip
Stock: Meiko L9P-Fold
Ammunition: 5.56 NATO High Velocity
VEL-46 loadout
Barrel: VB-46 Series 11
Muzzle: TA TacPro-56
Underbarrel: FSS Fireline Grip
Stock: VEL 46 Extended
Rear Grip: LM Combat Grip
Secondary Weapon
Sang 9mm
Perks
Perk 1: Kill Chain
Perk 2: Ninja
Perk 3: Battle Hardened
Equipment
Lethal: Frag Grenade / Semtex Grenade
Tactical: Concussion Grenade / Smoke Grenade
Field Upgrade
Trophy System
Search & Destroy allows you to make use of the revamped Smoke Grenade in Modern Warfare 4, which can be a great help to cross the map safely or get out of trouble quickly. But everything else on the loadout remains the same from Hardpoint.
And there you have it, that’s both competitive loadouts for Hardpoint and Search & Destroy in Modern Warfare 4. Things are fairly stagnant in terms of the loadout items right now, but that could change once the Season 1 update in MW4 is released in November.

items.title: Football Manager 27 Out Now with Game Pass: Discover 5 Unmissable Additions
items.content:
Summary
FM27 and FM27 Console deliver greater control over your tactical vision and a deeper football world to explore.
Discover some of the new additions that turn your footballing vision into reality.
FM27 is out now for XBOX on PC and FM27 Console is out now for XBOX Series X|S. Both are available with Game Pass.
It’s time for you to start making this season’s big calls, with FM27 and FM27 Console out now, including with Game Pass.
FM27 delivers greater control over your tactical vision and a deeper football world to explore from the moment your career begins. In FM27 Console, meanwhile, a host of new additions, refinements and returning favourites are waiting for you to discover them.
This year’s new additions come together to turn your footballing vision into reality. So, here are five for you to make the most of from day one in the hotseat.
Tactical Tweaks
In FM27 and FM27 Console, you’ll exert a new level of influence from the touchline with the introduction of Tactical Tweaks.
Inspired by conversations with contacts in professional football, this system allows you to make quick play style adjustments at a team and individual level without needing to dive into the Tactics menu.
So, if you want to exploit the width to target a weakness in the opposition defence, throw the kitchen sink to chase a late winner, or shut up shop to secure a memorable cup upset, you’re now better empowered to react to the action unfolding in front of you.
Box Attacking Instructions
You’ve also got more tactical tools at your disposal to play to your attackers’ strengths.
New Player Instructions allow you to command your stars on how you want them to attack the box. You’ve got the choice of asking a player to arrive late in the box, or directly attack the defensive line. In addition, you can then vary where they attack, whether it’s near post, far post or central areas.
Combined with new movement animations and a reworking of how players run in matches, the power is in your hands to create new ways to overload the opposition.
Time-of-Day Match System
No matter the tactical style you implement, a 3pm kick-off on a Saturday in December should feel distinct from one kicking off at the same time in the middle of August.
Now, thanks to a new time-of-day system, you’ll get to experience the sun setting over your players, all while the lighting, shadows, and weather, dynamically shift throughout the course of the 90 minutes. It’s a visual cue that mirrors the action playing out on the pitch, making every match feel like a real-life event.
More authentic playing conditions set the tone for the thrill of match day and these lighting changes are enhanced by deeper visual upgrades to stadiums, environments, and crowds.
Tactical Effectiveness and Match Preparation
Underpinning your Match Day preparations in FM27 is the brand-new Tactical Effectiveness system.
Connecting your training schedules with your unique footballing philosophy, this system gauges how effectively your players can carry out your approach based on their ability, their buy-in to you as manager, their tactical understanding and offers information on the next opponents.
Tactical Effectiveness will inform your choices across the game. From guiding your focuses for next week’s sessions on the training ground to helping you make decisions on which of your targets is the best fit for your title-challengers, every decision is now more informed.
In FM27 Console, Match Preparation messages make their debut to help you get the most out of your team ahead of kick-off.
You can build out Match Preparation with up to 3 unique sessions, covering In Possession, Out of Possession, and Set Pieces. This gives you greater control over your team’s readiness and helps ensure no detail is overlooked as you look ahead to the next fixture. Whether you’re fine-tuning your tactics for a pre-season friendly or preparing for a FIFA World Cup knockout clash, the decisions are yours to make. Get your preparations right, give your team the best possible platform, and let your management do the talking on the pitch.
Introducing Shuffle Draft
Giving you a new way to play and create moments that’ll linger long after the final whistle, Shuffle Draft debuts in FM27 and FM27 Console.
Putting managerial strategy at the heart of the action, Shuffle Draft offers both league and knockout formats for 2-32 players and is available in public and private lobbies as well as offline against the AI.
Each manager picks a player from a set of 20 players, derived from a player pool you’ve selected, and that set is then passed on to the next manager in the following round, and so on. This allows draft picks to happen simultaneously, so there’s no more waiting around for the spotlight to come back to you.
Fast paced and packed with variety, Shuffle Draft challenges you to assemble different squads, experiment with your tactical approach, and outsmart your opponents – be they friends, family or online rivals.

The Outer Worlds 2’s first DLC arrives December 2
items.content:
The time has come to expand on the experience for The Outer Worlds 2 with the first of a two-part story expansion, Side Effects Guaranteed, arriving on December 2. After a distress signal from a derelict ship is picked up, you and your crew quickly get embroiled into the story of an abandoned settlement, a power struggle for the future of the Sub Rosa criminal organization, and the fate of a team who has been subjected to something that will cause them all to die from explosive cell death. Really, it’s more a liquefaction than explosion, but it means death nonetheless.
Play Video
A brand new story filled with moral quandaries and consequences big and small isn’t the only thing you’ll experience in the first DLC. An Earth Directorate Commander should always be sure to have a weapon at their side, and there are five new weapons to add to the arsenal. Such as the Immobilizer. Think of it like a gun that makes gravity forget to exist around its target, allowing them to float in the air, so you can switch to another weapon and pick them off as you like. Great for combining with grenades for anti-gravity explosions or the Tactical Time Dilation device for slowing down time and getting some critical shots in.
There is also the 1/6 Resolver that allows every sixth bullet that is fired from it to pack an extra special punch. For those who built their characters just right, they won’t have to empty the gun every time to get that critical hit, either. Other weapons include a weapon that does additional damage to creatures, a special Tossball Stick, and a new plasma weapon for some energy fun.
Yet it isn’t all about the weapons. Side Effects Guaranteed will also bring with it a level cap increase up to 36, new perks, new flaws, and a new Sub Rosa radio station with 20 new songs. There is also the all-new region of Elysium Valley to explore with unique quests and new facilities to make your way through. That’s a lot of new!
While the events of the DLC do trigger right before the point of no return in the main game, there is also a way to jump easily into the action. From the main menu if you start a new game, you will see an option to start Side Effects Guaranteed directly. This will load a pre-made character at level 27 that you can assign skill points and perks to so you can experience the DLC however you’d like and get started right away.
Not happy with the character you made (or the one you already have)? Coming to everyone at the same time as the release of Side Effects Guaranteed is a new update that will allow players to respec their character at any time. And for those who want more skills to play around with, a new addition to the custom game options allows you to adjust how many skill points you get per level. Find the balance that is right for you. Or become an Earth Director demi-god. Your worlds, your way.
But remember, however you decide to deal with Sub Rosa or the subjects of Elysium Valley will have consequences. Side effects, some might say, that will lead directly into the next installment of The Outer Worlds 2 two-part story expansion when it releases in the spring of 2027. Until then, may skill catch you where fortune fails. Side Effects Guaranteed releases on December 2nd or is available in the Premium Edition or Premium Edition Upgrade for The Outer Worlds 2.

items.title: How To Get A Sleeping Bag In World Of Warcraft: Forever
KitGuru Games: NBA 2K27 wasn’t hurt by GTA 6, it was hurt by years of bad decisions
items.content:
Take-Two says NBA 2K27 fell short of expectations despite selling more than 4 million copies and delivering the second-highest net bookings performance in franchise history. After spending thousands of hours with the NBA 2K series over the years, I find it difficult to believe GTA 6 is the reason why.
During Take-Two's latest earnings report, the publisher revealed that NBA 2K27 had underperformed relative to expectations. That is a remarkable statement considering the game has already sold more than 4 million copies and reportedly delivered the second-best bookings result in franchise history. At the same time, Take-Two is claiming that Grand Theft Auto 6 pre-orders are tracking “far above” expectations.
The easy narrative is that GTA 6 is soaking up all of the attention. The problem is that the timing doesn't really make sense. NBA 2K27 launched in late August and early September, depending on which edition players purchased, with GTA 6 close to 12 weeks away at the time. Most players deciding whether or not to buy NBA 2K27 months ago weren't choosing between a basketball game and Rockstar's next blockbuster release.
A more convincing explanation can be found by simply talking to NBA 2K players. For years now, Take-Two and Visual Concepts have ratcheted up the importance of Virtual Currency, better known as VC. In NBA 2K27, it now costs around 375,000 VC to fully upgrade a MyPlayer to a 99 overall rating. Earning that amount through gameplay alone requires a huge time investment. A typical Rec game lasts around 20 minutes and pays roughly 1,000 VC for a win, while losses pay significantly less. Given the game's heavy reliance on skill-based matchmaking, most players aren't maintaining dominant win rates. Realistically, earning enough VC to max out a build without spending money can take hundreds of hours. The grind has become so extreme that most dedicated players don't even consider earning enough VC naturally to be a realistic option.
The build system has become another source of frustration. Building a competitive character now requires more planning than ever thanks to cap breakers, attribute thresholds and seasonal content. Earlier this year, Take-Two issued cease and desist notices against community tools that helped players better understand the game's builder system. In one letter, the company argued that these tools allowed players to “learn the inner workings of the NBA 2K games without expending the time in trial and error that other players must invest”, adding that such shortcuts were “plainly unfair” and harmful to the player experience.
That argument becomes much harder to accept when a single 99-rated build now has such a high cost attached to it. Players willing to grind everything out can spend hundreds of hours earning that currency through gameplay. Most don't. Instead, they buy VC packs, with enough VC for a fully upgraded build costing roughly £80. In other words, creating a single fully upgraded player can require an investment greater than the cost of the game itself. In that environment, I don't see build-planning tools as an ‘unfair advantage', I see it as the community helping themselves avoid highly expensive mistakes.
If anything, those tools arguably encouraged experimentation. Making a second or third build is exactly what Take-Two wants players to do, but players are understandably reluctant to start over when each build can represent either hundreds of hours of gameplay or another £80 investment.
Then there are the long-running concerns around competitive integrity. Devices such as Cronus Zen remain a frequent complaint within the community, with many players arguing that scripted inputs and automated shot timing continue to undermine the online experience. Meanwhile, 2K continues to introduce new monetisation systems, including seasonal GOAT builds that offer combinations of ratings unavailable through the standard player builder. Miss a season, and some of those builds disappear along with it.
None of this means GTA 6 isn't a factor. It is unquestionably the biggest entertainment launch of the decade. But when a game can become one of the most successful NBA 2K launches ever and still miss internal expectations, perhaps it is time to look beyond GTA 6 and consider the frustrations NBA 2K players have spent years talking about.
KitGuru says: If you've played NBA 2K27, what do you think is hurting the series more right now – monetisation, progression systems or competitive integrity?

items.title: Side Effects Guaranteed in the First DLC For The Outer Worlds 2, Coming December 2
items.content:
A distress signal beckons you and your crew of the Incognito to a derelict ship, where you discover the ship’s crew in suspended animation. All signs point to foul play, especially the puddle of what was most likely a person. You recover a video message left by the captain of the vessel, who explains that the crew has been contaminated with something while on a heist that will cause explosive cell death unless they find a cure. And by explosive cell death, she means more like a… “liquefaction”.
By the looks of the puddle on the floor: liquefaction indeed.
The stakes are set for the release of the first of a two-part narrative DLC expansion of The Outer Worlds 2 on December 2. In Side Effects Guaranteed, the video message you found leads you to Gordon Hazen, one of the leading agents in Sub Rosa, a criminal organization made up of like-minded individuals who have chosen to live their lives stealing from the various factions instead of working for them. Gordon in turn sends you to Elysium Valley, a new region on Eden that is home to a settlement of former Protectorate subjects that have been forgotten by their Protectorate leaders. He believes they may have the answers to saving his crew. He personally favors diplomacy over violence but needs you to do whatever you need to in order to get the information he needs.
But Gordon isn’t the only one with interest in Elysium Valley. Another Sub Rosa agent, Algernon Lankester, wants to recruit you to help him exploit the subjects for his own personal gain. The fate of the subjects, the frozen Sub Rosa agents, and the future of Sub Rosa itself is up for you, our intrepid Commander, to decide.
A new narrative story is not all that will be coming when Side Effects Guaranteed launches in a few weeks, however.
Along with the new region of Elysium Valley to explore, players will encounter new threats like vicious canids and primal sprats. What’s a primal sprat? Just a normal sprat, but about 100 times the size. Surely, they’re just as friendly and forgiving of all the time you “accidentally” shot their much smaller cousins while exploring Arcadia.
With these new threats comes the ability to make your Commander even stronger and, of course, more flawed (but in a good way). The level cap will increase from 30 to 36, bringing more skill points to broaden your build. Being able to go to level 36 also means there are three more perks you can acquire, with 15 brand new perks being added into the mix.
Four new flaws will also be introduced that can change how your Commander plays, like “Lethally Tolerant,” a flaw that recognizes your built-up resistance to chemicals so your max toxicity will increase. This is great in the moment, but if you ever experience a Toxicity Crash, you will die instantly. Another example is “Must Have Been the Wind,” which will mark an “assassination target” for a combat group. Killing the target will grant a 20% damage and speed buff until the combat ends, but failing to do so or attacking someone who isn’t the target applies a 10% damage and speed debuff to the player for 30 seconds. Truly rewards that come with great risks.
Side Effects Guaranteed will also see new weapons, new armors, and new outfits for each of the companions, as well as a brand-new Sub Rosa-run radio station featuring 20 new songs for the game. For those who want to jump straight to the action in the DLC, a new alternate starting point is being added to the main menu when you choose a new game that will allow you to start with a custom save that lands you at the start of the DLC. Start the game, allot your skill and perk points, and enjoy Side Effects Guaranteed right away!
This jam-packed adventure with a deep story and systems to build your ideal commander will set up the next DLC for The Outer Worlds 2 that will be coming in Spring of 2027, and choices made will directly impact the next DLC. Part one of this overarching expansion story, Side Effects Guaranteed, will release on December 2 for $14.99, or is available in the Premium Edition or Premium Edition Upgrade for The Outer Worlds 2.

Time to clear your calendar – get ready for an action-packed adventure with a new crew, new weapons, and new enemies in a new colony! So much newness!
As a daring and most likely good-looking Earth Directorate agent, you must uncover the source of devastating rifts threatening to destroy all of humanity. Your investigation leads to Arcadia, home of skip drive technology, where the fate of the colony, and ultimately the entire galaxy, rests on your decisions – your strengths, your flaws, your crew, and the factions you choose to trust.
Explore a New Frontier
The Arcadia colony is engulfed in a factional war, as the Protectorate’s so-called benevolent rule is challenged by the rebellion of their religious order and a corporate invasion. As destructive rifts spread across the colony, each faction fights to control or close them for their own ends. Navigate diverse zones, uncover hidden lore, and shape the fate of a system on the brink!
Your Commander, Your Way
Build your character with the abilities and choices that reflect your playstyle. The colony reacts to your every move, crafting a narrative that’s yours to own -whether you’re a disciple of diplomacy, an astute strategist, a crusader for chaos, or something different altogether. And yes, you can dumb!
Enlist Your Companions
Recruit companions with unique traits, backgrounds and goals. Whether you choose to help them achieve their ambitions or steer them toward your own objectives, your influence shapes their growth (or death), making them an integral part of the immersive story you create together.

items.title: Nacon’s new Revo controllers bring Hall Effect sticks to the budget market
items.content:
Nacon has launched its new Revo controller lineup for Xbox and PC, bringing Hall Effect sticks and triggers to gamepads ranging from entry-level models through to more enthusiast-focused offerings.
Hall Effect technology has become one of the most sought-after features in modern controllers thanks to its potential to reduce stick drift issues. With the new Revo family, Nacon is building the technology into its latest Xbox and PC gamepads while targeting multiple price points.
The entry-level Revo model features Hall Effect joysticks and triggers alongside an asymmetrical layout. Buyers can choose between the standard Revo for PC and Smart TVs or the Revo X, which adds support for Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One and PC. Depending on the model, users also gain access to either dual or quad vibration motors.
The Revo Max builds on the standard design with adjustable stick tension, micro-switch buttons and D-pad controls, instant triggers and two programmable rear buttons. Nacon is also including a dedicated “Shooter Pro” mode aimed at eliminating stick dead zones. Like the base model, the Revo Max is available in both PC and Xbox variants.
Pricing starts at £24.90 for the PC-focused Revo controller, rising to £39.90 for the Xbox-compatible Revo X. The more feature-rich Revo PC Max and Revo X Max are priced at £49.90 and £59.90 respectively. Nacon also confirmed that a Revo Pro controller will join the lineup in 2027.
KitGuru says: Hall Effect sensors are quickly becoming a must-have feature for many gamers. Would you spend extra for Hall Effect sticks, or are traditional analogue sticks still good enough for you?

Microsoft explores paying users for idle GPU compute
items.content:
Microsoft has published a patent application describing a system that would allow users to volunteer idle gaming PCs and laptops for AI training in exchange for rewards.
Published on the 5th of November 2026, the patent (via PCGH) titled “Opportunistic Micro-training on Edge Devices Using Spare GPU Utilization” outlines a platform that splits large AI workloads into independent subtasks. Microsoft explains that the system monitors end devices to detect spare capacity, matching task sizes to metrics such as GPU utilisation, graphics memory, operating temperatures and power consumption.
Image credit: US Patent Office
To verify output accuracy, identical calculations can be sent to multiple systems to catch erroneous or manipulated data before being combined. Safety limits are also designed to scale back compute loads or restrict VRAM usage if a machine heats up or launches demanding software like a game. Participation would be entirely voluntary, with Microsoft noting potential incentives could include direct financial compensation, software access or account credits.
As is often the case with patent filings, there is no guarantee that Microsoft intends to turn the concept into a commercial product. The filing also does not detail exact payout figures or how rewards would be calculated.
Running AI workloads on a gaming graphics card would place additional load on the hardware, and on your electricity meter, so the economics of this system would largely depend on the reward structure. Personal data management and practical real-world testing also remain unaddressed in the document.
KitGuru says: Monetising your system while you sleep sounds neat, but would the rewards be enough to justify the extra power consumption? Would you volunteer your idle GPU cycles for AI training?

items.title: NZXT refreshes H7, H5 and Kraken lineup with curved glass and Asetek cooling
items.content:
NZXT has refreshed some of its most popular PC hardware lines, introducing redesigned H7 and H5 cases alongside a new Kraken liquid cooling lineup. The launch brings single-piece curved glass panels to both case families, while the new Kraken coolers adopt Asetek pumps throughout the range.
The biggest change to the H7 and H5 is the introduction of single-piece curved tempered glass panels spanning the front and side of the chassis, removing the corner pillar typically found on dual-panel showcase / fishtank style cases. NZXT is also introducing its new Vista Mode design on select models, extending the glass-covered look to the top of the case for a more uninterrupted view of internal components. The larger H7 adds a swappable top panel design, allowing users to switch between a glass top panel, or a perforated top panel for more airflow.
NZXT has also updated its Kraken cooler lineup with the new Kraken Plus 360 RGB and Kraken Core series, with both product families now using Asetek pumps. The Kraken Plus includes a 1.8-inch customisable display, while the Kraken Core strips things back with a simpler screen-free design. Across the range, NZXT is also continuing its push towards single-frame fan designs, combining three fans into a single frame to help reduce cable clutter.
Alongside the cases and coolers, NZXT also announced new F360Q and F420Q Quiet Airflow fans, a C1200 Platinum ATX 3.1 power supply and a PCIe 5.0 vertical GPU mounting kit. The new hardware begins rolling out through retailers globally starting today, with H5 pricing starting at €89.90, H7 models starting at €169.90 and Kraken coolers starting at €79.99.

items.title: NVIDIA Expands Open Source Commitment With OpenShell Donation and New AI Infrastructure
items.content:
Kubernetes, the open source system that manages how applications run across thousands of AI factories, has become the foundation for AI, and the demands on it are only growing.
To help meet them, NVIDIA is deepening its commitment to open source at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon, the flagship conference for the Kubernetes and cloud-native communities.
NVIDIA is contributing NVIDIA OpenShell, an open source runtime for securing and governing autonomous agents, to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), a nonprofit that is part of the Linux Foundation and the host of KubeCon. As a CNCF Sandbox project, OpenShell will be governed by the organizations building it into their products and strengthened by the expertise of security professionals worldwide.
NVIDIA is also contributing to Agent Substrate, an open source Google-led framework for operating long-running agent workloads at scale on Kubernetes that has been accepted into the CNCF Sandbox.
Additionally, NVIDIA announced new components of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform: NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine, NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes and NVIDIA Snapshot. These tools help teams deploy, manage and scale GPU infrastructure on Kubernetes for AI factories.
Together, these advancements mark a step forward in making Kubernetes the leading foundation for AI workloads at scale — empowering developers to build safer, more efficient AI infrastructure for the future.
Securing AI Agents in the Open
NVIDIA’s contribution of OpenShell to CNCF puts security infrastructure for autonomous agents in the community’s hands to build, inspect and improve — accelerating development and hardening its safeguards.
“The cloud-native community has a new infrastructure challenge: giving agents secure environments in which to operate,” said Jim Zemlin, CEO of the Linux Foundation. “NVIDIA’s contribution of OpenShell to CNCF gives developers a shared foundation to build on and an opportunity to shape how agent security evolves. Bringing this work into the community enables broader collaboration on infrastructure that will be critical to the next generation of cloud-native applications.”
OpenShell gives organizations control over what AI agents can do. It applies deterministic controls to agent activity, so teams can enforce policies as agents use tools, access inference services and execute workloads. Its extensible architecture lets teams connect their own compute, inference providers, credential storage and monitoring tools. This allows organizations to apply governance across different deployment environments while integrating OpenShell with their existing enterprise systems.
Hundreds of organizations have put OpenShell to use, and the project has received tens of thousands of contributions in less than a year since launch.
Scaling Agent Execution on Kubernetes
Governing agents is only part of the challenge. Organizations also need to deploy them at scale.
NVIDIA is contributing to Agent Substrate, a Google-originated project in the CNCF Sandbox, and ensuring it works with NVIDIA Dynamo for model inference and KAI Scheduler for shared cluster resource allocation. This effort brings together agent execution, inference serving and resource scheduling on Kubernetes.
Agent Substrate preserves agent environments between tasks while releasing compute when agents are idle. By suspending and resuming those environments across a shared pool of agents, it lets teams scale agent workloads without keeping dedicated compute running for every session.
NVIDIA and Google are also collaborating on an integration of OpenShell and Agent Substrate, so enterprises can secure and govern agents across clouds and on-premises systems.
Building an Open Foundation for AI Factories
AI factories need to offer customers managed Kubernetes services while retaining control of their infrastructure, software and customer experience. Three new open source projects extend the DSX AI Factory Platform to make Kubernetes easier to run and inference faster to scale.
The NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform software stack, from GPU infrastructure and Kubernetes management to workload orchestration and model serving.
NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE) and NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes (NVKR) — now available in public preview — provide open source building blocks for delivering managed Kubernetes services on GPU infrastructure. They automate cluster lifecycle management and provide signed, version-pinned images.
NVKE and NVKR are launching with ecosystem support that extends their reach across AI infrastructure platforms and cloud services. Mirantis, Netris, OpenNebula Systems, Rafay, Spectro Cloud and vCluster, together with Firmus and SK Telecom, have aligned with NVIDIA on integration plans to bring NVKE and NVKR capabilities into their offerings.
NVIDIA Snapshot addresses the challenge of bringing additional inference capacity online quickly. Loading models and warming up workloads can delay scaling and recovery. The open source, modular component restores checkpointed replicas in seconds, without model reload or warmup, supporting faster startup, recovery and elasticity for inference and agentic workloads on Kubernetes.
Design partners Crusoe and Saturn Cloud have evaluated Snapshot on their own workloads using NVIDIA HGX B300 systems. Crusoe, an upstream contributor to Snapshot, tested GLM-5.3 on Crusoe Cloud and reduced the time for the workload to become ready from roughly eight minutes to 31 seconds. Saturn Cloud, a token factory platform, benchmarked Snapshot for scale-from-zero inference and reduced vLLM startup times from between two and 8.5 minutes to six and 34 seconds.
Learn more by joining NVIDIA at KubeCon.

items.title: GTA 6 targets 30FPS, with RT seemingly reserved for PS5 Pro
items.content:
Rockstar has shared another round of Grand Theft Auto 6 technical details following Take-Two's quarterly earnings call, confirming a 30FPS target on consoles while also outlining the visual enhancements available on PS5 Pro.
In a new statement, Rockstar confirmed that GTA 6 has been built specifically for current-generation console hardware, with the studio targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their limits. According to Rockstar, the goal is to maintain the visual fidelity and world density needed to bring Leonida to life while delivering the best possible experience on current-generation consoles.
Rockstar also confirmed that the PS5 Pro version will feature improved image quality through PSSR, alongside ray-traced shadows exclusive to Sony's upgraded console. Rockstar only specifically mentions ray-traced shadows for PS5 Pro, with no ray-tracing features currently confirmed for the standard PS5 or Xbox Series consoles. Given that ray-traced shadows are typically among the less demanding forms of ray tracing, it seems unlikely that Rockstar is reserving more advanced RT effects like RTGI for lower-powered hardware.
Unfortunately, specific resolution targets are still under wraps, so we'll have to wait for Digital Foundry's pixel count once the game drops on consoles later this month. Considering everything we know about GTA 6 so far, I'd be surprised if it ran at native 4K on any console, but we shall see. The advertising of PSSR support is already a pretty big indicator that upscaling will be relied on.
Interestingly, while you won't be able to play GTA 6 on a PS4, you will be able to play it if you have an Xbox One. The game will be available through Xbox Cloud Gaming, so you'll be able to access the Xbox Series S version of the game across older Xbox consoles, as well as mobile devices and PCs. Remote Play functionality will be supported on both PS5 and Xbox Series X/S when the game launches later this month.
KitGuru says: Were you expecting Rockstar to target 60FPS on current-generation consoles?

items.title: AMD investigating Radeon driver bug causing excessive SSD writes
items.content:
AMD appears to be investigating reports of excessive SSD writes linked to recent Radeon drivers. The issue stems from AMD's External Events Client Module (atieclxx.exe), which some users have found entering an apparent write loop that continuously writes data to storage drives.
Running in Windows as part of the AMD External Events Utility, the atieclxx.exe process typically handles monitor detection and responds to Radeon software hotkeys. However, reports (via Neowin) show the process becoming stuck in an endless write loop, generating write rates between 0.3MB/s and 1.5MB/s, with one Reddit user documenting sustained activity reaching 5MB/s.
While those write rates may not sound particularly high at first glance, they can add up quickly on long-running systems. Continuous background writes increase NAND wear, creating unnecessary stress on storage devices at a time when replacing a high-capacity SSD is considerably more expensive than it was just a few years ago. At the higher end of reported activity, a system writing 5MB/s continuously could generate more than 400GB of writes over a 24-hour period.
AMD has not yet published a formal statement on the issue, but an AMD employee responding on Reddit indicated the problem is being looked at, suggesting a driver-side fix may follow soon.
Users seeking temporary workarounds can disable the AMD External Events Utility service or toggle off Resizable BAR in BIOS settings. Even so, disabling the utility can cause display quirks, while switching off Resizable BAR risks reducing gaming performance.
KitGuru says: Uncontrolled background writes can quietly chew through your SSD's endurance if left running around the clock. Have you noticed any unusual disk activity from atieclxx.exe on your system?

items.title: Marathon Symbiosis update launches December 8, adding new PvE and PvP modes, weapons, and more
items.content:
Marathon‘s Symbiosis update arrives December 8, bringing new PvE and PvP modes, weapons, a Runner shell, and expanded areas to explore on Tau Ceti IV. Today we’ve got first details on the updated Perimeter zone, Expedition mode, and more.
What’s new in Marathon: Symbiosis
Updated Perimeter zone: Fungal growth and alien life have transformed Perimeter, introducing new playable spaces including the underground Burrows and submerged Reservoir. Runners will also encounter the Tick Queen, who lurks deep beneath the surface.
Expedition: Phase 1 of a new PvE-only mode built around a three-run series. Play solo or with a crew, face new combat and environmental challenges without PvP threats, and use Flash Boosts to shape your build during a run.
Deathmatch (Beta): An experimental PvP mode featuring bite-sized 3v3 Team Deathmatch matches. Two crews compete for points without risking their permanent loadouts.
Limbo: A new social space where Runners can connect, test weapons and gear in firing ranges, and challenge each other in a dueling pit.
Bishop Runner shell: A new Runner shell built around the fantasy of a fast, surgical blade-wielding robot.
New weapons: The V17 Flamethrower brings short-range area denial, while the Maverick introduces a new revolver archetype with a hand-cannon feel.
Open Play Week begins December 8
Players can experience Marathon during Open Play Week, running December 8 – 15, alongside the launch of Symbiosis.
Marathon is available now on PS5, with full cross-play and cross-save support.** The Symbiosis update launches December 8 for all players.
* Gameplay requires internet access and paid-for subscription on console (sold separately).
**Cross-save requires an internet connection, and for each system you play on: 1) a copy of the Marathon game compatible with your system (other versions sold separately); and 2) system network account linked to your Bungie.net account.

Multiple Capcom franchises hit new sales milestones
items.content:
Ever since they found their footing around 2017, Capcom have been on a bit of a generational run, with the publisher’s output making strides both critically and commercially. From industry staples such as Resident Evil to long-dormant classics, many of Capcom’s franchises have since gone on to hit major sales milestones.
Alongside the release of their latest fiscal earnings report, Capcom updated their publicly-published ‘Platinum titles’ list – aka games which have sold in excess of 1 million copies.
Representing data up to the 30th of September 2026, multiple franchises have either reached, or are approaching major sales milestones, including:
Onimusha [11 million]
Dragon’s Dogma [14 million]
Ace Attorney [15 million]
Dead Rising [19 million]
Devil May Cry [42 million]
Mega Man [45 million]
Street Fighter [60 million]
Monster Hunter [132 million]
Resident Evil [218 million]
The Onimusha franchise passing 10 million units is of particular note due to the recent release of Onimusha: Way of the Sword. Despite being the first proper original entry in two decades, the action title wound up selling 1.7 million copies in just under a month.
With regards to Dragon’s Dogma, the figure above does not take into the account the recently-released DD2: Dark Arisen expansion / Switch 2 port, and so it is safe to assume that by the time Capcom updates its Platinum Titles in Late December / early January, it will have easily hit the 15 million mark (especially as the publisher has already stated that sales have been above expectations for the release.)
While Resident Evil and Monster Hunter remain by far Capcom’s biggest franchises, it is encouraging to see the publisher’s other, more niche, offerings continuing to succeed while reaching new highs.

Street Fighter 6 is 500k copies away from becoming the best-selling entry in the franchise
items.content:
Prior to the game’s release, Capcom revealed that they had high hopes for Street Fighter 6, with the publisher’s president expressing desires for the game to sell a total of 10 million copies when all is said and done. While the title has yet to achieve this milestone, it is well on its way to doing so, with Capcom now confirming that Street Fighter 6 has officially sold over 7.5 million copies – just 500k units behind SFV.
Following the release of its latest fiscal earnings report, Capcom updated its public ranking of the publisher’s best-selling games of all time, revealing that as of the 30th of September 2026 Street Fighter 6 has officially sold 7.5 million copies (pushing total franchise sales past 60 million).
While in and of itself an achievement, 7.5 million copies puts it at just 500,000 behind 2016’s Street Fighter V; meaning it’s also just half a million units away from becoming the best-selling entry in the franchise.
It is worth noting that Street Fighter II is technically the best-selling entry in the series, with a reported 31 million copies sold. That said, this combines dozens of variants from across multiple platforms including arcades, compilations and more. Officially, Capcom reports SFII as having sold 6.3 million copies, meaning Street Fighter 6 has already surpassed it.
As mentioned, prior to the game’s release, Capcom revealed that it hoped to sell 10 million copies throughout the game’s lifecycle. Considering the fact that Street Fighter 6 is currently on its 4th year of post-launch support with seemingly no signs of slowing down, it's safe to assume that this 10 million figure is more of a matter of ‘when’ and not ‘if’.

items.title: Sony announces updated PlayStation Portal with “an eye towards future functionality”
items.content:
Since its initial release back in late 2023, Sony’s PlayStation Portal Remote Player has slowly but surely seen an increase in functionality, with the remote play enabled device being expanded with proper cloud streaming support alongside some additional quality-of-life improvements. In a curious announcement, Sony has now unveiled an updated version of the PS Portal with an increase to its internal storage capacity – claiming it to be in service of “future functionality.”
Making the official announcement on the Japanese PlayStation Blog, Sony unveiled its new Japan-exclusive midnight black PS Portal. Outside of its new colour scheme and a free 1 month of PS Plus Premium, the device appears to be pretty much the same as previous models.
That said, in an interesting move, the console maker revealed that this new Portal includes an increase to its internal storage. While details remain light at this time, Sony claims that this is in service of “an eye towards future functionality” – though what this functionality is remains to be seen.
For the uninitiated, the PS Portal’s OS is based on Android, and as such does have potential for far more than is currently being offered. In fact, mere months on from its initial release, hackers managed to get a PSP emulator running on the device, showcasing that the hardware has more capability than what is being utilised.
While it is unlikely that this updated PS Portal will feature native support for emulators, the increase in internal storage could mean that we’ll see new apps being added to the handheld in future such as YouTube, Netflix, Crunchyroll and other such streaming services.
We will have to wait and see, but this does feel like another small step towards the console maker’s long-rumoured PS6 handheld.

Warhammer Survivors Out Now on XBOX Game Pass! Defeat the Gloomspite Gitz With These Tips
items.content:
Summary
Warhammer Survivors is out now on XBOX Series X|S and XBOX Game Pass.
Experience an addictive bullet-heaven survivor set in the Warhammer 40,000 and Warhammer Age of Sigmar universes.
Get an early edge with these top tips for facing the Gloomspite Gitz – one of the game’s enemy factions.
Big news – Warhammer Survivors is out now!
If this is your first time hearing about Warhammer Survivors, buckle in for addictive bullet-heaven survivor gameplay set across the battlefields of the 41st Millennium and the Mortal Realms. You might know us, Auroch Digital, from our other Warhammer game, Warhammer 40,000 Boltgun. We’ve teamed up with poncle and Warhammer to create an officially licensed Warhammer Survivors.
Following the green theme of our previous entry, we’ve prepared a primer for you to take on the fungus-festooned Gloomspite Gitz!
Who are the Gloomspite Gitz?
The Gloomspite Gitz are a rabble of different cave-dwelling grots that worship the ‘Bad Moon’, a deity they believe will bring about the Everdank, an era of perpetual twilight. This calamitous cohort of crazed Gitz includes several enemy types, each with their own unique attacks and movement patterns you’ll need to learn to have any chance of survival!
Prepare for lots of Gitz…
Moonclan Stabbas are the foot soldiers of the Gloomspite Gitz, swarming the battlefield in tremendous numbers, stabbing wildly at everything in their path. Moonclan Stabbas try to overwhelm with sheer number of bodies and sharp, pointy objects – and while they may not be the scariest, look out for the company they keep…
…And the stampeding forces of the Squigalanche!
Squig Hoppers are grots that have bravely decided to mount feral Squigs and have somehow survived the process. These enemies bounce across the battlefield in unpredictable movements due to the nature of their wild mounts, and their attack damage will be bolstered by any nearby Loonboss on Giant Cave Squig who – you guessed it – also moves unpredictably!
Boinggrot Bounders, on the other hand, are veteran Squig-riders who have survived at least one battle (the life expectancy of a grot is low). For their prowess, they’ve been rewarded with lances, charging with precision toward the player.
Stampeding at the head of this Squigalanche are the wild and gargantuan Mangler Squigs. These two boisterous balls of fury are so ravenous they’ve been chained together. The beasts rampage across the screen, pulled taut by the chain that binds them together. Watch out for both the teeth of Mangler Squig and the chain as each can damage the player. Mangler Squigs always come in pairs, but when one dies, the remaining giant Squig becomes frenzied – deadlier than ever before!
Resilient, lumbering Troggoth allies
If you can survive the pointy blades of the Gitz and the sharp teeth of the Squigs, then you may encounter an even greater threat… Troggoths!
Rockgut Troggoths lumber toward the player, and while they may be slow, they’re tough and have regeneration properties, making them tricky to bring down. Our recommendation? Get yourself a pair of Maleneth’s Poisoned Daggers and whittle them down from afar.
Should you survive all that, then we’ve got news for you: it doesn’t get better!
Beware the Troggoth King
Trugg the Troggoth King is the mightiest of all troggoths, a towering mass of strength with an ill temper. He carries an arcane keystone of ancient design on his back which unleashes unpredictable bursts of elemental magic…
If you somehow manage to be strong enough to face this foe, he’ll begin the fight by swiping at you with his humungous Ironshell Club, which creates wide, telegraphed impact zones. If you’re hit, you’ll be sent flying. Trugg. You’ll also have to contend with that keystone of his, avoiding wild barrages of elemental projectiles. Getting hit by one of these stray projectiles will inflict your Survivor with negative status effects such as burning, poisoning, or bleeding.
As an Extremis-level threat, not just anyone, or any weapon, will be able to take down the Troggoth King. You’ll have to discover what his weakness is or face certain death!
If you want to see all of this (and more!) in action, check out the latest trailer now!
We’ve had great fun creating the sprites and animations of the fungus-addled Gloomspite Gitz. Warhammer Survivors has been a passion project for us, and we can’t wait to get the game into your hands!
Warhammer Survivors is out now!

items.title: GTA VI appears to include PSSR and 40fps support on PS5 Pro
items.content:
Despite being one of the biggest games the industry has seen in a generation, we still know relatively little regarding Rockstar’s upcoming Grand Theft Auto VI – particularly when it comes to the game’s technical specifications. With the game package now officially live on Sony’s back-end servers however, dataminers have begun to uncover a number of specifics, including the fact that PS5 Pro users should benefit from both PSSR support as well as a potential 40fps mode.
As reported by dataminer ‘andshrew’ via ResetEra, the game package for GTA VI has gone live on Sony’s backend servers, allowing for a certain degree of additional insight regarding what features the upcoming open-world juggernaut will and won’t support.
Based on the included flags, GTA VI will – unsurprisingly – support the PlayStation 5 Pro, with the code noting that it uses PSSR version 13.60 (likely just a slightly newer version of their ‘Enhanced’ PSSR which was first released earlier this year).
Perhaps more interesting however is the fact that GTA VI might include a 40fps option on the Pro. As mentioned, Rockstar themselves have yet to officially share any tech specs for GTA VI, though all of the footage shared so far has been limited to 30fps.
According to these datamined flags, the game does support a 120hz output, but does not allow for the use of VRR. While this ultimately may lead to little, it is possible that this means a 40fps option might be on the cards for PS5 Pro users.
All that said, we won’t have to wait too much longer to find out officially, with GTA VI being just over a week away from release. It will be interesting to learn exactly how the game shakes up between the Xbox Series S, Series X, PS5 and PS5 Pro when it launches on the 19th of November.

items.title: New open-source tool reveals exactly what’s using up all your GPU VRAM
items.content:
Microsoft developer Scott Hanselman has released gputaskman, an experimental open-source utility that provides detailed per-process GPU monitoring. The tool can track GPU utilisation, VRAM usage, power draw and AI workloads on a per-application basis.
Hanselman's tool (via Tom's Hardware) displays real-time metrics for individual applications, including power draw, clock speeds, PCIe traffic, encoder activity and VRAM usage. The utility aims to provide a much more detailed breakdown of graphics workloads than Windows Task Manager currently exposes by default.
The tool also includes specific monitoring features for local AI workloads. Beyond simple memory figures, gputaskman can identify active AI processes and surface information about their runtime, model weights, quantisation format and layer count. Hanselman says the project is still experimental, so users should expect occasional bugs and incomplete telemetry.
gputaskman currently supports Windows, Linux, WSL and Apple Silicon Macs, with Nvidia and AMD GPU support available depending on platform.
KitGuru says: Getting more visibility into what background applications are doing with your graphics card is always welcome. Will you be testing out gputaskman on your PC?

items.title: CPU-Z Validator sees shift back towards lower-capacity RAM
items.content:
CPU-Z Validator data is showing an unusual shift towards lower-capacity memory configurations, with 16GB and 8GB systems increasing their share of submissions while 32GB and 64GB setups lose ground. According to one of CPU-Z's developers, it is the first year-over-year decline in system memory capacity recorded by the validator.
Based on CPU-Z Validator statistics (via TechPowerUp), 32GB remains the most common memory configuration, accounting for 37.2% of submissions. However, its share has fallen by 2.5% compared to the same period last year. Higher-capacity configurations also lost share, with 64GB dropping 18% to 7.3%, while 96GB and 128GB systems each fell by more than 26%.
Meanwhile, lower-capacity configurations increased their share of submissions. Systems equipped with 16GB of RAM increased 12.9% to 33.0% of submissions, while 8GB systems grew 5.5% to reach 11.0%.
The same dataset also shows DDR4 increasing its share of validator submissions. DDR4 accounted for 54.5% of systems submitted during the period, up 6.0%, while DDR5 fell 2.9% to 32.9%.
It is worth keeping the source of the data in mind. These figures only cover systems submitted to CPU-Z Validator over the past three months rather than the wider PC market. While the data does not point to a specific cause, memory pricing remains one possible factor. As we recently reported, Exceleram believes current RAM shortages are continuing to worsen, potentially impacting upgrade decisions for some builders.
KitGuru says: CPU-Z's validator data paints an interesting picture, but it will be worth watching whether larger datasets show the same trend over the coming months.

WoW Forever dungeon XP gets major boost in live hotfix
items.content:
Blizzard has increased dungeon enemy XP in WoW Forever by 50%, just days after launch. The change arrived via a live hotfix over the weekend and should make dungeon levelling noticeably more rewarding for players who prefer running instances over questing.
WoW Forever launched with reduced dungeon levelling efficiency, potentially as a way to encourage more players into the open world rather than chain-running dungeons. While the approach succeeded in pushing more players towards questing zones, it also drew criticism from those who enjoy levelling primarily through dungeon runs.
In a post on the official WoW forums, Blizzard confirmed that dungeon enemy XP has been increased by 50%. “At about 11:05 PST today, we deployed a hotfix that increased kill experience in dungeons by 50%, so it feels better to go back in for more runs”.
What's particularly interesting is that Blizzard already has a larger round of balance changes planned for the 10th of November. Rather than waiting a couple of days for that update, the studio opted to push the dungeon XP increase immediately, so clearly Blizzard is paying close attention to player feedback over the launch week.
Rather than XP gain adjustments, the 10th of November update will instead focus on class tuning. Blizzard has already outlined plans to make Hunter pets and Warlock Voidwalkers more durable, improve Affliction Warlock spell interactions, and adjust Enhancement Shamans so Strength and Attack Power once again become the spec's most desirable stats while levelling.
KitGuru says: Dungeon levelling probably shouldn't outpace open-world questing, but the launch numbers may have swung a little too far in the opposite direction. Have you been levelling through dungeons or sticking to questing?

items.title: FragPunk Reveals Farlands: New Delivery PvPvE Adventure Now Available in Early Access
items.content:
FragPunk has launched its biggest new chapter yet with Farlands, a permanent, multiplayer delivery-driven PvPvE adventure where dozens of players share a persistent world, now available in Global Early Access on PC and console.
Farlands combines high-stakes cargo deliveries with resource gathering, combat, and long-term progression in a sandbox combat experience. Players take on delivery orders, venture into dangerous territories to collect resources, and transport their cargo safely to its destination. But delivering cargo is more than simply traveling from point A to point B. Cargo weight, changing environmental conditions, and encounters with other players can all influence the outcome of a run.
What makes Farlands particularly unique is that all of this takes place in a persistent world that continues to evolve over time.
A World in Constant Flux: Inside Farlands’ Core Design
Farlands features a persistent server system that allows players to return to the same continuously evolving environment.
Persistent Sandbox Combat: Each server operates on a five-day cycle, with in-game time progressing continuously. Players can repeatedly return to the same server to gather resources, complete orders, and engage in combat. Their actions, including fighting enemies, contribute to changes in faction levels within the server, affecting the strength, number, and distribution of hostile forces.
An Evolving NPC Ecosystem: Within the persistent server system, the NPC ecosystem is constantly evolving. Even after players clear hostile forces from an outpost, the area won’t necessarily remain safe. Over time, enemies may return and grow stronger, and defeating these tougher opponents can reward players with rarer resources.
Dynamic Weather: Weather conditions such as heat, cold, and rain accelerate the depletion of players’ health and affect cargo transportation. Players need to monitor their condition and consider how different weather conditions affect their ability to carry cargo, carefully planning their loads and delivery objectives while keeping themselves in good condition.
Multiplayer Cooperation and Progression
Beyond its evolving environment, Farlands also brings player interactions and long-term progression into its core delivery gameplay loop.
Unpredictable Player Encounters: Farlands features global voice chat and an emote system, allowing players to communicate during combat and deliveries. Strangers may reach temporary agreements to escort valuable cargo together, only to turn against one another at a critical moment and claim the loot for themselves. With these interactions driven by player communication, every encounter carries an element of uncertainty.
Long-Term Resource Progression: Resources earned from successful deliveries can be invested in strengthening personal equipment and developing bases. By continuously gathering and investing resources, players can gradually improve their capabilities and prepare for more demanding combat encounters and delivery missions.
Before You Hit the Road
Whether you’re preparing for your first delivery or looking to improve your chances of survival, here are four tips to help you become one of the best couriers in Farlands.
1. Build Your Loadout Around Sets
Farlands features an extensive attribute system, with different pieces of equipment directly affecting character stats. We recommend combining gear from matching sets to improve your overall performance.
2. Upgrade Your Equipment, Weapon and Character
As a server progresses, the environment becomes increasingly dangerous. Players can visit NPCs at the Hub to upgrade their equipment, helping them prepare for the battles ahead.
3. Prioritize Hub Level-Up
Your base plays an important role in long-term progression. Upgrading it unlocks advanced crafting options, character skill trees, and expanded cargo storage, giving players more ways to develop their capabilities and prepare for future deliveries.
4. Acquire Vehicles and Blueprints
Beyond the basic equipment system, Farlands features more advanced progression options through vehicles and blueprints. Players can discover blueprints while scavenging, gradually expanding their options for the mid-to-late game and preparing for tougher enemies and more demanding delivery missions.
Ready for Your First Delivery?
In Farlands, every cargo run brings new risks, shifting opportunities, and decisions that can determine your success.
Prepare your equipment, strengthen your capabilities, and stay ready to adapt to the changing world around you.

Bit Reactor reportedly begins layoffs weeks after bringing back staff
items.content:
Just weeks after beginning the process of bringing furloughed staff back to work, Star Wars Zero Company studio Bit Reactor has reportedly conducted a round of layoffs.
As we reported last month, Bit Reactor had started returning staff to active development following the launch of Star Wars Zero Company. Prior to release, the studio had furloughed a significant portion of its workforce after running into financial difficulties, leaving a smaller team in place to support launch and post-release updates.
According to a report from Bespin Bulletin, a number of Bit Reactor employees confirmed on LinkedIn that they had been laid off on the 6th of November. While the total number of affected staff remains unclear, multiple developers across environment art, UI engineering, QA and production have publicly stated that they were impacted.
Subsequent updates suggest several of those laid off were part of the original furlough group, rather than employees who had recently returned to full-time work on the project. For now, the core team supporting Star Wars Zero Company appears to remain in place, although Bit Reactor has not commented publicly on future staffing plans.
The layoffs come just weeks after the release of one of this year's best-reviewed strategy games. Star Wars Zero Company surpassed one million copies sold and received widespread critical praise, but Bit Reactor's financial challenges appear to have continued well beyond launch.
KitGuru says: It's never pleasant seeing talented developers lose their jobs, especially so soon after shipping a critically acclaimed game. Hopefully those affected can land on their feet quickly.

items.title: Epic Games Launcher will support SteamOS
items.content:
Epic Games has confirmed that its new native Linux launcher will support SteamOS, alongside distributions such as Fedora, Cachy and Omarchy.
While the client is currently in preview for Debian and Ubuntu, Epic communications director Jake Jones confirmed to GamingOnLinux (via VideoCardz) that the company plans to support as many Linux distributions as possible, including gaming-focused platforms such as SteamOS.
Epic is still evaluating how it will distribute the launcher across different Linux platforms. The current preview is available as a .deb package, but the company says it is testing additional packaging formats and plans to restore AppImage downloads later this month.
For Steam Deck owners, native support gives users an official way to access their Epic Games library without relying on third-party tools like Heroic Games Launcher. However, Epic has yet to confirm how the launcher will integrate with SteamOS Game Mode or whether any handheld-specific interface is planned.
SteamOS support also doesn't mean Fortnite will immediately become playable on Steam Deck. Epic previously confirmed that Fortnite's Linux release depends on the arrival of Easy Anti-Cheat Linux v2, with additional platform requirements still needing to be addressed. The company has previously said the Steam Deck does not currently meet all of those requirements, although discussions with Valve are ongoing.

Practice Makes Precise: At CoRL, NVIDIA and Partners Reveal How Robots Rehearse Delicate Work in Simulation
items.content:
Simulation, which has long been the proving ground for robots learning to walk, roll and hop, is now helping researchers teach robots tasks that require a finer touch: aligning gears, connecting cables and assembling small components.
The shift from locomotion to manipulation is taking center stage at this week’s Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) in Austin, Texas, alongside the rise of agentic robotics — a new paradigm that integrates frontier agents to create interpretable code for physical robotics systems.
At CoRL, NVIDIA is introducing new open robotics technologies, including world action models, simulation tools, benchmarks and agentic workflows.
Two NVIDIA papers are among six finalists out of thousands of submissions for the Best Paper Awards at CoRL:
GRAIL (Generating Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from World Models), which presents a digital generation pipeline for 3D assets and simulator-ready scenes for robot learning.
RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies, which introduces a robot model and training recipe that scales visuomotor context three orders of magnitude beyond state-of-the-art policies without growing inference latency.
These advancements help researchers train robots on complex tasks, evaluate their performance across changing conditions and use failures to guide further learning — building the precision, adaptability and autonomy needed to move from lab demonstrations to industrial deployment.
NVIDIA is working with partners like Ambi Robotics, Bosch Research, Dexmate, Dyna Robotics, FieldAI, Flexion, Noitom Robotics, Siemens, Skild AI, RLWRLD, UC Berkeley, Walden Robotics and the University of Washington to bring these advancements to the broader robotics community.
World Action Models Enable Next Level of Robot Autonomy
The next level of robot autonomy requires robots to perceive their surroundings, anticipate how their actions will change the environment and execute complex, multistep tasks with a high degree of precision. World action models enable exactly that.
At CoRL, NVIDIA is introducing GR00T 2, an open frontier world action model built on NVIDIA Cosmos. Trained on diverse robot and human data, including 100,000 hours of NVIDIA open source human egocentric data, the model enables robots to learn dexterous manipulation skills. Key features include:
Out-of-the-box performance: Completed 40 of 50 evaluated tasks at least once without task-specific demonstrations.
Skill transfer: Learns from human demonstrations and transfers skills between different robot bodies without robot demonstrations
Generalization with little data: Achieved 71% average success across 50 tasks with just one demonstration per task, increasing to 95% with five.
Agent control: AI agents can use GR00T 2’s application programming interface and supporting tools to run skills in sequence and recover from errors.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/groot-2-shipping-label.mp4
GR00T 2 currently ranks among the top three models across all vision language action and world action model categories for the RoboCasa365, RoboLab, RoboDojo and MolmoSpaces benchmarks, with multiple leaderboard wins.
Nexuni is testing it for robotic laundry handling, Foxconn is applying GR00T 2 to factory automation for server manufacturing and Siemens is evaluating it across industrial use cases.
MicroAGI is using GR00T 2, post-trained through reinforcement learning, to perform Ethernet cable swapping with a YAM robotic arm. Its agentic robotics approach automates the creation and calibration of simulation environments using Isaac Lab 3.0 and Newton, where the policy is trained. The agentic robotics workflow will be demonstrated at CoRL.
Training capable robots requires diverse data. Open NVIDIA workflows and models equip researchers with better tools for data collection and annotation:
For researchers building robot-training datasets, NVIDIA’s new open Video to Data workflow turns human video into simulated robot demonstrations, with a challenge inviting researchers to advance it.
The NVIDIA EgoHand open model — being demoed at CoRL and with over 40,000 Hugging Face downloads in the two weeks since launch — reconstructs 3D hand motion, trained with data from Noitom Robotics.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/egohand-demo.mp4
Where the Training and Scaling Happens — in Simulation
A pretrained model gives robots a core set of skills. Simulation lets researchers train, refine and evaluate skills at scale before deploying them on physical robots.
NVIDIA Isaac Lab, an open source robot-learning framework, provides the foundation for that work. Its latest release, Isaac Lab 3.0, allows researchers to use agents to quickly set up training environments with simulation-ready assets, switch between NVIDIA PhysX and Newton physics solvers, choose renderers for perception-based training and apply a new reinforcement post-training library to foundation models like GR00T.
Accurate physics is critical to transferring learned skills from simulation to the real robot. Tighter integration with Newton, an open source physics engine, now allows Isaac Lab to model deformable objects such as cables and cloth, along with complex articulated systems such as robotic hands with many interacting joints.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/newton-strawberry.mp4
Integration with Newton simulates how a strawberry deforms under a robot’s grip.
Together, Isaac Lab and Newton combine accurate physics with scale to enable researchers to train thousands of simulated robots in parallel. In a vision-based dexterous manipulation benchmark, Isaac Lab 3.0 with Newton achieved up to 2.5x the training throughput of Isaac Lab 2.3 with PhysX.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/newton-physx-web.mp4
Isaac Lab supports robot simulation with Newton and NVIDIA PhysX.
Developers are extending Newton’s capabilities. At CoRL, Skild AI announced Scalable Throughput-optimized Engine for Embodied Learning, or STEEL, a new rigid-body physics solver built on Newton to accelerate robot training with Isaac Lab.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/robotics-montage-8s.mp4
Skild AI’s STEEL Solver.
Flexion showcased how Isaac Lab and Newton help train Reflect, its robot-intelligence model combining reasoning and whole-body manipulation.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/flexion-newton-isaac-lab.mp4
Flexion uses Newton for RL with Isaac Lab.
FieldAI is using Newton — as well as Isaac Lab and Isaac Sim, built on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries — to train and validate robot policies for deployment in unstructured real-world environments. Dyna Robotics will demonstrate how parallel simulation in Isaac Lab helps train whole-body controllers for its semi-humanoid Taku robot for work in warehouses, hotels and food services.
Walden Robotics is using Isaac Sim’s photorealistic rendering to train and evaluate its general-purpose robot in virtual environments for manufacturing and logistics, while Dexmate is exploring how coding agents can rehearse and refine manipulation strategies in Isaac Sim before executing them on its Vega robot.
AlphaNIST, built in Isaac Lab, demonstrates how efficient practice can translate into precision. A single policy learns all 20 tasks on the NIST Assembly Task Board, manipulating millimeter-scale parts using only a yes-or-no success signal. It achieves more than 98% training success, compared with 81% for separate per-task policies, using roughly 39x less GPU time.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/alphanist-6-16s-web.mp4
AlphaNIST uses Isaac Lab to train a single robot policy across 20 precision tasks on the NIST Assembly Task Board.
Behind those results is Success-Guided Sampling, or SGS, from the University of Washington and NVIDIA. The method focuses practice on tasks a policy succeeds at about half the time, directing training toward skills it’s still learning. With SGS, robot training can scale beyond a million parallel environments.
The University of Texas at Austin’s School of Computing and Texas Robotics uses Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab to train robotic skills in simulation, letting students start developing before physical hardware is available.
New Industrial Benchmarks for Robot Evaluation
Learning a skill is one challenge. Performing it reliably across changing conditions is another.
NVIDIA Isaac Lab-Arena, an open source framework for scaled policy evaluation, enables developers to compose diverse and repeatable evaluations, then run policies across thousands of variations in parallel. Analyses expose which conditions cause failures, so researchers know what to fix in their next training run. The developer preview of its latest version, 0.4, is arriving at CoRL.
DexBench and VABAR, two new open benchmarks, are among the first designed to measure robot dexterity and adaptability across industrial tasks using Isaac Lab-Arena and Newton.
DexBench, developed by RLWRLD in collaboration with NVIDIA, takes dexterity evaluation off the tabletop and into real-world workflows. Built using NVIDIA Isaac Lab-Arena, it features 15 tasks across four scenes spanning retail, logistics, manufacturing and hospitality, testing generalization across object, spatial and physics variations.
Genesis AI, mimic robotics and other industry partners are evaluating DexBench through early access.
Teams can run DexBench on Manifold, Bifrost’s evaluation platform for scaling robotics simulations, with no setup required, built-in failure analysis and free credits for initial evaluations.
VABAR — the Variational Automation Benchmark for Agentic Robotics — from UC Berkeley and NVIDIA, evaluates robots across six industrial tasks. Each carries standardized variations, difficulty tiers and success metrics.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/task-tool-sorting.mp4
A simulated tool-sorting task demonstrates how VABAR evaluates robot manipulation skills for industrial workflows.
Agents Turn Skills Into Robot Programs
Successful task completion requires robots to coordinate multiple skills and adapt when something goes wrong. Building reliable programs for these multistep tasks remains a challenge.
Agentic robotics helps solve that challenge.
UC Berkeley’s new Graph-as-Policy (GaP) framework uses agents to connect individual skills into robot programs. Agents test these programs using NVIDIA Isaac open simulation technologies and refine them based on failures. This helps researchers scale development with less data while keeping the programs interpretable for engineers to review and verify before deployment.
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/wipe-the-bar.mp4
GaP uses agents and simulation to turn individual robot skills into coordinated actions, such as wiping a bar.
“To me, agentic robotics is the most exciting technological development since the internet in 1995,” said Ken Goldberg, professor of robotics at UC Berkeley and a lead on the VABAR and GaP projects.
Ambi Robotics is exploring GaP for industrial automation.
Ambi Robotics, Bosch Research and Siemens are all exploring GaP for its agentic robotics workflows across diverse industrial scenarios.
Learn more by joining NVIDIA at CoRL.
