items.title: Mahesh Babu invests in Shortgun Games
items.content:
Backing co-founders Jeet Chandan and Vidhit Mehta, Superstar Mahesh Babu joins forces with Shortgun Games. (Photo credit: Press Release)
Actor Mahesh Babu has joined Mumbai-based game development studio Shortgun Games as a strategic investor, backing its ambition to build original Indian gaming franchises for international PC and console markets.
Founded by Jeet Chandan and Vidhit Mehta, Shortgun Games is developing titles exclusively for PC and modern consoles, including PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The investment amount and Mahesh Babu's stake in the company have not been disclosed.
The studio's flagship project, PROJECT TAKEDOWN, is a narrative-driven action-adventure game being developed for international markets, including North America, Europe and the United Kingdom.
Mahesh Babu said, “India has extraordinary creative potential, and the time is right to build original characters and cinematic worlds from here that resonate across the globe.”
He added, “What drew me to this company is Jeet Chandan and Vidhit Mehta’s clarity of ambition and their drive to create high-end PC and console experiences that stand shoulder-to-shoulder with international studio benchmarks.”
The studio's focus on PC and console platforms marks a deliberate shift from the mobile-led approach that has traditionally dominated India's gaming market. Shortgun Games aims to develop high-fidelity experiences and original intellectual properties that can appeal to global gaming audiences.
To strengthen PROJECT TAKEDOWN's action design, the studio has brought on board Indian action director Vicky Arora, whose credits include Uri: The Surgical Strike, RRR and Tanaav. His team is working on motion-capture choreography, combat pre-visualisation and physical stunt mechanics for the game.
Vidhit Mehta, Co-founder and Director of Shortgun Games, said, “We founded Shortgun Games with a singular focus- to prove that India can engineer world-class interactive entertainment for PC and modern consoles. Having Mahesh Babu sir come on board alongside Jeet and me as a strategic investor is an extraordinary milestone.”
Jeet Chandan, Co-founder and Director, said, “Our goal has always been to build durable, cross-media franchises that transcend regional boundaries. Mahesh Babu sir's trust in our roadmap provides a massive vote of confidence for our entire team.”
The collaboration brings together Indian cinema and game development as Shortgun Games looks to establish original Indian intellectual properties in the global premium gaming market.

items.content:
Microsoft's planned divestment of Arkane Studios has taken another turn, with one of the studio's employee unions accusing Xbox of actively “sabotaging” development of Marvel's Blade.
As spotted by VGC, French workers' union STJV has published a strongly worded statement concerning the ongoing situation at Arkane. The union claims that despite Blade progressing well internally, the studio now faces the possibility of closure due to Microsoft's wider restructuring efforts.
“Today, as work on Blade is going fine, and the level of quality of the game to be expected is on par with what Arkane has accustomed its players, workers have to face the harsh reality: our studio might get closed because, and only because, Microsoft decided to, even if that means sabotaging the game it funded,” the statement reads. The union goes on to argue that Arkane is profitable, but “just not profitable enough for Microsoft”.
Beyond its criticism of Microsoft, STJV is also pushing for greater protections for Arkane staff. The union is demanding that employees be given a say in any potential acquisition of the studio, while also seeking improved redundancy packages should Microsoft ultimately decide to close the developer. According to the union, the current severance offer remains “outrageously low”.
As we reported previously, several publishers have expressed interest in acquiring the studio, including fellow French games giant Ubisoft. If a deal can be reached, Arkane could potentially continue operating under new ownership while completing work on Blade. There has also been discussion of Arkane management leading a buyout of the studio, which would turn Arkane into an independent studio.

items.title: The Wizard of Open Weights: Chris Alexiuk Makes AI Easy With Open Models
items.content:
Chris Alexiuk has a simple rule about open source AI: If you believe in it, be loud about it.
“We should be shouting about this technology from the rooftops,” said Alexiuk, a Toronto-based senior product research engineer in deep learning at NVIDIA who specializes in making open large language models (LLMs) practical for working developers.
Alexiuk’s preferred “rooftop” is YouTube, where he’s built a following teaching curious thousands how to build, fine-tune, evaluate and ship production LLM applications and agents.
“I think the people who will most help us understand how to build and apply AI likely haven’t even heard of it yet,” he said. “Trying to get knowledge and information out to as many people as humanly possible is what continues to drive me.”
Bringing NVIDIA Nemotron to Developers Everywhere
Having spent years teaching developers to build with open models, Alexiuk has concluded that transparency isn’t a feature of good AI; it’s the precondition for it.
“Fully open source AI is necessary for the democratization of intelligence,” he said. “You should have access to the weights, the data that went into it, the training recipes, everything.”
That’s why, on his LinkedIn profile, Alexiuk styles himself “No. 1 Nemotron Fan,” referring to the NVIDIA Nemotron family of open source, multimodal models built for long-running, self-evolving and specialized AI agents.
“I think Nemotron is the most important project that exists,” said Alexiuk, who also uses the pseudonym “Joe Nemotron” across social media. “I’m a firm believer that openness is a very important thing to undertake, so I’m going to be the No. 1 fan of whoever is doing that the best. And that is Nemotron.”
https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/ChrisAlexiuk_captions_9MB.mp4
It’s this matter-of-fact directness and affable approachability that makes Alexiuk’s teaching style so appealing. On the social media platform X, he goes by the handle “llm_wizard.” His avatar: a laughing cartoon caricature sporting a slouchy sorcerer’s hat and brandishing a magic wand.
It’s no surprise, then, that Alexiuk likens Nemotron to a magical library — its users fellow wizards in search of knowledge that can move mountains.
“You’re a wizard in search of prepared spells, and Nemotron has a spell for everything,” he said. “Just choose the one you need.”
In non-wizard terms?
“There’s a category of model that’s going to be close to the kind of work you want to accomplish,” Alexiuk said, explaining that Nemotron supports that whole ecosystem of AI users: from individual developers using a model like Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for repetitive, high-frequency execution work to a company deploying Nemotron Ultra for long-running autonomous agents, deep research and enterprise tasks.
NVIDIAN Chris Alexiuk (left) engages with developers during the Build-a-Claw event at GTC Berlin.
“I think that openness helps more people understand AI and hopefully leads to more people doing really ingenious things with these tools at the limit,” Alexiuk said. “If a tool is amplifying skill, it’s amplifying human expression.”
From Birding to Model-Building
Alexiuk first became fascinated with machine learning in a computational physics class at Trent University in Ontario, Canada.
“After that, I learned about TensorFlow and that you could build image classifiers that ran on your GPU,” he recalled. As an initial one-off project, Alexiuk built a classifier that would alert him whenever his friend’s distinctive pet bird, a Yellow-Faced Gray Budgerigar, appeared in frame on his webcam during shared video game sessions.
“Because we were playing video games, I wasn’t focused on my friend’s webcam, but I didn’t want to miss seeing the bird when it appeared,” Alexiuk said. “And then my whole life changed, because in that instance I realized it’s crazy what you could do with technology.”
Since then, he’s been embedding himself in the open source AI community.
“To imagine within the span of a few years going from freaking out because I could know my friend’s bird was in the camera frame to being able to make any website in a matter of minutes with a model that’s running on my laptop — I cannot wait to see what’s next,” Alexiuk said. “It’s never been more accessible to get into and learn about AI.”
And if another LLM wizard arises to challenge him for the title of No. 1 Nemotron Fan?
“It would be the greatest day of my life to be surpassed by an even bigger fan of Nemotron, who had heard about Nemotron through the work I was doing,” Alexiuk said. “That would be a capstone to my career that I can only dream of.”
Hear more from Alexiuk by following the NVIDIA Nemotron Labs Livestreams series on YouTube.

items.title: More Performance From Every Byte: How Full-Stack Codesign Solves AI’s Memory Challenge
items.content:
Larger models, longer contexts and agentic applications are increasing GPU memory pressure while supply tightens and prices rise — a trend expected to continue through the near term.
NVIDIA works closely with memory partners to rapidly adopt the latest memory technologies. NVIDIA was first to adopt HBM3e and HBM4 technologies into an accelerated computing stack.
But the approach isn’t to simply pack more memory onto the GPU. It’s full-stack codesign. NVIDIA intentionally designs GPUs, CPUs, networking, storage and software together to get more useful work out of memory at every layer of the AI factory.
That matters because an AI factory runs on a memory and storage hierarchy. GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM) is the fastest, most expensive and most contested tier — with model weights and KV cache competing for limited capacity. Below it sit CPU memory, local SSDs and shared storage, each trading speed for more capacity at a lower cost per bit.
How much useful work a byte does depends on how well the whole hierarchy is used: shrinking what must be stored, placing it on the right tier and bringing it back to the GPU before it’s needed.
Byte for byte, NVIDIA makes the most efficient use of memory at every layer — and the results show it. From NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra to the Vera Rubin platform, HBM capacity per GPU rose roughly 3%, while agentic throughput per dollar rose by up to 30x on SemiAnalysis AgentX.
Agentic Inference Is Putting More Pressure on HBM
Frontier models now have trillions of parameters — the values that hold what an AI model learned in training.
KV cache, which holds the context the model needs to understand each active request without reprocessing the same information, is also expanding. Agentic trajectories carry prior context across repeated model and tool calls, in some cases processing up to 3 million tokens, so each request’s working memory grows over time.
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) adds relevant enterprise information to prompts, creating even more context to process and retain.
During inference, HBM primarily holds both model parameters and KV cache. The result: greater pressure on HBM.
Why AI Factories Need a Memory Hierarchy
Adding more HBM capacity per GPU is the obvious response to that pressure, but capacity delivers only what bandwidth can move.
Think of HBM as a warehouse and memory bandwidth as its loading docks. A larger warehouse holds more inventory, but the docks set how much can move in and out at a time. Once the docks are at capacity, moving more inventory takes longer and slows response times. If delays exceed the required service level, the added space can’t be used effectively, even as it adds cost and draws power.
That’s also why no operation keeps all its inventory in the closest, fastest space. What’s in motion stays near the line. What’s waiting moves to a larger, cheaper space nearby and returns before it’s needed.
An AI factory faces the same limit.
More HBM can hold more KV cache and support more concurrent users. Every added user shares the same compute and memory bandwidth. But when each user expects fast responses, eventually memory bandwidth is unable to supply data as fast as compute can use it: a limit engineers call the memory wall.
Past that point, extra HBM capacity can’t be put to work, yet it still adds costs and draws power. The data still needs a place to live, but not all of it needs the fastest, most expensive tier. This is why an AI factory manages data across a memory and storage hierarchy.
Maximizing the Value of Every Byte With Full-Stack Codesign
NVIDIA’s full-stack codesign makes every byte of HBM count by relieving pressure from model weights, KV cache and RAG data. It does this with techniques that each target a different source of inefficiency:
Shrink model weights and distribute them across the NVL72 domain.
The NVFP4 format reduces the space required for weights compared to FP8, the lowest precision possible on the NVIDIA Hopper platform. Recent models, including FLUX.2 [klein] from Black Forest Labs, Inkling from Thinking Machines Lab, Beam 1.0 from Reflection, Meta Muse Spark from Meta, Step 5 Preview from StepFun and NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL have been released with NVFP4 checkpoints, demonstrating growing model-builder adoption of 4-bit precision for faster, more memory-efficient inference.
Within an NVL72 system, model weights can be distributed across up to 72 GPUs, so each GPU holds a smaller share of the model — leaving more HBM for KV cache and concurrent users.
Shrink KV-cache and offload inactive context to lower-cost storage tiers.
Applying NVFP4 to the KV cache reduces its footprint compared with FP8, so more context can stay resident in HBM.
NVIDIA Vera CPU helps in two ways. Faster tool execution shortens the time KV cache sits inactive during tool calls, and its large LPDDR memory, connected to NVIDIA Rubin GPUs over NVIDIA NVLink-C2C interconnect, gives paused context a nearby place to wait and return quickly.
When context isn’t actively in use, NVIDIA Dynamo inference software moves it to NVIDIA CMX context memory storage — a tier built for capacity at far lower cost per bit than HBM — and returns it before reuse. Unlike local SSDs, CMX is shared across servers, and unlike enterprise storage, it skips the overhead of long-term data protection that short-lived context doesn’t need. NVIDIA CMX context memory storage partners include Cloudian, DDN, Dell Technologies, Everpure (previously Pure Storage), HPE, IBM, NetApp, VAST and WEKA.
Dynamo’s KV Cache Reuse ties the tiers together, managing KV cache as one system-wide resource across GPU memory, CPU memory and storage, so context computed once can be reused across the system.
Compact RAG embeddings and keeping the index outside HBM.
RAG turns enterprise documents into embeddings — numerical representations that let a system search by meaning rather than keyword — organized into a searchable index. NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever models produce smaller embeddings with higher retrieval accuracy, while the NVIDIA cuVS library enables that index to be built and served across CPU and storage. The knowledge base never occupies HBM, and only the passages the model needs enter context.
The result is less HBM used for model weights, less HBM tied up by idle context and more of it available to serve concurrent users.
More Useful Output per Dollar With Each Generation
Across successive NVIDIA platform generations, tokens per second per dollar has risen far faster than HBM capacity.
On the SemiAnalysis AgentX DeepSeek V4 Pro workload, NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 delivers up to 10x higher throughput per dollar than NVIDIA H200 platform at 100 tokens per second per user, with HBM capacity per GPU roughly doubling. At 125 tokens per second per user, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivers up to 30x higher throughput per dollar than GB300 NVL72, with HBM capacity per GPU up about 3%.
For AI factory operators, the metric that matters is how many useful tokens the factory can deliver within its power budget while meeting user response-time needs. More tokens per second per watt means more work and revenue from the same power, and a lower cost for every token. NVIDIA’s full-stack codesign lowers token costs by increasing the useful work every byte of memory delivers.
Learn more in the video explainer and technical deep dive on how NVIDIA full-stack codesign reduces inference memory pressure.

items.title: Blizzard’s WoW Forever mega-server gamble appears to be paying off
items.content:
World of Warcraft Forever officially launched last night, and Blizzard appears to have pulled off something many players thought would be impossible. Despite introducing a radically different server structure built around mega servers spanning multiple regions, the launch avoided the lengthy queues, login problems and server instability that have often accompanied major Blizzard releases.
Rather than relying on dozens of separate regional realms, WoW Forever consolidates players onto large-scale mega servers capable of supporting far larger populations. This is one of the biggest technical changes Blizzard has made to the Classic formula, leading many players to expect at least some level of launch-day disruption as thousands of users logged in simultaneously.
Instead, the launch has gone remarkably smoothly, a sentiment that has been echoed by fans on Reddit, where hundreds of players have been discussing the stable launch experience. Rather than complaining about server crashes and connection problems, many players have instead found themselves praising Blizzard's ambitious mega-server rollout and expressing surprise at just how smoothly things have gone.
While the launch has broadly been viewed as a success, WoW Classic and Forever developer Josh Greenfield acknowledged that a handful of issues did emerge during the game's opening hours. Blizzard encountered problems with the service managing boats and zeppelins, prompting the team to temporarily add portals while a permanent fix was prepared. Some zones also felt quieter than intended due to layer population settings, another issue Blizzard is actively addressing.
My own experience has largely reflected the wider community sentiment. I was able to get straight into the game without any queues at around 11:30pm last night, with my only issues being one bugged quest that required me to restart the game, and one very annoying crab-fetching quest where the mobs simply weren't spawning in often enough based on the number of players actively trying to farm the same quest item. These were very minor setbacks though, setting me back mere minutes rather than hours. At no point did I have to sit in a queue, which is fantastic for an opening-hour MMO launch.
With the first day now in the books, Blizzard's mega-server gamble appears to be paying off. The true test will come over the next few weeks as player populations spread across the world and more players join the game, but Blizzard has nevertheless delivered one of the smoothest World of Warcraft launches in its history.

items.content:
Sony rarely discusses future PlayStation hardware publicly, but the company has now provided a fresh update on PlayStation 6 development. During its latest earnings call, Sony said progress on its next-generation platform remains on track, while preparations for the company's next console will ramp up from the next fiscal year.
VGC sat in on the earnings call, coming away with some interesting quotes from Sony CFO Lin Tao. During the call, Tao said Sony intends to make “solid progress” on preparations for its next-generation platform, while later adding that development of the company's next PlayStation console is progressing as planned. Sony also confirmed that investment in the new platform will begin from the next fiscal year.
The comments arrived alongside Sony's latest financial results, which showed PS5 sales reaching 97.9 million units after another 2.6 million consoles were sold during the quarter ending 30th September. While hardware sales are naturally slowing as the console matures, Tao said the broader PlayStation platform continues to expand and grow in a stable manner.
Sony also discussed memory procurement during the call, stating that it has already aligned with suppliers on the memory volumes required for next fiscal year. While the company stopped short of explicitly linking those agreements to PlayStation 6 production, the comments came as part of a broader discussion about preparations for future PlayStation hardware.
The wider PlayStation business remains in a healthy position. Sony reported a 9% year-on-year increase in gaming revenue and an 89% increase in operating income, while monthly active users reached a record 127 million during September.

items.title: Hope in the City: Why This Detective Uses a Sketchbook Instead of a Badge
items.content:
Summary
Hope in the City launches November 11, 2026, on XBOX Series X|S, XBOX on PC, and Steam, and will be available day one with XBOX Game Pass.
No traditional detective tools? No problem. Discover how Hope uses her artist’s eye, a sketchbook, and some creative imagination, to solve the mystery of her parents’ disappearance.
Go behind the scenes to discover how we designed a unique investigation system and brought Hope’s sketchbook to life with more than 100 hand-drawn illustrations.
What if your greatest tool for solving the mystery of your parents’ disappearance wasn’t a badge, but a sketchbook?
Launching November 11 on XBOX Series X|S, XBOX on PC, and Steam, and available day one with XBOX Game Pass, Hope in the City is a narrative mystery adventure where you play as Hope Song, a 17-year-old aspiring artist living in Shenyang, Northeast China. Just as she’s preparing to leave for art school overseas, she comes home to find her apartment ransacked and her parents missing.
Hope isn’t a traditional detective. She has no authority to demand answers and people around her aren’t willing to talk. When we began designing the game, we asked ourselves: how would someone like Hope investigate?
The answer was her sketchbook.
Giving Players Freedom to Think
As Hope explores Shenyang, you’ll collect clues, engage in conversations, and discover observations that she records in her notebook. You can combine any two thoughts to see what connections they make. Successful combinations form insights and breakthroughs that unlock new dialogue, locations, and leads. You can also take what you’ve learned to other characters and decide what to ask them.
But this mechanic grew from something more than our love of detective games. We wanted to explore what choice means when the world around you limits your options. Hope can’t always say what she’s thinking or convince others to help. In her notebook, however, she can question anything, make unexpected connections, and consider ideas she would never say out loud.
Her actions may be constrained, but her thoughts are not. That’s where we gave players the greatest freedom.
Notebook breakthrough
Making Every Combination Count
During early prototyping, I noticed something frustrating: whenever players combined unrelated observations, Hope gave the same generic response. After seeing it a few times, it became boring!
So, our writers created individual responses for every combination, even when they don’t advance the investigation. Hope might make a joke, reveal a little of her personality, or stumble toward a subtle hint. We wanted you to feel encouraged to experiment rather than worry about getting things wrong.
Finding the right balance still took extensive playtesting. Some connections we thought were obvious proved surprisingly difficult for players, so we repeatedly refined the notebook interface and clues. The goal was to preserve that satisfying moment when two ideas finally click, while making the “wrong” answers more enjoyable and engaging too.
Gameplay screenshot showing Hope’s notebook and thoughts being combined
Drawing Hope’s World
We also wanted the notebook to feel like something Hope would actually draw, rather than conventional game assets.
Artist Calista Antonio created more than 100 hand-drawn sketches for the game. She approached each page as a quick visual impression, capturing what Hope notices and how she feels, rather than producing polished illustrations.
Given that she’s also a 3D animator, Calista’s process combined 3D tools with drawing. She used the models and assets from the game to block out perspectives and pose characters in 3D, then developed the sketches with linework and digital watercolour. While the game features a sharp angular art style, Calista interpreted
There’s also a little bit of Calista herself in Hope. She also has Chinese heritage and, like Hope, she left Asia at 17 to pursue her passion for art in Canada. Calista drew on that experience to capture the emotions of Hope’s journey. Some of Calista’s own paintings even hang on the walls of Hope’s bedroom, bringing a personal touch to the character and her world.
We’re sharing original sketches and process artwork here for a closer look at how the notebook came to life.
Artist Calista Antonio working on Hope’s in-game sketches
The Mystery Is Yours to Uncover

Your sketches may be the only clues you have. Play as 17-year-old Hope Song in this narrative mystery set in Shenyang, China. While everyone around her cracks under exam pressure, Hope escapes into her drawings, until her parents disappear. Investigate what happened, connect the clues, and uncover the truth hidden beneath the city's calm.
NO NOTE. NO WARNING.
You come home from school like any other day. But the house is quiet. Your parents are gone, the apartment is in shambles. No note, no warning, no answers.
AN ARTIST'S EYE
Hope isn't a detective. And everyone she turns to seems intent on avoiding trouble. But with an artist's eye, she notices details others overlook, and that's what makes her dangerous to whoever's hiding the truth. Drawing is no longer an escape; it's her best chance to solve her parents' mystery.
Wherever Hope goes and whoever she speaks with, she finds elements that don't add up. Investigate each one and capture your observations as sketches in Hope's notebook. Every detail matters.
FROM OBSERVATION TO TRUTH
Combine Hope's sketches into insights, and keep adding new thoughts until they grow into breakthroughs. Piece by piece, sketch by sketch, watch the picture of what happened to your parents take shape, and grow darker than you ever imagined.
A CITY FULL OF SECRETS
Shenyang isn't just a backdrop, it's a character of its own. Rendered in a bold, stylized art style with an edge, every street, storefront, and shadowed alley is begging to be explored. Wander past neon signs and quiet corners, and let the city's striking visuals pull you deeper into its secrets.
WHO CAN YOU TRUST?
On the surface, it's just home: familiar streets, quiet neighbors, ordinary life. But beneath the quiet, something is hidden. Hope can't be sure who she can trust. And she can't afford to wait for someone to help her find the truth.
Hope in the City is made by the team behind the 2026 GDC Best in Play Winner Sky of Tides and the 2024 Peabody Award-nominated Eternal Spring.

items.content:
Assassin’s Creed Valhalla: The Most Requested Update, a free update bringing several player-requested and quality-of-life features to the game, is live today on PlayStation 5 and PlayStation 5 Pro. The update has new content, a progression update, and more, including:
New Game+
2 New Achievements
Enhanced Progression Mode option
New Power calculation
Master Assassin Naoe outfit
Upgraded PSSR optimizations
Animus Hub synchronization update
Play Video
The new PSSR update is exclusive to PlayStation 5 Pro players, giving them an even higher visual quality as they embark on or continue their Viking adventures in England. We spoke to Priscilla Nguyen, Engineering Studio Manager, to learn more about this update and why it’s essential for PlayStation 5 Pro players.
What can you tell us about the PSSR update for the PS5 Pro?
Priscilla Nguyen: It was about integrating the upgraded PSSR into the game, to have better graphics when upscaling at a better framerate. The upgraded PSSR is more efficient than the original, and easier to implement in the game source code.
The upgraded PSSR is an enhanced version, and slightly more efficient than the game’s current Temporal Upscaler. More importantly, it’s much crisper and more visually stable, giving you seamless and stunning environments to explore in England.
Why bring these improvements to Assassin’s Creed Valhalla?
PN: At Ubisoft, it is important to remain at the forefront of technological innovation to ensure players continue to benefit from the best possible gaming experience, and as the upgraded PSSR was already successfully integrated into our latest releases, Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced and Assassin’s Creed Shadows, we thought it would be great to have in Valhalla too. The Assassin’s Creed Valhalla update presented an excellent opportunity to integrate the upgraded PSSR, delivering a noticeably sharper and more visually refined image quality in 4K and smoothness with 60FPS.
One of the aspects players appreciated most about Assassin’s Creed Valhalla was the beauty and visual variety of its open world, from the snowy mountains of Norway to the flourishing meadows, robust forests, and frigid highlands of England. Now, with the new PSSR optimizations, those graphics have been enhanced and preserved to meet today’s technical standards and continue to deliver a high-quality, smooth visual experience for our players.
Assassin’s Creed Valhalla came out a few years before the PS5 Pro. Were there any challenges updating the visuals for PSSR?
PN: We didn’t need to overhaul the game’s content or visual assets. Instead, we leveraged the upgraded PSSR within our engine and rendering pipeline to enhance 4K image quality and deliver our Quality mode at 60FPS on PS5 Pro.
The interesting challenge was finding the right balance between image quality, performance, and integration within an existing game that was originally built years before the PS5 Pro existed. The upgraded PSSR proved to be a very efficient solution, allowing us to maximize the new hardware’s capabilities while delivering a noticeable visual uplift and stronger performance without requiring extensive changes to the game’s content, making it an effective way to modernize the experience for PS5 Pro players.
Play Assassin’s Creed Valhalla’s The Most Requested update today on PlayStation 5 and PlayStation 5 Pro!

Assassin’s Creed Valhalla: The Most Requested Update – New Game+, Rune Forge Update, New Resource, and More
items.content:
Summary
Assassin’s Creed Valhalla‘s The Most Requested Update is live now, a free patch that enhances your endgame experience.
The update brings New Game+, extended progression mode, new resources and rune upgrades, and more.
Lead Game Designer David Larouche shares his insights on creating a player-focused update.
Assassin’s Creed Valhalla’s The Most Requested Update is now live on XBOX Series X|S and XBOX One. This update brings several exciting new features to the game, giving you new ways to enjoy your Viking adventure. The Most Requested Update is centered around the addition of New Game+, one of the most fan-requested features for Assassin’s Creed Valhalla. The other features included in the patch all ensure that your endgame and New Game+ experience is fresh and challenging, with rewards that make it worth your while.
Here’s what you can expect to find in The Most Requested Update:
New Game+: This can be accessed after completing the Holy Day Quest. With each iteration of New Game+, the game will scale in difficulty to keep your experience challenging and rewarding
Mithril: A new resource that can be used to upgrade divine gear. You will get Mithril when receiving a piece of gear or interacting with a book of knowledge you already own while in New Game+, or it can be found in Nilfheim and Mastery and River Raid shops
Gear Upgrades: The maximum level for each piece of gear is now 27, up from 13
Looting Carbon, Nickel, and Tungsten in a Wealth Chest will instead give Platinum in New Game+
Extended Progression Mode: When active, gear upgrades, runes, and masteries contribute to your overall power level
Stash: A feature found in Ravensthorpe that allows you to store any piece of gear and any rune from your inventory
Rune Forge Update: Runes can be upgraded for silver from the menu, and can now be upgraded to the new Superior tier
Over 300 engravable runes have been added to the game
We spoke to Lead Game Designer David Larouche to learn more about the update and how the team keeps players at the forefront of everything they do.
What parts of this update are a direct response to community feedback?
David Larouche: The New Game+ feature was definitely the most requested feature from fans. Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is a massive game, but for some, playing it once is not enough. With this update, we are incredible excited to now allow our most dedicated Vikings to play through the adventure once again, but this time, with their endgame character.
How did the team ensure the requested features would meet player expectations?
DL: We wanted the New Game+ experience to not simply be a do-over; we wanted to allow players to keep climbing in power, feel a more granular progression, and to keep improving their characters. For all those reasons, we added an extended progression mode, further upgrades on all pieces of divine gear, a new tier of rune and over 300 possible new rune perks that can be engraved in the rune forge – and all of those features are available without New Game+ as well. With all those additional features, we believe that the New Game+ experience will encourage players to push Eivor to their full potential.
Were there any surprising challenges implementing any of these updates?
DL: I think the most surprising thing to us was that there weren’t really any big challenges that had us stumped. We managed to put a really strong team of devs who are experienced in adding New Game+ onto already existing games; the production process was incredibly smooth.
Is there a feature you’re most excited to see in the game?
DL: With the update, we’ve added basically every single perk that was on an item as a rune that can be engraved in the rune forge, regardless of if it was released in the extended experience, from an expansion, or even from the Store. I can’t wait to see how players use all of these different perks together and create all sorts of different synergies. I’m sure there are many overpowered combinations to be found!
Assassin’s Creed Valhalla had its final content update years ago. Why give The Most Requested Update to players now?
DL: Valhalla may have released its final content update years ago, but that doesn’t mean players stopped caring about the game, and neither did we. We know New Game+ is something the community has wanted for a long time, and when the opportunity came up to finally make it happen, we couldn’t wait to pursue it.[MB1] [BS2] Ultimately, it’s about giving longtime players another reason to return to a world they’ve invested so much time in, and to experience Eivor’s journey again from a different perspective while bringing along much of what they’ve earned along the way. The fact that some time has passed doesn’t make that experience any less meaningful to us, or, hopefully, to our players.
How important is the Assassin’s Creed community to the Assassin’s Creed team?
DL: Community is incredibly important to me and to the team. Personally, I check social networks regularly to see what players are talking about, and as a team, we pay close attention to feedback and conversations across the internet. We love seeing what players create and share around our games. That connection with community is incredibly rewarding, and it’s a big part of why we do what we do.

items.title: Nvidia’s RTX Spark GPU management feature appears to be heading to GeForce RTX GPUs
items.content:
Nvidia appears to be testing GPU App Prioritization for GeForce RTX graphics cards, weeks after introducing similar GPU resource management controls for RTX Spark devices. However, while the feature has appeared for some users in the Nvidia App, the company has yet to officially announce its arrival on GeForce hardware.
As spotted by Reddit users and highlighted by Wccftech, the new setting appears under System > Advanced in Nvidia App version 11.0.9.585. Screenshots show options for prioritising foreground or background applications. Community reports suggest the default profile uses an 80/20 split, while foreground prioritisation shifts that balance to 90/10. Custom settings reportedly allow ratios as high as 95/5.
Nvidia only just introduced similar GPU resource management controls for RTX Spark systems in late October, allowing foreground applications to share GPU resources with background AI workloads. If the same functionality is heading to GeForce RTX GPUs, it could potentially allow GPU resources to be prioritised between games and competing workloads, such as local AI models, rendering tasks or livestreaming software. However, Nvidia has not explained how the feature works on GeForce hardware, and the percentages shown in the app should not be interpreted as strict GPU utilisation limits.
Exactly what Nvidia's plans remain unclear. Reports indicate that some users can access the feature while others running the same Nvidia App version and recent drivers cannot. Nvidia's official release notes for version 11.0.9.585 make no mention of GPU App Prioritization, so it is unclear if this rollout was intended or not.

Steam’s ‘pre-release’ process now takes up to 4X longer due to “significant increase in submissions”
items.content:
Before a game can be published to Steam’s storefront, Valve will review the submission to ensure that the title is playable and free from any malware. Thanks to the recent influx of AI-generated games however, this process seemed to be taking much longer than the 3-5 days advertised. Valve has now officially acknowledged the delay, announcing that future game submission could now take up to 12 days to be approved.
Taking to their blog to make the announcement, Valve confirmed that they have been falling behind on their game approval process, writing:
“We've seen a significant increase in submissions for store page and build review in recent months, and have spent the last several weeks working to scale our process to match it. Though we still have a ways to go, we want to share the initial improvements that have shipped in the past weeks.”
While the full blogpost can be found HERE, some of the newly implemented checks include the following:
Devs must have played the game for at least 5 minutes through Steam directly
Achievements support must be completed
Store page must include 5 screenshots categorized as gameplay
Cloud save support must be checked beforehand
As part of this update, Valve has now officially offered an extended timeline for how long a submission could take to be verified, writing: “We aim to test every game build in a timely manner, typically within 3-5 business days. However, we're running a little behind right now and taking up to 12 business days.”
Though not outwardly stated, much of the “significant increase in submissions” can be attributed to AI-generated games, with recent reports revealing that half of all games released on Steam last month included an AI disclosure.
Whether these new checks will help to curtail the onslaught of AI games on Steam remains to be seen. Regardless, it appears as though customers are not the only ones being impacted negatively by the platform’s lax rules surrounding the controversial technology.

From Polish Museums to XBOX: Bringing the World of The End of the Sun to Life
items.content:
Some of the quests in The End of the Sun began in an unusual way – with objects we discovered in small museums across Poland. Sometimes, an old tool or a fascinating piece of traditional craftsmanship inspired us so much that we decided to build part of the game’s story around it.
When we first started creating The End of the Sun, a first-person adventure inspired by Slavic folklore, we wanted to build a world that would do more than tell an engaging story. We wanted it to feel truly alive, with every building, object, and detail having its own history.
As a Slavic sorcerer investigating the mystery of an abandoned village, you enter a world inspired by Polish culture, ancient beliefs, and traditions rarely explored in video games. To bring that world to life, we decided to look beyond our computer screens and explore the real places where pieces of this history are still preserved.
From Polish Museums to a Living Game World
One of the most important techniques we used was photogrammetry, which allowed us to bring real-world objects directly into the game as detailed 3D models.
We partnered with local ethnographic museums in Poland, including the Open-Air Museum in Szymbark and the Grociarnia Ethnographic Museum in Jastrzębia. Thanks to their support, we were able to scan hundreds of historical objects, including entire buildings.
We’ve always believed that we’re surrounded by remarkable cultural heritage worth sharing, and creating The End of the Sun gave us an opportunity to introduce some of it to players around the world.
There’s also something special about preserving these objects digitally. Over time, some of the original artifacts may deteriorate or disappear, but their digital recreations can help preserve a record of them for future generations.
After taking thousands of photographs during our research trips, we began recreating these objects and buildings inside the game. Even now, when we compare our original photographs with screenshots from The End of the Sun, we’re sometimes surprised by just how closely the virtual world resembles the real one.
But creating authentic-looking environments was only the beginning. We wanted these objects to become something more than decorations.
When Historical Artifacts Inspire Gameplay
From the start, our goal was to make historical objects an integral part of the experience, rather than simply filling the environments with interesting props. We wanted you to interact with them, discover how they worked, and learn something about the everyday lives of the people who once used them.
For example, one of the game’s quests introduces you to a traditional hand mill used for grinding grain into flour. You can examine its individual parts and discover how the mechanism works. Other quests involve using traditional tools for twisting rope or sharpening a knife.
We also included optional “Learn More” points throughout the game world. When you encounter an unfamiliar object, you can discover what it was used for and learn a little about its history.
This approach helped us introduce traditional crafts, customs, and Slavic beliefs naturally, without interrupting the adventure with lengthy historical explanations.
Interestingly, the relationship between historical artifacts and gameplay sometimes worked in the opposite direction. Instead of looking for objects to fit a quest we had already designed, we occasionally discovered an artifact so fascinating that we adapted parts of the story around it.
These objects also became an important part of environmental storytelling. A carpenter’s workshop or a collection of weaving tools can tell you something about a character’s profession, personality, and everyday life.
Sometimes, the environment can tell a story more effectively than dialogue. All you need to do is slow down, look around, and pay attention to the details.
In fact, approximately 80% of the objects you encounter while exploring the game’s locations were scanned from real-world originals. Each one carries small imperfections, signs of wear, and traces of its previous use – details that would be difficult to recreate with the same authenticity when modeling everything from scratch.
Walking through one of our cottages can sometimes feel like exploring a small, interactive museum. But rather than presenting these objects behind glass, we’ve placed them in a world where you can discover their purpose and the stories behind them.
Capturing the Details of Polish Culture and Nature
Our world isn’t built exclusively from museum collections. We also wanted to capture the beauty of Poland’s natural landscapes and the richness of its traditional craftsmanship.
While exploring the village and its surroundings, you will encounter rocks of different shapes and sizes that we scanned in local nature reserves. We also paid close attention to smaller decorative details. For example, the game features intricate bobbin lace from a local gallery, while cottage interiors and everyday objects are decorated with beautiful hand-painted floral patterns inspired by the village of Zalipie, famous for its colorful painted houses.
These details might seem small individually, but together they give the world its identity. They help make the village feel like a place where people once lived, worked, and celebrated their traditions. We wanted you to experience this cultural heritage naturally, through exploration and curiosity, rather than feeling as though you were being given a history lesson.
A Village That Changes with Time
Our approach to environmental storytelling extends beyond individual objects to the buildings themselves.
The cottages we scanned in open-air museums aren’t simply static 3D models placed into the game. Because The End of the Sun unfolds across all four seasons and different points in time, we carefully modified these buildings to reflect changes throughout the story.
A cottage might show signs of damage or neglect at one point, only to appear renovated at another. We wanted you to notice these differences and experience the passage of time through the environment itself.
Nature plays an equally important role in creating that atmosphere. We made sure the vegetation reflects the character of the Central European climate, with landscapes changing naturally between the seasons.
To make the world feel even more alive, we also recorded authentic sounds of nature ourselves, visiting outdoor locations throughout all four seasons. These recordings became part of the game’s soundscape, helping us recreate not only the appearance of these places but also their atmosphere. Combining real historical objects, carefully recreated buildings, changing seasons, and authentic environmental sounds allowed us to create something that feels both rooted in history and alive with mystery.
For us, the most fascinating part of this process was discovering how much character real objects already possess. Their imperfections, signs of age, and tiny details tell stories of their own. By bringing them into The End of the Sun, we hope players will feel a connection to the people, traditions, and places that inspired our world.
We can’t wait for you to explore this mysterious Slavic village, uncover its secrets, and discover these pieces of history for yourselves when The End of the Sun is out today on XBOX Series X|S.

Will you be able to harness your powers to stop the ancient powers and change the inhabitants’ fate?
The End of the Sun is a mystery-filled first-person adventure and exploration game set in a Slavic fantasy world. Fully kindled bonfires become gateways to time travel.

Each hearth you connect with is a unique investigation, filled with unusual riddles and serving as a gateway to the ancient Slavic world – a realm of magic, fantastic creatures, mythology, and forgotten rituals. Every fire of time you ignite is a piece of the larger tale.
2. UNLEASH THE POWER – Use the flames to travel through time and shape human destinies
Feel the might of the fire of time. Influence the paths of heroes’ fates – restore the course of events to its rightful track and discover new fragments of an epic story. Travel across four seasons, separated from each other by many years. Witness the lives of the same heroes at different stages, during the greatest Slavic festivals. Time and hearths are intertwined. Your actions affect the world around you – make changes and carefully observe the consequences.
3. INVESTIGATE – Explore a mysterious village, born from the real world and museum treasures
Hundreds of museum artifacts and entire buildings, brought into the game from the real world through photogrammetry, open before you a land where every detail matters. Freely roam the ancient village and its one-of-a-kind surroundings. As you explore this open world, conduct a supernatural investigation rooted in Slavic mythology – more authentic and immersive than ever before.

How The Challenge Shrine Will Change How you Play Halls of Torment
items.content:
Hello, adventurers!
The Lost Archives, the second DLC forHalls of Torment, is available now on XBOX! There’s also a large and free update for all players.From the swamps of our first DLC, the Boglands, we are marching into The Lost Archives, where cultists and forgotten knowledge await us.
You’re a new tormented Soul? Here’s a quick overview.
Halls of Torment is a horde survival game with roguelite elements, made in the style of the late-90s action RPGs: pre-rendered graphics, dark dungeons and lots of loot.
Set 30 minutes aside, pick a hero and try to survive as wave after wave of monsters closes in. You can take full control of your hero or use automatic attacks. What’s truly important are your choices: abilities, traits and items that can turn a good build into an unstoppable one. In the depths the Tormented Lords are awaiting, unique bosses that dominate their halls.
Between runs, quests unlock new heroes, abilities, items and blessings that make you permanently stronger, so every attempt takes you a bit further, even when you don’t make it out alive.
The Lost Archives adds a new hall and two new heroes: the Inquisitor, who maintains an iron defense with a harsh focus on retribution and judgement, and the Blood Apostle, who sacrifices her own health for immense gains. Each comes with new abilities, upgrades for existing ones and three full sets of equipment, opening up entirely new combinations.
Both heroes take existing mechanics and push them further. The Inquisitor heralds Block, Defense and Retribution, with several new Retribution items. It introduces two new mechanics: Judgement and Execution. Whenever the Inquisitor takes damage, he puts Judgement on all enemies around him, while his mace triggers Executions. Judgement stacks spread between enemies until they are triggered, then deal unblockable damage, a great way to get rid of strong enemies hiding in a swarm.
The Blood Apostle brings back Sacrifices, a mechanic that has barely featured in the game until now. She trades health for power. The higher her maximum health, the stronger her sacrifices, her health recovery and Affliction. This returning status effect now also jumps to the next enemy when a foe is slain. Preview Two New Ways to Play with XBOX Cloud Gaming
items.content:
Starting today, we’re rolling out two previews for XBOX Cloud Gaming. On supported Smart TVs, you can use your phone as a controller when you don’t have one nearby. In the US, you can also preview cloud connect with the new XBOX Nano Controller. It uses Wi-Fi to connect directly to your cloud gaming session, which can help make gameplay feel more responsive.
Both experiences are still being tested. Availability and supported games or devices may be limited while we learn from your feedback.
Use your phone as a controller on a Smart TV
Want to play a cloud game on your TV but don’t have a controller handy? In this preview, you can use a supported Android or iOS phone as your controller on a supported Smart TV. The controls open in your phone’s browser, so you don’t need a separate controller. Some games will also have controls tailored to how they play.
To try it, turn on Preview Features under Settings > Account in the latest supported Smart TV experience. When you launch a game without a physical controller connected, you’ll see an option to use your phone for that session.
The preview is rolling out today on supported TVs, in countries where XBOX Cloud Gaming is supported.
Try cloud connect with the XBOX Nano Controller
Players in the U.S. can preview cloud connect with the XBOX Nano Controller starting today. Instead of a Bluetooth connection to your TV, cloud connect uses your Wi-Fi to connect directly to the cloud server running your game. That can help reduce input latency, so gameplay may feel more responsive.
Cloud connect is still an early test, so it won’t work with every cloud gaming experience yet. For now, you can try it on supported Smart TVs and the web.
Ready to try it?
Set up your controller: Use the XBOX beta app on Android, or the Xbox Accessories app on PC, to set up cloud connect on your XBOX Nano Controller. XBOX Insider enrollment is required for setup through the PC app.
Connect to Wi-Fi: Follow the steps in the app to connect your controller to your Wi-Fi network.
Start playing: Open a supported XBOX Cloud Gaming experience and sign in with the same XBOX account used during setup. Your controller will connect through cloud connect.
Check out the cloud connect setup guide for detailed instructions: https://support.xbox.com/en-US/help/hardware-network/controller/cloud-connect.
Help shape what comes next
We’re testing both experiences to learn what works well and what needs improvement. If you have a suggestion or run into an issue, please share your feedback through the preview experience. We’ll use what we learn to help shape future updates.
How to provide feedback
For phone controller, you can share feedback right from your phone or through a supported Smart TV app:
On Your Phone: After scanning the QR code displayed on your TV to connect your phone as a controller, tap the Xbox icon in the top-left corner and select “Give Feedback.”
On Your TV:
Open the Guide by pressing the XBOX button on your controller or pressing the XBOX icon in the top left corner and selecting Give Feedback.
In the XBOX app’s main menu, click on the profile icon in the top right corner and select “Give Feedback”.
For cloud connect, you can submit feedback through the XBOX Accessories app on PC or the XBOX mobile app by selecting the “Feedback” icon.

Sony delays God of War Laufey out of crowded February release window
items.content:
February 2027's increasingly crowded release schedule has claimed its first major casualty. Sony Santa Monica has announced a delay for God of War Laufey, pushing the game out of February and into a new May release window.
God of War Laufey was previously scheduled to launch in February 2027, placing it alongside several other high-profile releases. However, in a statement shared on X, Sony Santa Monica confirmed that the game will now launch on the 20th of May 2027. The studio says the extra development time will be used to further polish the game ahead of release:
“Since the reveal of God of War Laufey in June, we've been deeply grateful to see so much excitement for Faye's journey through the Everywhen,” the studio said. “With this in mind, we've made the decision to delay God of War Laufey's release to May 20th 2027.”
The delay eases pressure on what was shaping up to be one of the busiest months in recent gaming memory. February already features a number of major releases, including Fable, Final Fantasy 14: Evercold and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis.
While delays are rarely welcomed by fans, a move of just a few months suggests Sony Santa Monica believes the project is close to the finish line. The studio says it intends to spend the additional time “putting in the finishing touches” and pushing the game to its “fullest potential” ahead of launch.

items.title: Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School – Become a Valedictorian with These Tips
items.content:
Summary
Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School is available November 5, 2026 on XBOX Series X|S and XBOX on PC, as well as XBOX Game Pass.
It expands on the timed escape room puzzles of the first Escape Academy, connecting them up into a huge, explorable, puzzle-filled campus.
Cram a little early studying in to start the school year off right with these tips for escape room novices.
For a certain kind of gamer, nothing lights them up more than the promise of a big space full of environmental puzzles. Puzzles can be tricky to make accessible, though, presenting a thin line sometimes between childishly easy and frustratingly difficult.
Fortunately, Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School fills a great niche: providing a mountain of puzzles, but with clear structure, unobtrusive in-game hints, and a colorful, family-friendly, punny presentation that’s perfect for enjoying with anyone in local or online co-op (but can be played entirely solo if that’s your bag). It’s available November 5, 2026 for XBOX Series X|S and XBOX on PC, as well as day one with XBOX Game Pass.
Like the original Escape Academy, Back 2 School features lots of discrete, timed and graded escape rooms, which are delightfully free from the constraints of budget, space and physics that limit their real-world counterparts. New for the sequel, however, is that between rooms you can explore the Escape Academy campus directly as a progressively expanding hub world, which is itself full of puzzles to solve and secrets to find.
I really liked this balance between the intensity of the timed escape rooms and the more low-pressure puzzle solving and exploration between them. Connecting up the escape rooms with an interactive, puzzle-filled environment instead of clicking through a menu of static images really elevates the whole experience.
After a few hours puzzling through the game’s opening hours (and many years of real-world escape room experience), I’ve put together the following general, spoiler-free tips for aspiring escape artists:
Have a pencil and paper ready
Old-school Myst fans know that sometimes the most powerful tool at your disposal is a simple pencil and paper. Many – if not most – of the game’s puzzles can be made much easier just through the cognitive offloading of getting it down on paper in front of you. Whether for a cipher or a sudoku, my notebook for this piece ended up getting used more to solve puzzles than anything else.
Check everything
First step in any room is to systematically make sure you look at anything interactable. Any given thing, however mundane looking, might just be a crucial component to a puzzle or a hint to solving one (or at least a fun pun). If you can pick it up or meaningfully interact with it, it’s there for a reason and you will need it eventually.
If you see something, say something
Like real-world escape rooms, Escape Academy 2 is best enjoyed with friends. During that initial step of scouring the room to catalogue everything you’re working with, be sure to say out loud whenever you find something that seems relevant. Countless escape rooms have timed out because people had all the pieces between them, but weren’t properly communicating.
Think backwards
Once you’ve assessed everything currently available to you, one useful way to sort the signal from the noise is by thinking backwards from your objective. What does it look like you’ll need to achieve the final goal, and where might you find that? Continue like that until you find a problem that asks for a solution you have ready to go.
Use hints
Just like a good real escape room will have staff on hand to gently guide you toward solutions when you’re stumped, Escape Academy 2 has a nice and unobtrusive hint system that you should feel no shame in using. If you ever feel stuck, pulling up a hint will direct you towards the next step, and the hints are broken down over multiple screens to click through with increasing specificity, so you can get just the nudge you need without having the solution presented directly, if you don’t want it. Relying heavily on hints will affect your grade, but you can absolutely still get an A grade while using one or two – you may in fact score higher from the saved time.
Have a side hustle
One new addition along with the explorable campus between escape rooms is a school currency that you can collect for completing optional side tasks for other students. These are individual little puzzles with no timer that reward Escape Bucks, which you will need at several points to progress through the story, so you’ll probably want to stay on top of those side tasks as you go, rather than having to go earn everything when you need it. You can also supplement your income by finding Escape Bucks tucked away all over campus – between couch cushions, in toilets, etc.

DIGITAL ESCAPE ROOMS DESIGNED BY MASTERS OF THE CRAFT
Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School features an all-new campaign boasting handcrafted, best-in-class escape rooms built by our team of veteran puzzle designers. But unlike real-life escape rooms, the puzzles in Escape Academy aren’t bound by those stuffy safety regulations: Spiked ceilings? Check. 100 foot drops? Check. And, most-dreaded of all… Final exams? Double check.
The curriculum here at the Academy is equal parts life-threatening and wacky, because what better way to learn than while confronting one's mortality.
EXPLORE A LIVING CAMPUS
In Escape Academy 2, the campus is one big puzzle room. Between classes, explore a sprawling, secret-filled hub with mysterious passage ways, hidden tunnels, and dangerous traps. Or chill out with your pals and take in all the *vibes* that student life has to offer.
Whatever the case, the Academy’s your new home away from home.
GRAB A CLASSMATE AND GET ESCAPIN’ WITH ONLINE OR COUCH CO-OP
Escaping with a friend has never been this fun. Escape Academy 2 features both online and splitscreen couch co-op support. And thanks to the new optional No-Timer Mode, students of all backgrounds can puzzle at their preferred pace.
DIVE INTO AN ALL-NEW NARRATIVE
Escape Academy 2’s all-new story has something for new and returning players alike! You’ll discover a dark mystery surrounding the school’s founding, leading to shocking new revelations about the very nature of The Academy. Connect with new teachers and familiar faces from the first game with an expanded curriculum offering character-driven storylines and puzzle-stuffed side quests!
GOING BACK 2 SCHOOL!
We’ve rebuilt the look of Escape Academy for the sequel, featuring new environments, tons of details, and even some snazzy new getups for our professors and pupils.
Plus, evil genius DJ Doseone is back with a sick round of fresh beats to chill and study to. The all-new OST provides the perfect audio background for puzzling.
So whatcha waiting for? It’s time to go…Back 2 School!

One of Nintendo’s Switch cartridge makers is getting out of the market
items.content:
One of Nintendo's suppliers for Switch game cartridges is reportedly exiting the business. According to industry analyst David Gibson, Macronix, which manufactures ROM chips used in Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 game cards, is phasing out its ROM division as the company shifts investment towards other forms of memory.
Writing on X, MST Financial Senior Analyst David Gibson brought attention to comments made by Macronix in its latest financial results. The company manufactures ROM chips used in Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2 game cards, but plans to discontinue development of new ROM products and will stop reporting ROM sales as a standalone category after the current quarter. According to Gibson, ROM accounted for just 5% of Macronix's revenue during the latest quarter, down significantly from 26% a year earlier.
While that may sound alarming for fans of physical games, there is currently no indication that Nintendo plans to abandon cartridges. Gibson notes that Macronix is not Nintendo's only cartridge supplier, meaning physical Switch game production should continue for the foreseeable future.
The news follows recent reports that Sony is repurposing facilities previously used for PlayStation game disc production as the wider games industry continues its gradual shift towards digital distribution. Unlike Sony's situation, however, there is currently nothing to suggest Nintendo is actively moving away from physical media, nor that Macronix's decision was influenced by Nintendo itself.

items.title: Spill Games hits ₹400 crore valuation after ₹100 crore Series A
items.content:
The ₹400 crore valuation represents a 3.5x jump from the startup's ₹115 crore seed-stage valuation in April 2026. (Photo credit: Entrackr)
Bengaluru-based mobile gaming startup Spill Games has raised around ₹100 crore ($10.5 million) in a Series A funding round led by Elevation Capital, taking its valuation to approximately ₹400 crore.
Existing investors Centre Court Capital and PeerCapital also participated in the round. According to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr, the latest allotment values the company at around 3.5 times its ₹115 crore valuation during its seed round in April 2026.
Elevation Capital invested ₹80 crore in the Series A, while Centre Court Capital and PeerCapital contributed ₹12.6 crore and ₹8 crore, respectively.
The funding comes as Spill Games looks to scale its existing portfolio, expand into new gaming categories and strengthen its technology capabilities. The company plans to use the proceeds for user acquisition, AI and technology development, and selective hiring.
How the cap table looks
Following the latest allotment, Elevation Capital has emerged as Spill Games' largest external shareholder, holding a 20% stake. Centre Court Capital holds 11.78%, while PeerCapital owns 8.93%.
Other investors include All In Capital, with 7.48%, and CRED founder Kunal Shah, who holds 0.68%. M-League Limited holds a 2.70% stake, according to the filings.
The company's three co-founders collectively retain 41.23% ownership. Om Misra holds 14.02%, while Tapan Ranjan and Harsh Garg each hold 13.61%.
The latest share allotment involved 6,094 compulsory convertible preference shares at an issue price of ₹1,65,110 per share, alongside 10 equity shares.
Building a mobile gaming portfolio
Founded in 2024 by former PlaySimple Games executives Om Misra, Tapan Ranjan and Harsh Garg, Spill Games is building an AI-led mobile gaming studio focused on free-to-play casual, puzzle and hybrid-casual games.
Its portfolio includes titles such as Cozy Finds, Sticker by Number, Zen Math Crossword, Bird Rescue Jam and Grill Master. The company is looking to build a diversified portfolio rather than depend on a single breakout title.
The startup had previously raised around ₹27 crore in its seed round in April 2026, co-led by Centre Court Capital and PeerCapital.
With its latest fundraise, Spill Games is looking to accelerate game development and scale titles that have gained traction with players. Its investment in AI and technology is also intended to strengthen its ability to develop and expand games for global audiences.
The ₹400 crore valuation marks a significant increase from its seed-stage valuation in April, while the latest cap table shows the founders retaining a substantial collective stake as the company brings in additional institutional capital.

items.title: Razer unveils £350 Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition controller
items.content:
Razer has announced the Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition, a limited-production PS5 controller priced at £349.99. Limited to 1,337 units worldwide, the controller features contactless TMR thumbsticks, six remappable buttons and support for up to 2000Hz polling on PC.
The Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition is built around a magnesium alloy chassis, helping to keep weight down to 260g. Razer has paired the metal construction with textured TPU grips, a semi-transparent glass touchpad and double-shot PBT buttons, giving the controller a noticeably more premium design than standard gaming pads.
Performance-focused features remain at the core of the package. The controller uses contactless TMR thumbsticks in a symmetrical layout and includes six remappable inputs, consisting of two additional shoulder buttons and four rear-mounted paddles. On PC, users can take advantage of Razer's HyperSpeed Wireless dongle for polling rates of up to 2000Hz. Button remapping, stick sensitivity adjustments and custom profiles can be configured through Razer Synapse or the Razer PS mobile app and stored directly on the controller.
Each controller also ships with a leatherette carrying case, interchangeable convex and concave thumbstick caps, replacement rear-button covers, an anodised aluminium removal tool and a USB Type-A to Type-C cable for wired play and charging. The package doesn't come cheap, however, with a £349.99 price tag.

items.title: Hator’s new wireless gaming mouse weighs 59g and costs under £35
items.content:
Hator has launched the Pulsar 4 Wireless gaming mouse in the UK. Combining a 59g lightweight design with tri-mode connectivity, optical switches and a PixArt sensor, the company is aiming to deliver enthusiast-focused features at a sub-£35 price point.
The Pulsar 4 Wireless is built around a PixArt PAW3315 optical sensor capable of up to 16,000 DPI, 35G acceleration and Motion Sync support. The mouse uses Hator x TTC optical switches rated for up to 100 million clicks, while textured side panels and 100% PTFE feet are designed to improve grip and glide performance. Hator also includes a spare set of PTFE feet in the box.
Connectivity options include 2.4GHz wireless, Bluetooth 5.1 and wired USB operation, with polling rates of up to 1000Hz. Hator claims the integrated 500mAh battery can deliver up to 110 hours of use between charges, while a detachable 1.8m paracord cable is included for charging and wired play.
Users can customise lighting, macros and button assignments through a browser-based configuration tool without installing dedicated software. For those who prefer a traditional application, Hator also offers its SyncHUB software for Windows 10 and Windows 11, while macOS support is expected later this month. The mouse comes available in both black and white colour options, priced at £34.99.

Thermal Grizzly unveils upgraded PhaseSheet PTM Pro thermal pad
items.content:
Thermal Grizzly has introduced the PhaseSheet PTM Pro, a new phase-change thermal pad designed for CPUs and GPUs. According to the company's own testing, the new pad delivered lower temperatures than the original PhaseSheet PTM, KryoSheet and Kryonaut Extreme thermal paste.
The PhaseSheet PTM Pro remains solid at room temperature and begins to liquefy at temperatures above 45°C. Thermal Grizzly says this helps reduce the pump-out effect that can occur over time as repeated heating and cooling cycles gradually displace thermal interface material. The material is also electrically non-conductive, making it suitable for use on CPUs, GPUs and other bare-die applications.
Thermal Grizzly has also updated the carrier film used with the pad. The company says the revised film can be removed cleanly from either side of the sheet, reducing the risk of tearing during installation and making the material easier to handle.
In Thermal Grizzly's testing, the PhaseSheet PTM Pro achieved a temperature delta of 5.83°C. By comparison, the original PhaseSheet PTM measured 6.36°C, while KryoSheet and Kryonaut Extreme posted results of 6.13°C and 6.87°C respectively.
The PhaseSheet PTM Pro is available now, with pricing starting at €19.90/$23.28.
