items.title: Bringing Jin Sakai back to life for Ghost of Yōtei: Most Wanted
items.content:
It’s been amazing to watch the response to Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition, from photo mode shots to Echoes of Sekigahara* reactions to flawless fights against Nobushige and beyond. But some of our favorite videos we’ve seen since launch feature Jin Sakai in Most Wanted*, and we’ve loved watching people tear through bounties as the returning Ghost of Tsushima.
With all of these great new moments featuring Jin, we wanted to dive into a little bit of the process behind bringing him back for Ghost of Yōtei, including all the tiny details that help make him feel like himself. Here’s some insight from some members of our team who helped bring him back to life.
How Most Wanted opened the door for Jin’s return
With Most Wanted our goal was to create a new way to experience Ghost of Yotei’s combat. We were excited to focus on challenge and mastery in a highly replayable format.
We wanted to give players new opportunities to grow stronger and master specific forms of combat, building on the foundation established in the main campaign. Very quickly the idea of a class-based, roguelike model emerged as a path to achieve these goals and as an opportunity to experience combat from perspectives other than only Atsu.
As the team got excited about the idea, plenty of production and logistical questions emerged about what would be possible. We thought Jin Sakai would fit perfectly in this mode, but we wanted to make sure we could deliver an experience that was authentic to his character. During the initial prototyping of Most Wanted, we started with other characters to prove out the idea and get a better understanding of what would be necessary to bring Jin back.
After an early playtest with Jin, I had a conversation with our Lead Combat Designer, Ted Fishman. The joy of playing with Jin again was undeniable, but something had become clearly apparent to Ted. There wasn’t a partial implementation that would deliver the fantasy of playing as Jin. No, if we were to push forward, we had to bring back all of Jin.
The team understood that bringing back Jin would be an ambitious challenge. It would involve the creation of new art assets, adapting to the evolution of combat mechanics between Tsushima and Yōtei, and much, much more. The requirements grew as we discussed the ultimate fantasy of ensuring Jin could play with all his Stances and use his iconic sticky bomb.
As the scope of the work became clearer, the team’s excitement only grew. Instead, everyone was so excited about the prospect of Jin’s return they continued to identify areas where we could deliver the best version possible, and we are so proud everyone can play that version today.
– Parker Hamilton, Systems Design Lead
Adapting Jin’s combat styles to work in Ghost of Yōtei
Playing as Jin Sakai in Ghost of Tsushima, you feel like a master swordsman. It took a lot of collaboration across disciplines to recreate that feeling and bring it forward into Most Wanted. By the end of production though, we were having a blast doing runs as Jin. It was honestly a big relief! It was gratifying to see him finally come back to form after many months.
Jin’s 60+ attack animations, most with their own bespoke kill animations, had to be retargeted to the new character rig, retouched (sorry Mark), and rebalanced for Ghost of Yōtei’s combat systems. Stone Stance’s Piercing Strike in particular decimated everything in Yōtei as originally implemented. In addition, Mark created custom strafe animations for each of Jin’s stances to support the new Focus Attack model (thank you Mark).
We wanted Jin’s perks to play into his classic feel. For example, classic Jin would immediately interrupt enemy combos with a well-timed press of the Block button. The distinction between Parry Deflect and Parry Interrupt didn’t exist in Ghost of Tsushima. In Most Wanted, the Rattling Parry perk causes Jin to deal more Stagger damage on successful parries, causing Parry Interrupt to happen more often. He also has a basket of perks that encourage Perfect Parry.
His unique fighting style is more than that though. Jin’s formally trained Stone Stance is complemented by his ability to dance between katana stances and scrappier tactics like his Quickfire. Empowering Quickfire even directly rewards following up Quickfire with melee.
A bunch of team members including our QA department contributed to filling out his set of perks. As we continued experimenting with the possibilities of Most Wanted, we really embraced the chaos and had a great time finding creative ways of having a great time, even bringing back Jin’s connection with the wind in perks.
Personally, I’m just glad people are having fun with Jin again out in the wild. I saw a clip that was something like, Jin flying through the air in bullet-time, head-shotting an enemy with a Tanegashima, following up with a Sticky Bomb, then a Water Stance flurry which triggered a lightning strike, and it had me beaming.
– Nate Slottow, Programmer
Reviving his animation styles and adding a nod to a cinematic Ghost of Tsushima moment…
When the Animation Team joined Most Wanted, we were ecstatic to bring Jin back into the game. The team was equally struck at the amount of effort we knew it would take to really bring back the whole essence of Jin, considering the amount of production time remaining. The Most Wanted team put an incredible amount of work into making it happen, and seeing Jin back again has been absolutely worth it.
As well as reviving more than 60+ combat animations, the team brought back Jin’s idle actions, which are iconic to his character. Near the end of production, the team had a great idea to incorporate Jin’s rarely seen “bird hold idle” into the Most Wanted menu. The character selection menu gave us an additional way to showcase each character’s demeanor. Jin’s selection animation was inspired by the cinematic moment in Ghost of Tsushima when Jin first recovers the storm blade.
Seeing all the fans’ reactions to Jin’s return has been absolutely awesome. Bringing Jin back to life has been a rewarding experience, and our team hopes everyone has as much fun playing Most Wanted as we’ve had.
– Mark Wheeler, Senior Staff Animator
…and keeping the character model and armor authentic to the original while adding visual updates
Jin Sakai has become an iconic character and has an equally iconic look. Reviving him to not just his former glory but matching the fidelity of Atsu was a challenge but an exciting one. Jin’s armor was one of the first things brought back. Fortunately, thanks to the stellar work of the artist who initially created it (Emre Ekmekci), a large portion of the model still held up. That left a lot of the hard work on the modeling side handled and the fun of giving it a new coat of paint as the primary challenge. Updating the metal, leather, and cloth to match how it looked during Tsushima, yet still have detail now possible in Yōtei, was a fine balance. I used his old texture files as a reference point to match materials to what they were before then added subtle details on top to push it that last 10%. I wanted to add some wear and age to the armor without disrupting how people remembered it.
Now that the armor was in a place we were happy with, the next hurdle was his face and hair. Skin textures, shaders, facial hair, everything had to be tackled and held next to Atsu to make it feel like they were both made in the same era. This was a challenge: I couldn’t tweak his skin too much or else he would look like a different character, but if I left things too unchanged he would look odd next to his counterpart. Using the same textures from Tsushima as a base, we built up from there, tweaking his skin tone, redness, lips, even his scar to look sharper and more defined. We also baked new normal maps to help push his skin detail a bit further. A lot of intentionality went into bringing him back.
Once everything came together, being able to see him posed in all his glory was a real spark of joy. It was an honor to have a part in bringing this character back to life. Seeing fan reactions to his reveal and their excitement while they fight through bounty after bounty has been a highlight of my career.
– Nate Ramsey, Character Artist
Redesigning audio, a new take on Jin’s musical theme…and bringing back Daisuke Tsuji
It was so fun to revisit Jin Sakai and revive many of his special attacks. We took great care in reviving iconic moves like the Heavenly Slash, Dance of Wrath and even Jin’s Ghost Stance directly from the assets used in Ghost of Tsushima.
Reviving his musical theme, including the amazing new version we recorded with Justin Johnson on lap steel guitar, was another fun aspect we knew fans would love to hear.
One of the biggest considerations in bringing Jin back to life was his character movement sounds. We completely overhauled the way we handle character movement sounds between Ghost of Tsushima and Ghost of Yōtei so we needed to take Jin’s old sounds and rebuild them in a way that stayed true to the original, while supporting our new, more dynamic animation tagging system. One of our sound designers, Chris Walasek, took all of our assets we recorded for Jin’s iconic Ghost armor and re-designed his movement sounds to match this new system ensuring the transients of Jin’s movement sounds were consistent with our other characters.
We also knew, when first considering bringing Jin into the world of Ghost of Yōtei: Most Wanted, it wouldn’t be possible without the voice of Jin himself, Daisuke Tsuji. Getting Daisuke back into the booth was a great experience as always. He’s a brilliant actor and really fun to riff with. Hearing his takes on the confrontations with each Yotei 6 member brought us big smiles during the recording sessions and even allowed us to sneak a few Jin lines into the main game.
We hoped fans would be excited to play this fun new mode with one of their favorite characters, and it has been a joy watching as they’ve repeatedly struck down the Yōtei Six with everyone’s favorite samurai-turned-Ghost.
– Rev. Dr. Brad Meyer, Audio Director
We were really excited to work with Daisuke Tsuji again and bring back Jin while staying true to the character. From an art perspective, Jin was originally created for PS4, while Yōtei was built entirely for PS5, so our rendering technology has come a long way. Our goal was to maintain the familiarity of his original design while bringing him forward with the visual fidelity of Yōtei.
This time around, we could push much more detail into his face, hair, clothing, and especially his armor, while keeping the shapes players remember. We also wanted to bring back his iconic imagery and gestures, like the quiet moment before a duel where his thumb pushes the tsuba, and the way he wipes blood from his blade after a kill.
For us, it really came down to honoring Jin while applying everything we’ve learned artistically and technically since Tsushima, and I am so proud of the way everything came together.
– Joanna Wang, Production Art Director
*Internet connection, account for PlayStation, and patch v.2.0 or later required.

November’s Humble Choice line-up available now
items.content:
Each month, all those with a Humble Choice subscription are privy to a selection of 8 games or so for the relatively low price of £11.49. Available now, November’s line-up has been officially published, including the likes of Mafia: The Old Country; The Outer Worlds 2 and half a dozen others.
Available to add to your PC library right now, November’s Humble Choice line-up features the following:
Mafia: The Old Country + DLC
The Outer Worlds 2 [Battle.net]
Shinobi: Art of Vengeance
Yakuza 6: The Song of Life
Crisol: Theater of Idols
Space Haven
Dysmantle
Squeakross: Home Squeak Home
For many, the headliner of the month is Mafia: The Old Country. Released back in 2025, this prequel proved to be a hit with many who are fans of the franchise. Offering a tighter experience more comparable to that of the first two entries (as opposed to the more generic open-world of Mafia III), The Old Country – while not without its flaws – is worth checking out.
The Outer Worlds 2 meanwhile is a well-regarded RPG from the team at Obsidian Entertainment. Also released last year, the title was seen as an improvement over the original across the board; particularly when it comes to gameplay and roleplaying. As with the first game however, opinions on its story and characters will vary depending on your personal preferences. All that said, for those who prefer Steam as a platform, Humble is unfortunately only offering keys for The Outer Worlds 2 via Battle.net.
Full details on this month’s offerings, including November’s charity of choice, can be found HERE.

Mark's enthusiasm for computers dampened at an early age by the rubber-keyed Sinclair Spectrum 48K and feelings of Commodore 64 envy. However, in the mid-80s, hope in a digital future was rekindled by the purchase of an Atari 520 STe. Since that time Mark has used a multitude of computers for fun and professional endeavors. He often owned both Macs and PCs but went cold on the former after OS9 was killed off, and warmed to the latter with the introduction of Windows XP.

Early work years were spent in artwork and reprographics but in the late noughties, Mark started to blog about computers, Taiwanese food culture, and guitar design. This activity led to a full-time position writing about breaking PC tech news for HEXUS, for the best part of a decade. When HEXUS was abruptly closed, Mark helped with the foundation of Club386, before finding a new home at Tom's Hardware.

When not wearing through the keycap legends on his PC keyboards, Mark can be found wandering the computer malls of Taiwan's neon-lit conurbations and enjoying local and international cuisine.

items.title: Call of Duty Warzone Season 1 officially launches this Friday
items.content:
With the launch of a brand new entry in Activision’s annual Call of Duty series comes the arrival of a new iteration of the franchise’s Warzone Battle Royale. In alignment with Modern Warfare 4 Season 1, Infinity Ward / Raven Software have detailed everything coming to Warzone when it officially goes live later this week.
While the team previously shared its Season 1 roadmap for the multiplayer and DMZ portions of Modern Warfare 4, the ‘Call of Duty Staff’ have now offered a look at everything coming to the refreshed Warzone when it goes live on the 6th of November.
As always, being the first Season following the arrival of a brand new COD, the full list of changes and additions is lengthy. That said, some of the most notable include:
Movement and gameplay overhaul to align with MW4’s mechanics
You can drag teammates out of harm’s way
Added air assassinations
No more omnimovement
Full integration with MW4 (weapons, equipment, Apex Attachments etc…)
Includes Zipline launcher, Grabber Drone
Overhauled perks
Brand new Battle Royale map: Hajin
Features variable weather conditions
Gulag now comes in two different variants/layouts
Brand new Resurgence map: Zodiac
New interactive objects
Legacy weapons (from MW2–BO7) are no longer customisable
Updated Battle Royale map: Verdansk [in-Season]
Updated Resurgence map: Rebirth Island [in-Season]
As mentioned, the full minutiae of everything being changed can be found HERE, and goes into specifics regarding each and every perk; mastery camo; field upgrade; vehicle and more.

That one local eccentric he came to love is nowhere to be seen. There’s a Starbucks — or an archery range, I mean — in town now. Seriously? But underneath the jarring changes that taunt your memory, you know that the place that you love is still there. You can feel its heart beat when you plant yourself in the shade of that tall tree you played around as a kid.

Jowi Morales is a writer and journalist covering the tech beat since 2021. However, he’s been interested in technology far earlier than that. He started discovering desktop computers when his father brought home a Windows 95 PC, but his first real experience working under the hood of the PC was when the old computer’s hard drive was filled to the brim in the year 2000. He deleted the Windows folder to attempt to rectify the situation, which led to his dad buying a new desktop PC. Since then, he learned a lot more about computers, and he’s always been the go-to tech expert for his family and friends.

Jowi primarily uses a Windows workstation and an Android phone, but he also bought into the Apple ecosystem with the 6th-gen iPad, iPhone 14 Pro Max, and the M1 MacBook Air. Today, Jowi covers hardware and software from Redmond and Cupertino, while also looking at the tech industry in general.

Aside from covering technology, Jowi is an avid photographer and writes about automobiles, aviation, and tanks. You can find his bylines at MakeUseOf, SlashGear, and, of course, Tom’s Hardware.

Lords of the Fallen 2’s relatively modest budget has been revealed
items.content:
While there was once a time when a game having a massive budget was viewed as a positive by fans, the recent inflation seen across most game studios has shifted this mentality quite a bit – especially as said games are requiring an ever-increasing number of sales in order to just break even. As such, it comes as a breath of fresh air that the team at Hexworks have managed to develop the upcoming Lords of the Fallen 2 for “just under €55 million.”
Following the release of their reboot for Lords of the Fallen in 2023, studio Hexworks would go on to begin developing a sequel – officially announcing Lords of the Fallen 2 during Gamescom last year. Initially slated to arrive in late 2026, the game was eventually delayed to Q1 2027 in order to move out of the way of GTA VI.
Despite this delay, it appears as though Lords of the Fallen 2 has managed to maintain a relatively svelte budget, with publisher CI Games founder and CEO Marek Tyminski taking to Twitter to write:
“Production, global marketing, and launch: funded. We are targeting a total dev and marketing budget just under €55M. Now the only job left is the one that matters. Ship a great Lords of the Fallen II.”
Tyminski made sure to note that “the game is not finished,” clarifying that “production continues and is soon moving to pure polishing” – a factor likely calculated into their 55 million estimate.
Of course, video game budgets are a complex topic with countless factors going into the equation, including but not limited to salaries; overheads and variances based on where the studio is located.
Either way, given that 2023’s Lords of the Fallen has sold around 2.5 million copies with a similar budget, it is encouraging to see the team managing to produce its sequel for roughly the same cost.

Multiple companies are reportedly interested in acquiring Arkane Studios, potentially securing the future of one of gaming's most respected immersive sim developers. The timing is particularly significant given that Arkane is currently working on Marvel's Blade, which was announced in 2023. According to Bloomberg, any deal would likely allow development to continue uninterrupted, with the game still expected to launch within the next few years.

items.title: Corner Shop: NightShift How we Built Horror Around an Ordinary Life
items.content:
Summary
Out now on Xbox Series X|S and PC with XPA.
Try to rebuild your life facing serious family problems and deteriorating mental health.
How working with psychologists informed our approach to mental health without resorting to simple horror tropes
When people think about psychological horror, they usually think about abandoned buildings, monsters, strange rituals, or someone being chased through a dark corridor.
With Corner Shop: NightShift, I wanted to begin somewhere much more ordinary.
A job.
Adam Callahan works the night shift in a small convenience store. He receives deliveries, puts products on shelves, cleans the floor, scans groceries, checks the cameras and deals with customers. Most of these things are not frightening by themselves. They are things thousands of people do every night.
And that was exactly the point.
Adam is trying to do a normal job while the rest of his life is anything but normal. His relationship with his wife has fallen apart. He has lost contact with his daughter. His financial situation is bad, his mental health is deteriorating, and at the same time he still has to get up, go to work and somehow make it through another shift.
This contrast became one of the most important parts of the game.
Horror Between Completely Normal Things
We did not want Adam’s problems to exist only in cutscenes and then disappear when gameplay starts.
You can have a difficult conversation and, a few moments later, a customer is waiting at the counter. You still have shelves to refill. Something needs cleaning. A delivery arrives. The store does not stop because Adam is having a bad night.
That happens in Real Life Too.
People dealing with serious mental health problems, family conflict, separation or financial pressure very often still go to work. They still talk to customers and coworkers. They still pay bills. From the outside, their day can look completely ordinary.
That idea became more interesting to me than simply creating another horror game where everything around the player is obviously dangerous.
In Corner Shop: NightShift, sometimes something really is wrong. There are blackouts, alarms, disturbing customers and events that should not be happening. But other times, Adam himself is no longer certain what happened.
Did something move on the security camera?
Was somebody actually standing there?
Did Adam remember that conversation correctly?
Or is stress changing the way he understands what is happening around him?
That uncertainty is where much of the horror comes from.
Getting the Conversations Right
Once we decided that Adam’s mental health and family situation would be important parts of the story, we also knew that we had to be careful with them.
It is very easy to write a dramatic conversation about mental illness. It is much harder to write one that sounds like two actual people talking.
During development, we discussed the subject with psychologists experienced in serious mental health conditions as well as specialists familiar with difficult family situations. This was especially important for scenes involving Adam’s psychologist and conversations with his wife. Dialogues and cutscenes touching these subjects were developed and reviewed with specialist input. We did not do this because we wanted the game to feel like a medical textbook. It is still a fictional psychological horror game, and at times we deliberately exaggerate situations to create tension.
What we wanted to avoid were the easiest shortcuts.
A psychologist should not simply appear to explain the plot to the player. A wife dealing with a collapsing family should not exist only to make the protagonist feel guilty. And Adam should not become nothing more than a collection of symptoms. He is a person before he is a horror protagonist.
He can be tired. Angry. Funny. Defensive. He can make good decisions and terrible ones. He can misunderstand somebody, or somebody can misunderstand him.
Mental illness itself was never supposed to be the monster.
The frightening part is losing confidence in your own situation while still being expected to function normally.
You’re Still Doing the Night Shift
We also wanted the simulation side of the game to remain important. You still need to run the store. Customers need serving. Deliveries need handling. Security can be improved with cameras, alarms and stronger locks. Money matters, and Adam’s decisions matter.
As the story develops, these ordinary systems start mixing with what is happening to Adam. A security camera is useful because you need to protect the store, but it can also make you question what you saw.
Working longer gives you money you need, but exhaustion has consequences. Something as simple as finishing another shift can start feeling like an achievement. The story does not stop the simulation. The simulation becomes part of the story.
Adam’s Story is Not Only About Falling Apart
There are dark parts of Corner Shop: NightShift, but Adam’s story is not simply about watching someone collapse. You make choices throughout the game, and those choices influence what you discover and which of the game’s four endings you reach. For me, that was important.
You cannot magically solve every problem Adam has, because people do not work that way. But you can decide how to react to them. This was part of the real human experience we were looking for. Sometimes psychological horror works best when the strange part is surrounded by something completely familiar.
A fluorescent light above a checkout. The sound of a refrigerator at 3:00 AM. An empty CCTV screen. A phone call you do not want to answer.
And then another customer walks through the door, and you still have a job to do.

Corner Shop: Nightshift is a first-person narrative horror sim set in a failing convenience store.
Play as Adam Callahan and try to put your life back together.
Story Mode: ~15 hours at an average pace, with 4 endings based on player choices.
Endless Mode: Infinite gameplay focused on growing and managing the store, with ongoing horror elements.
A night shift and a broken life. Blackouts, alarms, and unsettling customers pull you into a puzzle you can’t escape. Find the truth, manage your stress, and don’t let paranoia win. Take your meds. Keep going.
Stock shelves, clean up, take deliveries, scan items, and serve customers with snacks, sandwiches, and kebabs. Upgrade the store with cameras, alarms, and stronger locks. Manage your time, your money, and your sanity. Meds don’t pay for themselves.
You play as Adam Callahan. His wife is gone, his daughter was taken, and his life is falling apart. He works the night shift to prove he can start over, but the store keeps dragging his past back to the surface, out of order and out of his control. Your choices shape what you uncover and which ending you reach.

items.title: AOC’s new OLED monitor offers 4K 240Hz and 480Hz modes
items.content:
AOC has unveiled the Agon Ultra AGP277UZD gaming monitor on its Chinese website, featuring a 26.5-inch tandem WOLED panel with an RGB subpixel layout. The display runs natively at 4K and 240Hz, while a built-in dual-mode feature allows users to switch to 1080p at up to 480Hz.
As spotted by HardwareLuxx, the monitor features a 0.03ms G2G response time, 10-bit colour depth and a 1,500,000:1 contrast ratio. AOC rates peak HDR brightness at up to 1000 nits and includes VESA DisplayHDR True Black 400 certification. The monitor also covers 100% of the sRGB colour gamut and 99% of DCI-P3, while supporting Adaptive Sync and G-Sync compatibility.
Connectivity is headlined by a full-bandwidth 80Gbps DisplayPort 2.1 connection, alongside two HDMI 2.1 ports and a USB-C port with DisplayPort Alt Mode and 98W Power Delivery. AOC has also included a USB hub, integrated KVM switch and PiP/PbP functionality for users connecting multiple devices.
The included stand offers 150mm of height adjustment, alongside tilt, swivel and pivot functionality. AOC has also integrated a CMOS-based presence sensor that can detect when a user steps away from their desk, helping to reduce power consumption and minimise the risk of OLED burn-in. For now, the Agon Ultra AGP277UZD has only been announced for the Chinese market, with no word yet on pricing or availability in Western regions.
KitGuru says: Dual-mode OLED monitors are becoming increasingly common, but full-bandwidth DisplayPort 2.1 support and a tandem WOLED panel certainly help this display stand out.

items.title: D&D’s World of Warcraft Crossover Is the Bold Shake-Up the Game Needed
items.content: Wizards of the Coast has been playing things safe since updating the rules of Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition in 2024. After lead designers Jeremy Crawford and Chris Perkins left Wizards in 2025 to join Critical Role’s Darrington Press, Wizards slowed the pace of new D&D releases. AI Is Changing How Semiconductor Fabs Work — and Engineers Are Moving Faster Because of It
items.content:
Demand for advanced chips is rising. The processes to build them are getting more complex. And the margin for error is shrinking.
For engineers, understanding how a process change will behave, how a material will interact with a new step, how a defect maps back to a root cause are critical, challenging steps in semiconductor manufacturing — and these analyses can take days. Physical experiments on a fab line are slow and expensive. A wrong call on yield or process quality has real consequences.
AI is transforming semiconductor manufacturing, impacting what engineers can do — and how fast.
Accelerated computing shortens simulation time, allowing engineers to evaluate more alternatives before committing to physical trials.
Physics-based AI helps engineers predict process behavior without running a full simulation every time.
AI agents handle sequences of engineering tasks that once consumed hours.
And digital twins let teams test changes in a virtual environment before committing to physical trials.
Together, these capabilities describe an AI-defined fab: a semiconductor manufacturing factory where AI helps engineers optimize processes, catch problems earlier and make better decisions across the full manufacturing chip lifecycle. Engineers direct the work and make decisions based on their expertise while spending less time waiting for answers.
Shorter Simulation Cycles Change What Engineers Can Explore
Accelerated computing doesn’t just speed up individual calculations — it changes how many alternatives engineers can test before committing.
Multiphysics simulations model interactions among physical effects, such as heat transfer, electrical behavior and mechanical stress.
Using the NVIDIA cuDSS library, multiphysics software provider COMSOL is accelerating such simulations for semiconductor manufacturing by up to 10x. This helps engineers optimize equipment and processes, compare alternatives and decide which changes to test physically.
Applied Materials and NVIDIA are collaborating to accelerate atomic-scale materials discovery and process development. By integrating NVIDIA cuDSS, Applied’s Ginestra simulation platform runs up to 10x faster than CPU-only approaches. And with NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo, Applied’s ACE+ multiphysics platform delivers topography simulations up to 35x faster.
In some cases, acceleration doesn’t just shorten the calculation — it enables it altogether. Computational lithography — which defines how circuit patterns are printed onto silicon — involves calculations too intensive to complete on CPU at production scale. Siemens is integrating NVIDIA cuLitho into its Calibre lithography software, delivering up to 17x acceleration on key simulation workloads. That expands what engineers can verify before a wafer goes to print.
As such, faster calculations can help researchers explore material behavior and reaction pathways that influence next-generation semiconductor processes.
Predicting Process Behavior Without Running Every Simulation
In addition to accelerating simulations, AI trained on physics can predict how materials and processes will behave — without running a full simulation each time.
The payoff is most visible in complex calculations that are expensive even on accelerated hardware.
Plasma — the electrically charged gas used in semiconductor etch processes — is one example. Modeling plasma behavior requires solving equations that capture how electrical, chemical and thermal processes interact, making repeated simulation costly. Lam Research demonstrated that the NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo framework can predict plasma behavior in milliseconds, compared with days for a full simulation — giving engineers a faster way to explore process conditions without rerunning the full model each time.
Applied Materials uses digital twins built on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to simulate fab-level optimizations in layout, throughput, cost and process control.
Agents Handle the Steps Between Decisions
Engineers turn analyses into decisions — revising a design, investigating a test failure, adjusting a production process and more.
AI agents can help carry out the steps between those decisions.
Evaluating which AI model to apply to a given task is one example: a sequential, manual process that can consume hours on the test floor.
Advantest is using NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard AI agents to automate that selection, reducing response times from hours to minutes.
Testing Factory Changes Before They Reach the Line
Digital twins let teams simulate equipment configurations, layouts and process changes in a virtual environment before committing to physical trials. This reduces experimentation costs, especially as fabs become more complex and the stakes of a wrong change get higher.
A photorealistic fab digital twin built with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries, used to simulate material flow, spot bottlenecks and validate operational strategies before deployment. Image courtesy of Applied Materials.
Applied Materials uses NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to build physically accurate digital twins of entire fabs. Teams can simulate material movement, identify bottlenecks and evaluate layouts and operating strategies — extending virtual experimentation beyond individual processes to how the factory works as a whole.
The Connected Loop
The future of semiconductor manufacturing lies in connecting these capabilities: using production data to inform models and models to evaluate changes, then bringing those findings back to the engineers making production decisions.
That’s the promise of the AI-defined fab: where AI helps people learn from each production cycle and act on that knowledge sooner.
Explore how NVIDIA is working with semiconductor leaders across the chip lifecycle.

items.title: The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel revealed in new teaser
items.content:
The Elder Scrolls VI finally has a name. After years of speculation, Bethesda has officially revealed that the next entry in the series is titled The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel, confirming long-standing fan theories about the game's setting in the process.
A newly released teaser offers little in the way of gameplay or story details, instead focusing on a brief cinematic sequence. The trailer shows sand being swept away to reveal an Elder Scrolls scroll, which then unfolds into the game's title reveal. More importantly, the teaser confirms that the city of Sentinel and the province of Hammerfell will play a central role in the upcoming RPG.
The reveal won't come as a huge surprise to Elder Scrolls fans. For years, players have dissected the original teaser trailer, developer comments and in-game references in search of clues about the sequel's setting, with Hammerfell consistently emerging as one of the leading theories. The latest teaser appears to finally put those rumours to rest.
While Bethesda stopped short of revealing any gameplay, the teaser does include a small lore snippet, a quote from Yazar, Moth Priest to High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell, spoken during the year 4E 206: “The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate.”
For now, Bethesda has provided little beyond the title and setting confirmation, so there is still no word on when we might see more of the game, or when it will release.

items.content:
Nearly two months after debuting in NBA 2K27, Nvidia's DLSS 5 technology is finally headed to more games. Nvidia has announced that Hogwarts Legacy, War Thunder and Where Winds Meet will all receive DLSS 5 updates this month, marking the first wave of new titles to adopt the technology.
The highest-profile addition is Hogwarts Legacy, which will gain DLSS 5 support on the 5th of November. The update adds 3D-Guided Neural Rendering for RTX 50-series users, with Nvidia claiming improvements to lighting, materials and environmental detail. According to Nvidia, the game can run at up to 300FPS at 4K on an RTX 5090 when paired with DLSS Multi Frame Generation, Ray Reconstruction and other DLSS technologies.
While DLSS 5 was one of the headline features introduced for the RTX 50-series generation, adoption has been noticeably slower than previous DLSS releases. Until now, NBA 2K27 has been the only title to support the technology. The arrival of three additional games in November suggests developers are beginning to embrace the feature, although the rollout remains considerably slower than previous DLSS iterations.
Hogwarts Legacy won't be the only game updated this month. War Thunder will gain DLSS 5 support through its Eagle's Shadow update in mid-November, while Where Winds Meet will add support on the 23rd of November in North America and the 24th of November globally. Nvidia also announced additional DLSS updates for several other games, including Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Phantom Blade Zero, Hunting Simulator 3 and GRAVHOUNDS.

We sat down with the development team of Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds to get some behind the scenes details about the road to Year Two.
In Year Two, several new features have been added to further expand the ways players can enjoy CrossWorlds, including Duel Mode, new Gadgets, and the Super Slot. How did the team approach designing these additions?
Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds dev team: One of the core appeals of CrossWorlds is the ability to discover your own play style and refine how you race as you continue to play and gain experience. For Year Two, our goal was to expand those possibilities even further.
For example, Duel Mode was created to offer a different experience from the standard 12-player races by focusing on the unique strategy that comes with one-on-one competition. By letting players focus on their distance from their opponent and how they use items, races can unfold in entirely different ways.
Gadgets are another feature that allows players to experiment and discover combinations that best suit their personal play style. In Year Two, we’re introducing the Super Slot, a dedicated slot for one-slot Gadgets. The Gadget placed in that slot will have its effects enhanced, opening up even more possibilities for combinations and strategies.
New strategies emerge from both the race rules and the choices players make with customization. With Year Two, we aimed to create a game that continues to offer new discoveries every time you play.
Some eagle-eyed fans might have noticed that one of our bonus exclusives for Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds Year Two Digital Deluxe Edition and Season Pass Two first appeared online as an April Fool’s joke… and they’re right!
The Sega Consoles Pack, featuring three vehicles inspired by Sega’s historic consoles, make their debut in Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds. But turning a video game console into a racing vehicle is no easy feat. We decided to dive in a bit more with the dev team on how they chose to design the vehicles while maintaining the iconic consoles’ identities.
The Sega Consoles Pack features vehicles inspired by classic Sega hardware. What design choices did the team make to evoke a sense of nostalgia?
We incorporated design elements that instantly remind players of each console, such as their colors, shapes, and button layouts. The Dreamcast’s rounded form and distinctive color scheme, as well as the Genesis and Sega Saturn’s angular silhouettes and subdued tones, are all expressed as part of each machine’s identity. We also recreated the Dreamcast’s Visual Memory Unit (VMU) using original reference data from the era.

items.title: The Silver Seas and How We “Ship” New Features for Age of Wonders 4
items.content:
Summary
The Silver Seas, the latest expansion for Age of Wonders 4, is out now and is loaded with pirates, sharks, and more things our players have been asking to see.
Community reactions to the game have helped shape the new things we’re adding today and in the future.
Also, there is a sea shanty, because why shouldn’t there be a sea shanty?
Ahoy there, folks! I’m the Captain of Age of Wonders 4, a game we’ve been sharing with you for either four years or twenty-seven years, depending on how long you’ve been playing the series. Everyone here at Triumph Studios has spent a lifetime coming up with fantastical ideas to add to our games, but now that Age of Wonders 4 is entering its fourth year and kicking off its fourth set of expansions, it’s officially the longest-running title in the franchise in terms of ongoing support.
It makes me proud to work on a game whose players are still hungry for more new stuff, from dragons to vampires to otherworldly terrors beyond comprehension. It makes me even more proud to have players who are so enthusiastic that we have enough great suggestions and ideas from all of you that we can make entire expansions themed around your requests, which is what The Silver Seas is all about. It’s out today, and it’s loaded with goodies that you’ve asked to see!
Let’s start with Pirates. Age of Wonders 4 is a game where your empires and armies sprawl across forests, deserts, underground caverns, on land and at sea, but our players have been asking for more seabound gameplay since launch. Of course, you all made it very clear that you didn’t want to expand onto the sea without being able to build your own swashbuckling pirate fantasies in the process, so we started there. The heart of The Silver Seas is the new Mercantile Culture, which allows you to place cities at sea, and transform them into floating fortresses to rule the waves. We built around two different “flavors” of piracy, adding the Cartel, who grow through smuggling and secrecy, and the Barony, who use their lavish fortunes to place bounties on their enemies and import whatever their empire needs.
Of course, we couldn’t do an aquatic expansion without adding some watery new forms for your people to take. The Silver Seas comes with Sharkkin and Aqualon, two seafaring people who are both, believe it or not, based on player suggestions in their own ways. The Aqualon made their debut (sort of) as a piece of concept art that we shared with our community while working on the Eldritch Realms expansion. So many of you commented that it was a unique and intriguing design that we decided to dive back in and explore what they might become! As for the Sharkkin, every time we’ve asked players what sort of new people we ought to add to the game, there has always been a healthy portion of “Sharks!” in the responses.
Now that we can see how that looks, yeah, fair enough; you were right. Just look at these smiling faces.
Once we had all of these ideas to build out The Silver Seas, the rest came together with designs that just made sense. If we’re going to play out in the water, we ought to add a Magic Tome that uses water magic, and ice magic is a natural progression for water magic. We didn’t add any vapor magic this time around, but who knows? We also added new Pirate Dwellings and pirate-themed stories, terrifying sea creatures to battle, and so much more.
I especially want to thank all of our players for these ideas because it’s not just all of you who get to enjoy playing your Inner Pirate selves. We’ve been indulging in all things buccaneer and swashbuckler here at Triumph, and it’s finally given us an excuse to write a Sea Shanty for work. As you sail The Silver Seas, may this tune keep your compass straight and your sails full. We’ll be seeing ye, me hearties!

Seek powerful tomes of magic to enchant your armies and evolve your people! See your people physically change as they morph into angelic beings or scions of chaos to face their enemies. items.title: Cougar DuoAir Review – Glass or Mesh?
items.content:
The Cougar DuoAir gets its slightly clunky name from the inclusion of two front panels in the package. The default panel is clear glass but you can switch to the alternate metal mesh panel in a matter of moments. No matter which panel you select the two 140mm ARGB fans in the front of the case shine through brightly and the overall effect of our finished PC is utterly blingtastic.
Timestamps
00:00 Intro
00:34 A slight logistics issue…
01:38 Key features of the DuoAir
02:42 A quick teardown
05:17 Building the PC
07:17 Smoke airflow tests
07:54 Thermal + acoustic tests
10:22 Pricing discussion + closing thoughts
Main features
Interchangeable glass/mesh front panels allow for easy transition between maximum cooling and premium build visibility.
A front-mounted PSU placement clears space for true vertical intake.
Perforated bottom side panels significantly enhance lower fan intake.
Pre-installed 5-fan configuration: 2x 140mm ARGB front fans, 1x 120mm ARGB rear fan, and 2x 120mm bottom fans.
Premium ZPX/ZPB fans utilise Rifle Bearing and stabilising rings to reduce turbulence and ensure silent, long-lasting operation.
Accommodates large 410mm GPUs while maintaining a compact overall footprint.
Refined rounded edges offer a modern alternative aesthetic and gentler handling.
Three integrated dust filters, including a stylish quick-slide front filter, provide effortless maintenance and long-term protection.
A discreetly positioned ARGB light bar adds ambience without disrupting front profile.
Specification:
Motherboard support: ATX, Micro-ATX, Mini-ITX.
Power supply support: ATX.
Expansion slots: 7.
Included fans: 2x 140mm ZPX ARGB 1,800rpm front intake, 1x 120mm 2,200rpm ZPX ARGB rear exhaust, 2x 120mm 2,200rpm ZPB floor intake.
Fan mounts: 2x 140mm front, 2x 140mm/3x 120mm roof, 1x 120mm/140mm rear, 2x 120mm floor.
Radiator mounts: 280mm/360mm roof.
5.25-inch optical drive bays: None.
Internal drive bays: 2x 3.5-inch or 1x 3.5-inch and 2x 2.5-inch.
Front I/O ports: 2x USB 3.0 Type-A, 1x USB 3.2 2×2 Type-C, audio.
Dimensions: 479mm H x 460mm D x 220mm W.
Testing
To put this case through its cooling paces we will be using a test system consisting of an AMD Ryzen 7 9850X3D, Sapphire RX 9070 XT and an SSD. This system allows us to produce a substantial amount of heat and effectively test the Cougar DuoAir‘s cooling capabilities.
Test System:
Processor: AMD Ryzen 7 9850X3D
CPU Cooler: Montech HyperFlow ARGB 360
Motherboard: Sapphire Nitro+ X870EA PhantomLink Polar Edition
Memory: 32GB G.Skill Trident Z5 NeoX RGB DDR5-6000
Graphics card: Sapphire Nitro+ AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT 16GB
Power supply: Fractal Design Ion 3 Gold 1000W
SSD: Crucial T700 Gen 5 M.2 NVMe
OS: Windows 11
Cooling Performance
Cooling Performance Overview
We saw a spread of 10 degrees C in CPU temperatures during our testing which is a very significant figure. Running the fans at a low speed so they are nice and quiet leads to a slightly hot PC, however increasing fan speeds to the maximum is horribly noisy. Our conclusion is that most people should use the mesh front panel and ignore the glass alternative, and that you should run the fans between 1,000rpm and 1,500rpm so you get a decent balance of noise to performance.
Closing Thoughts
The headline feature of the Cougar DuoAir is the choice of mesh or glass front panel and while it is a nice touch we consider it is a minor matter. The glass looks nice enough however the mesh also looks good and performs significantly better while also giving you a full ARGB light show. In our opinion the only reason to stick with the glass is an aesthetic choice as mesh is better in every practical sense.
Beyond that the DuoAir is solidly built and is supplied with five fans which means you have the minimum of assembly to perform when you build your PC. The fundamentals of this case are absolutely sound and Cougar has made no grievous errors or poor choices. The biggest compliment we can pay the DuoAir is that it looks entirely conventional while managing to tuck away a few neat touches just below the surface.
You will be able to buy the Cougar DuoAir for US$89.99.
Pros:
Smart looks with clean styling.
It’s clever without being too clever.
The graphics card cooling system works well.
Cons:
Cable management space is tight.
The location of the front IO lends itself to having your PC on your desk.
There is no separate fan rack in the top of the case.
Does not support rear connection motherboards.
KitGuru says: Cougar DuoAir focuses on airflow to your graphics card, and also delivers an impressive ARGB light show from the fans and front panel.

items.title: Helldivers 2: new poisonous Terminid types, more bug caves spawn across the galaxy today
items.content:
Attention, Helldivers.
The Ministry of Truth confirms that a new Terminid strain is skittering across the front lines. Designated the Noxious strain, these menaces are fast, venomous, and fundamentally opposed to Managed Democracy.
Play Video
Worse still, the bugs have been digging. Terminid cave networks now course beneath more biomes in the galaxy from scorched deserts to frozen tundras. Every planet may have a hive beneath it.
Here is everything a Helldiver needs to know courtesy of the Ministry of Truth:
Noxious Scavenger: small, fast, and full of venom
At first glance these resemble ordinary Scavengers. Their additional vileness becomes more apparent when they skitter in to attack.
Noxious Scavengers are noticeably quicker than their cousins which makes them hard to keep in your sights. Every bite delivers a deadly dose of poison and they are ready to bite again almost immediately. Fortunately, they are fragile. Weapons that reward volume over precision such as shotguns, flamethrowers, and grenades, will make short work of them. Super Earth reminds you that ammunition is cheaper than antivenom.
Noxious Spewer: the big one
Forget everything you know about Spewers dragging themselves across the ground. The Noxious Spewer is a hulking monstrosity that moves with unsettling speed and it is responsible for the webs now draped across the battlefield.
At medium range, watch for its Web Spit. One hit and you lose the ability to sprint, which is exactly what the abomination wants: to slow its prey and close the gap. Beware its bite, which is quick, has surprising reach, and carries a stronger dose of venom than anything a Scavenger can deliver.
While its head is protected by medium armor, its web-filled abdomen has no armor at all. Be cautious when targeting this location, as when the sac bursts in a Web Explosion, it will snare every Helldiver and bug nearby. Super Earth recommends not being caught in the explosion.
Noxious venom: All sorts of bad news
Every Noxious bite inflicts poison, which can cripple the Democratic spirit of even the most stalwart Helldivers. You can track your condition with the new poison icon on your HUD. Super Earth categorizes the poisoning as follows:
Lightly poisoned: Your vision starts to haze, the poison begins to eat away at your health
Heavily poisoned: Damage over time increases, you lose the ability to sprint, your vision hazes, Lady Liberty comes to visit you
Thankfully, your stims will help cure your condition, so ration them wisely. A poisoned squadmate may need that stim to keep going and fulfill your mission.
Caves on more biomes
The Terminids have gone underground and Super Earth is hunting them down. Bug caves are no longer limited to a handful of worlds; they now have a chance to appear across more biomes on the Galactic map.
Inside these tunnels sightlines are short, corners are blind, and fast enemies arrive before you hear them. Absolutely ideal territory for those Noxious bugs. Bring close-range firepower, stay with your squad, and keep a stim in reserve for whoever wandered too far ahead.
Suit up, Helldiver
The Noxious strain want the galaxy wrapped in silk and soaked in venom. Super Earth has other plans, and those plans involve you.
Pack your stims, aim for the abdomen, and remember: arachnophobia is not a recognized exemption from military service. See you in the caves, Helldiver. Remember, a cleaner galaxy starts with YOU, Helldiver.
A cleaner galaxy starts with YOU.

items.title: SteamOS now runs on Apple Silicon thanks to new open-source project
items.content:
An open-source project called FX Steam Launcher is bringing SteamOS to Apple Silicon Macs. Rather than replacing macOS, the software runs Valve's ARM64 version of SteamOS inside a virtual machine, allowing Mac users to access SteamOS, Proton and a growing number of Windows-compatible games.
As demonstrated by ETAPrime (via VideoCardz), early testing has produced surprisingly promising results. Running on a MacBook Pro equipped with an M4 Max chip, Left 4 Dead 2 exceeded 200FPS, while Stellar Blade and The Witcher 3 both reportedly ran at over 70FPS using the SteamOS virtual machine.
The project relies on Valve's official ARM64 version of SteamOS, with Windows game compatibility handled through Proton and additional translation layers that convert x86 code and DirectX instructions for Apple Silicon hardware. The software can run in either a window or fullscreen mode while retaining audio and controller support.
The project remains a work in progress, however. Testing revealed graphical glitches, shader compilation stutter and compatibility issues in some games, with titles including DOOM Eternal, Ghost of Tsushima and Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales failing to launch correctly. Earlier testing on a Mac mini with 16GB of memory also highlighted performance limitations when system memory became constrained.
KitGuru says: SteamOS running on Apple Silicon felt like a long shot not too long ago. Would you be tempted to use a SteamOS VM on your Mac for gaming?

items.title: Phantom Blade Zero officially sells 4 million copies in 3 days
items.content:
Almost a decade on from its initial inception, the fast-paced action-RPG Phantom Blade Zero is finally here. While it was clear that the game had amassed a major audience from the get-go (achieving a peak concurrent player count of 800,000 on Steam alone), studio S-GAME has now come out with an even more impressive figure – revealing that Phantom Blade Zero has officially sold 4 million copies in its first 3 days.
Taking to Twitter to make the announcement, studio S-GAME officially revealed just how successful the game has been during its first few days on the market, stating: “Phantom Blade Zero has sold over 4 million copies in just 72 hours! Thank you everyone from the bottom of our hearts for all the love and support!”
As mentioned, it was quite clear from early on that Phantom Blade Zero was going to have a strong launch, with the game’s director revealing back in September that the title had amassed more than 3 million wishlists.
Of course, wishlists are just that – wishlists – and so the real question which remained was how many of those 3 million would wind up purchasing the actual game. As it turns out, all of them and then some.
While not quite a 1:1 comparison, 2024’s Black Myth Wukong (which initially launched on both PC and PS5) sold a total of 10 million copies within its first 3 days on the market. So, while Phantom Blade Zero is still a far cry from the behemoth that was Black Myth Wukong, the latter remains one of the fastest-selling games of all time, and so being in the conversion at all is an achievement in and of itself.
Regardless, with incredibly strong early sales and an aggregate review score quite a bit higher than Wukong, it may not be long before Phantom Blade Zero manages to surpass another major milestone.

He started discovering desktop computers when his father brought home a Windows 95 PC, but his first real experience working under the hood of the PC was when the old computer’s hard drive was filled to the brim in the year 2000. He deleted the Windows folder to attempt to rectify the situation, which led to his dad buying a new desktop PC. Since then, he learned a lot more about computers, and he’s always been the go-to tech expert for his family and friends.

Jowi primarily uses a Windows workstation and an Android phone, but he also bought into the Apple ecosystem with the 6th-gen iPad, iPhone 14 Pro Max, and the M1 MacBook Air. Today, Jowi covers hardware and software from Redmond and Cupertino, while also looking at the tech industry in general.

Aside from covering technology, Jowi is an avid photographer and writes about automobiles, aviation, and tanks. You can find his bylines at MakeUseOf, SlashGear, and, of course, Tom’s Hardware.

Mark's enthusiasm for computers dampened at an early age by the rubber-keyed Sinclair Spectrum 48K and feelings of Commodore 64 envy. However, in the mid-80s, hope in a digital future was rekindled by the purchase of an Atari 520 STe. Since that time Mark has used a multitude of computers for fun and professional endeavors. He often owned both Macs and PCs but went cold on the former after OS9 was killed off, and warmed to the latter with the introduction of Windows XP.

Early work years were spent in artwork and reprographics but in the late noughties, Mark started to blog about computers, Taiwanese food culture, and guitar design. This activity led to a full-time position writing about breaking PC tech news for HEXUS, for the best part of a decade. When HEXUS was abruptly closed, Mark helped with the foundation of Club386, before finding a new home at Tom's Hardware.

When not wearing through the keycap legends on his PC keyboards, Mark can be found wandering the computer malls of Taiwan's neon-lit conurbations and enjoying local and international cuisine.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (2009) appears on game ratings board
items.content:
Earlier this year, during the mid-way point in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7’s lifecycle, Activision announced and released current-gen ports for both Black Ops 1 and 2 for PlayStation, marking the first time that PS4/5 owners have been able to play either game on their system (due to the lack of backwards compatibility with PS3). It appears as though something similar might be happening with the OG Modern Warfare 2 – as the 2009 classic has now popped up on the Australian games rating board.
As reported by multiple users, the Australian Classifications board recently published a new listing for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (2009). As of now, the listing does not include too much in the way of details, and so it is unknown whether this port will be exclusive to PlayStation (as was the case with BO1+2).
That said, what is clear is the fact that this port appears to be the full MW2 experience, with the rating making explicit note of “Online Interactivity and Chat” – meaning unlike 2020’s Modern Warfare 2 Campaign Remastered, this release should include the game’s iconic multiplayer modes.
In a less positive comparison to Campaign Remastered however, this port is likely to be just that: a port, meaning players can expect pretty much the exact same visuals and settings as the PS3 original (meaning 60fps and a low-FOV) albeit at a slightly higher resolution.
Regardless, given the fact that the aforementioned BO1+2 ports ended up selling over 11 million copies in its first month alone, it’s safe to assume that Activision will port over all of the 7th-gen Call of Duty offerings eventually.
KitGuru says: What do you think of this listing? Could we see MW2 ported over within Modern Warfare 4’s lifecycle? Would you rather they release a basic port or a more comprehensive remaster (as was the case with the OG Modern Warfare)? Let us know down below.
The post Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (2009) appears on game ratings board first appeared on KitGuru.

More than a decade on from the first game’s release, the campy interactive horror adventure Until Dawn is set to receive a sequel. items.title: Square Enix originally wanted Final Fantasy Resonance to be a “simple port”
items.content:
Following a decade of operation, Square Enix officially shut down the mobile-exclusive Final Fantasy: Brave Exvius last year. That said, the game would later be revived and rebuilt in Square’s signature HD-2D art style for PC and consoles under the name Final Fantasy Resonance. Commenting on the title’s early success, producer Keisuke Nakashima revealed that Square Enix initially just wanted to do “a simple port.”
Officially launched on the 22nd of October, Final Fantasy Resonance has been met with a great deal of positivity, amassing a Metacritic score of 86 and an ‘Overwhelmingly Positive’ reception on Steam.
While the game is based on the bones of 2015’s mobile exclusive FF: Brave Exvius, Resonance was pretty much entirely rebuilt – most noticeably when it comes to the game’s art style, arriving as the first Final Fantasy title to make use of Square’s HD-2D aesthetic.
According to the game’s producer ‘Keisuke Nakashima’ however, this wasn’t always the case. In an interview with the publication Bloomberg (paywalled) and as reported by NintendoEverything, Nakashima revealed that “initially there was some resistance to the idea from Square Enix executives”, with the higher-ups wanting a more basic port.
As claimed by Nakashima: “I didn’t want to go down that route. I wanted to create an original version for consoles that was a full-blown gameplay experience.”
Part of the mentality behind this reimagining came due to the producer's desire to remove Brave Exvius’ gacha mechanics from Resonance, claiming that “It was really disappointing to hear people didn’t want to play it just because of the gacha elements. That was another reason we wanted to make this a console game, to bring it to a wider audience.”
Whether it be the lack of gacha, the embrace of HD-2D or a combination of multiple factors, Final Fantasy Resonance appears to be a success on all fronts. It will be interesting to see what lessons Square Enix will take away from this.

October Steam Survey reverses many of September’s biggest shifts
items.content:
Valve has published its October 2026 Steam Hardware & Software Survey results, and many of last month's most dramatic changes have already begun to reverse. Several categories that saw unusually large shifts in September, including memory capacity, GPU market share and language distribution, have largely moved back towards their previous positions.
September's survey saw 32GB of RAM briefly overtake 16GB as the most common memory configuration among Steam users, while the GeForce RTX 5070 surged ahead of the RTX 3060. October's results tell a different story. 16GB has regained the top spot at 41.42%, up 3.60 percentage points month-on-month, while 32GB fell 5.16 points to 37.06%. The RTX 3060 has also reclaimed its position as Steam's most popular graphics card at 3.62%, narrowly ahead of the RTX 5070 at 3.56%.
The most likely explanation appears to be a change in survey demographics rather than a sudden shift in purchasing behaviour. Simplified Chinese users accounted for 21.98% of survey responses in October, down 9.41 percentage points from the previous month. Meanwhile, English-language users increased by 4.84 percentage points to 39.04%, helping to explain why several hardware categories appear to have swung back towards earlier trends.
Elsewhere, Windows 11 continued its steady rise, gaining 1.17 percentage points to reach 72.51% of surveyed systems. Intel also extended its lead among Windows CPU users, increasing its share to 53.48%, while AMD slipped to 46.51%. The survey also showed Linux growing to 3.95% of systems, although Windows remains overwhelmingly dominant among Steam users.
KitGuru says: September's Steam Survey always looked a little unusual. Do October's results paint a more accurate picture of the current PC gaming market?

items.title: Cities Worldwide Build and Scale AI Services With NVIDIA Physical and Agentic AI
items.content:
Cities generate enormous amounts of data from cameras, sensors and operational systems, but turning it into useful action — for planning, maintenance and public services — remains a challenge.
Physical and agentic AI offer new ways to close that gap, from digital twins for infrastructure planning to vision and service agents, while keeping local governments in control of how sensitive data is processed and used.
Building on initiatives announced at GTC Berlin, NVIDIA and its partners are expanding physical AI and AI agents to cities worldwide. Shared computing infrastructure gives city departments, neighboring municipalities and local developers a common foundation to build on — extending services without each organization having to acquire and manage resources of their own.
Agentic AI for Cities
From resident services to vision agents, cities are adopting NVIDIA agentic AI to deliver faster, more responsive public services. City teams don’t need a massive infrastructure investment to get started building these AI services: depending on the workload, NVIDIA RTX workstations or a small GPU system may be enough.
In Spain, 1MillionBot combines open source ALIA models trained at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center with NVIDIA Nemotron and other models in resident-service agents for Madrid Digital (Comunidad de Madrid), Administració Oberta de Catalunya and 150+ deployments across Spain, handling municipal procedures, appointment requests, urban-planning incidents and service inquiries.
In the San Francisco Bay Area, LiveX is bringing its AI City vision to life with NVIDIA Cosmos world models and Nemotron open models, and Omniverse and Metropolis libraries on NVIDIA RTX PRO GPUs. The interactive, conversational AI hosts understand people’s needs, provide answers and take action, and can be tailored to local languages and service needs in airports, hospitals, local events and other public spaces.
Vision AI agents can turn existing city camera feeds into operational insights, helping teams identify mobility and safety issues and coordinate emergency responses across city services.
In Wrocław, Poland, K2K is building shared AI infrastructure using NVIDIA accelerated computing, NVIDIA Cosmos world reasoning models, and NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) to transform existing camera streams into actionable intelligence for mobility, safety and event response — using the same infrastructure across several city functions.
In Malaysia, ITMAX bundles infrastructure and agentic AI applications into long-term managed services for cities, including for traffic management. Built with reference to Cosmos, Nemotron and the Metropolis VSS blueprint, ITMAX’s SamurAI V2 vision agents are scaling on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs to support 17,000+ cameras by 2027. ITMAX integrates TeraSim, an open source traffic simulation platform from Laplace Intelligence, to test signal timing, reducing peak-hour corridor travel times by up to 26%.
Plan and Operate Critical Infrastructure With Digital Twins
Beyond public-facing services, digital twins can help cities expedite infrastructure planning, minimizing disruption to local communities. City digital twins can also serve as a real-time operational simulation to facilitate faster decision-making.
At Dangote’s Lekki refinery in Nigeria, Honeywell Technologies’ Forge Plant Cognition uses Nemotron-powered AI agents to understand operational data. A digital twin of the plant and its processes, built using Omniverse libraries, is also planned to support simulation and training. The platform, built on Dell PowerEdge servers with NVIDIA RTX PRO accelerators, helps operators identify bottlenecks, anticipate equipment and process issues, and optimize plant performance.
In Taiwan, Linker Vision and Dutch architecture firm MVRDV are using NVIDIA Omniverse and Nemotron to build environmental, social and governance agents that can assess the environmental impact of various urban planning scenarios, simulating 15-year outcomes of an urban forest canopy in 10 minutes — increasing design iteration speed from two weeks per iteration to less than an hour.
Build a Broader Local AI Ecosystem
Cities can extend AI to more services by building on infrastructure already in place and adding capacity. Shared resources and managed services can help extend those capabilities across departments and municipalities.
At Morocco’s Tanger Med port, Cires Technologies is expanding a sovereign AI factory for planned applications in worker safety, congestion analysis, cargo routing and port operations. Cires Technologies is also building an ecosystem of application providers to develop local models and applications for ports and cities.
Beyond city services, Barcelona Supercomputing Center’s AI Factory Accelerator Programme gives startups access to sovereign computing, technical support and training. BSC AI Factory also supports research and innovation for startups — spanning agriculture, medical imaging, knowledge access and speech services.
Learn how NVIDIA and its ecosystem are bringing physical AI, agentic AI and local AI factories to cities worldwide at Smart City Expo World Congress, running Nov. 3-5 in Barcelona, where NVIDIA Vice President of EMEA Paolo Guglielmini will deliver a keynote address followed by a panel moderated by Charbel Aoun, director of smart city and spaces for EMEA at NVIDIA.

items.title: Borderlands franchise surpasses 100M copies sold as Gearbox teases future plans
items.content:
The Borderlands franchise has officially surpassed 100 million copies sold, a milestone reached more than 17 years after the release of the original game. Alongside the announcement, Gearbox has also begun teasing its long-term plans for the series following the completion of Borderlands 4's first year of post-launch content.
First released in 2009, Borderlands helped popularise the looter shooter genre and has since grown into one of 2K's biggest gaming franchises. The series now spans multiple mainline entries, spin-offs and expansions, with Borderlands 4 serving as the latest chapter following its launch just over a year ago.
Gearbox also used the milestone announcement to look back on Borderlands 4's first year of support. Since launch, the game has received two Story Packs, five Bounty Packs, two additional Vault Hunters, two free Raid Boss encounters, an endgame Takedown activity and a range of quality-of-life improvements and gameplay updates. The studio confirmed that weekly activity refreshes and community challenges will continue, with additional Borderlands 4 content planned for 2027.
Perhaps more interestingly, Gearbox hinted at a broader future for the franchise beyond its current content roadmap. In a message to players, the studio said it is exploring new character arcs, storylines and the overall direction of the Borderlands universe. While no new projects were announced, the comments suggest that planning for the next phase of the franchise is already underway.

items.title: World of Warcraft: Forever – How Controller Support Reimagines the Way We Can Play in Azeroth
items.content:
My approach to World of Warcraft has largely been one of logging in and enjoying a casual adventure in Azeroth. I’m not messing around with macros or trying to carry a team through a dungeon. I’m more than happy to spend my time chewing on scenery and gobbling up lore. Yes, I’m that guy that wants to know exactly why he must fell 15 trolls.
This taps into one of the many things that makes World of Warcraft great, in that Blizzard wants to make sure there’s a WoW experience that suits everybody. Whether it’s through PC hardware support, innovations in battle mechanics like Single-Button Assistant, and rolling out numerous accessibility features such as Text to Speech, the game constantly hits it out of the park for creating a world for so many players to access and enjoy.
This is one of the things that has made me excited for World of Warcraft: Forever, in that Blizzard can now take all the years of learned knowledge of creating a welcoming Azeroth and return us to an age when it still felt fresh and unknown; like an adventure every time you logged in – and now we’ll be able to play with a controller in our hands thanks to Gamepad (Alpha) support.
Vanilla Ice Cream
I suppose I should back up just a bit to give you a refresher on what World of Warcraft: Forever is and why it’s a pretty big deal. Essentially, we’ll return to a version of the game’s world that is very similar to the WoW that arrived in 2004, but with many new stories, locations, and improved features that work to strike that middle ground between that Classic feel, mixed with added improvements to make the experience welcoming for newcomers. And it’s going to stay that way, hence the Forever in the game’s title.
What does that mean lore-wise? We’re back to the two main continents, Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor, and the classic races featuring humans, orcs, elves, trolls, dwarfs, and others. But don’t expect a 1:1 experience as there will still be a lot of new to explore. The most significant are the Skyborne, a new race of elves that occupy the recently uncovered floating Zephras Isle.
Back on the ground, there will be new areas to discover in the Riverglades and Mount Hyjal, improved lighting and graphics to make familiar locations feel new, as well as revamps to class combos, like being able to roll with a Forsaken Paladin.
Think of Forever as filling the gaps of Azeroth with denser content to keep the Classic vibes in play. And it’s all included in your current subscription, so there’s no additional purchase required to experience this old-new world. And one of those new ways to experience Azeroth will influence not only how to play but also where.
Couch Surfing
My personal PC gaming rig is about the size of a game console, which occasionally finds a home next to my XBOX Series X|S in the living room; I’m rocking an AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D and ASUS Prime Radeon RX 9070 all in a small form factor Fractal Ridge case. Now with World of Warcraft: Forever and its Gamepad (Alpha) support, I’m as close as I’ve ever been to a console-like Warcraft experience – and it’s awesome.
Consider using Compact Action Bar to free up screen space from the UI.
Enabling the controller support is seamless from the main menu – just go into Options and check the box for “Gamepad (Alpha)” support. That will change your on-screen icons to match your controller’s buttons and from there you can start adventuring. I would recommend a modern XBOX Wireless Controller to use since every on-screen button icon maps perfectly.
The first thing I wanted to work out with the Gamepad (Alpha) feature was accessing my normal routines – how to access Bags; where are my Quests; how do I look at my character? This has come together over time. I haven’t found anything that I can’t access through just the controller, and that’s a good thing for this feature’s future support.
I recommend a modern XBOX Wireless Controller to use since every on-screen button icon maps perfectly.
Like learning the controls of any new role-playing game, there’s a certain rhythm you’ll become accustomed to with combat. For those who have already been playing World of Warcraft for a long time, you’ll have the added benefit of understanding how character progression, buffs, order of attacks, and additional skills will unlock. I will say that combat in Forever feels more rhythmic than modern Warcraft, which leans in the controller support’s favor, giving you a little bit more time to think through your next attack.
Combat itself involves cycling through actions tied to the controller’s Triggers and Bumpers, which when pressed alternate the actions that are mapped to your controller’s buttons. Once I got that hang of it, I was really moving into a nice combat flow, triggering enemies, casting spells, running away, and more.
Nudge others in your party on with commands like, Attack, Warning, On My Way, and Assist.
What I’m still working on is interacting with other players with just the controller. There is a ping system tied to holding down the right analog stick that can help you nudge others in your party on with commands like, Attack, Warning, On My Way, and Assist, but having a keyboard and/or voice chat still feels like the way to go. Having my wireless keyboard next to me on the couch is a good fallback option.
Warcraft Forever, Wherever
Another fun piece of PC gaming hardware I’m fortunate to have on hand is an ASUS ROG XBOX Ally. As fellow owners know, it features a lot of customization options to get most modern games running on it in some capacity. And since it runs Windows 11, apps like Battle.net can run on it too. So that got me thinking – could I get World of Warcraft: Forever running on it too? Yes, I could.
Use the UI’s Edit Mode and adjust to your liking.
There is a bit of a caveat though, in that it takes some patience to get there. And it isn’t officially supported yet, but by using a mix of the system’s touchscreen and onscreen keyboard, you can navigate to the main menu to toggle the Gamepad (Alpha) controller support feature.
I’d also recommend taking a few minutes to go into the UI’s Edit Mode and reduce the size of the Chat Frame and lowering the Player and Targeting Frames to the bottom of the screen to give you some more visibility to the action on the screen. The default positioning of the Gamepad Action Bar is pretty good, but consider checking the box to use Compact Action Bar to free up some more of that screen space from the UI. After that it’s a pretty seamless gameplay experience in your hands comparable to my time playing Forever on my couch.
Throughout the beta leading up to launch, I would swap between playing on desktop, couch, and handheld with Forever and it has been a delight in experimenting with first-party controller support for one of my favorite games. I never thought I’d be able to lay back in bed with a handheld and play World of Warcraft, or lounge back on the couch while running a dungeon, but here we are!
Excitement around World of Warcraft: Forever is palpable. On November 4, PC players can return to a nostalgic world many grew up with – and others will discover for the first time – now with the freedom to play wherever and whenever they choose with the addition of Gamepad (Alpha) support. Forever has reimagined a way for us to explore Azeroth in more ways than one, and I can’t wait to dive in. Again.
