items.title: Persona 1 remake apparently revealed through leaked trailer
items.content:
A newly leaked trailer appears to show Atlus' next Persona remake project. Following Persona 3 Reload and a Persona 4 remake due in early 2027, the publisher now looks to be revisiting the very first entry in the series.
The trailer has begun circulating online ahead of any official announcement and appears to show gameplay from a remake of the original Persona. While Atlus has yet to comment on the footage, the leak includes combat sequences, exploration and a fully realised user interface.
As with any leak, there is no way to immediately verify its authenticity. The footage could be an elaborate fan-made project, although there are several details that make it difficult to dismiss outright. Alongside gameplay footage and completed menu systems, the trailer also appears to contain work-in-progress story segments using what look to be storyboard placeholders rather than final assets.
If legitimate, the remake would continue Atlus' recent effort to modernise older entries in the series. Persona 3 Reload was followed by plans for a Persona 4 remake, while Persona 6 remains in development for a later release. A remake of the original game would make sense given comments from Atlus producers in recent years expressing interest in revisiting Persona's earliest entries.
The original Persona launched for the PlayStation in 1996 under the title Revelations: Persona in Western markets. While later games in the series became global hits, the first entry has largely remained locked to older platforms, receiving just one major re-release via the PSP in 2009.

Gang of Dragon studio closes just one year after game reveal
items.content:
Yakuza creator Toshihiro Nagoshi's new studio is shutting down, just 11 months after unveiling its debut game, Gang of Dragon. The closure means the Sleeping Dogs and Yakuza-inspired action title has effectively been cancelled before it ever reached players.
Nagoshi Studio was founded in 2021 after Toshihiro Nagoshi's departure from Sega, with financial backing from NetEase. The studio finally unveiled its first project, Gang of Dragon, during The Game Awards 2025, presenting it as a gritty action game starring actor Ma Dong-seok. At the time, the project appeared to be a major new venture from one of Japan's most recognisable game creators.
However, the studio's future reportedly came into question earlier this year when Bloomberg reported that NetEase planned to end funding for the project as part of broader cutbacks to its games business. According to the report, the publisher baulked after learning that Gang of Dragon would need an additional ¥7 billion (around $44M) to reach completion.
Now, Japanese publication 4Gamer reports that shareholders voted to dissolve Nagoshi Studio during a meeting held on the 31st of October. While no formal cancellation announcement for Gang of Dragon has been issued, the closure of the studio effectively brings development of the project to an end.

Final Fantasy XIV players will have to wait a little longer for Evercold. Square Enix has delayed the MMORPG's next expansion from its planned January release window, pushing the launch back by a few weeks to the 23rd of February 2027.

‘90s style sci-fi horror Derelikt launches Nov 13 on PS5
items.content:
Back in 1999, gaming was good. Games that were released late in the original PlayStation generation squeezed the last drop of performance out of the hardware, resulting in impressive visuals and all-time classics whose sequels we still play today. Fast forward 26 years and we’re excited to announce that our sci-fi horror game Derelikt will make you feel like your console shed 5 generations when it launches on PlayStation 5 on November 13.
Play Video
Derelikt takes place aboard Von Neumann Outpost, grafted onto an anomalous asteroid discovered in Saturn’s orbit. Things are rough. The work is hard, home is a million miles away, and people are stressed out. Plus, a mysterious drone is driving everyone closer to their breaking point…
You arrive as an outside contractor tasked with finding out the fate of Excavation Team Delta, who went missing on the derelict surface. What you discover turns things from bad to worse fast! The halls are dark, the systems are failing, and the survivors that you come across aren’t telling the same story. Nailing that feeling of not being able to trust those around you, while simultaneously coming face to face with truly out-of-this-world horrors, was paramount for us.
The Von Neumann Outpost is well stocked with an arsenal of traditional weapons, and as you progress, you might even find a few more outlandish weapon prototypes and even alien weapons at your disposal. There are also over a dozen to interact with in Derelikt, each featuring their own secrets, and agendas. Some are useful, some are dangerous, some are doomed, and some (let’s be real, most) are all three!
We wanted to not only create this horrifyingly tense world full of scary moments and fast gunplay, but also make sure to make managing resources, exploration, dialogues and old-school puzzle solving a core part of the tension experience.
Derelikt is very much inspired by the PSOne-era of sci-fi horror, and it feels like a full-circle moment to be writing this today. The goal was to make it appear as if we found Derelikt on a CD-R in the dusty, long-abandoned storage unit of a defunct late-90s developer and simply ported it to modern platforms. I’m of the firm opinion that retro doesn’t have to mean crude and primitive, and I set out to create the most faithful homage to 5th generation graphics available on the market.
Our game features 100% lovingly hand-painted textures and vertex colour lighting. Affine Texture warping was deliberately implemented and mitigated in the next step by dynamically subdividing the geometry – just like the most high-end games of the era did – and the game also features retro-style full-motion CGI cutscenes. This way, a delicate balance was achieved – Derelikt looks aesthetically pleasing while still conceivably plausible on period hardware. Our team made a conscious effort to implement modern game design while keeping the core feeling and charm of that era of sci-fi horror intact, including an option for players to toggle on or off effects to match their particular taste.
Derelikt has been in development in some form since late 2021 and has had a turbulent and exciting development journey. We hope the game is as wild a ride for players as it has been to develop!

Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered fighter guide
items.content:
With its giant-sized fanbase, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered has plenty of players ready to get tooth, nail, and claw stuck into its PlayStation 5 release on November 3. Although it would be understandable that newcomers might feel a little intimidated choosing between 12 world crushing kaiju, each with their own stats, moveset, and special abilities. Never fear – we have the rundown on which colossus matches your playstyle to ensure you’re the true king of the monsters.
Heisei Godzilla
Ideal for: Players who want to dive straight in.
The face which sank a thousand ships. Godzilla is the iconic kaiju who all other kaiju want to be, beat, or be friends with. As the game’s default character, the giant lizard is balanced for newbies and veterans alike, with a high amount of starting health and decent all-round stats.
Godzilla also possesses a tail useful enough for a mighty wake-up strike when he’s downed, and some fairly swift claws, so many of his melee combos are effective for beginners. But don’t rely too much on his high-energy pulse – while it’s formidable, the slow charge leaves him open to counters. Similarly, ranged attackers can take advantage of his relatively sluggish projectiles, so close that distance or you’ll be heading back to Monster Island with your giant tail between your legs.
Godzilla 2000
Ideal for: Players annoyed at their friend for picking Heisei Godzilla.
In terms of film history, Godzilla 2000 is a more modern incarnation of the legendary lizard, reflecting a new era for the new millennium. Although he’s arguably a slightly more vulnerable version of his Heisei predecessor.
As a result, while Godzilla 2000 is a bit faster than his kaiju shoto fighter twin, he’s not quite as strong. He’s still fairly well balanced and arguably easier to use than Heisei, so makes for a solid alternative. And his distinctive purple dorsal plates look pretty cool, too.
King Ghidorah
Ideal for: Players who want to control the battlefield.
There’s a reason why this fearsome three-headed beast is seen as Godzilla’s archnemesis. Giant wings, gravity beams, and a desire to annihilate humanity, the threat of King Ghidorah should never be taken lightly.
Given his monstrous size it shouldn’t be a surprise that the ‘supreme ruler of the cosmos’ isn’t the fastest kaiju on the block, but he’s resilient and a perfect ‘zoning’ character, capable of keeping foes at a distance with a variety of projectiles. His flight is a little limited due to its energy drain, but it’s balanced by a lightning blast that has no charge while airborne. However, despite his colossal wings, Ghidorah’s lack of arms and stubby legs makes him a poor melee fighter.
Anguirus
Ideal for: Players who think defense is the best offense.
He might look a bit like Godzooky with more spikes, but mutant dinosaur Anguirus is one of Godzilla’s most loyal allies – even if his track record against other kaiju hasn’t been the best in the movies.
The Monster Island citizen is fast and aggressive, but his low power and lack of long-range attacks means Anguirus is best utilized as a counter-attack specialist. His block might be on the slow side due to its turning animation, but it actually damages an attacking opponent due to Anguirus’ rear spines. With his high defense and solid grappling skills, this mutant shouldn’t be underestimated.
Megalon
Ideal for: Players who love to hit and run.
Given its status as a guardian to the ancient underground civilisation of Seatopia, Megalon is more of an antagonist than an out-and-out villain in Godzilla lore. While not quite as domineering as its colossal rivals, the subterranean kaiju is still capable of putting a hurt on with its drill-like appendages.
Megalon’s primary advantage is its tunnelling skill which not only allows it to avoid attacks, but also pop-up and grab opponents. Even though burrowing uses energy, it still makes Megalon a difficult fighter to pin down, especially when used in tandem with its myriad of electricity attacks. On the flip side, Megalon isn’t the most durable of beasts with below average defense. Stick and move, or die.
Gigan
Ideal for: Players wanting to attack with deadly speed.
One of the most sadistic fighters to hail from M Space Hunter Nebula, cyborg kaiju Gigan is easily one of Godzilla’s more vicious adversaries. Despite being defeated multiple times, the hook-clawed Gigan just keeps coming back for more.
Unsurprisingly, Gigan’s tenacious approach makes him perfect for aggressive rushdown tactics. He’s not only swift, but his teleportation ability gives him incredible range and evasion skills. And those hooks aren’t for decoration either, delivering damage-heavy edged strikes. His Laser Eye is a little unwieldy, and he’s vulnerable to energy attacks, but Gigan remains a versatile option for anyone wanting a decent melee and range mix-up.
Destoroyah
Ideal for: Players wanting a classic tank character.
Known as ‘death incarnate’, everything about Destoroyah is built to intimidate. Giant wings, clawed hands, taloned feet… this mutant crustacean almost has it all.
Which is to say, Destoroyah is one of the more powerful creatures in the game with brutal physical assaults and a wide variety of high-damage – and often unblockable – energy attacks that truly make him the perfect mid-range monster. But there’s a cost. Destoroyah’s best abilities are extremely power hungry, so without them he’s potentially ineffective given how painfully slow his movement is.
Rodan
Ideal for: Players wanting speed above all else.
With his dominance of the skies and fearsome pteranodon looks, you’d be fooled into thinking Rodan is an out-and-out villain, but he’s more a force of chaos, even capable of being selfless in some parts of Godzilla lore.
True to type, Rodan is not only the fastest monster in the game, but also the most mobile in the air. With his powerful breath attack and speedy melee attacks, he’s another great hit-and-run character. However, Rodan has shockingly low durability, with the weakest defense of the entire roster, so going toe-to-toe is not recommended.
Mecha-King Ghidorah
Ideal for: Players wanting a long-range grappler.
When one possible future sees the three-headed beast defeated, his body is salvaged and rebuilt by 23rd century scientists to serve humanity. The result is a cyborg that merges Ghidorah’s ferocity with bionic enhancements, including a shield, and projectiles with draining abilities.
So while Mecha-King Ghidorah doesn’t quite have the raw power of his original form, his weapons are far more useful on a whole, and his grappling versatility is impressive. That said, he’s just as slow, and he relies on energy to maintain his best attacks including his shield, meaning Mecha-King Ghidorah can be vulnerable to powerful prolonged assaults.
Mechagodzilla
Ideal for: Players wanting a heavy duty ranged fighter.
Mechagodzilla is the alien Vortaak’s heavily weaponised answer to the fire-breathing giant lizard, in their attempt to conquer Earth. And with near indestructible space titanium, lasers, missiles, and even a plasma cannon, they’ve left very little to chance.
Unlike its Kiryu sibling, Mechagodzilla is more specialised, with a greater degree of weapons and better defensive stats. And let’s not forget its iconic flying head-butt. Mechagodzilla’s main issue? Its reliance on energy for flying and many of its ranged attacks – so if that’s depleted, the automaton is left with its underwhelming grabs and sluggish melee.
Orga
Ideal for: Players wanting the best grappler in the game.
A terrifying looking alien in its own right, Orga hasn’t many appearances in Godzilla media, but the goliath – mutated from some of Godzilla’s DNA – is able to hold its own… not least due to its venomous maw and gigantic hands.
It’s those mitts which make Orga a menace in the arena, with its long reach offering a massive advantage to close and mid-range confrontations. But while Orga isn’t the slowest of monsters, it’s still relatively sluggish, and limited against anyone resistant to blunt attacks, or too fast for grabs. And as useful as its paralysing goo is, the high energy cost can leave Orga exposed if it misses.
Kiryu
Ideal for: Players needing a more weapons-focused Godzilla.
What do you get when you place the original Godzilla’s skeleton inside of a robot body? In this case, a slightly unstable anti-kaiju cyborg designed to protect humanity. Kiryu (translated into ‘machine dragon” from the original kanji) is one of the more popular iterations of Mechagodzilla, and a heavily armoured walking, flying arsenal.
Compared to Mechagodzilla, Kiryu has better balanced stats, which makes it the optimal choice for those looking for a more weapons-ready, energy hungry version of the base Godzillas, with a punchy rage attack thanks to its Absolute Zero Cannon.
Ready to see if you can keep up with your chosen kaiju? Get smashing when Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered fights its way to PlayStation 5 on November 3.

items.title: Soulframe enters Open Beta this week
items.content:
Soulframe is finally opening its doors to everyone. After years of invite-only testing, Digital Extremes has announced that its fantasy action RPG will enter Open Preludes this week, allowing anyone on PC to jump in and try the game without waiting for an invitation.
Since first entering closed testing, Soulframe has generated plenty of interest among players looking for a different take on the online RPG formula. Unlike many modern MMOs, Soulframe places a greater emphasis on melee combat, exploration and a slower-paced fantasy setting. The move to Open Preludes marks the game's biggest testing phase yet.
The upcoming Verse of the Veillands update will arrive alongside Open Preludes, bringing a substantial overhaul to progression and a more structured introduction to the world of Midrath. After completing an early quest, players will begin cleansing corrupted regions known as the Veillands, unlocking resources, activities and new areas along the way. The update will also introduce a wolf companion that can eventually be trained into a mount, with further updates to the Veillands system planned for future builds.
Soulframe's timing is interesting. Open Preludes arrives just as Blizzard prepares to launch World of Warcraft: Forever, placing the game's biggest public test yet alongside one of the year's largest MMO releases.

Windows 11 Preview adds Cloud Rebuild to reinstall OS and drivers
items.content:
Microsoft has introduced Cloud Rebuild, a recovery feature that wipes and reinstalls Windows 11 while pulling fresh system drivers directly from Windows Update. Rolling out via optional preview update KB5127936 for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2, the tool can retrieve a clean OS image even when the local installation refuses to boot.
According to VideoCardz, users can initiate a Cloud Rebuild through Settings > System > Recovery as “Rebuild PC” whenever the OS boots normally. When startup fails repeatedly, the machine drops into the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE), where Cloud rebuild appears under the Troubleshoot menu. Unlike the existing Cloud download setting in the Reset menu, Microsoft states that Cloud Rebuild doesn't rely on an intact local Windows installation.
Initiating the process completely wipes the primary drive, erasing installed software, local files, and user accounts, with only cloud-synced data surviving. For machines being repurposed or sold, a sanitize mode provides a secure disk erase. Moreover, system administrators can trigger rebuilds remotely using the Recovery CSP.
Executing the process requires a functioning WinRE partition and active network connectivity via Wi-Fi or Ethernet using pre-installed manufacturer drivers. WinRE can now reuse saved Wi-Fi profiles from Windows, though Microsoft notes the rebuild will fail if a system's drivers aren't published on Windows Update.
KitGuru says: Having an official recovery option that pulls fresh drivers alongside a clean image could save plenty of headaches when troubleshooting broken boots. Do you keep a dedicated Windows installer USB around, or will you start to rely on Cloud Rebuild from now on?

Phantom Blade Zero launches to over 800,000 concurrent players on Steam alone
items.content:
After almost a decade in development, S-GAME’s long-awaited Phantom Blade Zero has finally arrived. Already a success critically, the action-focused RPG has proven to be a commercial juggernaut – having officially landed on Steam with a concurrent player count of over 800K in total.
Officially released this past Thursday, S-GAME’s Phantom Blade Zero is off to an excellent start so far, with the PC / PS5 exclusive arriving to an aggregate review score of 89%. Said critic scores, alongside a substantial amount of pre-launch excitement, appears to have led to an explosive launch for the game, with Phantom Blade Zero peaking at over 800,000 concurrent players on Steam alone (hitting 833K on Sunday).
This puts Phantom Blade Zero as one of the most-played games of all time on the platform, with its peak CCU landing at no. 14 on Steam’s all-time list – nestled in between Battlefield 6 (747K) and Baldur’s Gate 3 (875K).
While we of course do not have any public data for how the game is performing on PS5, Phantom Blade Zero is currently sitting at an average score of 4.71 stars across its 15,000+ reviews on the platform (compared to Steam’s 78,000 ratings).
Prior to the title’s release, the team at S-GAME revealed that Phantom Blade Zero had amassed more than 3 million wishlists. While we have yet to learn just how many copies have been sold since its launch on the 29th of October, it is safe to say that with over 800K concurrent players on Steam alone, Phantom Blade Zero is already easily a 1 million+ seller.

items.title: OpenMouse expands beyond gaming mice with keyboard support
items.content:
OpenMouse, the open-source alternative to software suites like Logitech G Hub, Razer Synapse and SteelSeries GG, has expanded beyond gaming mice with new keyboard support. The latest beta release adds compatibility for keyboards from Logitech, Razer, SteelSeries and Wooting, allowing users to manage settings without relying on each manufacturer's software package.
As spotted by TechPowerUp, the OpenMouse project originally launched as a community-driven alternative to proprietary mouse configuration tools and now supports more than 260 mice across dozens of brands. With the latest beta, OpenMouse is beginning to extend the same approach to gaming keyboards, bringing support for features such as adjustable actuation, Rapid Trigger, SOCD, per-key RGB lighting and profile management, depending on the keyboard model.
Image credit: TechPowerUp
Keyboard support remains a work in progress, however. According to reports, some models are already functioning correctly, while others still exhibit issues. For example, a Wooting 80HE reportedly connected successfully during testing but was unable to correctly load keymaps or apply configuration changes. Key remapping functionality also appears to be absent from the current beta release.
OpenMouse's developers are continuing to expand compatibility and are encouraging users to participate in testing. If the project reaches its goals, it could eventually offer a single configuration tool for peripherals from multiple manufacturers, reducing the need to install separate software suites for each device.

Assassin’s Creed Valhalla celebrates 40 million players with NG+ mode and more
items.content:
Despite many of their modern entries being somewhat by-the-numbers, Ubisoft’s Assassin’s Creed franchise continues to be a massive part of the publisher’s portfolio. As part of the company’s recent Fall 2026 franchise update, the team at Ubisoft announced that 2020’s Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is set to receive a surprise update in celebration of the game’s latest milestone – having officially surpassed 40 million total players.
During the team’s latest franchise update (where-in they confirmed that there are currently no AC remakes in the works), Ubisoft revealed that one of the franchise’s most maligned releases – Assassin’s Creed Valhalla – continues to attract millions of new players, writing:
“Assassin's Creed Valhalla recently surpassed 40 million players and, to celebrate, we're bringing one of the community's most requested features: the (very, very, very) long-awaited New Game+, arriving November 5.”
Of course, 40 million players does not equate to 40 million copies sold, especially as Valhalla has been playable across a multitude of services including but not limited to PlayStation Plus and the publisher’s own Ubisoft+ subscription platform.
Still, for a game which is deemed by many to be one of Assassin’s Creed’s weakest entries (mired by a bloat of content and minimal opportunities to roleplay as an actual assassin), 40 million players is a massive figure.
Assuming Valhalla’s 100+ hour experience wasn’t enough for you, the new game+ mode introduces a suite of additions, including:
New runes
A stash system
New rewards / cosmetics
Mithril – “a new resource to upgrade Divine Gear and strengthen runes”
Additionally, the team announced that the upcoming patch will bring with it “current-generation console updates”. Given the fact that Valhalla already has a native current-gen release, it will be interesting to see what exactly is added. Official PS5 Pro support perhaps? We won’t have to wait long to find out.

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day has reportedly sold 400,000 copies despite half a Billion Dollars budget
items.content:
Initially set to launch across PC, Xbox and PlayStation, The Coalition’s Gears of War: E-Day was seemingly pivoted to becoming an Xbox console exclusive at the last-minute in an effort to boost Microsoft’s console output. Whether this will prove to have been a smart move in the long-term remains to be seen, but according to insiders, Gears of War E-Day has been off to a slow start – with the title reportedly having sold less than half-a-million units so far (despite costing $500 million to develop).
As expected from Microsoft, the console maker has not shared any official data regarding the early performance of their most-recent exclusive: Gears of War: E-Day. That said, multiple insiders have since come out to offer some preliminary figures, with The Verge’s Tom Warren claiming: “One source tells me that more than 400,000 copies of the game have been sold across Xbox and Steam.”
While 400K units sold is certainly nothing to sniff as (especially as the game released less than a month ago and was available day-one on Xbox Game Pass), E-Day will likely need to sell well over 5 million copies in order to break-even.
This is due to the fact that according to multiple sources – including known insider Jason Schreier – the total budget for Gears of War: E-Day landed at around $500 million. Considering the fact that the best-selling entry of all time (Gears 2) is said to have sold fewer than 7 million units, it begs the question as to whether E-Day will be able to make its money back at all.
Of course, being a console exclusive, E-Day is in some ways intended as an Xbox-seller more so than a title designed to push as many units as possible. Still, with its half a Billion budget and fewer than 500,000 copies sold so far, it will be interesting to see whether Microsoft deems their strategy of making the game exclusive as having been a success or not.

items.title: Sony’s Bend Studio will reportedly release its next game in 2027
items.content:
Since the arrival of their last game all the way back in 2019, we’ve heard very little from Sony’s Bend Studio, with the most recent reports claiming that the team were at one point working on a live-service title which was ultimately cancelled – leading to nearly a 3rd of the studio’s workforce being laid off. Despite this, the team appear to have been working hard on another new project, with reports claiming that Sony Bend’s next title is set to be announced and released in 2027.
As reported by the publication mp1st, despite having their previous live-service game cancelled by Sony, the Days Gone team at Bend Studio are currently in the advanced stages of development on an entirely new project.
Though early details remain light, according to the report, Sony Bend is currently planning to unveil their new game some time in 2027. That’s not all however, with the publication claiming that this title is also scheduled to launch next year, owing to it being “much further along in development” than some might expect.
That said, little else is known about the title as of right now, with the only other ‘confirmed’ details being the fact that it will be an entirely new IP which utilises a 3rd-person perspective, alongside some form of co-op functionality (though the extent of this remains unknown).
Though Days Gone failed to match the highs of other first-party PlayStation offerings critically, the open-world shooter did manage to be a commercial success in the long-run, with the infamous Insomniac Games leak revealing that the title had reached nearly 7.5 million copies sold as of early 2022.
While leaked details on the live-service ‘Project Mirror Pond’ did show some promise, it is encouraging to see that its cancellation appears to have not set the team back too much. Still, with Days Gone nearing 8 years old, it is high time we got to see something new from the studio.

Epomaker launches affordable EM3 tri-mode gaming mouse with charging dock
items.content:
Epomaker has announced the EM3, a new lightweight wireless gaming mouse featuring a carbon fibre-reinforced shell and a bundled magnetic charging dock. Despite those premium touches, the mouse arrives with an affordable $35.99 price tag.
Weighing around 56g, the EM3 is aimed at gamers looking for a lightweight mouse without venturing into enthusiast-level pricing territory. The mouse uses a PAW3315 optical sensor with support for up to 16,000 DPI and offers tri-mode connectivity via 2.4GHz wireless, Bluetooth and USB. Epomaker says the shape has been designed for small to medium-sized hands, particularly for claw-grip users.
Power comes from a 600mAh battery, which Epomaker rates for up to 55 hours of use on a full charge. The EM3 also ships with a magnetic charging dock that uses contact pins to recharge the mouse when docked. Alongside charging duties, the dock incorporates RGB lighting controls through a dedicated hardware button.
Users can customise settings through Epomaker's Driver 3.0 software or the browser-based Epomaker Hub utility. The software supports features such as button remapping, macro creation and DPI adjustment, allowing users to tailor the mouse to their own preferences.
The Epomaker EM3 is available in black, silver and pink, with pricing set at $35.99.

items.title: 8 Years Later, a Buffy Star's Obscure Thriller Is Waiting to Be Discovered on Free Streaming
items.content: There was a time in the distant past when good things could occasionally come out of Twitter. Back in 2017, novelists Sam Sykes (the Aeons’ Gate series) and Chuck Wendig (Blackbirds, Star Wars: Aftermath) got on the website currently known as X to co-write an improvised horror satire. The result was a firmly tongue-in-cheek deconstruction of slasher movies, concerning Sykes' unnamed character’s new job as a camp counselor and an unfolding massacre in the woods. The story quickly went viral. (While the tweets are still up, Wendig has since abandoned X and locked his account, so the original story can no longer be read outside of a handful of unofficial screenshot archives.)

items.content: The original Fable checked all of the boxes of a good fairy tale: a classic good-versus-evil tale set in a high-fantasy version of Fake Britain. You played as a hero (literally, the “Hero of Oakvale”) fighting against a guy who considered burning down villages his idea of a good time. Fable’s big innovation lay in its morality system: Depending on your actions, the hero’s appearance would change (ex: you’d grow devil horns if you were evil), as would the way the citizens of Albion would react to him. Just like the main characters of stories like Jack and the Beanstalk, Little Red Riding Hood, and other quintessential fairy tales, you were consigned to live with the consequences of your actions — good or bad.

items.title: 6 Perfect Star Trek Episodes to Watch to Say Goodbye to Patrick Stewart
items.content: Even more significant than the quantity of Star Trek that Stewart made was the quality. Kirk is in many ways a classic pulp action hero. He faces conflicts head on, never afraid to throw a punch or flirt with a sexy alien. Picard represents a different form of masculinity, valuing compassion, knowledge, and communication above all else. He is the endlessly patient father figure for his crew, and for the next generation of Star Trek viewers, presiding over one of the most beautiful visions of what the future could look like. It’s that connection that has left fans in mourning following his death on Thursday at the age of 86.

Mark's enthusiasm for computers dampened at an early age by the rubber-keyed Sinclair Spectrum 48K and feelings of Commodore 64 envy. However, in the mid-80s, hope in a digital future was rekindled by the purchase of an Atari 520 STe. Since that time Mark has used a multitude of computers for fun and professional endeavors. He often owned both Macs and PCs but went cold on the former after OS9 was killed off, and warmed to the latter with the introduction of Windows XP.

Early work years were spent in artwork and reprographics but in the late noughties, Mark started to blog about computers, Taiwanese food culture, and guitar design. This activity led to a full-time position writing about breaking PC tech news for HEXUS, for the best part of a decade. When HEXUS was abruptly closed, Mark helped with the foundation of Club386, before finding a new home at Tom's Hardware.

When not wearing through the keycap legends on his PC keyboards, Mark can be found wandering the computer malls of Taiwan's neon-lit conurbations and enjoying local and international cuisine.

items.title: Let’s Game Now raises ₹30 Crore to build Indian Super Gaming League
items.content:
The capital will support the development of the Indian Super Gaming League (ISGL), a franchise-based gaming and entertainment property. (Photo credit: Inc 42)
Bengaluru-based esports company Let’s Game Now has raised ₹30 crore to accelerate the development of the Indian Super Gaming League (ISGL), a franchise-based gaming and entertainment property.
The investment round was led by industrialist Anand Mahindra and Bestvantage Investments, with participation from an undisclosed UAE-based family office, according to Inc42. The company has not disclosed its valuation, the equity stake involved or the individual contributions of the investors.
The funding will support the development of ISGL, which aims to bring competitive gaming, sports and entertainment together through a structured franchise model.
Building a franchise-based esports league
ISGL is central to Let’s Game Now’s expansion plans. The proposed league is designed around teams and recurring competitions, moving beyond standalone tournaments and brand-led gaming events.
The league was announced with eight teams associated with established sporting properties: Mumbai City FC, FC Goa, Chennaiyin FC, Kerala Blasters FC, Inter Kashi, Puneri Paltan, Bangalore Bhargavas and Andhra Agneyas.
Its format spans five games: chess, EA Sports FC 26, Call of Duty: Mobile, FAU-G and Cricket 26. The competition is designed to use city-based qualifiers as a route for players to enter the league.
The funding is expected to help Let’s Game Now advance the league's development. However, the company has not announced a detailed timeline for its next stage or disclosed the proposed franchise economics.
Anand Mahindra’s investment in esports
Mahindra’s participation connects the venture with an investor who has previously been involved in building professional sports leagues in India, including the Pro Kabaddi League and the Global Chess League.
The investment also comes as esports companies explore business models built around franchises, sponsorships, broadcasting and organised competitions.
For ISGL, the challenge will be to attract franchise owners and commercial partners while building a consistent audience across games and seasons.
Let’s Game Now’s existing gaming network
Founded in 2018 by Santanu Basu, Let’s Game Now operates an esports platform that connects brands with gaming communities. Its services include online competitions, offline events, and live broadcasting across South Asia and Southeast Asia.
The company claims to have a community of more than 1.4 million members and to have organised over 2,000 events across more than 18 countries. It also says it works with over 30 clients.
This existing network could provide a base for acquiring participants and audiences for ISGL. The company will, however, need to convert that reach into sustained viewership and recurring commercial revenue.
The commercial test for ISGL
India's large gaming audience offers an opportunity for organised esports properties, but building a franchise-based league requires more than a large player base.
ISGL will need to establish a sustainable model for franchise participation, sponsorships, media partnerships and audience engagement. The costs of production, marketing and league operations will also have to be supported by recurring revenue.
The ₹30 crore investment gives Let’s Game Now capital to develop the property. Its longer-term prospects will depend on whether it can turn the league into a commercially sustainable competition with consistent participation and viewership.

Mark's enthusiasm for computers dampened at an early age by the rubber-keyed Sinclair Spectrum 48K and feelings of Commodore 64 envy. However, in the mid-80s, hope in a digital future was rekindled by the purchase of an Atari 520 STe. Since that time Mark has used a multitude of computers for fun and professional endeavors. He often owned both Macs and PCs but went cold on the former after OS9 was killed off, and warmed to the latter with the introduction of Windows XP.

Early work years were spent in artwork and reprographics but in the late noughties, Mark started to blog about computers, Taiwanese food culture, and guitar design. This activity led to a full-time position writing about breaking PC tech news for HEXUS, for the best part of a decade. When HEXUS was abruptly closed, Mark helped with the foundation of Club386, before finding a new home at Tom's Hardware.

When not wearing through the keycap legends on his PC keyboards, Mark can be found wandering the computer malls of Taiwan's neon-lit conurbations and enjoying local and international cuisine.

This activity led to a full-time position writing about breaking PC tech news for HEXUS, for the best part of a decade. When HEXUS was abruptly closed, Mark helped with the foundation of Club386, before finding a new home at Tom's Hardware.

When not wearing through the keycap legends on his PC keyboards, Mark can be found wandering the computer malls of Taiwan's neon-lit conurbations and enjoying local and international cuisine.

In Puckoff: Reloaded, Hockey Is About More Than Scoring Goals
items.content:
Summary
Chaotic new take on hockey out now on Xbox Series X|S.
Brutal fights, ridiculous takedowns and riveting action within a unique narrative.
How we imagined a game inspired by childhood hockey playing and storytelling.
What happens when five Finnish developers take the hockey they grew up playing on frozen ponds and turn it into a story about the greatest underground hockey player who ever lived?
When I think about my childhood, some of my best memories aren’t from school, holidays or birthday parties.
They’re from the ice.
Growing up in Finland, I spent enormous amounts of time on frozen outdoor rinks and ponds, playing hockey with friends. You didn’t need to organize it weeks in advance or check everyone’s calendar. You just went to the rink. Games happened. Friendships happened. Some of the people I met through hockey back then are still my friends today.
There was something special about those games. The rules could be flexible, teams could change, and somebody would inevitably try something ridiculous. That feeling became one of the starting points for Puckoff.
When we created Puckoff: Reloaded, we wanted to bring some of that feeling back. Many of the game’s rinks are frozen outdoor ponds inspired by the places where we grew up playing.
Then we asked ourselves a simple question: What if winning didn’t mean scoring more goals?
A Different Kind of Hockey
In most hockey games, you know what you’re supposed to do: Get the puck. Score goals. Win the game. In Puckoff: Reloaded, there are a few more options. You can score. Set up a teammate. Make the perfect pass. Or you can knock someone out.
And nobody in this world seems particularly bothered by that last option.
That’s the world we wanted to create: a story-driven hockey game where fighting isn’t a random side activity, but part of the sport and its strange underground culture. I’ve played a lot of the big hockey games over the years. They’re great at what they do, but I always found myself thinking: “Why can’t I just do that?”
You know the feeling. An opponent does something you don’t like, and you want to give them a little… extra attention. But the game tells you no. That’s when I realized one of the things I love about games. They let us experiment, cause chaos and do things we wouldn’t necessarily do in real life. So, I thought: what if a hockey game actually embraced that? That’s how Puckoff: Reloaded began.
In our version of hockey, scoring goals is still useful. It’s just not the only way to win.
We’re Not Just Making a Hockey Game
I’ve always loved storytelling, and for years I’ve had a particular dream: What would it be like if a big hockey game actually had a real story? Not just a career mode where you play a season and upgrade your player. I mean a proper story. Characters you care about. Mysteries. Rivalries. Friendships. A reason to wonder what happens next. That’s what we wanted Puckoff: Reloaded to be.
Between matches, the game uses a visual-novel-inspired presentation to tell a larger story. The hockey games aren’t disconnected challenges. They’re part of a journey. And that journey is about finding a legend.
The Search for Dominator
At the heart of Puckoff: Reloaded is a hockey legend named Dominator. He’s been playing underground hockey matches for decades, and nobody really knows how he’s managed to keep going for so long. What everyone does know is that he has never lost a game.
For the player character, Dominator isn’t just another hockey player. He’s the reason to keep playing. The dream is simple: find Dominator and eventually play alongside him. Getting there means meeting the people who inhabit this underground hockey world and proving you’re good enough to belong in it. Eventually, that leads to the Cage.
Welcome to the Cage
The biggest fights in Puckoff: Reloaded don’t happen in a traditional hockey arena. They happen underground.
The Cage is where some of the game’s most dangerous opponents are waiting. These boss matches are different from ordinary games: you’re not simply facing another team and trying to score more goals. You’re facing a character with their own identity, abilities and way of playing. And if you’re going to get closer to Dominator, you’ll have to get through them.
Our Dream is Bigger Than This Game
I’m proud of what our five-person team has created, but I also see Puckoff: Reloaded as the beginning of something. My dream has always been to make story-driven hockey games with the scope and production values of the big-budget games. I want hockey games where you remember the characters as much as the matches. Stories that make you care who wins. I want a game where you can spend an evening playing hockey with your friends, laughing when somebody gets knocked out—and then come back the next day because you genuinely want to know what happens to the characters.
We’re not a huge studio. We’re five people in Finland making the game we wanted to play. For me, that’s what Puckoff has always been about. It started with the frozen ponds where some of my best childhood memories were made. Now we’re taking those memories, adding a ridiculous amount of fighting, creating a hockey legend who hasn’t lost in decades, and turning the whole thing into a story.
We just have to find Dominator first.
Puckoff: Reloaded launches on Xbox Series X|S today.

items.title: Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game Enters the Avatar State
items.content:
The Avatar State Patch is available today for Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game on XBOX Series X|S, and it’s the biggest update the game has seen. It brings a fresh new look for the game’s menus and in-match displays, two totally reimagined fighters, Ranked Mode 2.0, quality-of-life upgrades for story, versus, and online play, plus balance changes for every character on the roster.
Since the game launched earlier this year with 12 characters from “Avatar: The Last Airbender” and “The Legend of Korra,” fighters have been putting their bending (or boomerangs) to the test, and our team has been watching closely. This patch is the result. It’s the game we envisioned from the beginning, and now it’s ready for you to play.
What’s in the Avatar State Patch:
A new look, everywhere. Menus, character select, stage select and the in-match interface have all been redesigned.
Two reimagined fighters. Avatar Aang and Nightmare Korra return with new art, new attacks and new super moves.
Every fighter rebalanced. From Aang to Zaheer, every character has been fine-tuned for fairer, more exciting matches.
More ways to play and learn. Story Mode+, Story difficulty settings, new tutorials and Combo Trials, Story stages in Versus, and more.
Reimagined Characters: Avatar Aang and Nightmare Korra
The two fighters at the heart of this patch are among the most powerful forms in the Avatar universe. Studio Art Director Giancarlo Montalbano, Art Director Santiago R. Villa, and Combat Director Young share how they brought them to life, and why they took the pair in opposite directions. “For Aang, his Avatar pose looks to elevate his presence in all ways, while for Korra it looks to diminish it. One is solemn and imposing while the other is languid and elusive.” Villa explains.
Avatar Aang
Avatar Aang’s character sheet, with his glowing Air Nomad tattoos idle pose, full turnaround and the lightning scar on his back.
In the Avatar State, Aang taps into the power of every Avatar who came before him. Young points to his final showdown with Fire Lord Ozai as the biggest touchstone, along with Avatar State moments across the series, from channeling Kyoshi on Avatar Day to facing the Sandbenders. While regular Aang is playful, Young describes this version as pure, overwhelming power, landing precise elemental attacks with the smallest movements. Villa adds that he’s the only fighter in the game lit from below, a deliberate choice to make him look mysterious and boss-like. Young’s favorite move is his signature special, Avatar’s Ascension, which lifts him into an air sphere packed with callbacks to the Ozai fight.
His new Level 4 super, his most powerful attack, brings in a special guest: Avatar Roku, straight out of the Winter Solstice two-parter. “Aang’s direct manifestations of prior Avatars ended up being something very unique to him,” says Young, “so we felt like we had to include it!”
Montalbano admits Avatar Aang was the trickier of the two, since his arm tattoos had to read correctly from every angle. Villa shares another hard call: Aang’s foot scar is missing, because with fighters switching sides, it would have been on the wrong foot half the time.
Nightmare Korra
Nightmare Korra’s character sheet. Her hunched idle pose, chains on both wrists, and menacingly glowing eyes set her apart from Korra.
Young explains that Nightmare Korra is the dark reflection that haunted Korra in “The Legend of Korra” episode Korra Alone, with her final fight against Zaheer at the end of Book 3 as another influence. “She’s a manifestation of that berserk state…alongside being a kind of spooky, ghost-like entity so we wanted to try and hit both of those angles pretty sharply. So you’ll see big contrasts between her slowly dragging her feet, then suddenly exploding into big chain swings or teleports.” Villa notes that she now wears chains on both wrists instead of one, a nod to how much weight they carry in her story.
Her visual effects are some of the wildest in the game. Montalbano highlights the mercury in her super moves and a victory pose that zooms through a fish-eye lens into her transformation into Vaatu, which he calls “very unique compared to a lot of other stuff in the game.” For Young, the standout is her Final Technique, Eternal Nightmare, a big team effort that looks just as striking when it misses as when it lands.
Young also shared a fun fact: early prototypes had her health constantly draining to represent mercury poisoning. It didn’t make for interesting play, so she simply starts with less health instead.
What’s new in battle
Battle Balance
There’s a lot to dig into, but here’s a closer look at two of the biggest shifts.
Azula’s Ambition’s Spark, her Focused Stance exclusive move, has vastly improved to allow much more variety in gameplay. It now automatically tracks much closer to your opponent’s position. Its detonation is a much greater hitbox and can also be flow cancelable.
Sokka’s sword special techniques, under certain circumstances using his Master Piandao support, can now directly cancel into a boomerang toss! Upon having at least 10 stacks of successful sword hits, Sokka permanently unlocks that ability for the rest of the match!
You can find the full patch notes on the Paramount Games site when the patch goes live.
Nightmare Korra: a new moveset to match
Nightmare Korra’s new look goes deeper than just that. Her kit has been rebuilt to match her haunting presence.
Avatar Aang: enter Roku!
Roku’s Inferno is Avatar Aang’s new Super Technique. Aang communicates with the spirit world, temporarily transforming him into Roku who engulfs the entire battlefield with a scorching flame.
Character Vote: You Pick the Next Fighter
If you pre-ordered Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game or upgraded to the Deluxe Edition, you get a say in who completes the Year 1 Pass, the set of five extra characters included with the Deluxe Edition. Iroh, Ty Lee, Lin Beifong and Bolin are confirmed, and the fifth spot is up to you. Standard Edition pre-orders get one vote, Deluxe Edition comes with an extra vote for Year 1 Pass. (For example: If you have two votes, you can either submit a new voting ranking, or duplicate the first vote). Upgrading to Deluxe (even without pre-order) will also entitle you to a vote. Voting runs for one month. Just look for the voting option on the main menu. The candidates are:
Tenzin
Kuvira
Amon
King Bumi
Asami Sato
The Avatar State Patch for Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game is available now on XBOX Series X|S. The Standard Edition is just $29.99, and the Deluxe Edition, which includes the Year 1 Pass, is $49.99. Thanks for fighting alongside us. The Avatar State Awaits.

items.title: Curse of Resthaven: Tips and Tricks to Unravel the Island’s Secrets
items.content:
Hi there! I’m Scott Christian, the studio director of Hilltop Studios here in Toronto, and the game director of Curse of Resthaven. We make games with a particular emphasis on strong characters, intricate storytelling, unique mechanics, and the occasional musical interlude.
Before making games, I spent fifteen years working as a composer and conductor here in Toronto, mainly in theatre. That background informs how we approach our games at Hilltop: character, timing, and a good dramatic reveal go a long way. Our debut, Lil’ Guardsman, was a comedic fantasy gate-guard simulator about a twelve-year-old put in charge of a castle gate, with the fate of the world in her hands.
For our follow-up, Curse of Resthaven, we decided to take a different turn into gothic horror, creeping dread, and a mystery that unfolds over a repeating six-day time loop. You play as Ambrose, the island’s newly appointed governor, tasked with restoring prosperity to the colony but he also has his own agenda: finding his missing niece, Amalia. The problem is that Resthaven is destroyed six days into his tenure… and Ambrose is sent back to the day of his arrival, the only one to remember the island’s fate.
Mashing up mechanics from narrative adventures, trading sims, deckbuilders, and roguelikes, Curse of Resthaven challenges you to investigate a town full of secrets, keep its economy running, and venture into the strange wilderness beyond its borders. You have six days to work with before disaster strikes and the island resets. Fortunately, you get to keep what you learn.
Solving the mystery is just the first step. You’ll soon discover there are three different timelines to explore, and only by reaching all three conclusions will you unlock the fourth, true ending.
Whether you’re stepping onto Resthaven for the first time or looking to make the most of your next loop, here are a few tips to help you get started.
A Few Simple Tips
Curse of Resthaven is a game about connecting the dots. Its systems feed into one another, and the best discoveries often come from combining information gathered in different ways. Here are a few things to keep in mind as you investigate the island.
Talk to everyone, and then talk to them again. Resthaven’s residents have their own motivations, grudges, and secrets. What someone tells you depends on what Ambrose already knows, what topics you bring up, and what has happened during the current loop. If a character isn’t being helpful, you may simply need to learn a little more before approaching them. Your journal can be counted on to let you know when to ask someone about something again.
Pay attention during interrogations. You can question characters about different topics to uncover clues, advance quests, and learn more about the island. Information gathered from one resident may unlock the topic needed to move the needle with another. If you’re stuck, revisit people you’ve spoken to and see whether they have a perspective on newly acquired topics or, better yet, can guide you in the right direction.
Don’t treat trading as a side activity. As governor, Ambrose is responsible for keeping Resthaven’s economy moving. Merchant ships bring goods to buy and sell, while the island’s businesses can be upgraded to produce useful resources. Money is only part of the equation: having the right resources is essential for pursuing opportunities elsewhere, including expeditions into the wilderness.
Experiment with your approach. Not every problem has an obvious solution, and not every promising lead will pay off immediately. Try different approaches, pursue unexpected conversations, and see where your investigations take you. Even a botched loop may teach you something useful for the next one.
Make the Most of the Time Loop
The six-day time loop is at the heart of Curse of Resthaven. Each loop begins with the island’s inhabitants returning to their usual routines, but Ambrose retains his knowledge and progression. That distinction is everything.
You aren’t expected to solve the entire mystery in one pass. Instead, each loop gives you another opportunity to apply what you’ve learned, approach old problems differently, and uncover information that was previously out of reach.
Knowledge is your most valuable resource. A character who refuses to cooperate on Day 1 might be much more forthcoming once you’ve discovered what motivates them. An apparently impossible obstacle might become straightforward once you know the right person to talk to or the right question to ask.
Plan your days around what you want to learn. There are more people to question, businesses to manage, and places to explore than you can necessarily get to in a single loop. Focus on the leads that seem most promising, and don’t worry if you have to leave something for next time.
Use each reset as an opportunity. When the island resets, you can take a different approach with the benefit of everything you’ve discovered. You don’t have to repeat the same actions just because you did them last time. If you already know where a particular lead is going, spend that time pursuing something new.
The goal isn’t simply to repeat the same six days until you get everything right. It’s to use what you learned last time to change what happens the next time.
Venture Beyond the Town
Beyond the safety of Resthaven’s fortified walls lies a much stranger version of the island. Expeditions take Ambrose into this wilderness through a card-based narrative system that blends roguelikes, deckbuilders, and choose-your-own-adventure games.
Each expedition draws encounters from a pool, meaning your journey can unfold differently from one attempt to the next. You’ll face decisions, discover strange events, and encounter opportunities that may not appear again on your next trip.
Expect the unexpected. Expeditions aren’t fixed sequences of events. The encounters you discover on one outing may be very different from those on another, so stay curious and be prepared to adapt.
Don’t assume you’ve seen everything. There are more encounters than you’ll experience in a single run. Returning to the wilderness on subsequent playthroughs can reveal entirely new stories and discoveries.
Remember that expeditions are part of the larger investigation. The wilderness isn’t separate from the mystery unfolding in town. Information and resources you gather can help you make progress elsewhere, so consider how an expedition might support your other goals.
Explore Every Corner Of Resthaven
It’s worth taking the time to look around. Beyond the main investigation, Resthaven contains optional discoveries, including collectible moth relics and other secrets tucked away throughout the town.
These discoveries reward players who aren’t in a rush. You can barely take a single step if you rely heavily on the handy town map + fast travel functionality, but you’ll certainly miss out on some optional, flavourful side content. Give yourself permission to wander a little. After all, in Resthaven you have nothing but time (in six-day intervals)!
And don’t be afraid to revisit familiar places. As you learn more about the colony and its inhabitants, locations and conversations that seemed unremarkable at first may take on new significance.
What To Do If You’re Stuck
Your journal is your best friend. Check your active leads for hints about what to pursue next. If you’ve exhausted all the possibilities in town, it may be time to head back out on expeditions and look for Amalia’s campsites. And your journal will probably tell you so!
Your journal has another trick up its sleeve, too. After the opening hours, you’ll unlock a timeline showing important events across the six-day loop and where they take place. If you’re stumped by a “???” on the timeline, it means something important is happening at that moment you haven’t discovered yet. To progress, you might just need to be in the right place at the right time.
The town map is another easy-to-miss resource. It shows which characters are accessible in each zone at any given time. Once you’ve spoken to a named NPC, their question mark becomes a portrait, making it much easier to track them down in subsequent loops. Still seeing a “?” in a zone? That might be a good place to start looking for someone new.
Finally, don’t underestimate the power of a little community gossip. Some leads require interrogation, but the answer might simply be to ask the townspeople about a particular topic. Resthaven is a small, tight-knit community, and information has a way of getting around.
We’ve designed the investigation around a trail of clues(We’ve classed them as bronze/silver/gold behind the scenes, but you won’t see these terms in-game.)
Bronze clues give you a little information and nudge you in the right direction, and many townspeople have them
Silver clues offer more specific details and bring you closer to the truth; fewer townspeople have them
Gold clues unambiguously reveal the next step in a lead. Only one or two townspeople have them
Follow the trail, and you shouldn’t be left out in the cold for long.
Don’t Worry About Seeing Everything the First Time
Curse of Resthaven features three branching timelines, each revealing different pieces of the larger mystery. You won’t necessarily encounter every quest or revelation during a single playthrough, and that’s intentional.
As you progress, you’ll uncover new information that changes how you understand the island and its people. Some discoveries will answer questions, while others will leave you with even more to investigate.
Once you’ve completed a timeline, New Game+ introduces Ambrose’s growing sense of déjà vu, allowing you to fast-track through content you’ve already experienced and focus on what’s different. You can spend less time retracing familiar steps and more time exploring new possibilities.
So don’t worry about finding every secret on your first visit. Pay attention, follow the leads that interest you, and let your growing knowledge guide you through the next loop.
Resthaven has a great many secrets. The trick is figuring out which ones to pursue, when to pursue them, and what to do with what you discover.
Six days remain. Good luck, Governor. You’ll need it.

items.title: Queen’s Domain Releases Today! Some Beginner’s Pro Tips for Success
items.content:
Queen’s Domain is a retro-fantasy action RPG that strands you alone on the monster-infested isle of Neasied, available today on XBOX Series X|S. You’ll need wits as well as strength if you want to survive in this twisting, secretive world. Here’s a list of top tips for newly minted warriors, assembled by the Future Friends gang. Read on, if you don’t want to wind up as meat for the worms…
Your Sword is much more than just a weapon
If you think a sword can only be helpful for fighting monsters, think again! In Queen’s Domain, your sword is as much for traversing the world and platforming as it is for fighting. Practice ‘dashing’ with your holy sword, and soon you’ll be able to reach faraway places.
Each battle is a dance
Those who swing their weapons around wildly won’t last long on Neasied. If you are careless and don’t pay attention to the rhythms of your opponents, you’ll be defeated by even the most trifling of enemies. Watch carefully to learn their attack patterns, study the bestiary to learn their weaknesses, and make sure you use the right weapon for each encounter. Preparation is everything!
Curiosity pays
Queen’s Domain is designed to reward curiosity. Taking the path less trodden can lead you to hidden treasures, secret paths and much more. If you’re ever really stumped, here’s a top tip: the dead sometimes leave hints for the living…
Keep your eyes open
Enemies can come at you from any angle, and often when you least expect it. Make sure you equip your favourite throwable weapon when venturing out into the world and always look around you for potential threats around and above you. Blundering into open spaces is a quick way to a grisly end.
Not just you, your weapons Level Up too!
The more you practice with a weapon, the more powerful it will become! If you get stuck at an especially difficult place, try retracing your steps and leveling up your weapon of choice. Then you can save and return with a better chance at defeating the evils around you!
That’s all the wisdom we can offer you for now. This game is a labour of love from a small, passionate team, and we sincerely wish you the best of luck as you embark on this adventure.

items.title: Things That Go Beep in the Night: Agentic AI Joins the Search for Extraterrestrial Signals
items.content:
While science fiction lore tells us that humans will meet extraterrestrial life in the form of little green men, the detail that should raise hairs this Halloween is this: the search for extraterrestrial intelligence took a major leap forward with AI, and it increasingly focuses on AI agents built by humans listening for AI agents built by aliens.
Some scientists have suggested that extraterrestrial civilizations, if they exist, could be billions of years older than humanity. Such civilizations might have developed technologies far beyond humanity’s, including forms of AI.
Breakthrough Listen and the SETI Institute are bringing agentic AI into the daily search for extraterrestrial intelligence. At the Allen Telescope Array in Northern California, agents can now steer the instrument, enhance and correct incoming data, and apply AI models to the incoming stream — all from a single natural language request. The NVIDIA Holoscan platform processes the massive streams of sensor data, giving agents live data to act on.
The result is a faster, more adaptable search for potential signals from extraterrestrial life and technologies.
“As our new agentic observatories reach out into the universe, what they find may have much more in common with themselves than with the humans who created them,” said Andrew Siemion, Bernard M. Oliver chair for SETI at the SETI Institute and principal investigator of Breakthrough Listen. “But this isn’t something to fear. Rather, it’s a breakthrough in translation.”
Terabits a Second, Processed in Flight
Radio telescopes generate enormous volumes of data, creating a challenge for scientists who need to identify potentially interesting signals as observations unfold.
At the Allen Telescope Array, DAQIRI, a Holoscan platform library, enables the telescope to pull terabits per second of sensor data straight into GPU memory so observations are processed in flight rather than filling hard drives. CyberEther, a signal-processing framework developed at the SETI Institute, does the math using NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries including cuFFT and cuBLAS.
Nexus, a web-based observatory orchestrator, acts as the agent harness. It gives agents a single source of truth for instrument state, compute resources and pipelines and lets researchers monitor packet loss, read live spectrograms and rewrite signal-processing blocks — all by prompting in natural language. The system can handle 2.4 terabits per second on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, with inference running on premises, next to the instrument.
Put together, the system enables an agent to steer a telescope’s antennae, calibrate and focus the instrument for a clean signal, catch and fix data errors and plot the result. Agents compress what would take humans weeks or years into hours.
Science Fact, Not Fiction
The pipeline has already proven itself, achieving the first real-time AI detection of a pulsar — a rapidly spinning stellar remnant that pulses like a cosmic lighthouse — in the Crab Nebula.
Next, the team is evaluating open models including NVIDIA Nemotron for cases where data locality and turnaround matter most and for observatories that may someday run offline on the far side of the moon.
Learn more about NVIDIA AI for science.

items.title: Terrible Lizards: Movement Is Your Weapon
items.content:
Terrible Lizards, available now on XBOX Series X|S and Game Pass, is a first-person platforming game about escaping runaway dinosaur animatronics in an abandoned roadside attraction. That perspective was something we landed on pretty deliberately, through a process of both considering this particular game’s needs, as well as reviewing what we’ve loved about movement in other games.
When I think about the platforming games I’ve always enjoyed most, a lot of it comes down to rhythm. I like being able to move quickly, react to what’s coming, and string things together without constantly stopping to line everything up.
Jumping off the Shoulders of Giants
You can see that reactive flow really clearly in older 2D platformers like Donkey Kong Country or the early Mario games. With a limited screen in front of you, you don’t always have much time to plan. You’re reacting, trusting the mechanics, and finding a rhythm as you move through the level. That’s what I wanted to bring into Terrible Lizards, and the first-person perspective is a big part of bringing that satisfying, rhythmic, reactive gameplay to a 3D platformer.
Games like Mirror’s Edge and Dying Light are the obvious first-person platforming reference points, but we actually wanted Terrible Lizards to feel a little different moment to moment. We were chasing the tighter, more immediate game feel you get from games like Titanfall, Call of Duty, and Overwatch, where simply moving, jumping, and changing direction feels responsive and satisfying. You do see that kind of feel in first-person platforming games like Neon White, and that was closer to the balance we wanted: strong platforming mechanics built on top of controls that already feel good before you even start chaining moves together.
Floaty Empowerment
The controls needed to feel tight and immediate, but we also ended up giving the player a little bit of floatiness in the air. That mostly came from our aerial control system. Once you jump, you have the ability to adjust your trajectory before you land, and that became one of the most important pieces of the movement system.
For someone who isn’t especially confident with first-person platforming, it gives you room to correct yourself. If you jump too far, you can pull back. If you drift left or right, you can make a small adjustment. You have a little extra time to understand where you’re going and make the landing. At the same time, someone who gets really comfortable with the system can exploit that same freedom. They can make harder jumps, move through sections more efficiently, find faster routes, and occasionally bypass parts of a platforming sequence entirely.
That gave us something we were really happy with: a low skill floor, but a high skill ceiling. You don’t have to be amazing at platformers to play the game, but there’s a noticeably different way of moving through it once everything starts clicking. You can absolutely slow down, explore, look for collectibles, and work your way through the environments methodically. But once you understand the movement and start chaining together jumps, slides, wall runs, clambers, ledges, and swings without really thinking about each individual input, there’s a flow state to it that I find really satisfying.
No Fight, All Flight
We also made a very deliberate decision not to give the player weapons or other means to fight back. Your movement is really your main way of dealing with danger. When one of the creatures comes after you, the answer isn’t to turn around and shoot it. You have to move, and that made the monsters a natural way to test everything the player has been learning.
Sometimes that’s a direct chase. Sometimes a creature causes the environment around you to start collapsing and you have to survive. Other times you’re dropped into a more open arena where the monster is loose in the space with you and you have to complete objectives or figure out how to escape. Those moments let us use the same core movement mechanics in different ways without turning every encounter into the same kind of chase.
Between those moments, the game has more traditional platforming, exploration, environmental puzzles, and larger caverns where figuring out how to move through the space is part of the challenge. Then we can tighten things back down and put the player under pressure again. That variety was important to us. We didn’t want the whole game to be six hours of constant sprinting, and we also didn’t want movement to feel like something that only mattered in designated platforming sections.
It’s really the foundation of how you interact with the game. The story, collectibles, exploration, hunt arenas, and New Game Plus content all sit around that, but the movement is what everything keeps coming back to. Once players get comfortable with it, the hope is that they stop thinking about every individual mechanic and just start moving through the world naturally. That’s when the game shines, and obviously when something is chasing you, that familiarity with the movement starts to matter a lot more.
Terrible Lizards is available now on XBOX Series X|S and XBOX Game Pass.

items.title: The Journey of Crimson Desert Continues with Charting the Unknown
items.content:
Summary
Crimson Desert Enhanced: Charting the Unknown will be available on October 29, 2026 for XBOX Series X/S, XBOX on PC, with XBOX Play Anywhere support.
Charting the Unknown adds new storylines, ocean exploration, romance, stronghold management, boss rushes, and more.
XBOX players can try Crimson Desert Enhanced with a 5-hour Free Trial from October 29, 2026 through January 7, 2027.
Since its launch in March, the world of Crimson Desert — where Kliff and the Greymanes fight to rebuild what they lost — has grown with each update. Alongside improvements, the game has received brand new content, including boss rematches, and new features shaped by players’ adventures and stories across Pywel.
In August, we released Patch Version 2.00. The free update added new story moments and expanded voice-over and language support. Together with all the post-launch updates up to that date, the update came out as Crimson Desert Enhanced.
Lastly, with the launch of Charting the Unknown on October 29, Pywel is growing once again with even more adventures. The DLC brings new journeys across land and, for the first time, at sea, along with new ways to enrich your life in Pywel. Charting the Unknown is available now on XBOX Series X|S.
We want to thank all our Greymanes out there for the incredible support they have shown for Crimson Desert since launch. Your love for the game has brought us this far, and we are excited for you to experience what the DLC has to offer.
Now, let’s take a look at what awaits you in Charting the Unknown.
New Stories
Charting the Unknown introduces three new storylines, one each for Kliff, Oongka, and Damiane. With the fight for the Greymanes and Pywel behind them, each character sets out to forge their own path. Along the way, they will meet allies and threats both old and new, and chart their own course forward.
Exploring the Ocean
The DLC brings something many players have been asking for: ocean exploration. Dive into the sea and explore the underwater world, where you will discover ruins, treasure chests, and new creatures and mounts. You can also build your own ship and set sail across the Great Ocean of Pywel.
A Richer Life in Pywel
Charting the Unknown also deepens life in the world. Kliff, Oongka, and Damiane can form deeper bonds with some of Pywel’s inhabitants. Interact with them to build trust and strengthen your relationship, which may eventually blossom into romance and even marriage.
An upgraded housing system now lets you build your house from the ground up. And from the layout of the interior to the placement of walls, windows, and other structural elements, you have more control than ever to design your home, sweet home. There’s more: select castles, once liberated, can become yours. This will allow you to decorate their courtyards and interiors with unique objects and furnishings, turning a hard-won stronghold into another place you can call your own.
Also, if you want to take a more active role in the strongholds you have liberated, you can lease certain facilities such as a restaurant or a smithy and run them yourself. Assign equipment and comrades, decide which goods to sell, and grow each location’s recognition.
Garden of Trials
For those who don’t always like life too peaceful, Charting the Unknown has new content for you. The Garden of Trials is a combat-focused challenge where you face the bosses you have met throughout your adventures in Pywel, one after another. So test your skills and mettle to see if you hold up against these formidable foes.
Whether you are a seasoned Greymane or just taking your first steps in Pywel, there is plenty to discover.
And if you have not set out on the journey yet, this is the perfect time to do so! Crimson Desert is offering a 5-hour free trial of the base game for XBOX players from October 29 through January 6, so take the opportunity to step into Pywel and reach beyond!

The METRO Redux Next-Gen Update is out now on XBOX Series X|S consoles. First, the Next-Gen Update transforms the experience of playing both games through a series of major performance improvements. Once you’ve downloaded and applied the free update, you’ll be able to experience both titles in either true 4K resolution at 60fps or upscaled 4K at an even smoother 120fps. 4A TSR Upscaling and Antialiasing support will give players an even sharper, high fidelity experience.
